title: Print Server jobs stuck
description: Users in multiple departments at the Columbus office reported that documents sent to the shared HP LaserJet MFP on PS-PRINT01 were not printing reliably. The initial report was filed by Maria Gonzalez (emp ID E-40821) from the Finance group, noting that print jobs submitted from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MG remained stuck at 0% in the queue for over 30 minutes. The printer queue on PS-PRINT01 remained available, but some submitted jobs stalled and others delayed for extended periods, disrupting routine office printing across at least three floors. Initial reports referenced driver or spooler issues, but current checks did not show a consistent driver failure on the print server. Additional users including Derek Huang and Priya Nair confirmed similar behavior from their machines.
observed_errors: Print Spooler service errors (driver load failures)
root_cause: Intermittent print job processing failure not explained by queue state or driver version; likely related to specific document rendering or downstream printer handling, requiring further vendor or platform escalation.
resolution_steps: Capture failing sample job characteristics, including document type, size, application source, and exact time submitted through PS-PRINT01. Specifically collect the stalled jobs from mgonzalez (Q2_Finance_Report.xlsx, submitted 15:18 UTC) and dhuang (48-page PDF submitted 15:22 UTC from WORKSTATION-PC-DH) as representative failure samples.

Collect PrintService and Spooler event logs from PS-PRINT01 during a reproduced large-job failure and compare with a successful small-job submission. Include memory and CPU utilization snapshots from the print server during both scenarios. Logs should cover the window 15:00–16:00 UTC on 2026-05-09 and be packaged by the Workplace Services team for escalation.

Escalate to the print platform or printer vendor team (HP Enterprise Support) with the captured evidence — including spooler logs, job metadata, and driver version details from PS-PRINT01 — and validate whether a printer firmware update or application-specific rendering workaround is available. Reference case contact: Derek Huang (dhuang@corplabs.com, ext. 614-555-0247) as the on-site liaison at the Columbus office.
agent_questions: Please confirm whether all affected printers are mapped through PS-PRINT01 and whether users see the same 'Driver unavailable' message or only offline status. Also, can you verify the usernames of the affected staff so we can trace their specific print jobs in the queue? If possible, note the hostnames of the workstations experiencing the issue — for example, Maria Gonzalez mentioned her machine is WORKSTATION-PC-MG. Please send details to printops@corplabs.com or reach me at ext. 614-555-0193.

title: Users stuck in MFA prompt loop when accessing SSO apps (Okta/Azure AD)
description: Multiple staff users in the Portland office were trying to access Salesforce and Confluence through the SSO Portal, but after entering credentials they were returned to the MFA challenge repeatedly and Okta showed authentication rejected. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com, EMP-40821) and affected approximately 15 members of the 'Staff-West-Operations' Azure AD group. The problem began after a scheduled Azure AD group sync at 17:00 UTC on 2026-04-05 and blocked access to business SaaS applications through Okta/Azure AD SSO. Users confirmed that their Okta Verify push notifications were being sent but the session never completed.
observed_errors: Repeated MFA prompt with no session established
Conditional access evaluation indicates group mismatch
root_cause: Stale MFA enrollments on affected user accounts combined with an Azure AD group membership and conditional access policy mismatch after the recent group sync caused Okta SSO sessions to be rejected and users to loop back to MFA.
resolution_steps: Reproduced the MFA loop on test account testuser.ops1 and production account mchen (Maria Chen) from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (IP 10.42.16.88) and confirmed the session was being returned to the MFA challenge instead of completing SSO to the target application. Okta System Log showed repeated 'access_denied' outcomes.

Reset MFA enrollment for all 15 affected users in Okta, including mchen, rpatel, and dwhitfield, using self-service re-enrollment where possible via the Okta dashboard and admin-assisted reset (performed by kbriggs) for users who could not complete re-enrollment independently.

Reviewed the 'Staff-West-Operations' group's Azure AD membership and corrected the group GUID mapping used by the conditional access policy 'CA-SSO-SaaSApps-Staff' after the 2026-04-05T17:00Z delta sync changed the group object identifier.

Revalidated policy scope and application access so the 'Staff-West-Operations' group (all 15 members) was included in the expected SSO and conditional access path for Salesforce, Confluence, and Microsoft 365.

Tested successful sign-in for sample affected users — Maria Chen (mchen), Raj Patel (rpatel), and Donna Whitfield (dwhitfield) — to Salesforce and Confluence and confirmed the MFA prompt occurred only once before application access was granted.

Monitored Okta and Azure AD authentication activity for 24 hours (through 2026-04-06T20:00Z) and confirmed no further MFA loop behavior for the 'Staff-West-Operations' group. Agent Kevin Briggs (kbriggs) closed the incident after final verification with Maria Chen.

title: Expired TLS certificate on Load Balancer causing internal web service TLS failures
description: Users were trying to access the internal web service at https://internal.corplabs.com, but browsers displayed certificate warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and internal API clients failed TLS handshakes. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (EMP-40291) from the Portland office at approximately 17:45 UTC on 2025-12-19. The service was effectively unavailable over HTTPS because the TLS certificate presented by the F5 Big-IP load balancer lb-prod-01.corplabs.internal in us-east-1 had expired at 2025-12-19T04:00Z, impacting all internal services relying on that endpoint until the certificate and full chain were replaced.
root_cause: The TLS certificate terminating HTTPS on load balancer lb-prod-01 expired at 2025-12-19T04:00Z. Certificate renewal monitoring or alerting did not trigger in time, so the expired certificate and chain remained deployed and caused client validation failures.
resolution_steps: Request and issue a renewed TLS certificate for internal.corplabs.com from the internal Certificate Authority (ca-root-01.corplabs.internal), including the correct intermediate chain. CSR generated by nwilliams with SAN: internal.corplabs.com, key size RSA-2048, validity 1 year. Certificate issued with new serial and notAfter of 2026-12-19T04:00:00Z.

Install the renewed certificate and updated full chain on lb-prod-01.corplabs.internal and bind it to the HTTPS virtual server (VS-INTERNAL-443) handling internal.corplabs.com traffic. Deployment performed by nwilliams at 2025-12-19T18:42Z with a rolling reload to minimize connection drops.

Validate the certificate presented from client and load balancer perspectives to confirm the subject/SAN matches the service endpoint internal.corplabs.com and the chain no longer contains expired or missing intermediates. Verification performed from WORKSTATION-RK-4417 (10.22.14.87) and WORKSTATION-MC-3302 using openssl s_client and browser trust checks — all returned valid chain with correct notAfter date.

Run post-deployment HTTPS and API tests against internal.corplabs.com to confirm browser warnings and TLS handshake failures are cleared. Maria Chen (mchen) confirmed browser access restored without warnings. Automated API health checks from app-runner-07 returned HTTP 200 with valid TLS negotiation at 2025-12-19T18:55Z.

Restore and test certificate renewal monitoring and alerting in cert-monitor: jmartinez re-enabled the alert rule for internal.corplabs.com with a 30-day and 14-day pre-expiry notification schedule, sending to infra-certs@corplabs.com and dparker@corplabs.com. Updated the renewal process to verify both certificate issuance and successful deployment before expiry, including a post-deployment validation webhook.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused Internal Web Service TLS outages
description: Internal users and monitoring systems were trying to reach the Internal Web Service at https://appportal.corp.internal over HTTPS, but beginning around 2025-12-17 08:12 UTC the service presented certificate warnings and failed TLS handshakes. The issue was first reported by Danielle Ortega (dortega@corp.internal) from the Austin office, who received NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID errors in her browser. The load balancer LB-CENTRAL-01.corp.internal continued serving an expired certificate and outdated chain after renewal was missed, blocking normal access to the internal application and causing service unavailability over TLS for approximately 150 internal users.
root_cause: The primary TLS certificate for the Internal Web Service expired, and the renewed certificate and full chain were not deployed to the load balancer before expiration due to failed or missed renewal alerting.
resolution_steps: Requested and obtained a renewed TLS certificate (serial 4A:7C:9E:02:CC:40, valid 2025-12-17 through 2026-12-17) from the Certificate Authority CA-CENTRAL-01.corp.internal for the Internal Web Service at appportal.corp.internal, processed by Kevin Pratt (kpratt, EMP-90214).

Validated that the renewed certificate matched the service endpoint name appportal.corp.internal (SAN: DNS:appportal.corp.internal, DNS:appportal) and included the required intermediate and root certificate chain.

Deployed the renewed certificate and full chain to the load balancer LB-CENTRAL-01.corp.internal and Internal Web Service endpoint configuration on APPSRV-CENTRAL-02.corp.internal, replacing the expired certificate binding on port 443.

Restarted the load balancer TLS service on LB-CENTRAL-01.corp.internal so the updated certificate chain was actively served to clients. Verified successful handshake from WORKSTATION-PC-DO (10.42.8.77) and confirmed with Danielle Ortega in the Austin office that access was restored.

Re-enabled and tested certificate renewal monitoring in Nagios for appportal.corp.internal with 30/14/7-day expiry thresholds and alert escalation to kpratt@corp.internal and infra-alerts@corp.internal to detect future renewal failures before expiration.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: denied access to Finance shared drive
description: I was trying to open the Finance shared drive folder from both a mapped drive (F:) and the UNC path \\fileserver.corp\\Finance on my Windows 10 workstation WORKSTATION-PC-LM. Access prompted for credentials and then returned 'Access Denied,' preventing me from opening the department folder after a recent team change from Marketing to Finance and a password reset. My employee ID is EMP-40821 and my username is lmorales. Please help — I need access to prepare quarterly reports.
observed_errors: NTFS permission denied on folder open
root_cause: The user's AD account did not have the required Finance_Dept_Readers security group membership after the team change, so the user's refreshed and direct SMB access attempts were still denied by NTFS permissions on the Finance shared folder.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the Finance share access model and confirmed the required AD entitlement for the folder was the Finance_Dept_Readers security group. Verified this against the file server ACL for \\fileserver.corp\\Finance and confirmed with manager Derek Huang (dhuang@corplabs.com).
Validated that the user's account lmorales (employee ID EMP-40821) was missing Finance_Dept_Readers membership following the recent team change from Marketing to Finance.

Added the user lmorales to the Finance_Dept_Readers AD security group to restore the required read access to the Finance shared folder. Change performed by agent Marcus Bell (mbell) at 2026-03-14T14:19:00Z.

Had the user refresh authentication by purging cached tickets or signing out and back in so the updated group membership would be included in the access token. Laura confirmed she ran klist purge on WORKSTATION-PC-LM and then signed out and back in at the Charlotte office.
Retested access using the UNC path \\fileserver.corp\\Finance from WORKSTATION-PC-LM (IP 10.22.45.117) and confirmed the folder opened successfully without Access Denied for user lmorales.

Advised the user to remap the network drive (F:) if any stale credential prompt persisted on the mapped path, and provided instructions to contact the service desk at ext. 4200 if further issues arise.
agent_questions: Hi Laura, thanks for reaching out. Did you recently change teams or have a password reset, and does opening \\fileserver.corp\\Finance directly from your workstation at 10.22.45.117 show the same Access Denied result as the mapped drive? Also, can you confirm your AD username is lmorales and that you're working from the Charlotte office? I want to verify we're looking at the right account on the file server.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Users and internal integrations were trying to access the Internal Web Service at https://portal.internal.corplabs.com through the load balancer (LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal), but browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and dependent API calls from services owned by the Platform Engineering team failed TLS negotiation. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40291) from the Denver office at approximately 02:05 UTC on 2025-12-17. The service became unavailable over TLS after the presented certificate (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com, issued by CorpLabs Internal CA) passed its validity window on 2025-12-16T23:59:59Z, and the load balancer continued serving an outdated certificate chain containing an expired intermediate, blocking normal internal application access for all users in the us-east-1 environment.
root_cause: The Internal Web Service TLS certificate expired, the certificate renewal alerting path failed to trigger before expiration, and the load balancer continued presenting an outdated certificate chain instead of the renewed full chain.
resolution_steps: Validate the affected endpoint certificate validity period, subject names, and served chain from the client (tested from WORKSTATION-MC-4029 at 10.22.14.87) and load balancer path (LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal) to confirm expiration of CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com and chain mismatch with the expired intermediate.

Renew the Internal Web Service TLS certificate for portal.internal.corplabs.com through the Certificate Authority (CorpLabs Internal CA) and obtain the correct full certificate chain including the updated CorpLabs Internal Issuing CA G2 intermediate. Renewal performed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Deploy the renewed certificate (new serial issued 2025-12-17) and updated full chain to the load balancer LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal certificate store and replace the expired certificate references. Deployment handled by Robert Jackson (rjackson) from Network Operations.
Reload the load balancer configuration on LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal so new TLS assets are actively presented to clients and upstream services. Confirmed active by rjackson at 02:48 UTC.

Verify successful TLS handshakes and removal of browser certificate warnings from the service endpoint https://portal.internal.corplabs.com (confirmed by Maria Chen from WORKSTATION-MC-4029), then restore and test certificate expiration monitoring alert rule 'cert-expiry-30d-warning' targeting infra-certs@corplabs.com in the Certificate Management Service.
agent_questions: We are validating whether the TLS failure is caused by certificate expiration or an incomplete chain on the load balancer LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal. Please confirm whether users are seeing browser date-invalid warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) when accessing https://portal.internal.corplabs.com and whether internal API calls routed through the load balancer are failing during TLS handshake. I've asked rjackson (Robert Jackson, Network Operations) to pull the current certificate details from the LB while we investigate. — Agent: Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com)

title: Device marked noncompliant
description: User Rachel Nguyen (emp ID: EMP-40291) reports that her managed Windows 10 laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) became noncompliant in Intune after a recent policy resync on 2026-01-02, and Conditional Access is now blocking Microsoft 365 access. Company Portal shows the device has not checked in since 2025-12-25T10:12:00Z (9 days stale), and the encryption/BitLocker compliance signal is blank. Rachel is unable to reach Office 365 resources — including Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint — needed for her Sales team work out of the Denver office. Device IP at last known check-in was 10.42.18.77.
root_cause: The device had a stale Intune check-in state and was not reporting the required encryption compliance signal, so Intune could not complete policy re-evaluation and Conditional Access continued to treat the laptop as noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Have Rachel Nguyen open Company Portal on the affected laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and trigger a manual device sync so the endpoint sends a fresh compliance check-in to Intune, replacing the stale 2025-12-25 timestamp.

Verify on the device that BitLocker is enabled and the OS drive (C:) is encrypted by running 'manage-bde -status C:' from an elevated command prompt, then allow 10–15 minutes for the encryption status to report back to Intune after the sync completes.

Review the device record for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN in the Intune admin console under user rnguyen after the sync to confirm the last check-in timestamp updates to the current date/time and the encryption compliance signal is populated with a healthy BitLocker status.

If the device remains noncompliant after a successful sync, have Marcus Webb (mwebb) trigger a remote sync or compliance re-evaluation from the Intune admin console for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and confirm the assigned Corp_Device_Compliance_Policy is still targeted to the correct device/user scope for rnguyen in the Sales group.

If the device still does not report current compliance, escalate to Endpoint Support (Marcus Webb — mwebb@corplabs.com, ext. 4-7823) for deeper remediation of the Intune enrollment/check-in state on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN, including potential re-enrollment if the MDM certificate has expired, and re-push the Corp_Device_Compliance_Policy so Conditional Access can clear the block once the device reports healthy.

title: Multiple users unable to join Corporate Wi‑Fi
description: Multiple Sales users in the Charlotte office were trying to join the corporate SSID 'corp-wifi' on managed devices beginning around 09:45 ET this morning, but 802.1X authentication failed and the devices were disconnected shortly after association. Affected users — including Maria Delgado (mdelgado), Kevin Ostrowski (kostrowski), and at least four others — could not obtain normal network access for business work. NAC logs on nac-east-01.corp.internal showed RADIUS Access-Reject responses for all attempts, and wireless controller logging on wlc-charlotte-02.corp.internal indicated the controller certificate (CN=wlc-charlotte-02, issued 2024-05-01) had expired at midnight. The issue was reported initially by Maria Delgado via phone at (704) 555-2198.
root_cause: Expired certificate on the wireless controller disrupted 802.1X/RADIUS trust, causing NAC to return Access-Reject and deny Corporate Wi-Fi access for affected users.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the wireless controller certificate (serial 4A:7C:03:EE) on wlc-charlotte-02.corp.internal was expired as of 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z and identified it as the common failure point for affected 802.1X authentications on 'corp-wifi' in the Charlotte office.

Applied a temporary NAC allow rule on nac-east-01.corp.internal for the Sales user group (including mdelgado, kostrowski, pnair, tbeckett, and others) to reduce immediate business impact while permanent certificate remediation was prepared. Manager jwhitfield (EMP-40227) was notified of the workaround.

Renewed and deployed the wireless controller certificate on wlc-charlotte-02.corp.internal (new serial 7B:1F:09:DA, valid through 2028-05-01), then updated the controller and dependent RADIUS/NAC trust configuration on nac-east-01.corp.internal to use the new valid certificate chain. Work performed by engineer Raj Patel (rpatel).

Retested 802.1X authentication from affected devices — LAPTOP-MDELGADO (mdelgado), LAPTOP-KOSTROWSKI (kostrowski), and devices for pnair and tbeckett — and verified NAC/RADIUS responses changed from Access-Reject to successful Access-Accept authorization on all tested endpoints.

Removed the temporary NAC allow rule on nac-east-01.corp.internal after validation and monitored controller and NAC logs for 60 minutes to confirm stable reconnect behavior across all affected Sales users in Charlotte with no recurring certificate-related rejects.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether affected users fail only on 'corp-wifi' and whether reconnecting or reapplying the wireless profile changes the behavior on the impacted laptops. We need to distinguish between an endpoint profile issue and a shared NAC or controller problem. Could you also confirm the hostnames of the devices you and Kevin tested? I can see your machine LAPTOP-MDELGADO and Kevin's LAPTOP-KOSTROWSKI in the logs but want to verify. We are pulling RADIUS logs from nac-east-01.corp.internal in parallel.

title: Print jobs stuck on shared printer — driver unavailable on Print Server
description: Multiple Finance users in the Charlotte office were trying to print to the shared printer PRINTER-002 (mapped via \\PRINTSVR-EAST-02.corp.internal\PRINTER-002), but submitted jobs remained stuck in the shared queue and the queue reported "driver unavailable." The issue was first reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40218) and subsequently confirmed by at least four other Finance team members. The issue affected the Print Server-hosted queue rather than a single workstation, and users were blocked from completing normal printing tasks until the server-side driver and spooler issue was corrected.
observed_errors: Queue mapping error when assigning driver
root_cause: Corrupt printer driver package on the Windows Server 2019 Print Server prevented PRINTER-002 from loading the assigned driver correctly, causing queue mapping failures, repeated spooler errors, and stuck print jobs for multiple users.
resolution_steps: Removed the damaged PRINTER-002 driver package (HP Universal Print Driver v7.1.0) from PRINTSVR-EAST-02.corp.internal after confirming repeated driver load failures (Event ID 372) in the spooler-related errors. Removal performed by Taro Nakamura (t.nakamura) via Print Management Console.

Reinstalled the approved printer driver package from the corporate driver repository (\\corpfs01.corp.internal\DriverRepo\HP-UPD-7.1.0-approved) and confirmed the package signature and DLL hashes matched the approved source.

Remapped the PRINTER-002 shared queue on PRINTSVR-EAST-02.corp.internal to the refreshed driver so the queue no longer referenced the corrupt package. Verified the queue status returned to Online in Print Management Console.

Cleared all 14 residual stuck jobs from the shared print queue and restarted the Print Spooler service on PRINTSVR-EAST-02.corp.internal to reload the driver cleanly. Notified affected users (mgonzalez, dreeves, kpatel) to resubmit their documents.

Submitted test print jobs from multiple user accounts — mgonzalez on WORKSTATION-PC-MG (10.42.18.77), dreeves on WORKSTATION-PC-DR, and kpatel — and confirmed all jobs processed successfully without recurring driver unavailable or spooler load errors. Maria Gonzalez confirmed her AP batch report printed correctly.

title: GlobalProtect disconnects immediately
description: I was trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from my managed Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-LP-MKOVAC) at the Munich office. My username is mkovac and I authenticate via Okta Verify. After approving the Okta MFA push notification at approximately 22:50 UTC, the VPN tunnel established briefly against gateway vpn-emea.corplabs.net and then disconnected during the authentication handoff, leaving internal web applications (including https://intranet.corplabs.com) unreachable. My client IP at the time was 85.214.47.103. Reconnect attempts did not restore access, and the GlobalProtect client logs referenced a certificate-related error ("certificate expired during device authentication") tied to the device authentication stage. I need VPN access urgently for an engineering deployment tonight.
observed_errors: Client log: certificate expired during authentication
Rekey/handshake timeout reported in GlobalProtect logs
root_cause: Expired device certificate on the endpoint caused GlobalProtect to fail the post-MFA authentication handoff and drop the VPN tunnel.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the GlobalProtect client behavior on WORKSTATION-LP-MKOVAC (user mkovac, IP 85.214.47.103) and confirmed the tunnel dropped immediately after successful Okta MFA approval rather than during the MFA prompt itself, indicating a post-authentication certificate validation failure.

Checked the endpoint device certificate state via Device Certificate Service and verified the enrolled certificate (CN=mkovac,OU=Engineering,DC=corplabs,DC=internal, serial ...A7F3) used for VPN authentication had expired on 2026-04-14 and was no longer valid for the active GlobalProtect profile.

Forced a new device certificate issuance through Device Certificate Service for WORKSTATION-LP-MKOVAC to restore valid certificate-based authentication for the affected laptop. New certificate issued at 2026-04-15T23:10Z with a 12-month validity period.

Cleared the stale GlobalProtect profile on WORKSTATION-LP-MKOVAC and re-enrolled the device so the client refreshed its certificate association and active VPN configuration against vpn-emea.corplabs.net. Re-enrollment performed by desktop support agent Raj Patel.

Retested the full sign-in flow with Okta MFA for user mkovac and confirmed the VPN session to vpn-emea.corplabs.net remained connected and internal web applications including https://intranet.corplabs.com were reachable from IP 85.214.47.103.
agent_questions: Hi Miroslav, thanks for reporting this. I'm agent Priya Nair (EMP-40821) and I'll be handling your case. Could you please confirm whether the Okta MFA push to your Okta Verify app is approved successfully before the VPN drops? Also, can you open the GlobalProtect client logs under C:\Program Files\Palo Alto Networks\GlobalProtect\PanGPS.log and check whether there is a certificate-related message around the 22:50 UTC disconnect timestamp? If possible, please share the exact error string and the gateway address shown in the client.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to department shared drive
description: I was trying to open the Finance department shared drive at \\fileserver\Finance from a mapped network drive on my Windows 10 workstation (WORKSTATION-FIN-RC). The mapped drive repeatedly prompted for credentials and then returned "Access is denied," blocking access to the department folder and normal file-share work. My username is rchavez and I'm based in the Philadelphia office. Ticket review indicates likely access entitlement or cached credential mismatch, but the original investigation could not verify my AD group membership or current share permission inheritance from the ticket alone.
observed_errors: Mapped drive repeatedly prompts for credentials
root_cause: Access to the Finance shared drive was blocked by either missing or unrefreshed AD security group entitlement for the share and/or stale cached Windows credentials tied to the mapped drive session, causing repeated credential prompts and an access denied response.
resolution_steps: Verify the user's required Finance shared-drive AD security group membership against the share ACL and add or restore the user to the approved access group if missing. For rchavez, confirm membership in FS-Finance-RW and add the account if it is not present; Derek Morales performed this step and confirmed rchavez was re-added to the group.

Have the user sign out and sign back in to refresh the Windows access token so any updated group membership is applied to the client session. Rachel Chavez was instructed to log off WORKSTATION-FIN-RC and log back in to pick up the updated FS-Finance-RW membership.

Clear any saved Windows credentials for the file server from Credential Manager and remove the existing mapped drive connection to eliminate stale cached authentication. On WORKSTATION-FIN-RC, the stale entry for \\fileserver under rchavez's Windows Credential Manager was deleted and the mapped F: drive was disconnected.

Remap the drive using the current UNC path \\fileserver\Finance and confirm the user is connecting to the active share path rather than an older shortcut or stale drive mapping. The F: drive was remapped via net use F: \\fileserver\Finance /persistent:yes for rchavez.

Validate that the user can open the Finance folder without additional credential prompts and that access now follows the intended inherited share and NTFS permissions. Rachel Chavez confirmed she could browse and edit files in \\fileserver\Finance without any credential prompts from WORKSTATION-FIN-RC.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel Chavez, please confirm whether you recently changed your password, whether the drive is mapped from an older shortcut, and whether you are currently a member of the Finance shared-drive access group (FS-Finance-RW). I can see your account rchavez in Active Directory but need to verify your current group entitlements. You can reach me at ext. 4127 or email dmorales@corplabs.com if you have questions.

title: BitLocker failed to enable; recovery key not escrowed
description: My Windows 11 Surface Pro (hostname: WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MK) enrolled in Intune under my account (mkovacs@corplabs.com) did not automatically enable BitLocker after enrollment on January 22nd. The device was shown as noncompliant for encryption in Company Portal, and the Device Compliance Service reported recovery key escrow failure, blocking the device from reaching the expected protected and compliant state for the Corporate Laptops group. I'm based in the Charlotte office and need this resolved so I can access corporate resources. My employee ID is E-40291.
observed_errors: Recovery key escrow failed (Device Compliance Service reported escrow failure)
root_cause: BitLocker could not start because the device TPM protector was not initialized, and Intune was still assigning deprecated EncryptionPolicy_v1, which prevented successful recovery key escrow to the management service.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM state on the affected Surface Pro (WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MK, user mkovacs) using Get-Tpm and manage-bde, then initialized the TPM protector so BitLocker could create the required key protector on the OS volume.
Started the BitLocker enablement flow on WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MK and generated a new recovery key after TPM readiness was confirmed. Encryption began on the C: drive with XTS-AES 256-bit.

Rotated and escrowed the new BitLocker recovery key for WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MK to the Device Compliance Service via BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector, then verified the escrow record was present in the Intune portal under Maria Kovacs's device entry.

Removed the deprecated Intune assignment for EncryptionPolicy_v1 from the Corporate Laptops group and assigned the active EncryptionPolicy_v2 to the target device group, ensuring WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MK and other Charlotte devices receive the correct policy.

Forced an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MK (initiated by dlangston) and confirmed the endpoint received the updated EncryptionPolicy_v2 without assignment issues. Sync completed at 2026-01-23T19:38:00Z.

Rechecked encryption and compliance status for WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MK in both the Intune portal and Company Portal on the device. Verified BitLocker was enabled on the OS volume, recovery key was escrowed, and the device was marked compliant. Notified Maria Kovacs (mkovacs@corplabs.com) that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Maria, we are checking why BitLocker did not start on your enrolled Surface Pro (WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MK, IP 10.42.18.77). Could you please confirm whether the device recently completed Intune enrollment and whether encryption has ever shown as enabled in Settings or Company Portal? I can see the device is registered under mkovacs in the Charlotte device group. — Agent: Derek Langston, Desktop Support

title: Account locked after repeated failed sign-ins
description: I (Marcus Delgado, emp ID EMP-40821) was trying to sign in to the corporate SSO at https://sso.corplabs.com from my iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) at the Chicago office and access my account, but received an account locked message after repeated failed sign-in attempts. A self-service password reset was started via the Password Reset Portal, but the emailed reset token sent to m.delgado@corplabs.com expired before I completed it. I also reported a recent phone change and that a mobile device (IP 10.47.83.112) was still attempting sign-in with an old cached password, preventing access to SSO-dependent services until the lockout and stale credentials were cleared.
root_cause: Active Directory lockout was triggered by repeated failed authentication attempts from a mobile device using cached old credentials after the user's phone change. The expired self-service password reset token delayed credential recovery, leading to additional failed sign-in attempts while the account remained locked.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the account lockout condition in Active Directory for mdelgado (EMP-40821) on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and unlocked the user account after confirming the lockout threshold had been reached due to repeated attempts from IP 10.47.83.112.

Had the user re-add the account on the mobile device (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) using the newly reset password so background authentication no longer submitted stale credentials from IP 10.47.83.112.
Verified successful authentication to the SSO portal at https://sso.corplabs.com from both desktop and mobile (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) for mdelgado after the reset and mobile credential cleanup.
Documented the mobile cached-credential trigger for mdelgado (Marcus Delgado, Chicago office) and noted lockout policy review follow-up for the identity team, referencing INC-ALP-0058.

I can see your AD account (username: mdelgado) is currently locked. — Agent Priya Nair

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failure for api.internal.company.local
description: Internal developers on the DevOps and Platform Engineering teams are intermittently unable to resolve api.internal.company.local from corporate network locations, which prevents the internal-api/service-discovery workflow from reaching the endpoint by name. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40821) from the Austin office, and subsequently confirmed by additional developers in the Chicago and Portland offices. Affected users see NXDOMAIN or timeouts when querying corporate DNS resolvers (e.g., from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD at 10.42.17.88), while a public resolver (8.8.8.8) returns a valid address for the same hostname. Scope appears limited to corporate DNS pathing or internal zone handling rather than a full service outage, and no recent zone edits or resolver cache evidence were initially attached.
observed_errors: no answer from corporate DNS resolver
root_cause: Corporate DNS resolution for api.internal.company.local was intermittently failing because the internal zone/conditional forwarding path was not consistently returning the authoritative record across corporate resolvers, leading some resolvers to answer NXDOMAIN from stale or incorrect cache/forwarding state while public lookup still returned an address.
resolution_steps: Validated the authoritative A record for api.internal.company.local in the intended internal DNS zone (company.local) and corrected the record TTL to the current expected value of 300 seconds, confirming the record pointed to 10.200.5.34.

Reviewed corporate DNS resolver handling for company.local on dns-corp-01.infra.company.local and dns-corp-02.infra.company.local, and corrected the conditional forwarder/zone routing on dns-corp-02 (which was missing the company.local delegation) so queries for the internal namespace were sent to the proper authoritative path.

Flushed cache on impacted corporate DNS resolvers (dns-corp-01 and dns-corp-02) to remove stale NXDOMAIN or outdated entries being intermittently served to the Austin, Chicago, and Portland office locations.

Retested name resolution from affected corporate resolver paths — mdelgado (10.42.17.88, Austin), pnair (10.38.22.115, Chicago), and kortiz (10.55.9.201, Portland) — and confirmed api.internal.company.local returned the expected address 10.200.5.34 instead of NXDOMAIN.

Documented the need to capture resolver cache output and comparative nslookup/dig results from multiple sites (including client IPs and resolver targets) if symptoms recur, to distinguish cache poisoning/staleness from future forwarding drift. Added monitoring alert in Network Monitoring for NXDOMAIN spike detection on api.internal.company.local.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please compare nslookup or dig results for api.internal.company.local using the corporate DNS resolver (dns-corp-01.infra.company.local) and a known-good public resolver such as 8.8.8.8, and confirm whether the failure is NXDOMAIN, timeout, or no answer at each affected site. If possible, run the test from your workstation (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD) and ask Priya Nair (pnair) in the Chicago office to do the same so we can compare results across locations. Please include the full nslookup output and your client IP.

title: Device blocked by Conditional Access despite Intune showing compliant
description: I, Marcus Delgado (emp ID: EMP-40291), on a corporate-owned Windows 10 21H2 laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD) was blocked from accessing corporate resources (SharePoint, Outlook, Teams) even though the device showed Compliant in Intune with a recent sync approximately 10 minutes earlier. Azure AD/Conditional Access sign-in evaluation denied access with error ConditionalAccess.PolicyNotSatisfied citing a device compliance failure for missing encryption, preventing me from completing normal work at the Frankfurt office until the device encryption signal and Conditional Access evaluation aligned. My username is mdelgado and I was signing in from IP 10.47.83.112.
root_cause: Conditional Access evaluated a stale or incomplete device compliance signal for BitLocker encryption while Intune already showed the device as compliant. The device had checked in successfully, but the encryption state had not fully propagated to the Conditional Access evaluation path, creating a temporary mismatch between Intune compliance status and access enforcement.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (user: mdelgado, EMP-40291) had recently checked in to Intune at 15:38 UTC and compared the Intune compliance state with Conditional Access sign-in details for mdelgado@corplabs.com to isolate the failing signal as encryption (NoEncryptionDetected).

Re-applied the BitLocker compliance and enforcement policy to the affected Windows 10 device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD via Endpoint Manager Admin Console and initiated local encryption verification to refresh the reported BitLocker protection state.

Forced another device sync/check-in from the Endpoint Manager admin console for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD so the updated encryption telemetry was submitted again from the endpoint to device compliance services, and added mdelgado to a temporary Conditional Access exclusion group to unblock immediate work.

Had Marcus Delgado reboot the device and allow BitLocker status verification to complete, then validated that the encryption signal was reporting correctly (BitLocker: Enabled, compliant) after the next telemetry cycle at approximately 16:15 UTC.

Removed the temporary Conditional Access exclusion for mdelgado after a subsequent sign-in from 10.47.83.112 showed the device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD meeting all compliance requirements including encryption, and access to corporate resources was restored normally.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether BitLocker is shown as enabled locally on the laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD) and whether you can complete a reboot now so we can refresh the compliance and encryption telemetry. Also, can you confirm you're signing in with mdelgado@corplabs.com? I'll pull up the Conditional Access sign-in logs on our side in the meantime. — Priya Nair, Endpoint Support

title: Expired TLS certificate and incomplete load balancer chain update caused internal TLS
description: Internal users and dependent integrations (including the payroll sync service run by Maria Chen) were trying to access the Internal Web Service at svc-portal.corplabs.internal and Service API at api-internal.corplabs.internal over TLS through the F5 load balancer (VIP 10.42.16.50), but some clients reported certificate warnings while others failed with hostname mismatch and trust validation errors. The outage affected normal application access behind the us-east-1 load balancer even though the service team believed a recent certificate deployment had completed. Initial reports came from user rkapoor (Rahul Kapoor, EMP-40821) in the Arlington office and were escalated via the infrastructure on-call channel.
root_cause: The F5 load balancer was updated with a current certificate that did not match the Internal Web Service endpoint name. Renewal completed, but the wrong certificate asset was bound to the virtual server and hostname validation failed for clients.
resolution_steps: Retrieve the correct certificate (serial 9B:22:4D:EE) from the internal Certificate Authority (ca01.corplabs.internal) whose SANs include svc-portal.corplabs.internal and api-internal.corplabs.internal — the Internal Web Service and Service API endpoint names used by clients.

Update the F5 virtual server lb-east-vip01 SSL profile (/Common/svc-portal-ssl-profile) to use the correct certificate (CN=svc-portal.corplabs.internal, serial 9B:22:4D:EE) and retain the existing valid intermediate chain. Change applied by dmorales and verified in the F5 admin console.

Validate from client (WORKSTATION-LT-RK, 10.18.204.77, user rkapoor) and load balancer perspectives that the presented certificate is current, matches the service hostname svc-portal.corplabs.internal, and completes TLS handshakes successfully. Confirmed no further CERT_HAS_EXPIRED or ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR reports from the Arlington office or dependent integrations.

Extend certificate monitoring on certmon.corplabs.internal to validate hostname alignment (SAN vs. expected service FQDN) in addition to expiration and chain health. New alert rule cert-san-match-east created by pnair and tested against lb-east-vip01.
agent_questions: We can confirm renewal activity at the internal Certificate Authority (ca01.corplabs.internal), but need validation from the active endpoint. Are users still seeing CERT_HAS_EXPIRED when browsing to svc-portal.corplabs.internal, and do we have any record that the F5 load balancer (lb-east-vip01) chain was explicitly updated? I've asked dmorales to pull the current binding from the F5 admin console. — Agent: Priya Nair (pnair)

title: Internal hostname fails to resolve — stale A record in internal DNS
description: Internal users in the Portland office were trying to reach corp.local services by hostname, but some systems continued to fail name resolution even though others reported successful lookups. The issue was initially reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40218) via the monitoring-dashboard, noting that her workstation could not resolve app.example.internal or svc-registry.corp.local. The problem affected access to internal endpoints such as service-discovery and application dependencies, with symptoms most visible on clients that had recently changed networks or resumed from long-running sessions. Additional reports came in from developer Raj Patel (raj.patel@corplabs.com) whose machine WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RP also failed lookups intermittently. The incident needed DNS validation to determine whether the problem was in the central DNS infrastructure or limited to local resolver behavior on affected systems.
observed_errors: Application error: unable to resolve host
root_cause: No fault was found in the central internal DNS service; suspected client-side DNS caching, local network settings, or an already-cleared transient issue caused the earlier hostname resolution failures.
resolution_steps: Have affected users flush local DNS cache and renew network configuration on impacted endpoints or application hosts. Maria Chen (WORKSTATION-PC-MC, 10.22.47.113) ran ipconfig /flushdns and ipconfig /renew; Raj Patel (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RP, 10.22.48.86) reconnected to the Portland office VPN, which refreshed his DNS settings.

Verify the affected systems are using the expected corporate DNS servers (10.20.1.5 and 10.20.1.6) and not stale or alternate resolver settings. Both Maria Chen's and Raj Patel's endpoints were confirmed pointing to the correct resolvers after remediation. Agent dmorales validated via ipconfig /all output collected from each user.

Retest hostname resolution and application access from affected endpoints; if the issue persists, collect client-side DNS diagnostics for endpoint-focused follow-up. Post-fix nslookup app.example.internal from both WORKSTATION-PC-MC and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RP returned 10.50.12.40 successfully. Internal-app-service and monitoring-dashboard confirmed accessible by hostname from both endpoints. No further failures reported; ticket closed.

title: Users stuck in MFA prompt loop after SSO
description: Engineering users in the Austin office were trying to access SaaS applications through the Okta SSO portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) federated with Azure AD, but after approving MFA they were returned to another MFA challenge or received "401 Unauthorized (MFA required)" and access denied responses. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (rng0042) and confirmed by several members of the engineering-team I group. The issue began after a routine Okta MFA enforcement update pushed on 2026-04-02 and intermittently blocked access to Office365, Salesforce, and related SSO-connected apps for the engineering-team I group. Ticket opened on behalf of the team by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com).
platform: Okta SSO federated with Azure AD
root_cause: A configuration mismatch existed between Okta MFA enforcement and Azure AD Conditional Access targeting. Some affected users either had stale MFA factor state or were not included in the corrected Azure AD group assignment required by the conditional access policy, causing repeated MFA challenges and access denials after successful SSO initiation.
resolution_steps: Validated the affected sign-in path for users rng0042, kpratt, and aokonkwo and confirmed that users were looping at the MFA challenge or receiving conditional access denials (conditional_access:block) after SSO initiation through https://sso.corplabs.com.

Reset MFA enrollment for impacted users who had stale or inconsistent factor state — including Rachel Nguyen (rng0042) and Kevin Pratt (kpratt) — and resynced authenticator device time on WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RN and WORKSTATION-PC-KP where needed to restore successful factor validation.

Reviewed Azure AD Conditional Access policy 'CorpLabs-SSO-MFA-Enforce' targeting against the intended SSO Portal access group (engineering-team-sso-access) and identified accounts missing from the corrected group assignment, including aokonkwo (Aisha Okonkwo, emp ID E-50821) and jlin.

Updated the Azure AD Conditional Access group assignment and corrected the policy scope so the engineering-team SSO Portal users in the Austin office — including aokonkwo and jlin — were consistently included in the required access path. Change approved by identity team lead Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com).

Retested sign-in for a sample of affected users (rng0042, kpratt, aokonkwo) across Office365 and Salesforce and verified successful post-MFA access without repeated prompts. Rachel Nguyen confirmed normal access from WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RN at 23:15 UTC.

Monitored sign-in and conditional access logs on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal after the change to confirm the MFA loop and access denied condition stopped for the affected cohort. No further AUTH_INVALID_MFA or conditional_access:block events observed for engineering-team users over the subsequent 4-hour window. Case closed by Priya Sharma.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether the MFA prompt repeats after you approve it on your device (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RN) and whether the failure happens in all SSO apps or only specific ones such as Office365 or Salesforce. Also, can you let me know if other team members like Kevin Pratt or Aisha Okonkwo are seeing the same behavior? — Agent: Priya Sharma

title: BitLocker did not enable and recovery key failed to escrow
description: Sales representative Marco Delgado (EMP-40291) on a managed Windows 10 21H2 corporate laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD) at the Phoenix office was expected to receive BitLocker encryption through Intune, but the device showed encryption not enabled and became noncompliant in Intune. The BitLocker recovery key was not escrowed to the tenant, and a local retry from Control Panel did not start encryption. This blocked the device from meeting endpoint compliance requirements and left support unable to retrieve a recovery key from Intune. Ticket raised by Marco's manager via email to the service desk.
observed_errors: Recovery key escrow failed (Intune sync returned failure)
TPM initialization incomplete during BitLocker enablement
root_cause: The required Intune BitLocker encryption policy was not assigned to the device's Azure AD group, so the device did not receive the encryption configuration. During the failed enablement attempt, TPM protector initialization also had not completed, which prevented successful BitLocker activation and recovery key escrow.
resolution_steps: Assigned the Intune 'Require device encryption (BitLocker)' policy to the affected device's Azure AD group 'Sales-Endpoints-NA' so that WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD and all other endpoints in the group could receive the required encryption configuration.

Validated TPM readiness on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD with Kenji Ota on-site at the Phoenix office and initialized the TPM protector locally using manage-bde -tpm -TurnOn. Confirmed TPM status changed to 'Ready for use'.
Forced an Intune/MDM device sync from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (IP 10.42.18.77) to refresh policy assignment and apply the BitLocker configuration profile to user mdelgado's device.

Re-triggered BitLocker enablement on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD after policy receipt and TPM initialization were confirmed. Encryption of the OS volume (C:) began immediately and completed within 35 minutes.

Verified that the BitLocker recovery key for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD successfully escrowed to Intune under Marco Delgado's device record and that the device compliance state updated to compliant. Notified mdelgado at mdelgado@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Marco — please confirm whether BitLocker was manually retried on your laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD and whether the recovery key is visible anywhere in Intune or Company Portal. Also, can you verify the device is connected to the corporate network from your current IP (10.42.18.77) so we can check sync status? Please reply to this thread or reach me at dpratt@corplabs.com.

title: Print jobs stuck on PrintServer01 after driver update
description: Users in the Frankfurt office under Corporate Printing were trying to submit documents to the shared printer queue \\PrintServer01\CORP-HP-3F hosted on PrintServer01, but jobs remained stuck and the queue reported 'Error - driver unavailable' after a scheduled HP Universal Print Driver update pushed earlier today at approximately 09:15 UTC. The issue was first reported by Maria Engel (EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed by at least five other users on the same floor. The issue affected multiple users of the shared queue and blocked normal printing operations until the server-side driver and queue mapping were corrected. Ticket opened on behalf of the affected group by helpdesk agent r.kowalski.
observed_errors: Spooler error: Failed to load driver (0x800705b4)
Queue entries stuck with status 'Error - driver unavailable'
root_cause: A corrupt or mismatched printer driver package was deployed to PrintServer01 during the scheduled update. The package checksum did not match the approved repository version, causing the print queue to reject jobs and the Print Spooler to fail loading the assigned driver.
resolution_steps: Compared the installed HP Universal Print Driver package on PrintServer01 (IP 10.40.12.55) against the approved package in the centralized driver repository and confirmed the deployed package checksum (SHA256: 4a7f1c…) did not match the approved version (SHA256: 9e3b08…), with a file size discrepancy of 12.4 MB vs 14.1 MB.

Removed the corrupt or mismatched driver package from PrintServer01 via Print Management Console and reinstalled the approved HP Universal Print Driver package (v6.9.0.25000) from the centralized repository using the verified version, confirming post-install checksum matched SHA256: 9e3b08….

Remapped the affected shared print queue \\PrintServer01\CORP-HP-3F on PrintServer01 to the reinstalled approved driver so the queue no longer referenced the invalid driver state. Verified the queue properties reflected the correct driver assignment.

Cleared the 14 stuck print jobs from the affected queue \\PrintServer01\CORP-HP-3F and restarted the Print Spooler service on PrintServer01 to reload the corrected driver and reset queue processing. Notified affected users m.engel and t.richter that they could resubmit their documents.

Submitted validation print jobs from multiple client workstations including WORKSTATION-PC-ME (m.engel) and WORKSTATION-PC-TR (t.richter) in the Frankfurt office and monitored the queue to confirm jobs processed normally within expected timeframes without further driver unavailable errors. Confirmed resolution with Maria Engel via phone at +49 69 7540 2183.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether all users on the 3rd floor Frankfurt office are seeing the issue on the shared queue \\PrintServer01\CORP-HP-3F, and whether the failures started after today's scheduled driver update on PrintServer01. Also, can you let us know the hostname of the workstation you're printing from so we can cross-check client-side logs? — R. Kowalski

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to Finance shared drive for user jane.doe
description: I'm Jane Doe (employee ID FIN-20481) and I was trying to open the Finance shared drive from my usual mapped network drive (F:) on my workstation WORKSTATION-PC-JD as well as directly through \\fs01\Finance, but both returned Access Denied (0x5) with intermittent credential prompts. The issue was affecting access to Finance files needed for daily reconciliation work on the SMB file server. I contacted my colleague Mark Chen (ext. 4127) who confirmed he could still access the share without issues, so initial checks suggested the problem was limited to my access path or session rather than a broader department-wide outage. My IP address is 10.42.17.89 and I'm based in the Arlington office.
root_cause: User was connecting through a stale or retired Finance share path, so the mapped drive was targeting the wrong UNC location and producing Access Denied behavior despite valid access membership.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the approved current UNC path for the Finance shared drive (\\fs01\Finance) with the file services configuration and validated that \\fs01-old\Finance was officially retired during the Q1 2026 server consolidation managed by Kevin Ostrowski.

Removed the stale mapped drive (F: → \\fs01-old\Finance) on WORKSTATION-PC-JD using 'net use F: /delete', cleared cached credentials via Credential Manager for user jdoe, and remapped the drive to the current Finance share path with 'net use F: \\fs01\Finance /persistent:yes'.

Retested direct UNC access (\\fs01\Finance) and mapped-drive access (F:) with Jane Doe on WORKSTATION-PC-JD (10.42.17.89) and verified the Finance folder — including subfolders Reconciliation and Reports — opened without further Access Denied prompts or credential challenges.
agent_questions: Hi Jane, thanks for reporting this. I'm Kevin Ostrowski from the file services team. Could you please try opening \\fs01\Finance directly from Windows Explorer on WORKSTATION-PC-JD instead of using the mapped F: drive, and confirm whether you still receive Access Denied or a credential prompt? Also, please verify you're logged in as jdoe@corplabs.internal and not using any cached or alternate credentials. You can reach me at kostrowski@corplabs.com if you need to follow up offline.

title: Multiple users unable to join Corporate Wi‑Fi (CORP) — certificate expired
description: Multiple employees at the Frankfurt office were trying to connect managed Windows 11 devices to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID CORP using WPA2-Enterprise with 802.1X EAP-TLS, but authentication failed with expired certificate messages and devices received no network access after association. The issue was first reported by Marcus Lindgren (EMP-40821) around 13:30 UTC and quickly confirmed by approximately a dozen other users in the same location. The RADIUS authentication path was using a server certificate (CN=wifi-auth.corplabs.internal, Serial 4A:7C:0E:91:B3:DA:55:02) that had expired at midnight on 2026-05-04 after a one-year validity period (issued 2025-05-04). The outage blocked normal corporate network connectivity until the wireless authentication certificate was renewed, pushed to the RADIUS cluster (radius-emea-01.corplabs.internal through radius-emea-03.corplabs.internal), and client trust/cache issues were cleared on affected endpoints.
root_cause: Expired EAP-TLS certificate on the corporate wireless authentication path caused 802.1X authentication failures for CORP SSID clients until the certificate was renewed and propagated to the RADIUS cluster.
resolution_steps: Renewed the expired EAP-TLS server certificate (CN=wifi-auth.corplabs.internal, old Serial 4A:7C:0E:91:B3:DA:55:02, new Serial 4A:7C:0E:91:B3:DA:55:03, valid through 2027-05-04) used for Corporate Wi-Fi authentication on the Wireless Controller.

Pushed the renewed certificate to the RADIUS cluster nodes radius-emea-01.corplabs.internal, radius-emea-02.corplabs.internal, and radius-emea-03.corplabs.internal, and restarted RADIUS service members sequentially to load the updated certificate without full service interruption.

Validated successful TLS handshakes and 802.1X authentications in controller and RADIUS logs after the certificate update — confirmed successful reconnections for m.lindgren (10.60.14.87), p.nair (10.60.14.95), and t.kowalski (10.60.14.112).

Instructed affected users including Marcus Lindgren, Priya Nair, and Tomasz Kowalski to forget the CORP SSID and reconnect so devices would fetch the current trust state and clear cached certificate associations.

Directed any devices still failing after reconnect — including WORKSTATION-HP-TK (t.kowalski) — to complete Wi-Fi profile or certificate re-enrollment, and provided temporary guest access until remediation was finished. Tomasz Kowalski was contacted at +49 170 5529841 for follow-up re-enrollment assistance.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: denied access to department shared drive
description: I (j.kelly, employee ID EMP-40821) was trying to open the Marketing department shared folder from mapped drive Z: in Windows Explorer on my Windows 10 workstation WORKSTATION-MKT-JK. The share was visible, but opening the folder returned "Access is denied" and repeatedly prompted for credentials, preventing access to department files needed for normal work. I'm based in the Newark office and need these files for an upcoming campaign deadline. Initial checks indicated the file server share and NTFS permissions were in place, suggesting a user-specific access entitlement problem rather than a server outage.
observed_errors: Windows security dialog repeatedly prompts for credentials when opening Z:\Marketing
root_cause: User account j.kelly was not added to the required Active Directory security group Dept_Share_Access during provisioning, so the user's sign-in token did not contain the group-based permission needed for the Marketing shared folder.
resolution_steps: Verified the Marketing shared folder access model on FS-NYC-01 and confirmed that AD group Dept_Share_Access is the required entitlement for the mapped drive and NTFS permissions on \\FS-NYC-01\DeptShares\Marketing.
Added user j.kelly (EMP-40821) to the Active Directory security group Dept_Share_Access to restore the missing group-based access. Change approved by manager Rachel Simmons via email.

Forced a policy refresh (gpupdate /force) on workstation WORKSTATION-MKT-JK and instructed Jamie Kelly to sign out and sign back in so the updated security token would include the new Dept_Share_Access group membership.

Retested access to mapped drive Z: (\\FS-NYC-01\DeptShares\Marketing) from WORKSTATION-MKT-JK and confirmed j.kelly could open the Marketing department folder without further credential prompts or access denied errors.

Documented the provisioning gap for j.kelly and updated the onboarding checklist to include verification of required department shared-drive group membership. Notified HR contact Lisa Pham in the Newark office to ensure future Marketing hires are flagged for Dept_Share_Access during account setup.
agent_questions: Hi Jamie, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether the issue occurs when opening the Marketing folder from mapped drive Z: on your workstation WORKSTATION-MKT-JK and whether Windows keeps prompting for credentials after you enter them. Also, can you confirm you're using your j.kelly account and not an alternate login? — Derek Nguyen, Service Desk

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Customer-facing integration jobs between the Application and the downstream partner API (PartnerSync endpoint at partner-api.extdata.io) intermittently failed over the last 90 minutes during peak traffic. The Integration Gateway node igw-prod-07 in us-east-1 returned repeated HTTP 504 timeout responses on outbound partner API calls originating from service account svc-integrations, which caused inbound API Service requests to queue on the api-ingest-pool cluster, retries to accumulate, and data synchronization for the nightly billing feed to be delayed rather than completed in the expected 06:00–07:30 UTC window. Reported by Marcus Ellison (emp ID EMP-40821) from the Denver office.
root_cause: Most likely cause was intermittent latency and capacity degradation on the downstream partner API during peak traffic, causing outbound calls from the Integration Gateway to exceed the original timeout threshold and return HTTP 504 responses. Token rotation was not identified as causal because authentication monitoring showed no token expiry, authentication failure, or rate-limit pattern.
resolution_steps: Validated that the integration token for service account svc-integrations remained accepted by the downstream API at partner-api.extdata.io and confirmed no authentication expiry or auth-failure pattern was present in Monitoring System auth event logs.

Increased the Integration Gateway outbound call timeout threshold on igw-prod-07 from 30s to 60s to better match observed downstream response latency during peak traffic windows (p99 8.2s with tail spikes beyond 30s).

Applied an exponential retry backoff policy (initial interval 2s, max 32s, jitter enabled) to the svc-integrations job configuration to reduce retry amplification and request queue buildup on api-ingest-pool while the downstream API was slow to respond.

Restarted affected Integration Gateway pods (igw-prod-07, igw-prod-08) via kubectl rollout to clear 1,842 queued work items and restore normal processing after the timeout policy update. Confirmed queue depth returned to baseline (~120) within 10 minutes.

Escalated the incident to the downstream service owner at extdata.io (contact: Raj Mehta, rmehta@extdata.io) with collected HTTP 504 examples, latency traces, and Monitoring System evidence for capacity and latency investigation, while continuing post-change monitoring via the Monitoring System alerting channel for recurrence.
agent_questions: We are seeing repeated HTTP 504 responses on outbound partner API calls from Integration Gateway pod igw-prod-07. Reviewing traces for service account svc-integrations shows the failures cluster between 06:12 and 07:36 UTC. Please confirm whether the sync delays line up with peak job volume on the nightly billing feed and whether any partner-side maintenance or slowdown was reported. I've also asked Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) on the platform team to pull the Monitoring System dashboards for the affected window.

title: Laptop slow after login
description: My Windows 10 corporate laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-SALES-MH, asset tag LPT-EMEA-4417) sometimes becomes extremely slow right after sign-in, but the behavior is intermittent and was not consistently reproducible during live support. When the issue occurs, Outlook, browser sessions, and File Explorer can take much longer than expected to open — sometimes 20–30 seconds each — delaying the start of normal work. I believe it happens most often in the morning after the laptop has been off overnight, particularly when I'm working from the Munich office. My employee ID is E50832 and my username is mhoffmann.
observed_errors: MsMpEng.exe CPU spike to ~95% after login
root_cause: Intermittent post-login endpoint slowdown not reproducible during diagnostics; suspected transient startup or security activity, but no confirmed root cause was established.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts
description: Scheduled CustomerDataSync jobs through the Integration Gateway began failing during the overnight processing window on 2026-05-13, preventing timely customer record updates for the backend-syncers team and creating a backlog in the gateway worker queue. The issue was initially reported by Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) from the Austin office, who noticed that sync jobs for the CustomerDataSyncApp were timing out. Initial reports described the failures as API timeouts originating from host WORKSTATION-PNAIR-L1 (IP 10.42.17.88), but support review found the external endpoint was reachable and the integration was repeatedly being throttled while trying to process the batch volume.
root_cause: The overnight sync workload exceeded the downstream API's rate or quota limits, leading to 429 throttling responses and retry exhaustion that appeared as integration timeout failures.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the throttling pattern in gateway and downstream logs (batch-20260514-0115) and reduced request concurrency for the affected overnight batch jobs from 50 to 10 concurrent workers on the Integration Gateway EKS deployment in us-east-1.

Implemented stronger pacing, exponential backoff (initial delay 2s, max 60s, jitter enabled), and batch spreading on the Integration Gateway to stay within the downstream API rate limits of 100 requests/minute. Configuration was updated by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) and reviewed by Priya Nair.

Requested a quota review or temporary limit increase from the downstream API owner (contacted via api-support@partnerservices.net) where supported, referencing the CustomerDataSyncApp integration and projected batch volumes.

Monitored the next batch cycle (2026-05-15T01:15:00Z) via the Monitoring System and verified sync jobs completed without retry exhaustion or timeout symptoms. Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) confirmed all customer records were synced successfully and the backlog was fully cleared.
agent_questions: We are seeing 401 Unauthorized and 504 timeout errors during the scheduled sync window for the CustomerDataSyncApp running on pod cluster us-east-1. Logs from the Integration Gateway service account svc-custsync show repeated failures starting at approximately 2026-05-14T01:15:00Z. Please confirm whether there was any recent token or secret rotation change for the Integration Gateway service account. I have also looped in Marcus Delgado (EMP-40291) from the platform engineering team to assist with the investigation.

title: Internal hostname intermittently fails to resolve
description: Users and application hosts in the us-west-1-dc on-premises environment were trying to reach internal-service.internal.corp, but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN and some clients then timed out connecting to the service by name. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) from the Portland office and confirmed by several engineers on the same subnet (10.42.16.0/24). The problem affected multiple office subnets and engineering application workloads after a recent decommissioning of an older application host (app-legacy-07), blocking normal access to the internal endpoint until DNS data and caches were corrected.
root_cause: A stale A record for internal-service.internal.corp remained in the Internal DNS Zone after an older application host was decommissioned. Resolver caches across the DNS Resolver cluster continued serving stale or negative responses, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN and failed name resolution. The internal DNS zone ACL policy reference was also outdated and required update from v1.2 to v1.3.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the Internal DNS Zone entry for internal-service.internal.corp and identified that the A record still referenced the decommissioned host app-legacy-07 at 10.42.8.12 instead of the current service IP 10.42.8.45. Investigation performed by network engineer rchen.

Updated the internal A record from 10.42.8.12 (app-legacy-07) to the correct active host IP 10.42.8.45 (app-prod-03) and confirmed the zone now reflected the intended mapping and current service target with TTL 300.

Flushed stale cache entries across the DNS Resolver cluster (DNS-RES-W1-01 and DNS-RES-W1-02) so resolvers would stop returning outdated or negative responses for the hostname internal-service.internal.corp.

Validated successful name resolution and application connectivity from affected clients — including WORKSTATION-PC-MD (mdelgado, Portland) and deployment-service nodes — and monitoring paths across impacted subnets 10.42.16.0/24 and 10.42.18.0/24. Network Monitoring confirmed zero NXDOMAIN events post-remediation.

Scheduled and documented the follow-up zone policy maintenance to replace the stale Internal DNS zone ACL policy v1.2 reference with v1.3. Assigned to rchen with target completion 2026-01-22. Added DNS record review as a mandatory step in future host decommission runbooks.

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: I was trying to get the Azure AD joined Windows 10 21H2 device (hostname WORKSTATION-SALES-MR, asset tag SLS-4821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com, EMP-90274) into encryption compliance through Intune, but the endpoint showed BitLocker EncryptionState as Off, no recovery key was visible in Azure AD for this device, and the user never received a BitLocker PIN prompt. TPM management (tpm.msc) showed the TPM was not initialized, which prevented the device from enabling disk encryption and left it noncompliant in the Device Compliance Service. The device is located at our Phoenix office and connects from IP 10.42.17.88.
observed_errors: Device compliance state: Noncompliant for Encryption
root_cause: The device TPM was not initialized, so BitLocker could not create and use the required TPM protector to start encryption. In addition, the Intune BitLocker policy had not fully applied before remediation, so recovery key escrow to Azure AD had not occurred while the device remained noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Validated the endpoint state on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR (assigned to Marcus Reeves, mreeves, EMP-90274) in TPM management and BitLocker tooling, confirming TPM status was Not initialized, BitLocker was Off on C:, and no recovery key was escrowed to Azure AD for this device.

Initialized the TPM on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR using Initialize-Tpm and enabled the required TPM-based BitLocker protector on the device so the encryption prerequisites were satisfied. Verified tpm.msc now showed 'The TPM is ready for use.'

resolution_steps: Requested and obtained a renewed TLS certificate (CN=*.corp.internal) from the internal Certificate Authority for the internal web service endpoint. The renewal request was submitted by Kevin Marsh (kmarsh) and approved within 20 minutes.

Restarted the TLS termination process on load balancer LB-EAST-VIP-02 so the updated certificate and chain were actively presented to clients. Reload was confirmed successful at 2025-12-17T21:02:00Z by Priya Nair.

Validated the HTTPS endpoint (https://appportal.corp.internal) from the client side (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD at 10.42.17.88) and load balancer side to confirm the certificate was no longer expired and the full chain completed successfully. Marcus Delgado confirmed browser access was restored without warnings.

Re-enabled and tested certificate expiration monitoring and renewal alerting in Nagios for *.corp.internal to ensure future renewals are detected at least 30 days before expiry. Kevin Marsh verified alert delivery to the infrastructure on-call rotation managed by Raj Venkatesh.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused Internal Web Service TLS outages
description: Internal users and dependent services were trying to reach the internal-api HTTPS endpoint (internal-api.corplabs.internal), but starting 2025-12-19 09:13 UTC the service presented an expired TLS certificate. observed_errors: TLS handshake failure: certificate verify failed
root_cause: The Internal Web Service certificate expired, and the automated renewal process did not successfully update the renewed certificate and full chain on the Load Balancer. Certificate expiry alerting and renewal-job validation were not in place, allowing the expired certificate to remain in service until users and monitoring detected TLS failures.
resolution_steps: Obtain and validate a renewed TLS certificate from the Internal CA for internal-api, confirming the certificate subject and SANs matched the service endpoint. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-50184) submitted the CSR and received the renewed certificate (serial 7B:E2:44:AF:19, CN=internal-api.corplabs.internal, SAN: internal-api.corplabs.internal, internal-api.us-east-1.corplabs.internal) with a validity period through 2026-12-19.

Update the Kubernetes secret used by the Internal Web Service with the renewed certificate material and perform a controlled pod restart so the service consumed the new certificate. The secret tls-internal-api in namespace web-services was patched by Marcus Delgado at 12:34 UTC, and a rolling restart of the internal-api deployment (3 replicas) completed by 12:37 UTC.

Correct the certificate chain order and import the renewed certificate plus intermediates to the Load Balancer, then reload the Load Balancer configuration so clients were served the current full chain. The corrected bundle (leaf → IntCA-Corp-G2 → RootCA-Corp) was imported to LB-EAST-01 by Marcus Delgado and the configuration was reloaded at 12:41 UTC. Priya Sharma (psharma) confirmed from WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-PS (10.55.22.103) in the Boston office that the analytics-pipeline TLS calls resumed successfully.

Run end-to-end TLS validation from representative internal clients and CI paths to confirm successful handshakes, no certificate date warnings, and normal HTTPS connectivity to internal-api. Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com) verified from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (10.42.17.88) in the Austin office that browser access and curl tests returned valid certificate responses with no warnings. CI pipeline tls-smoke-test passed at 12:48 UTC.

Restore certificate expiry monitoring and validate the automated renewal workflow with alerting set before expiration, including a dry-run or job-history verification to confirm future renewals will update the served chain. Marcus Delgado re-enabled the certificate expiry monitoring rule in the observability platform with a 30-day and 7-day pre-expiry alert threshold, and updated the cert-renew-job-east webhook URL to point to the current LB-EAST-01 API endpoint. A dry-run of the renewal job was executed at 13:05 UTC and confirmed successful chain deployment to the Load Balancer. Alert notification was verified via email to infra-certs@corplabs.com and phone 303-719-5548 (on-call rotation).

title: Print jobs stuck on PrintServer01
description: Multiple users in the Floor2 Engineering group at the Bristol office were trying to print through the shared PRINTER_QUEUE (HP LaserJet 4250 queue) on PrintServer01, but jobs remained in spooling state and did not print. observed_errors: Spooler event: Unable to load driver component (corrupt driver cache)
root_cause: PRINTER_QUEUE on PrintServer01 remained mapped to an incorrect or partially corrupt printer driver package after the weekend reinstall, and residual corrupt driver cache entries caused the Windows Print Spooler to reference an unavailable driver and leave jobs stuck in the queue.
resolution_steps: Stop the Print Spooler service on PrintServer01 and clear all pending jobs (nine documents from r.okonkwo, d.hargreaves, p.nair, and other Floor2 Engineering users) from the affected shared PRINTER_QUEUE.

Remove the incorrect HP Universal Print Driver v2.1 vendor package (HPUniversalPrintDriver-v2.1.exe) from the server's driver store and clear residual driver cache files under C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\x64 associated with the failed weekend reinstall.

Install the approved printer driver package version 2.2 (HPUniversalPrintDriver-v2.2.exe) from the approved corporate driver repository on PrintServer01, verified by Marcus Tan (m.tan) from Desktop Support.

Remap PRINTER_QUEUE to the newly installed approved v2.2 driver and confirm the queue is no longer referencing the unavailable v2.1 driver package. Validate the driver mapping in Print Management Console.

Restart the Print Spooler service, submit test prints from affected user workstations (WORKSTATION-ROKONKWO and WORKSTATION-DHARGREAVES), and monitor queue processing to confirm jobs complete successfully without recurring spooling errors. Rachel Okonkwo (r.okonkwo) and David Hargreaves (d.hargreaves) confirmed successful printing after remediation.
