resolution_steps: Documented the inconsistent client sync behavior on both WORKSTATION-RN4417 and IPHONE-RNGUYEN for user rnguyen (rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com) and confirmed that profile rebuild on the desktop did not resolve the mailbox update issue — HTTP 429 throttling persisted across both clients.

Collected client and mailbox sync symptoms from desktop (WORKSTATION-RN4417, Windows 10) and mobile (IPHONE-RNGUYEN, iOS 16.5) to rule out a simple endpoint-specific failure. Cleared the stale ActiveSync partnership for IPHONE-RNGUYEN and re-paired the device, which temporarily restored mobile connectivity before throttling resumed.

Escalated the incident to Exchange Online support for mailbox-level investigation of throttling on rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com (case ref attached) and advised Rachel Nguyen to use Outlook on the web (https://outlook.office365.com) as a temporary workaround pending vendor findings. Notified manager Danielle Foster (dfoster@corplabs.com) of the escalation status.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether Outlook on the iPhone (IPHONE-RNGUYEN) still shows Disconnected after the desktop profile rebuild on WORKSTATION-RN4417, and whether the issue is now isolated to mobile only. I can see your mailbox is provisioned under the Corporate Mobile Users group — I'll also check the ActiveSync partnership from this side. — Kevin Marsh, Service Desk

title: Print jobs stuck on PrintServer01
description: Multiple users in the Engineering group at the Charlotte office were trying to print to the shared Office-Color and Finance-BW queues on PrintServer01, but submitted jobs remained stuck in the queue and the printers appeared offline. The issue was first reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40291) around 09:10 ET after a recent printer driver package deployment (v3.8.2 pushed 2026-03-04). The problem blocked normal printing for all affected users on the floor, and was associated with repeated driver load errors (Event ID 372, source: PrintService) and unstable Print Spooler behavior on the Windows Server 2019 print server.
root_cause: Corrupted or mismatched printer driver package on PrintServer01 after the recent driver deployment caused driver load failures, queue offline states, and recurring spooler instability for the affected shared printers.
resolution_steps: Removed the affected printer driver package (v3.8.2) from PrintServer01 using Print Management and reinstalled the previously approved driver version (v3.7.1) for the impacted shared queues (Office-Color and Finance-BW). Performed by Kevin Tran (ktran, EMP-55183).

Cleared all 167 stuck print jobs from the Office-Color and Finance-BW queues to remove the backlog created during the driver failure condition. Notified affected users mgonzalez, dpark, and lokafor to resubmit their jobs.

Restarted the Print Spooler service on PrintServer01 and validated that it remained stable for 30+ minutes after the corrected driver package (v3.7.1) was loaded. No further Event ID 372 or 7031 entries appeared.
Reassociated the impacted printer queues (Office-Color and Finance-BW) with the corrected v3.7.1 driver package and confirmed both queues returned to an online state in Print Management.

Submitted validation print jobs through the affected queues from WORKSTATION-MG-12 (mgonzalez) and WORKSTATION-DP-7 (dpark) and monitored PrintServer01 for recurrence for approximately 2 hours with successful job completion on both queues. No further driver errors observed.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether the issue affects only one printer queue or multiple shared queues on PrintServer01, and whether the problem started after the driver package v3.8.2 deployment last night. Also, can you let us know if other users on your team — for example, anyone printing from their own workstations — are seeing the same behavior?

title: Windows laptop slow after login
description: My Windows 10 Pro laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK, asset tag EP-SAL-4417) becomes very slow immediately after login. I'm Marko Kessler in the Frankfurt Sales team (employee ID EMP-90274) and every morning my device is largely unresponsive for several minutes. CPU is sustained around 90% and common applications such as Outlook, Teams, and Windows Explorer take 20-40 seconds to open. Task Manager showed MsMpEng.exe consuming most CPU during the slowdown, and I was blocked from normal morning work while the device remained largely unresponsive. Initial checks also found low free space on the C: drive at about 12%, increasing the likelihood of disk and IO contention during startup. My IP address at the time was 10.42.18.97.
root_cause: Windows Defender had a queued scan backlog that triggered heavy post-login scanning by MsMpEng.exe, causing sustained CPU contention and delayed application launches. Low available disk space on the system drive further worsened startup performance due to increased IO pressure.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Task Manager and endpoint status on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK to confirm MsMpEng.exe was the primary CPU consumer during the post-login slowdown for user mkessler and correlated the behavior with three queued Defender full-scan tasks.

Initiated and completed a manual Windows Defender full scan on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK during off-peak hours (scheduled at 19:00 CET) to clear the pending scan backlog and allow scheduled protection tasks to return to a normal state.

Disabled nonessential startup items for the mkessler profile on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK (removed four auto-start entries including OneDrive sync pre-fetch and Adobe Updater) to reduce competing resource demand during logon and application initialization.

Refreshed endpoint management and Defender policy via the Endpoint Management console so future scans on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK run outside business hours (rescheduled to 01:00 CET) and verified the updated scan schedule applied successfully to the laptop.
Freed disk space on C: by removing temporary files from %TEMP% (9.2 GB recovered) and running Disk Cleanup, increasing free space from 12% to above 22% and reducing disk contention during login.

Validated after remediation that post-login CPU utilization on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK dropped below 15% and affected applications (Outlook, Teams, Explorer) opened within normal timeframes (under 5 seconds). Marko Kessler confirmed improved performance the following morning.

title: Internal-service DNS resolution failures
description: Multiple internal application teams reported to engineer Priya Nair that they were unable to reach the inventory-sync service using the hostname internal-service.corp.local. Name resolution intermittently failed for approximately 2 hours starting around 18:10 UTC. Internal DNS resolvers (dns-resolver-east-01.corp.local and dns-resolver-east-02.corp.local) returned NXDOMAIN or timeouts from subnets in the Arlington data center, while direct access by IP (10.40.12.55) still worked, confirming the service itself was reachable and the outage was limited to internal DNS resolution. Affected teams included the order-processing group led by Marcus Okonkwo (emp ID E-90214) and the logistics integration team. Impact was loss of application connectivity by name until DNS zone updates and resolver caches were corrected.
observed_errors: lookup timed out from some subnets
root_cause: Stale cached DNS data on internal BIND9 resolver instances after a recent internal zone update caused inconsistent responses for internal-service.corp.local. The authoritative zone record and propagation state were not fully aligned across resolver/cache layers until the zone serial was incremented, the zone reloaded, and resolver caches flushed.
resolution_steps: Verified the correct A record value for internal-service.corp.local on the primary internal DNS zone (dns-auth-east-01.corp.local) and confirmed the record had been updated to the intended IP address 10.40.12.55 by Carlos Medina, replacing the decommissioned 10.40.12.40.

Incremented the DNS zone serial from 2026010701 to 2026010702 and reloaded the zone on the primary authoritative server dns-auth-east-01.corp.local using rndc reload so the change could propagate correctly to downstream resolvers.

Confirmed the zone reload and AXFR transfer/update state to secondary authoritative DNS servers (dns-auth-east-02.corp.local) handling the corp.local internal zone. Serial 2026010702 was reflected on all secondaries.

Flushed stale cache entries on internal BIND9 resolver instances dns-resolver-east-01.corp.local and dns-resolver-east-02.corp.local using rndc flush so resolvers would stop serving the outdated 10.40.12.40 result.

Validated fresh resolution with dig from multiple subnets (Arlington, Reston, Ashburn) including from Priya Nair's workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN and Marcus Okonkwo's host WORKSTATION-DESK-MO, and confirmed the hostname returned the expected address 10.40.12.55 consistently.

Confirmed Network Monitoring alerts for internal-service.corp.local cleared after cache flush and zone propagation completed at 20:41 UTC, indicating full service restoration. Priya Nair notified affected application teams including Marcus Okonkwo's order-processing group.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Customers and scheduled integration jobs managed by user rsanchez were attempting to synchronize data through the Integration Gateway to a third-party API (PartnerData API v2), but starting around 2025-12-09 08:00 UTC the syncs became delayed and some jobs failed intermittently. The visible impact was repeated HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout errors and request timeouts at the gateway, which caused queued work, increased sync lag, and delayed downstream data updates for batch-job processing in us-east-1 Kubernetes workloads. The issue was initially reported by Priya Nair (priya.nair@corplabs.com) from the Austin integration operations team after observing failed sync alerts on host WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN. Approximately 140 integration jobs were affected across the CustomerApp and API Integration pipelines.
root_cause: Downstream API latency spike caused Integration Gateway requests to exceed the configured client timeout, producing HTTP 504 errors and delayed sync processing.
resolution_steps: Correlated integration job failures (batch-sync-4401 through batch-sync-4438 and subsequent queued jobs submitted by rsanchez) with gateway traces from node 10.42.18.77 and downstream PartnerData API dependency latency to confirm the timeout condition was caused by backend response degradation rather than authentication failure.

Applied a temporary Integration Gateway timeout increase from 60s to 90s to reduce immediate job failures while the downstream service issue was being investigated. Change executed by Marcus Delgado (EMP-60891) and approved by Jennifer Okafor (EMP-70234).

Adjusted retry and backoff behavior on the Integration Gateway from 5 retries at 2s fixed interval to 2 retries with exponential backoff (ceiling 30s) to prevent rapid retry storms and reduce queue pressure during the degradation window.

Escalated to the downstream PartnerData API team via David Hwang (david.hwang@partnerdata.io, +1-512-555-0193) with trace evidence showing sustained 30-45s response times from gateway node 10.42.18.77, and coordinated remediation of the latency-inducing backend connection pool misconfiguration.

Validated that downstream latency returned to normal (p99 < 1.5s) after the vendor-side fix deployed at 20:38 UTC, then confirmed all ~140 queued sync jobs drained successfully and normal synchronization rates resumed. Priya Nair confirmed data integrity from the Austin operations side.

Updated monitoring thresholds on the Integration Gateway Prometheus alerting rules to trigger at p95 latency > 5s (previously 15s) and added a PagerDuty escalation path to better detect rising dependency latency before gateway timeouts impact customer and batch sync workloads. Follow-up review scheduled by Jennifer Okafor for 2025-12-16.

title: Laptop slow after login
description: User Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40291) reported that his Windows 10 corporate laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-MD) at the Philadelphia office became consistently slow immediately after login, with CPU sustained around 90-95% for several minutes and Microsoft Edge, Teams, and other applications taking 15-30 seconds to open. The issue recurred after an earlier partial fix applied on 2026-01-28 and was impacting normal work at the start of the day. Marcus's machine (IP 10.42.18.77) was investigated and the slowdown was tied to heavy startup items applied by StartupAppsPolicy together with queued Enterprise Antivirus Client scans causing post-login resource contention.
root_cause: A resource-heavy startup policy left multiple non-essential startup items and duplicate startup entries enabled, which coincided with a backlog of endpoint protection scans after login and drove sustained CPU contention and delayed application launches.
resolution_steps: Reviewed post-login resource usage on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD (IP 10.42.18.77) for user mdelgado and confirmed the main slowdown window (~5 minutes post-login) aligned with startup processing and Enterprise Antivirus Client activity rather than a single failing application.

Disabled non-essential startup items through StartupAppsPolicy and removed duplicate Outlook helper startup entries on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD so fewer processes launched immediately after mdelgado's sign-in; reduced startup item count from 11 to 5.

Forced a device policy refresh via the endpoint management console to apply the updated startup configuration consistently on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD; confirmed new policy sync timestamp of 2026-02-03T18:15:00Z.

Cleared the Enterprise Antivirus Client scan backlog (14 queued definition scans) by resetting scan throttling and rescheduling heavier scan activity to off-peak periods (daily at 12:30 AM) on mdelgado's endpoint.

Ran Disk Cleanup and removed temporary files from C:\Users\mdelgado\AppData\Local\Temp to recover approximately 12 GB of free space and reduce additional startup and scan overhead on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD.

Validated after remediation that CPU utilization on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD returned to normal (~15-20%) within 60 seconds of login and that application launch times for Edge and Teams were no longer delayed; confirmed with Marcus Delgado via phone at (215) 553-8104 that performance was restored. Ticket closed by Riku Nakamura.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this again. Could you please confirm available disk space on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD and whether Task Manager shows the Enterprise Antivirus Client (eavsvc.exe) or another startup process consuming most of the CPU after login? Also, can you let me know your current IP so I can pull the latest endpoint telemetry? You can reach me at r.nakamura@corplabs.com if it's easier to share screenshots.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused Internal Web Service TLS outage
description: Users were trying to access internal API endpoints and the internal web service at https://api.internal.corplabs.com, but browsers displayed certificate warnings and integrations failed TLS validation with ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and TLS handshake failures. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40821) from the Portland office around 2025-12-24 04:00 UTC and blocked normal internal service access because the load balancer (lb-prod-01.corplabs.internal) continued serving an expired certificate and outdated chain. Additional reports came in from users on the Denver floor including James Whitfield (jwhitfield@corplabs.com).
platform: on-premises F5 load balancer and internal application servers
observed_errors: 502 Bad Gateway from load balancer during TLS negotiation
root_cause: The Internal Web Service outage was caused by expiration of the deployed TLS certificate at 2025-12-24 04:00 UTC. The load balancer continued serving the old certificate chain after expiration, and certificate monitoring/renewal alerting was misconfigured, so no preventive alert was raised before client TLS validation began failing.
resolution_steps: Requested and obtained a renewed TLS certificate from the internal Certificate Authority (ca-root-01.corplabs.internal) and verified the certificate validity period (2025-12-24 through 2026-12-24) and service name coverage (CN=api.internal.corplabs.com with SAN entries for *.internal.corplabs.com) before deployment. The CSR was generated by Raj Patel (rpatel, EMP-29174) and approved by the PKI team.

Replaced the expired certificate on the load balancer (lb-prod-01.corplabs.internal) with the renewed certificate and updated the served certificate chain to remove the outdated chain elements, deploying the new chain bundle to /etc/ssl/certs/api-chain.pem with the current intermediate and root CA certificates.

Reloaded the load balancer TLS configuration on lb-prod-01.corplabs.internal so new client connections presented the corrected certificate and full chain. Raj Patel (rpatel) executed the reload at 14:45 UTC and confirmed the new certificate was being served on the VIP at 10.200.5.12.

Validated externally and from internal client paths that the endpoint no longer returned ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and that TLS handshakes completed successfully. Maria Chen (mchen) confirmed from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC at 10.42.18.97 and James Whitfield (jwhitfield) confirmed from WORKSTATION-DESK-JW at 10.42.19.44 that the service was accessible without warnings.

Restored and tested certificate monitoring and renewal alert rules so future certificate expirations generate warning before the renewal window is missed. Lisa Novak (lnovak) re-enabled the Nagios cert-expiry-api-internal check with a 30-day warning threshold and verified an alert fires correctly against the new certificate's expiration date of 2026-12-24.

title: Account locked
description: I (Marcus Delgado, emp ID E-20487) reset my password through the Password Reset Portal earlier the same day around 10:45 AM, but was then unable to sign in to the SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com from both my laptop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MD) and my iPhone. The account became locked almost immediately. My mobile device — connected from IP 10.42.18.77 — continued prompting with the old password and kept retrying stale cached credentials, which blocked me from regaining account access after the password change. I'm based in the Charlotte office and need access restored urgently for end-of-month reporting.
observed_errors: Account locked due to too many failed sign-in attempts
Authentication failure: invalid credentials from mobile device
root_cause: A mobile device retained the user's previous cached credentials after the password reset and continued submitting failed authentication attempts, triggering the Active Directory account lockout policy. The original self-service password reset token also expired during repeated sign-in attempts, delaying successful recovery.
resolution_steps: Verified the account lockout for mdelgado (Marcus Delgado, E-20487) in Active Directory on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and unlocked the user account to clear the immediate access block caused by the lockout policy (threshold: 10 failed attempts).

Reviewed authentication and lockout activity logs (Event ID 4740) to confirm repeated failed sign-in attempts were originating from Marcus's mobile device (iPhone at IP 10.42.18.77) using stale cached credentials stored in Outlook and Teams apps.

Issued a fresh password reset token for mdelgado through the Password Reset Portal at https://passwordreset.corplabs.com and confirmed the new token was valid, then sent the reset link to marcus.delgado@corplabs.com for the user to complete sign-in recovery.

Instructed Marcus to remove or refresh saved credentials on the iPhone mobile device — specifically clearing stored passwords in Outlook and Teams — and perform a full sign-out/sign-in so the updated password would be used going forward.
Validated successful authentication for mdelgado from both the laptop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MD) and the iPhone mobile device after credential refresh, confirming SSO Portal access was fully restored.

Monitored sign-in activity for mdelgado on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal for 30 minutes after the fix and confirmed no further failed attempts were being generated by any cached client. Advised Marcus to contact the Charlotte IT desk (ext. 4422) if the issue recurs.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reaching out. Please confirm whether any mobile mail or collaboration apps (e.g., Outlook, Teams) on your iPhone are still prompting for your old password after today's password reset. Repeated automatic retries from those apps can relock the account even after it's been unlocked. Also, can you confirm you're signing in with your AD username mdelgado? — Agent: Priya Nair

title: Outlook mobile not syncing
description: User Rachel Dominguez (rdominguez, EMP-40291) reported that Outlook email synchronization diverged between her Windows 10 desktop (WORKSTATION-DELL-RD) at the Charlotte office and her iPhone running iOS 16.4. Outlook Desktop resumed syncing after a restart and subsequent profile rebuild, while Outlook Mobile on iOS 16.4 continued to show "Disconnected" and stopped updating after 05:20 UTC on 2026-02-18. Exchange Online message-tracking logs for mailbox rdominguez@corplabs.com showed intermittent HTTP 429 throttling responses and "Mailbox unavailable" entries originating from client IP 10.42.18.77. The mobile device was later found to be noncompliant in MDM (Intune), which was actively blocking mobile mailbox access and delaying email updates for the user.
platform: Microsoft Exchange Online; Outlook Desktop and Mobile
root_cause: Primary cause was an MDM device compliance block preventing the iPhone from accessing the mailbox through mobile sync. A stale Outlook desktop profile caused separate desktop sync instability, while transient Exchange Online throttling generated additional log noise but was not the persistent blocker after compliance remediation.
resolution_steps: Validated that Outlook Desktop on WORKSTATION-DELL-RD and Outlook Mobile on IPHONE-RD-SALES were failing for different reasons by comparing client connection state and Exchange Online mailbox behavior for rdominguez@corplabs.com.

Rebuilt the Outlook desktop profile for rdominguez on WORKSTATION-DELL-RD (Windows 10), which restored normal desktop mailbox synchronization and cleared the stale local client state including the corrupted .ost cache.

Remediated the iPhone (IPHONE-RD-SALES) compliance issue in Intune MDM by applying the required OS security update and re-enrolled the device so Exchange Online mobile access for rdominguez was no longer blocked by conditional access policy.

Cleared the affected mobile sync partnership for rdominguez@corplabs.com in Exchange Online and forced the mailbox to establish a fresh mobile synchronization relationship with IPHONE-RD-SALES after compliance was restored.

Verified that Outlook Mobile on IPHONE-RD-SALES resumed mailbox updates for Rachel Dominguez and documented the remaining HTTP 429 entries from IP 10.42.18.77 as transient Exchange Online throttling for follow-up monitoring by kmarsh rather than the final blocking condition.

title: Windows laptop very slow
description: User Marco Bellini (emp ID: EMP-40291) reports that his managed Windows 10 Dell Latitude laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-LATITUDE-MB) becomes extremely slow immediately after sign-in. Within the first few minutes after login, CPU usage rises above 90% and disk activity remains elevated, causing Outlook, Chrome, Windows Explorer, and the internal Sales CRM tool to take 20-60 seconds to open or become responsive. The device IP is 10.42.17.83 and the user is based in the Milan office. The issue started after a recent device configuration or policy push (GPO update deployed 2026-01-27) and matches multiple similar reports in the same duplicate investigation (parent INC-LPD-0000), blocking normal post-login work for the Sales user.
observed_errors: CPU usage > 90% within 2 minutes of login
Applications taking 20-60 seconds to become responsive
root_cause: A recently applied resource-heavy startup policy triggered excessive post-login processing, and an endpoint protection scan backlog ran concurrently, causing sustained CPU and disk I/O contention that delayed application launches and degraded overall laptop responsiveness.
resolution_steps: Reviewed startup-impacting processes on the affected laptop WORKSTATION-LATITUDE-MB (user mbellini) and disabled 4 non-essential startup items (including redundant telemetry agents and a legacy inventory scanner) contributing to the post-login CPU spike.

Forced a device policy refresh through Endpoint Management (gpupdate /force) on WORKSTATION-LATITUDE-MB to correct the 2026-01-27 startup-related GPO policy application and prevent the heavy startup behavior from reapplying; confirmed the revised policy version was received.

Cleared the Endpoint Protection scan backlog of 14 queued definition updates by rescheduling full scans to off-hours (02:00 local Milan time) and allowing an immediate lighter quick-scan cycle to complete during support handling on mbellini's device.

Removed 11.1 GB of temporary files from C:\Windows\Temp and C:\Users\mbellini\AppData\Local\Temp and reclaimed disk space (free space restored to 19.3 GB) to reduce paging and startup disk contention during user sign-in on WORKSTATION-LATITUDE-MB.

Validated performance after logoff and logon on mbellini's session, then monitored CPU and disk I/O until they returned to normal startup levels (CPU below 25% within 90 seconds, disk queue length < 2) and Marco Bellini confirmed Outlook, Chrome, and the Sales CRM opened normally within 3-5 seconds. Advised agent Daniel Okonkwo to apply the same remediation to Lucia Ferraro's device under the parent investigation.
agent_questions: Hi Marco, can you confirm whether the slowness on WORKSTATION-LATITUDE-MB starts immediately after sign-in and whether Task Manager shows high CPU or disk usage while Outlook and Chrome are opening? Also, could you let us know if any colleagues in the Milan Sales team are experiencing the same behavior? I can be reached at d.okonkwo@corplabs.com if you'd prefer to share screenshots directly.

title: Internal DNS names failing to resolve from corporate resolver
description: Internal users and dependent services were unable to reliably reach several corp.local resources, including internal-portal.corp.local and inventory-api.corp.local, because hostname lookups through the corporate DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local, 10.20.1.10) were returning different answers than expected. Reports originated from the Austin office, initially filed by Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) after multiple teams noticed intermittent failures reaching internal endpoints by name following a recent infrastructure migration on 2026-05-09. The issue affected service connectivity across multiple internal applications including service-discovery. Workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD belonging to Marcus was among the first clients to surface NXDOMAIN responses. Initial reports suggested a resolver problem, but the current incident required validation of the internal DNS data and resolver path before proceeding.
root_cause: Outdated A records remained published in the authoritative internal DNS zone for the impacted corp.local hostnames, causing all resolvers to return retired internal addresses.
resolution_steps: Update the affected authoritative corp.local zone records on ns1-internal.corp.local and ns2-internal.corp.local so each hostname points to the current internal service address: internal-portal.corp.local → 10.20.50.20, inventory-api.corp.local → 10.20.50.22. Changes applied by Raj Okonkwo (rokonkwo).

Increment the zone serial from 2026050801 to 2026051001 and reload the internal DNS zone via rndc reload corp.local on both authoritative servers ns1-internal.corp.local and ns2-internal.corp.local to republish the corrected records.

Re-test lookups through the corporate resolver dns-resolver-01.corp.local (10.20.1.10) and directly against the authoritative servers to confirm both now return the current addresses (10.20.50.20 for internal-portal.corp.local, 10.20.50.22 for inventory-api.corp.local). Validated from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.20.44.112) and the Austin monitoring probe. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) confirmed application connectivity by hostname for internal-portal and inventory-api is fully restored.
agent_questions: Comparing affected corp.local lookups between the corporate resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local / 10.20.1.10) and authoritative DNS servers (ns1-internal.corp.local, ns2-internal.corp.local) now. Need to confirm whether failures are stale answers at the resolver or missing records in the internal zone. Running nslookup and dig queries from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.20.44.112) as reported by Marcus Delgado, and cross-referencing with queries from the monitoring host. — Priya Nair, Network Engineering

title: GlobalProtect disconnects immediately
description: I was trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from my managed Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-LP-DMORRIS) at the Austin office. After approving the Okta MFA push notification on my phone, the VPN tunnel established briefly and then disconnected within 10-20 seconds, leaving internal applications such as the HR portal, Salesforce via internal routing, and Confluence completely unreachable. My client IP at the time was 10.42.88.17. The issue began after the overnight automated certificate rotation on 2026-04-22 and affected a small subset of corporate-managed laptops in our group. I need VPN access restored to continue working on the Q2 compliance review. My employee ID is E-90214.
observed_errors: Windows Event: Schannel certificate validation failed
root_cause: Expired device certificate on affected managed laptops after the certificate rotation caused GlobalProtect to terminate the VPN tunnel shortly after successful Okta MFA and initial connection.
resolution_steps: Validated that Okta MFA was completing successfully for dmorris@helixtechgroup.com and confirmed the VPN disconnect on WORKSTATION-LP-DMORRIS occurred approximately 10-15 seconds after authentication rather than during the MFA challenge phase.

Reviewed GlobalProtect client symptoms and endpoint certificate-related errors on WORKSTATION-LP-DMORRIS, which indicated the Helix Device CA-issued device certificate (serial 4A:7C:91:DE:03, expired 2026-04-22T03:15:00Z) used by the VPN profile was expired following the failed auto-rotation.
Renewed the device certificate on Derek Morris's endpoint (WORKSTATION-LP-DMORRIS) through the Device Certificate Service, confirming the new certificate was issued and valid through 2027-04-22.

Refreshed the GlobalProtect VPN profile on WORKSTATION-LP-DMORRIS to clear the stale certificate association under CN=dmorris,OU=Corp Users,DC=helixtechgroup,DC=internal and pull the active enrolled profile with the renewed certificate.

Retested VPN connectivity from Derek's laptop (IP 10.42.88.17) and confirmed the tunnel to gp-east.helixtechgroup.com remained stable after MFA approval, with restored access to internal applications including the HR portal, Salesforce via internal routing, and Confluence.

Documented follow-up preventive action to monitor certificate expiration dates across the Austin Corporate Laptop Users group and trigger automatic profile refresh through MDM for similar endpoints; escalated to Priya Nair for tracking in the certificate lifecycle management backlog.
agent_questions: Hi Derek, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether the Okta MFA push completes successfully on your device and whether GlobalProtect disconnects before sign-in finishes or only after the VPN client shows a 'Connected' status. Also, could you share the exact gateway you're connecting to? I can see your account dmorris@helixtechgroup.com is provisioned for the us-east-1 gateway pool. — Priya Nair, Network Support

title: Users unable to join Corporate Wi‑Fi after authentication
description: Users in the Engineering group across the Austin campus were trying to join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) with 802.1X EAP-TLS authentication, but beginning the morning of 2026-05-04 after a planned certificate refresh window (02:00–04:00 UTC), devices either failed authentication or associated without receiving usable network access. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed across floors 3–7 of Building B, blocking normal wireless connectivity for approximately 140 employees until the wireless authentication certificate on WLC-AUSTIN-01.corp.local and affected client profiles were corrected. Ticket escalated by network lead David Kowalski.
observed_errors: Clients obtain IP but no network access (NAC denies access)
root_cause: The Wireless Controller was using an expired RADIUS/802.1X certificate, which caused EAP-TLS authentication failures and NAC-related loss of access for some clients; a subset of devices also retained stale wireless profiles and required re-enrollment after the certificate replacement.
resolution_steps: Verified that the corporate RADIUS/802.1X certificate (CN=radius.corp.local, serial 4A:7C:0E:91) on the Wireless Controller WLC-AUSTIN-01.corp.local had expired at 2026-05-04T01:59:59Z and confirmed it aligned with the start of user authentication failures reported by Maria Chen (mchen, EMP-40821) after the certificate refresh window.

Uploaded and activated the renewed wireless authentication certificate (serial 5B:8D:1F:A2, valid through 2028-05-03) on the Wireless Controller WLC-AUSTIN-01.corp.local, ensuring the correct certificate was presented for 802.1X EAP-TLS authentication to all access points across the Austin campus.

Restarted the Wireless Controller WLC-AUSTIN-01.corp.local at 02:38 UTC so the new certificate and authentication services were fully applied across affected wireless sessions on floors 3–7 of Building B.

Validated that clients could successfully authenticate to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) and receive normal network access after the certificate replacement; confirmed successful reconnection for users pnair (floor 7) and multiple other Engineering team members.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Integration jobs from the Integration Gateway to the downstream API began timing out around 11:15 UTC on 2025-12-11, causing failed sync runs and delayed data movement for CustomerDataSync and InternalAPIIntegration in us-east-1. The issue was reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Atlanta application support team. Monitoring on host INTGW-PROD-01.corplabs.internal correlated the failures with elevated downstream API latency and repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses from the API Service endpoint at api-service.corplabs.internal, preventing connectors from completing within the original retry and timeout window. Affected connector jobs included job_4729 and job_4731, both initiated from integration node 10.42.18.55.
root_cause: Elevated latency on the downstream API caused repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses, and the Integration Gateway connector retry/backoff behavior exhausted before requests could complete successfully.
resolution_steps: Validated that the integration API token for service account svc-intgateway remained active (expiry 2026-03-15) so authentication was not contributing to the failures.

Correlated Integration Gateway job failures (job_4729, job_4731) on node 10.42.18.55 with downstream API latency spikes and 504 Gateway Timeout events observed from 11:12 to 11:47 UTC on INTGW-PROD-01.corplabs.internal, as confirmed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Escalated the downstream latency condition to Downstream API Support under ticket DS-1023 — contacted Raj Okonkwo (rokonkwo@corplabs.com) for service-side investigation and stabilization of api-service.corplabs.internal.

Updated the Integration Gateway connector on 10.42.18.55 to use exponential retry/backoff behavior (base 2s, max 5 retries) and increased the request timeout from 30 seconds to 90 seconds to better tolerate temporary latency spikes.

Restarted the affected connectors (CustomerDataSync, InternalAPIIntegration), cleared the backlog of 47 queued sync tasks, and monitored sync processing until timeout errors subsided and delayed data synchronization returned to normal by 12:30 UTC.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: denied access to Finance shared drive
description: I was trying to open the Finance shared drive (\\FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal\Finance$) from a mapped network drive (F:) on my Windows 10 workstation WORKSTATION-PC-RGARCIA. Access to the Finance folder returned an "Access Denied" message and the mapped drive repeatedly prompted for credentials, preventing me from opening files I had previously been able to access for normal day-to-day work in the Philadelphia office.
observed_errors: Mapped drive repeatedly prompts for credentials
root_cause: User account lacked required FIN-Read Active Directory security group membership for the Finance shared drive, and the workstation was still presenting stale cached credentials/token data that caused repeated credential prompts and access denial.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the Finance shared drive access model on FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal and confirmed that Rosa Garcia's account (rgarcia, EMP FIN-20418) was missing membership in the approved FIN-Read Active Directory security group required for share and NTFS access to \\FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal\Finance$.

Added rgarcia's AD account (CN=rgarcia,OU=Finance Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) to the FIN-Read security group to restore the expected department shared drive permissions. Change approved by Kevin Marsh (kmarsh@corplabs.com).

Cleared stored network credentials (cmdkey /delete:FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal) and stale mapped drive session data on WORKSTATION-PC-RGARCIA (10.22.47.115), then remapped the F: drive to the current Finance share path \\FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal\Finance$.

Forced a Kerberos and group membership refresh on WORKSTATION-PC-RGARCIA via klist purge and gpupdate /force so the newly assigned FIN-Read entitlement applied without waiting for the next normal sign-in cycle.

Validated resolution by having Rosa Garcia reopen the Finance folder (\\FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal\Finance$) and multiple files including month-end close reports, confirming access succeeded and credential prompts stopped. User confirmed full functionality at 16:45 UTC.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: During the overnight CustomerSync batch window (02:00–04:30 UTC), the Integration Gateway at gw-prod-west-02.integrations.corplabs.internal began timing out on calls to the downstream customer API endpoint /api/v2/customers/sync, causing delayed customer data updates and failed sync jobs for dependent reporting workflows used by the Portland operations team. The issue was reported by Marcus Delgado (Application Support lead) and was concentrated during the scheduled batch period rather than throughout the day. Operations confirmed the external service was reachable from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (10.42.18.77) but responses were too slow for the integration to complete within its configured 30-second timeout.
root_cause: Elevated downstream API latency during the overnight processing window caused authenticated requests to exceed the Integration Gateway timeout threshold, resulting in timeout errors and failed batch synchronization jobs.
resolution_steps: Correlated batch-job failures with Integration Gateway latency metrics on gw-prod-west-02.integrations.corplabs.internal and downstream API traces (e.g., trx-8a3f19c7) to confirm the slowdown was external to gateway authentication and scheduling; p95 latency spiked from 4.2s to 52.1s during the 02:00–04:30 UTC window.

Escalated the incident to the downstream API provider (ticket ref EXT-CUS-20260513) with timestamps, trace samples (trx-8a3f19c7), and timeout evidence from the affected processing window. Escalation handled by Reiko Nakamura and acknowledged by downstream support contact Priya Venkatesh at priya.venkatesh@customerapi.io.

Applied a temporary timeout increase from 30s to 90s and tuned retry/backoff settings (exponential backoff with jitter, max 5 retries) on the Integration Gateway configuration for the CustomerSync Service endpoint to reduce failed overnight jobs until downstream performance stabilized. Change approved by team lead Marcus Delgado.

Re-ran the 47 affected synchronization jobs via the CustomerSync Service admin console and verified customer data updates completed successfully (all 312 records synced, 0 failures) after downstream API latency returned to normal baseline (~4s p95) at approximately 06:15 UTC on 2026-05-13.
agent_questions: We found repeated 504 timeouts during the overnight CustomerSync batch (02:00–04:30 UTC on 2026-05-13) on gw-prod-west-02.integrations.corplabs.internal and a failed token refresh event in the same window. Reviewing the Integration Gateway audit trail under service account svc-custsync, we see 47 consecutive timeout entries. Can you confirm whether any token rotation or downstream API credential change occurred before the sync delays started? Please reach out to me at r.nakamura@corplabs.com or ext. 4-7831 if you need to discuss offline. — Reiko Nakamura, Integration Support

title: Software Center installation blocked for FinanceApp (entitlement missing) — resolved

title: Finance queue print jobs stuck
description: Finance users including Rachel Whitmore (EMP-40821) and David Okonkwo were trying to print batch and individual documents through the shared Finance-Printer-01 queue hosted on psrv01.corp.local, but jobs became stuck in the queue and reported 'driver unavailable' with Error 0x00000709 after an earlier queue remap only temporarily restored service. Multiple Finance users at the Bristol office were affected, preventing normal document printing, and the Windows Server 2019 Print Spooler logged driver checksum and load failures on the print server. The issue was initially reported from workstation WORKSTATION-PC-RW (IP 10.42.17.85) by rwhitmore.
observed_errors: Driver package checksum mismatch during load
root_cause: Corrupt printer driver package on psrv01.corp.local caused spooler driver load and checksum failures, leaving Finance-Printer-01 jobs stuck and returning driver unavailable errors.
resolution_steps: Removed the corrupted Finance printer driver package from the print server driver store on psrv01.corp.local to eliminate the failing driver load state. Performed by Marcus Jennings (mjennings) in Desktop Support.

Installed the approved HP Universal Print Driver v6.8 from the corporate driver repository and associated the clean package with the Finance-Printer-01 queue. Driver hash verified against repository by mjennings.

Cleared all stuck jobs from the Finance-Printer-01 queue — including 14 pending jobs from rwhitmore, dokonkwo, and pnair — so failed spool files tied to the corrupt driver would not continue retrying.
Restarted the Print Spooler service on the print server to reload the updated driver package and reset queue processing. Confirmed spooler event logs showed clean driver load with no checksum errors.
Validated successful printing from Rachel Whitmore (rwhitmore) and David Okonkwo (dokonkwo) Finance user accounts and monitored the queue for 2 hours with no recurrence before closing the incident.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether all Finance users are seeing jobs stuck only on Finance-Printer-01 and whether the error shown is 'driver unavailable' or a different printer message. Also, can you check if David Okonkwo and others on your team are experiencing the same behaviour from their workstations?

title: Multiple users unable to authenticate to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple users in the Austin office, Building A on floors 2-3, were trying to join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) from managed Windows 10, macOS 11, and Android 11 devices, but 802.1X authentication failed and devices received no usable network access after attempting to connect. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40821) and escalated by team lead David Kowalski. It began after the automated wireless certificate rollover window at approximately 06:00 UTC on 2026-04-25 and primarily impacted EAP-TLS authentication against the Cisco AireOS/WLC cluster (wlc-primary.corp.aireos.local / wlc-secondary.corp.aireos.local), disrupting normal wireless access for Engineering and Sales users across roughly 45 affected endpoints.
root_cause: The Wireless Controller cluster presented an expired server certificate after the certificate rollover window, causing EAP-TLS validation failures during 802.1X authentication. A subset of older clients also continued to reference stale trust or cached certificate data after the controller certificate was renewed.
resolution_steps: Renew the Wireless Controller server certificate (CN=corp-wifi.globaledge.com) and install the updated certificate across the full controller cluster (wlc-primary and wlc-secondary) so all nodes present the same valid EAP-TLS identity. Certificate renewal was performed by Tomás Rivera (trivera) using the GlobalEdge Internal CA.

Clear stale certificate and authentication caches on affected controllers (wlc-primary.corp.aireos.local and wlc-secondary.corp.aireos.local), then restart the relevant controller authentication services during the approved maintenance window at 15:25 UTC.

Validate successful 802.1X authentication against the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) using test device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (user mchen, IP 10.22.3.117) and review controller and NAC logs on nac01.corp.globaledge.com to confirm certificate validation succeeds end to end.

Remediate impacted legacy clients by having users (dkowalski, pnair, rmehta) forget and re-add the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID and by pushing the updated trust anchor or wireless profile via MDM where device management supports it. Desktop support contacted each affected user in the Austin Building A, floors 2-3, to walk through the reconnection steps.

Monitor post-change authentication logs and client reconnect behavior on nac01.corp.globaledge.com and the WLC cluster for at least 24 hours to confirm roaming and reauthentication are stable and no further expired-certificate failures are occurring. Monitoring ownership assigned to Tomás Rivera (trivera, phone ext. 512-555-0147).
agent_questions: We are checking whether the issue is profile-related or controller-side. Please confirm whether affected devices see an 802.1X or certificate warning when joining Corporate Wi-Fi and whether this started after the recent certificate rollover. Specifically, can you verify if users like Maria Chen (mchen@globaledge.com) and David Kowalski are seeing a certificate trust prompt or a flat authentication rejection? Also, please note the MAC or hostname of at least one failing device so we can trace it in the NAC logs.

title: Device noncompliant: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key missing
description: I a corporate Windows 10 laptop assigned to Marcus Delgado (employee ID EMP-40291) is marked noncompliant in Intune because device encryption shows as not enabled. No BitLocker recovery key is visible in Azure AD, and the initial report did not include the device name, TPM state, or last Intune sync details. The user reached out from the Portland office and the issue affects BitLocker compliance and blocks the device from meeting endpoint security requirements for normal corporate use. The ticket was submitted on behalf of the user by mdelgado@corplabs.com.
observed_errors: No BitLocker recovery key found in Azure AD
Device Compliance Service shows noncompliant for encryption
root_cause: BitLocker was not fully enabled on the endpoint, so no valid recovery key had been escrowed to Azure AD. Based on the ticket evidence, the most likely contributing conditions were missing or unapplied Intune BitLocker policy and unverified TPM/protector readiness, which left the device reporting encryption as disabled and therefore noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Identify the affected device in Intune (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD, user mdelgado, EMP-40291) and confirm the assigned BitLocker or Endpoint Security disk encryption policy is targeted to the device without assignment conflicts. Verify the device object in Intune matches the expected hostname and user principal name mdelgado@corplabs.com.

Validate TPM readiness on the Windows endpoint WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD and initialize the TPM or BitLocker protector if it is present but not ready for use by encryption policy. Run tpm.msc or Get-Tpm via PowerShell to confirm TPM 2.0 is enabled and owned, and coordinate with Marcus Delgado (phone: 503-447-8126) if on-device action is needed.

Force an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD so the active encryption policy is reapplied and the endpoint can begin BitLocker enablement. This can be triggered from the Intune portal under the device record for mdelgado or via the Company Portal app on the device.

Enable BitLocker on the system drive (C:) using the managed policy path and verify the device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD reports encryption in progress or protection on. Confirm via manage-bde -status that the volume is fully encrypted with a TPM protector.

Escrow or rotate the BitLocker recovery key to Azure AD after protection is enabled on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD, then confirm the recovery key is visible in the device record under Azure AD > Devices > mdelgado's device > BitLocker keys.

Recheck Intune compliance after policy refresh and key escrow to confirm the device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD no longer reports 'Encryption not enabled' and returns to compliant status. Notify Marcus Delgado at mdelgado@corplabs.com and close the ticket once compliance is verified.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, please provide the device name (hostname), confirm whether TPM is ready on the laptop, and share the last Intune sync time so we can verify BitLocker policy application and recovery key escrow status. You can find the TPM status by running tpm.msc on the device. Also, please confirm if the device hostname is something like WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD or similar so we can look it up in Intune.

title: GlobalProtect drops immediately
description: I was trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from my managed Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-FIN-RGARCIA) at the Seattle office. My username is rgarcia and I authenticated via Okta MFA push to my phone (206-555-0147). The MFA approval succeeded, but the VPN tunnel disconnected within about 30 seconds of authentication, preventing access to internal applications including the intranet, Finance Portal, and SSH access to the bastion host. My IP at the time was 10.42.18.93. Similar intermittent impact was reported for other users in the Finance group (including mwatson and tnguyen) after a device certificate rotation change deployed the same morning.
observed_errors: Tunnel terminated by peer after authentication
root_cause: Expired device certificate on the endpoint caused certificate validation failure during GlobalProtect tunnel establishment after successful Okta MFA, resulting in the gateway terminating the session.
resolution_steps: Validated that the endpoint device certificate (serial 4A:7F:C2:91:03) on WORKSTATION-FIN-RGARCIA had expired at 06:00:00Z and requested a replacement certificate from the Device Certificate Service for CN=rgarcia,OU=Finance,DC=corplabs,DC=internal.

Installed and confirmed the renewed device certificate (new serial 4A:7F:C2:91:58, valid through 2027-04-19) was valid and matched the VPN enrollment requirements on Rachel Garcia's affected laptop WORKSTATION-FIN-RGARCIA.

Pushed an updated GlobalProtect VPN profile to WORKSTATION-FIN-RGARCIA so the client used the current certificate and profile settings; also pushed the same update to affected Finance group devices for mwatson and tnguyen.

Had rgarcia clear the local GlobalProtect profile cache and reconnect to force retrieval of the refreshed configuration and certificate mapping. Confirmed successful reconnection from IP 10.42.18.93 at the Seattle office.

Verified the VPN session for rgarcia remained established and internal application access (Intranet, Finance Portal, SSH bastion) was restored. Monitored for 24 hours with no further disconnects; also confirmed resolution for mwatson and tnguyen.

Notified Network Support (escalation contact: Lisa Pham, lpham@corplabs.com) to review certificate rotation monitoring and alerting to prevent recurrence after future certificate changes across the Finance group.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether the VPN drops before MFA approval or only after you approve the Okta prompt on your device, and whether you can see any GlobalProtect error dialog or status message before it disconnects. Also, can you confirm your machine hostname and whether you're connecting from the Seattle office or remotely? I'm assigning this to myself (Agent: David Kowalski, emp ID E-40291) for tracking.

title: Cannot connect to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple office users in the Frankfurt location were trying to join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) but could not complete 802.1X authentication. Devices associated to the wireless network and then failed EAP-TLS certificate validation, leaving users without network access. The issue was first reported by Maria Engel (EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed by at least six other staff members on the 4th floor. The issue affected corporate wireless access broadly rather than a single endpoint and blocked normal office connectivity until the wireless authentication certificate was corrected.
observed_errors: RADIUS: Access-Reject due to certificate validation failure
root_cause: The server certificate used by the RADIUS/WLC wireless authentication path had expired, causing EAP-TLS certificate validation failures and RADIUS Access-Reject responses for corporate Wi-Fi clients.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the wireless authentication failure was tied to certificate validation errors in AP, RADIUS (radius-fra.corp.internal), and controller (WLC-FRA-01) logs rather than AP connectivity or VLAN configuration. Network engineer Priya Nair (p.nair, EMP-55193) verified the expired certificate serial.

Renewed the expired RADIUS server certificate (CN=radius-fra.corp.internal) used for 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentication via the internal PKI portal, generating a new certificate with validity through 2028-04-23.

Deployed the renewed certificate and updated the certificate binding on WLC-FRA-01 and the related RADIUS authentication components on radius-fra.corp.internal. Binding was confirmed active by Priya Nair.
Restarted the RADIUS service on radius-fra.corp.internal and performed a controlled reload of WLC-FRA-01 so the new certificate chain was actively presented during 802.1X authentication handshakes.

Validated successful client re-authentication in infrastructure logs — confirmed Maria Engel (m.engel) on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-ME (10.42.18.97) and Tobias Richter (t.richter) on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-TR could connect after forgetting and rejoining the CorpNet-Secure SSID where re-enrollment was required. All affected Frankfurt users reported connectivity restored by 11:30 UTC.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether the Wi-Fi failure is affecting multiple users on the Frankfurt 4th floor and whether devices connect to the CorpNet-Secure SSID but fail during 802.1X authentication rather than showing no signal. Also, can you provide the hostname or MAC of the device you're using (e.g. your laptop) so we can trace it in the controller logs?

title: Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service caused TLS outage
description: Users and internal monitors were trying to reach internal-service.example.corp, but browsers displayed certificate expiration warnings and the load balancer (LB-PROD-EAST-02) health checks began failing TLS handshakes starting around 2025-12-15 08:45 UTC. The issue was first reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez@example.corp) from the Chicago office, who noticed ERR_SSL_CERT_EXPIRED errors when accessing the Internal Web Service from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MG. This prevented normal access to the Internal Web Service over HTTPS and caused the service to appear unavailable until the expired certificate and missing updated chain on the load balancer were corrected. Additional reports were received from employees in the Atlanta office shortly after.
root_cause: The TLS certificate deployed for internal-service.example.corp expired on 2025-12-15, and the renewed certificate and full chain were not deployed to the load balancer. Certificate renewal monitoring also failed to alert before expiration, allowing the outage to occur.
resolution_steps: Generated and signed a renewed TLS certificate for internal-service.example.corp (new serial 7B:12:E4:5A) through the internal CA (CA-INT-EAST-01), verified by Priya Nair (pnair).
Uploaded the renewed certificate and complete certificate chain to the load balancer LB-PROD-EAST-02 certificate store, replacing the expired deployment (old serial 4A:3F:C1:09).

Reloaded the load balancer LB-PROD-EAST-02 configuration so the new certificate and chain were presented on the service endpoint internal-service.example.corp:443. Reload performed by pnair at 2025-12-15 04:32 UTC.

Validated successful TLS handshakes from the endpoint using openssl s_client from 10.22.14.87 and confirmed load balancer health checks on LB-PROD-EAST-02 returned to healthy status. Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez@example.corp) confirmed browser access was restored from WORKSTATION-PC-MG.

Restored and corrected the certificate renewal monitoring alert (owned by rchen) so future renewal failures or upcoming expirations are detected at least 30 days before impact. Alert rule was updated to include both email notification to rchen@example.corp and PagerDuty escalation for the network_team.

title: account locked after failed sign-ins
description: I changed my corporate password through the Password Reset Portal on May 7th but continued to receive account lockouts when trying to access Corporate SSO (https://sso.corplabs.com) and OWA mailbox services. My username is mreeves and the lockouts started almost immediately after the reset completed. root_cause: A non-mobile service, legacy client, or integrated application continued using outdated stored credentials after the password reset, repeatedly triggering Active Directory lockouts.

Documented that mobile credential cleanup on WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MR (10.47.83.112) did not resolve the issue and correlated lockout timing on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal to a non-interactive authentication source submitting stale credentials for mreeves every ~3 minutes.

Please confirm whether the account is still signed in on your mobile device (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MR) or mail apps, as repeated failed logons are being recorded from a mobile user-agent originating from IP 10.47.83.112 after the password reset. I also see Event ID 4740 lockout entries on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal referencing your account. I'll begin investigating the lockout source while we wait for your confirmation. — Priya Nair, Service Desk

title: Print Server jobs stuck
description: Multiple users in the Newark office were trying to print through print server PS-PRINT01, but print jobs remained stuck in shared queues and several printers appeared offline. The visible queue error was "Driver unavailable," jobs stayed queued at 0%, and affected users — including Maria Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40218) and Kevin Ostrowski (kostrowski) — could not complete normal office printing. Investigation on Windows Server 2016 print server PS-PRINT01 showed repeated Print Spooler driver load failures tied to the HP Universal driver package (v6.9.0.24297), indicating the installed driver package had become corrupted after a recent SCCM push.
observed_errors: Print Spooler service errors (driver load failures)
root_cause: Corrupted HP Universal printer driver package on PS-PRINT01 caused the Print Spooler to fail loading the driver, leaving shared print jobs stuck with a 'Driver unavailable' state.
resolution_steps: Validated that the affected queues on PS-PRINT01 (\\PS-PRINT01\NWK-3F-HP4050, \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-3F-HP5200, \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-2F-HP4050) were failing with the message 'Driver unavailable' and identified the HP Universal driver package v6.9.0.24297 as the common failing component across all three queues.

Reinstalled the approved HP Universal driver package v6.9.0.24300 on PS-PRINT01 through SCCM to replace the corrupted driver files, verifying the SHA-256 hash of hpuni197.dll matched the deployment manifest after installation.

Cleared all 23 stuck print jobs from the affected queues and restarted the Print Spooler service on PS-PRINT01 to reload the corrected driver package cleanly. Confirmed the spooler started without Event ID 372 errors.
Remapped the affected printer queues (NWK-3F-HP4050, NWK-3F-HP5200, NWK-2F-HP4050) to the approved driver package v6.9.0.24300 so queue-to-driver associations were consistent after reinstall.

Submitted validation print jobs from multiple endpoints — WORKSTATION-PC-MD (mdelgado), kostrowski's workstation, and rpatel's workstation — and confirmed the queues processed normally without new spooler driver load failures. All test pages printed within 5 seconds of submission.

Updated the approved printer driver deployment policy in SCCM to pin HP Universal driver v6.9.0.24300 as the mandatory version and added a file-integrity pre-check to prevent the stale or corrupted package v6.9.0.24297 from being redeployed to the print server. Notified the Newark Workplace Services team lead, Sandra Chen (schen@corplabs.com), of the policy update.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — can you confirm whether all affected printers are mapped through PS-PRINT01? Also, are users seeing the same 'Driver unavailable' message in their queue, or only an offline status on the printer icon? If possible, please share the exact printer queue name (e.g., \\PS-PRINT01\NWK-3F-HP4050) that you were printing to when the issue occurred.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects shortly
description: I was trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from my managed Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-MH-4417) in the Frankfurt office. My username is mhansen and I authenticated through Okta MFA successfully, but the VPN tunnel stayed up only briefly and then disconnected within 20-40 seconds. While the tunnel was active, internal web apps were unreachable from my IP 10.42.88.115, blocking normal remote access. The recurrence after a prior profile reset pointed to a post-authentication certificate or profile validation problem rather than an MFA failure. Please contact me at marcus.hansen@corplabs.com or +49 172 5589301 if you need remote access to my machine.
observed_errors: TLS handshake failure during post-authentication (client log)

title: Print jobs stuck on Floor3-Color queue after prior resolution
description: Users on Engineering Floor 3 in the Austin campus were trying to print color documents through the shared Floor3-Color queue on PrintServer-PRD (10.40.3.15), but jobs remained queued since the prior day and the queue showed 'Driver unavailable'. root_cause: Corruption in the HP Universal printer driver package on PrintServer-PRD combined with a stale Floor3-Color queue mapping caused the Windows Print Spooler to reject or stall jobs, leaving the queue in a recurring 'Driver unavailable' state.
resolution_steps: Verified the Floor3-Color shared queue on PrintServer-PRD (10.40.3.15) was stalled and identified 14 queued jobs from users including mgonzalez and dliu showing 'Driver unavailable' with no timestamp movement since 2026-03-03T14:22:00Z.

Removed the corrupted HP driver package from PrintServer-PRD driver store and reinstalled the approved HP Universal Driver version 6.8 (clean package downloaded from the internal driver repository by rpatel), verifying checksum matched the approved baseline.
Cleared all 14 stuck jobs from the Floor3-Color queue and flushed the Windows Print Spooler cache on PrintServer-PRD to remove stale spool files from C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS.

Corrected the Floor3-Color queue mapping to the proper server path (\\PrintServer-PRD\Floor3-Color) and restarted the Windows Print Spooler service. Notified affected users mgonzalez and dliu via email that printing was restored.

Submitted validation print jobs from multiple workstations including WORKSTATION-MG-ENG3 (mgonzalez, 10.40.3.88) and WORKSTATION-DL-ENG3 (dliu, 10.40.3.91), and monitored queue processing for 30 minutes to confirm all jobs completed normally without returning to a stalled state. Raj Patel confirmed stable operation at 11:15 UTC.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failure for internal-service.local
description: Internal users in the Denver office were intermittently unable to resolve internal-service.local after a recent application migration completed on 2026-01-09. DNS queries for the service returned inconsistent results from the on-prem DNS path, including an outdated A record (10.10.5.3 instead of the expected 10.10.7.18), occasional NXDOMAIN responses, and lookup timeouts from subnet 10.20.0.0/16. The issue was first reported by Maria Castillo (emp ID E20481) who noticed that the internal-service endpoint was unreachable by name from her workstation WORKSTATION-MC2041. Multiple dependent applications and clients across the corporate network were unable to reliably reach the internal-service endpoint by name.
observed_errors: DNS lookup timeout from client subnet 10.20.0.0/16
root_cause: Primary on-prem DNS resolver and downstream caching forwarders were serving stale cached data for internal-service.local after the application migration changed the service IP, causing intermittent old A record responses and occasional NXDOMAIN during propagation.
resolution_steps: Validated the internal DNS zone entry for internal-service.local on the Internal DNS Zone and updated the A record to the correct post-migration IP address 10.10.7.18 (previously 10.10.5.3), ensuring the SOA serial was incremented.

Committed the zone change on the primary resolver dc-resolver1.corplabs.internal and confirmed the authoritative zone data reflected the current record (10.10.7.18) and intended TTL settings (reduced from 86400 to 300 seconds).

Flushed DNS cache on the primary resolver dc-resolver1 and on caching forwarders fw-resolver1 and fw-resolver2 to remove stale responses for internal-service.local. Executed by Kevin Briggs (kbriggs, Network Operations).

Adjusted internal zone refresh interval from 3600 to 900 seconds and reduced default TTL policy to 300 seconds to reduce the likelihood and duration of stale-cache behavior after future service IP changes.

Verified successful name resolution from multiple client subnets (10.20.0.0/16, 10.21.0.0/16), including workstations WORKSTATION-MC2041 (Maria Castillo) and WORKSTATION-RP3087 (Raj Patel), confirming consistent responses to the current address 10.10.7.18 with no further NXDOMAIN results.

Monitored DNS lookup alerts via Network Monitoring and client resolution behavior for 2 hours after the change (until 2026-01-10T09:15:00Z) and observed stable resolution with no recurrence. Confirmed with Maria Castillo (mcastillo@corplabs.com) that the issue was fully resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — we are checking the internal DNS path for internal-service.local from the corp-dc-east resolver infrastructure. Can you confirm whether the intermittent failures are only being reported by users in the Denver office, and whether the issue started after the application migration on 2026-01-09? title: Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service causing TLS outages
description: Users and automated clients were trying to reach the Internal Web Service at https://portal.internal.corplabs.com over TLS, but the endpoint began presenting an expired certificate after the overnight expiry window on 2025-12-16. Browsers showed ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and dependent integrations (including CI/CD pipelines and monitoring agents) failed TLS validation and handshake, blocking normal internal service access for the entire us-east-1 internal_services user group. The issue was reported initially by Maria Delgado from the Denver office and was traced to the HAProxy load balancer (lb-haproxy-east-01.corplabs.internal) serving an expired certificate for CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com and incomplete or stale chain material, with certificate renewal monitoring in Nagios not alerting before expiration.
root_cause: The Internal Web Service outage was caused by an expired TLS certificate remaining deployed on the HAProxy load balancer, along with a certificate chain that was not fully updated during reload attempts. A monitoring and renewal alert gap allowed the certificate to expire without preemptive intervention.
resolution_steps: Renewed the TLS certificate with the internal Certificate Authority (ca.corplabs.internal) and obtained the correct full certificate chain — including the updated CorpLabs Internal CA G2 intermediate — for the Internal Web Service endpoint portal.internal.corplabs.com. New certificate serial: 5B:9D:4F:02:CC, notAfter 2026-12-16T23:59:59Z.

Replaced the expired certificate and chain bundle at /etc/haproxy/certs/portal-chain.pem on the HAProxy load balancer lb-haproxy-east-01.corplabs.internal, ensuring the active bind listener on port 443 referenced the updated files rather than stale certificate material. Deployment performed by Kevin Marsh (kmarsh, EMP-4471).

Reloaded HAProxy (systemctl reload haproxy) after deployment on lb-haproxy-east-01.corplabs.internal and verified the service was presenting the renewed leaf certificate (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com, serial 5B:9D:4F:02:CC) together with the required CorpLabs Internal CA G2 intermediate chain via openssl s_client.

resolution_steps: Validated that the VPN disconnect for user mreeves (Marcus Reeves, EMP-40291) occurred after successful Okta MFA and confirmed the GlobalProtect gateway logs reported the device certificate on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR as expired (CERT_EXPIRED) at session termination.

title: Integration Gateway API calls timing out causing integration job failures
description: Integration jobs for the reporting application (managed by the Data Integration team under Marcus Delgado) began failing around 09:12 UTC on 2025-12-04 when API calls routed through the Integration Gateway on host INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 started timing out. The issue was first reported by analyst Priya Nair (emp ID DI-40287) who observed delayed real-time data syncs and failed nightly ingestion runs from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN (IP 10.42.18.93). Application and gateway logs showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout errors, and the Monitoring System dashboard indicated rising downstream latency and elevated error responses from the external analytics API endpoint. The outage affected the API integration path used by the reporting application and blocked normal data synchronization for the Austin office until the downstream rate-limit condition was mitigated.
observed_errors: integration job error: timeout waiting for response
root_cause: The downstream API enforced rate limits against the integration client, producing sustained 429 Too Many Requests responses. Gateway retries accumulated under elevated latency, exhausted the effective timeout window, and resulted in 504 Gateway Timeout errors that caused integration job failures and delayed data syncs.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Integration Gateway traces on INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 and Monitoring System dashboards to confirm the timeout pattern was driven by repeated downstream 429 responses (1,247 occurrences) and increasing response latency (p99 >28s) rather than an internal gateway failure. Analysis performed by Raymond Chen (rchen) with input from Priya Nair.

Applied temporary exponential backoff (initial delay 2s, max 60s, jitter enabled) and adjusted the Integration Gateway retry policy on INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 to cap retries at 3 attempts, reducing immediate retry storms while preserving successful completion for delayed downstream responses.

Coordinated with the downstream analytics API owner (contact: Tomás Rivera, trivera@partnerapi.net) to increase the request quota for integration client ID intg-rpt-prod-east from 200 req/min to 500 req/min after confirming sustained rate-limit enforcement against the Austin integration path.

Replayed the failed ingestion job RPT-INGEST-0412 and real-time synchronization jobs after the quota increase was confirmed at 11:02 UTC, and verified that all requests completed successfully without recurring gateway 504 errors. Priya Nair (pnair) confirmed data sync restored on her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN.

Updated the Integration Gateway retry and backoff policy for the reporting integration path on INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 and added Monitoring System alerting thresholds for 429 spike detection (>20 per 5-min window) and downstream latency growth (p95 >5s) to detect recurrence earlier. Alert recipients set to mdelgado@corplabs.com and rchen@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please confirm whether the downstream responses you're seeing show HTTP 429 or other 5xx status codes. Also, can you share the last successful job timing from the Data Ingestion Pipeline so we can determine whether this is a latency degradation or a rate-limit issue? You can pull the trace IDs from the Integration Gateway logs on INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 or forward them to me at r.chen@corplabs.com. — Raymond Chen

Validate queue permissions for the Finance security group and submit controlled test prints from the server console and from Robert Yuen's workstation (WORKSTATION-PC-RY, IP 10.42.17.88) under his user context (ryuen) to confirm jobs process normally without driver load errors.

description: Company-managed engineering laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-MK, asset tag ENG-04821) assigned to Marcus Kim (emp ID EMP-20947) on Windows 10 21H2 was reported noncompliant in Microsoft Intune because disk encryption was not enabled and no BitLocker recovery key was escrowed to Azure AD. title: Intermittent NXDOMAIN for svc-inventory.internal
description: Users were trying to reach the internal svc-inventory service by hostname, but svc-inventory.internal intermittently returned NXDOMAIN from internal DNS resolvers across multiple on-prem hosts in the Richmond data center (us-east-1). The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40821) from the platform engineering team, and subsequently confirmed by additional users including DevOps engineer Raj Patel. Direct access to the service IP (10.42.16.55) and basic network reachability tests succeeded, indicating the application and network path were available while name resolution was failing. The issue intermittently blocked internal services and users from reaching the inventory endpoint by name, affecting automated deployments and CI/CD pipelines.
observed_errors: NXDOMAIN returned by internal resolver for svc-inventory.internal
intermittent negative responses in DNS query logs
root_cause: Intermittent NXDOMAIN responses were caused by an internal DNS configuration issue for the svc-inventory.internal resolution path, most likely a stale or inconsistent zone/forwarder state on the internal resolver that served negative cached responses for the record until cache and record path were corrected.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS record path for svc-inventory.internal and confirmed the expected A host record (10.42.16.55, TTL 300) existed in the authoritative internal zone managed on the primary zone server.

Validated the conditional forwarder used for the .internal namespace on dns-resolver-east-01.corp.internal and identified that one forwarder target pointed to a decommissioned secondary authoritative server. Corrected the resolver path so queries for svc-inventory.internal were sent exclusively to the active authoritative source.
Cleared stale negative cache entries on the affected internal DNS resolver dns-resolver-east-01.corp.internal after the DNS path and record state were verified by network engineer Priya Nair (pnair).

Retested name resolution for svc-inventory.internal from multiple internal hosts — WORKSTATION-LP-MCHEN (10.10.34.112, user mchen), WORKSTATION-DT-RPATEL (10.10.35.78, user rpatel), and additional endpoints — and from the resolver directly to confirm the hostname consistently returned the expected address 10.42.16.55 instead of NXDOMAIN.

Monitored follow-up queries during the affected window using Network Monitoring dashboards and confirmed name-based access to the svc-inventory service was restored without requiring direct IP usage. No further NXDOMAIN responses were observed over the subsequent 2-hour monitoring period.

title: Integration Gateway timeouts causing delayed data sync to downstream service
description: Nightly batch data synchronization from DataSyncApp (service account svc-datasync) through the Integration Gateway to the downstream InventoryAPI service began failing between 03:20 and 03:50 UTC on 2025-12-03. The API Service running on pod datasyncapp-worker-7b in namespace appsync-prod (us-east-1) received repeated HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses, and at least one scheduled sync job (sync-20251203-batch4) failed, delaying data availability for downstream consumers in the Chicago fulfillment group. Investigation by Marcus Ellison showed the gateway was still referencing a deprecated retry/backoff policy (v1.2) while downstream latency was elevated, causing retries to amplify timeout behavior rather than allowing the batch to complete. Reported initially by Priya Nagarajan via the Application Support on-call channel.
root_cause: Elevated downstream service latency caused upstream request timeouts, and the impact was amplified because the Integration Gateway was still using a stale deprecated retry/backoff policy that extended retry behavior beyond the effective integration window.
resolution_steps: Replaced the deprecated Integration Gateway retry policy v1.2 (rtpol-0012-deprecated) with the supported v1.3 production configuration on gw-east-prod-01.corplabs.internal in the appsync-prod namespace, applied by Marcus Ellison.

Updated gateway retry behavior to exponential backoff with jitter (base 2s, max 16s, jitter factor 0.5) and reduced the cumulative retry window from 180s to 60s to avoid amplifying downstream latency spikes against InventoryAPI.
