title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failing
description: Users and monitoring reported intermittent DNS resolution failures for api.internal.corp affecting access to the internal service API. The issue was initially flagged by Marcus Delgado (Service Owner, EMP-40291) and confirmed by the Network Monitoring dashboard. Some client lookups from workstations in the Phoenix datacenter returned an outdated A record (10.10.10.5) while the authoritative internal DNS zone showed the newer IP (10.10.10.6), causing application requests to be routed to the decommissioned endpoint or fail intermittently with connection timeouts. Impact was limited to internal name resolution through corporate resolvers in corp-datacenter-1, primarily affecting clients on the 10.10.12.0/24 subnet.
observed_errors: Cached A record 10.10.10.5 returned by resolver for api.internal.corp while authoritative shows 10.10.10.6
root_cause: Stale cached A record on internal DNS resolvers caused api.internal.corp to intermittently resolve to 10.10.10.5 instead of the authoritative 10.10.10.6 after the zone record changed.
resolution_steps: Validated the authoritative DNS zone on ns-auth01.corp-datacenter-1.internal for api.internal.corp and corrected any mismatched A record entries so the intended address was 10.10.10.6. Priya Nair confirmed zone serial 2026011402 reflected the latest update.

Temporarily lowered the TTL on the affected DNS record from 3600 to 300 seconds to reduce stale-cache duration and speed propagation of the corrected value across all resolver infrastructure in the Phoenix datacenter.

Flushed cached entries for the hostname on primary and secondary internal resolvers, including resolver01.corp-datacenter-1.internal and resolver02.corp-datacenter-1.internal, using rndc flushname api.internal.corp to remove the stale 10.10.10.5 response.

Retested resolution from affected clients (including WORKSTATION-PC-MD at 10.10.12.47, user mdelgado) and internal resolvers to confirm they now returned the authoritative address 10.10.10.6 consistently. Marcus Delgado verified API connectivity was restored.

Updated Network Monitoring to compare resolver responses against authoritative DNS data on ns-auth01 so future stale-cache conditions are detected earlier. Added a scheduled check that alerts the network_team distribution list (netops@corplabs.com) when resolver and authoritative answers diverge for critical internal hostnames.

title: Internal hostname resolving to stale IP
description: Multiple internal services, including the Inventory Service and Internal API Gateway, could not reliably reach api.internal.corp by name from Linux application servers in corp-dc-1 at the Denver data center. DNS lookups intermittently returned either a stale A record (10.0.1.45) or NXDOMAIN, blocking application connectivity to the internal API endpoint after a recent internal DNS record update. Issue was first reported by Marcus Jennings (emp ID: E-40821) from the platform engineering team, and subsequently confirmed by additional users on the same subnet.
observed_errors: stale A record 10.0.1.45 returned from resolver
root_cause: An outdated A record and stale cached DNS data for api.internal.corp were being served by internal resolvers after the zone record changed, causing inconsistent responses between the authoritative internal zone and resolver cache.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the authoritative internal DNS zone entry on ns1.corp-dc-1.internal for api.internal.corp and corrected the A record to the current service IP (10.0.2.90), confirming the update applied by kaldrich on 2026-01-15.
Validated the zone update in DNS management on ns1.corp-dc-1.internal and confirmed the record TTL (300s) and recent change state were consistent with the intended configuration.
Flushed stale cache entries on the primary DNS resolver dns-resolver-01.corp-dc-1.internal so new queries would no longer return the prior IP address 10.0.1.45.

Cleared local resolver caches on affected Linux application servers, including WORKSTATION-LNX-MJ (10.20.5.12) and the host at 10.20.5.17 where nscd had been restarted, to remove retained stale answers.

Retested name resolution and application connectivity from affected servers — Marcus Jennings confirmed api.internal.corp consistently resolved to 10.0.2.90 from WORKSTATION-LNX-MJ without NXDOMAIN responses, and Priya Nair verified the same from her host.

Monitored DNS and application health via Network Monitoring dashboards for two hours after remediation and confirmed no recurrence of lookup failures across the Denver data center. Kevin Aldrich closed the ticket after final verification.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether all affected hosts are resolving api.internal.corp to the same IP and whether failures show a stale address or NXDOMAIN. Could you also run nslookup from WORKSTATION-LNX-MJ and from at least one other app server (e.g., the host Priya Nair uses at 10.20.5.17) so we can compare? — Kevin Aldrich, Network Operations

title: Reopened: Finance queue print jobs stuck
description: Finance users reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40218) were unable to print to the shared Finance-Printer1 queue on print server PRNSRV-EAST-02. Jobs submitted from workstations in the Newark office remained stuck in the queue and could not complete. The issue affected the entire Finance shared printer workflow, blocking normal document printing for approximately 14 users until the queue mapping and driver state were corrected.
root_cause: Approved printer driver package was reinstalled previously, but Finance-Printer1 remained mapped to an incorrect or mismatched print server queue/driver association, causing the spooler to report driver unavailable and leaving jobs stuck in the shared queue.
resolution_steps: Validated the Finance-Printer1 queue state on print server PRNSRV-EAST-02 and confirmed 23 stalled jobs with repeated "driver unavailable" (Event ID 372) spooler errors across Finance user accounts in the Newark office.

Compared the installed driver package for Finance-Printer1 with the approved HP Universal Print Driver v7.1.0.25 (PCL6) package from the central repository and reinstalled the approved driver package with SHA-256 checksum verification, confirming the binary matched the repository baseline.

Cleared all 23 pending jobs from the Finance-Printer1 queue on PRNSRV-EAST-02 and restarted the Windows Print Spooler service to remove the stuck spool state and release locked spool files from C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS.

Corrected the Finance-Printer1 mapping on PRNSRV-EAST-02 so the shared printer pointed to the proper print server queue and matching PCL6 driver association (GUID {D7E9-FA03-PCL6}), replacing the stale legacy PCL5 reference that persisted from the prior incomplete reinstall.

Submitted test prints from Finance user accounts mgonzalez (WORKSTATION-PC-MG), rpatel, and jnorris (WORKSTATION-PC-JN) and confirmed the queue accepted and processed jobs successfully without new spooler retry or service errors. Notified Maria Gonzalez at mgonzalez@corplabs.com that the Finance-Printer1 queue was fully operational.
agent_questions: We are checking whether Finance-Printer1 on PRNSRV-EAST-02 is failing due to the queue state only or if the shared printer is still tied to the wrong driver or server queue association. title: Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service behind Load Balancer
description: Internal users and dependent services were trying to reach the svc-internal endpoint (svc-internal.corplabs.internal) over TLS through the load balancer LB-EAST-02, but clients began showing certificate warnings and rejecting the connection. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, who noticed that requests from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MC were returning NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID errors. The load balancer presented an expired certificate (CN=svc-internal.corplabs.internal, expired 2025-12-10T00:00:00Z) and an incomplete chain after the renewal window was missed, which blocked normal access to the internal web service and caused TLS handshake failures for internal integrations in us-east-1. Multiple teams including the payroll integration service (contact: David Ortiz, emp ID E-40291) confirmed downstream failures.
observed_errors: certificate expired presented by load balancer
root_cause: The svc-internal certificate presented by the load balancer expired, and the load balancer configuration was not updated with the renewed intermediate certificate. Certificate monitoring and renewal alerting also failed to notify before expiration, allowing the invalid chain to remain in production.
resolution_steps: Renew the svc-internal TLS certificate (CN=svc-internal.corplabs.internal) with the internal Certificate Authority CA-EAST-01 and verify the renewed certificate matches the service endpoint name and SAN entries. Renewal performed by Raj Patel (rpatel, E-50184).

Deploy the renewed server certificate and the full trusted chain, including the renewed CorpLabs Internal Intermediate CA G2 certificate, to load balancer LB-EAST-02 serving svc-internal. Deployment coordinated by Lisa Nguyen (lnguyen).

Remove the temporary self-signed certificate workaround from LB-EAST-02 listener configuration and update the load balancer certificate chain configuration so clients receive the correct full chain (root → intermediate → leaf) for svc-internal.corplabs.internal.

Validate from a client perspective that load balancer LB-EAST-02 now presents a non-expired certificate (new expiry 2026-12-10) and a complete chain, and confirm TLS handshakes succeed for dependent internal services. Verification performed from WORKSTATION-PC-MC (10.42.17.88) and WORKSTATION-LX-RP (10.42.18.203) in the Arlington office.

Restore certificate renewal monitoring and alerting on CA-EAST-01 for svc-internal.corplabs.internal, re-enable the 30-day expiry alert rule, configure notifications to infra-alerts@corplabs.com and lnguyen@corplabs.com, then test that certificate expiration warnings and renewal job failures generate notifications before the next renewal window.
agent_questions: Please confirm whether clients are failing on certificate expiry only or also reporting chain trust issues from the load balancer endpoint LB-EAST-02 for svc-internal.corplabs.internal. Maria Chen (mchen) reported the initial browser warnings from 10.42.17.88 — can the network team verify what the load balancer is actually presenting? Also, has anyone checked whether the renewal job on CA-EAST-01 ran successfully? — Raj Patel, Infrastructure Support

title: BitLocker recovery key escrow failed
description: My managed Windows 10 21H2 corporate laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, hostname mreeves-PC) was showing as noncompliant for disk encryption in the Endpoint Compliance portal even though Intune showed the BitLocker policy assigned to my device. Support found that the device — registered to my account mreeves@corplabs.com (EMP-40291) — did not have a recovery key visible in Azure AD/Intune escrow, and I was blocked by the compliance state mismatch until encryption status and key escrow were reconciled. My manager Diane Hollis flagged this during a routine compliance audit for the Dallas office Sales team.
observed_errors: Event log: BitLocker-API escrow upload failed (timeout)
root_cause: Initial BitLocker enablement partially succeeded on the device, but recovery key escrow to Azure AD/Intune failed during the first encryption attempt due to a transient escrow timeout. A later TPM protector initialization on the endpoint created conflicting local evidence, leaving cloud key inventory and compliance telemetry temporarily out of sync until the key was rotated, escrowed, and the device resynchronized.
resolution_steps: Verified the active BitLocker policy was assigned to device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR in Intune under the Dallas Sales device group and confirmed the device registered to mreeves (EMP-40291) had received the encryption configuration.

Rotated the local BitLocker recovery key on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and manually escrowed the current key to Azure AD/Intune from the endpoint under mreeves's session so support could confirm a valid recovery key record existed. Key rotation approved and executed by Kevin Osei (kosei).
Reinitialized the TPM protector on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and restarted BitLocker protection/encryption to correct the incomplete local protector state seen in event history from 2026-01-22T09:15:00Z.

Forced an Intune device sync from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (IP 10.42.18.77) and triggered a fresh compliance evaluation so encryption status and escrow inventory could be re-read by the Device Compliance Service.

Validated that the rotated recovery key was present in Azure AD under mreeves's device record and confirmed the device compliance state updated to Compliant after the final sync. Notified Marcus Reeves at mreeves@corplabs.com and manager Diane Hollis (dhollis@corplabs.com) that the incident was resolved, then closed the incident once telemetry aligned.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, we can see the BitLocker policy is assigned to your device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (IP 10.42.18.77), but the recovery key is missing from Azure AD/Intune. Can you confirm whether the laptop recently started encryption or showed any restart or encryption prompts? Cleared stored Windows Credential Manager entries related to the file server on WORKSTATION-FIN-LM (IP 10.42.18.97) to remove stale authentication prompts that were causing repeated credential dialogs for lmoretti.
Removed and remapped the \\fileserver01\Finance network drive using the current server path so the user lmoretti reconnected with updated credentials and token information on WORKSTATION-FIN-LM.

Reviewed server-side ACLs on the Finance folder, identified broken NTFS inheritance, and restored/realigned folder permissions to the standard inherited access model so group-based permissions applied consistently. title: Intermittent corporate Wi-Fi access denied after certificate update
description: Multiple managed Windows 10 and macOS 12 corporate laptops at the Denver office, Building A floors 3-4, can associate to the corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) but then receive no network access, no DHCP lease, and messages such as "Access denied by NAC" or authentication failure. observed_errors: Authentication failed - EAP TLS: certificate expired
No DHCP lease assigned after association
root_cause: Wireless 802.1X/NAC authentication failures were caused by the certificate rollover not being fully trusted by all managed endpoints and NAC/authentication chain components, leaving some devices with stale Wi-Fi profiles or unrefreshed client trust state after the controller/RADIUS certificate update.
resolution_steps: Validated and corrected the renewed wireless/RADIUS certificate chain presented by the controller so the full trust chain matched endpoint and NAC expectations after the rollover. Priya Nagarajan verified the intermediate CA was properly included in the chain.
Restarted wireless controller authentication services to ensure the updated certificate and chain were actively loaded for new client authentications.

Reviewed NAC authentication results and confirmed affected devices (LAPTOP-RTHORN-W10, MACBOOK-KOSEI-12, and others) were being denied during 802.1X/EAP-TLS evaluation rather than at DHCP or RF association stages.

Remediated impacted endpoints by refreshing the corporate Wi-Fi profile and re-enrolling device certificates on clients that still held stale trust or profile data after the rollover. Desktop support technician Luis Medina handled the on-site re-enrollment for floors 3-4.

Had affected users — including Rachel Thornton and Kevin Osei — forget and reconnect to the corporate SSID, then verified successful NAC authorization and IP assignment on previously failing devices. Both LAPTOP-RTHORN-W10 and MACBOOK-KOSEI-12 received valid DHCP leases and full network access.

title: Multiple devices marked noncompliant after stale policy reference in Intune
description: Multiple remote users on corporate Windows 10 21H2 devices across the Frankfurt and London offices were blocked from Exchange Online and SharePoint Online because Conditional Access evaluated their endpoints as noncompliant in Intune after a compliance policy change pushed by admin mkovacs the prior night (2025-12-26 ~22:00 UTC). Approximately 18 devices showed noncompliant status or stale compliance reporting in the Intune admin console, and the assigned compliance policy was still referencing the retired ComplianceBaseline_v1 baseline, preventing normal sign-in for affected users. Initial reports came from user Elena Brandt (ebrandt@corplabs.com) and several others in the EMEA RemoteWorkers group.
observed_errors: Conditional Access blocked sign-in: device not compliant
Compliance status not updating after policy change
root_cause: The Intune device compliance policy was left pointing to the deprecated ComplianceBaseline_v1 assignment after the recent policy update. Devices that had not checked in after the change were re-evaluated against a stale baseline reference, so encryption and related compliance signals were not refreshed correctly and Conditional Access denied access based on noncompliant state.
resolution_steps: Updated the Intune compliance policy to replace the deprecated ComplianceBaseline_v1 reference with ComplianceBaseline_v2 in the Intune admin center, verified by admin mkovacs and the service desk.

Triggered a forced device check-in via the Intune admin console for all 18 impacted endpoints in the EMEA-RemoteWorkers group so the corrected policy and current compliance signals were evaluated immediately against ComplianceBaseline_v2.

Reviewed the remaining four noncompliant devices (Lars Henriksen WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-LH, Amir Youssef WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-AY, Sofia Ruiz, Chen Wei) to identify the specific failing signals, which were pending BitLocker enablement on two devices and required Windows cumulative update KB5048652 on the other two.

Sent targeted remediation guidance via email to the four affected users (lhenriksen@corplabs.com, sruiz@corplabs.com, ayoussef@corplabs.com, cwei@corplabs.com) instructing them to enable BitLocker via Control Panel > System and Security, install pending Windows updates including KB5048652, and reboot their devices to complete remediation.

Verified that all 18 devices re-reported compliant status in the Intune admin console after policy refresh and user remediation, restoring Conditional Access eligibility for Exchange Online and SharePoint Online. Final confirmation received from Elena Brandt and Priya Nair that access was restored.

title: Multiple users stuck in MFA prompt loop
description: Multiple Finance and Sales users — including reports from Lisa Nguyen (EMP-40821) and Derek Holloway (EMP-33190) — were trying to access SaaS applications including Salesforce, Office365, and Concur through the SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) after the morning deploy window (06:30 UTC), but were trapped in a repeated MFA challenge loop. After the Okta Verify MFA prompt appeared, the challenge immediately failed or returned users to the prompt screen instead of completing sign-in. Okta and Azure AD sign-in activity showed repeated MFA challenge failures for the same sessions originating from the Charlotte office network (10.42.16.0/24), blocking access to business applications needed for normal work. Initial reports came in via the #identity-support Slack channel around 07:00 UTC.
observed_errors: Azure AD: AADSTS50076 - MFA is required but challenge failed
root_cause: A deprecated conditional access policy, 'Legacy-MFA-Bypass' (CAS-legacy-001), remained enabled after the deployment and still referenced a stale MFA enrollment mapping. For users who had recently re-enrolled their authenticator, the legacy policy evaluated outdated enrollment attributes, causing Okta and Azure AD MFA resolution to mismatch and loop the challenge instead of completing SSO.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Okta system log and Azure AD sign-in failures for affected users (lnguyen, dholloway, pkapoor) and confirmed the active legacy conditional access policy CAS-legacy-001 ('Legacy-MFA-Bypass') was being applied during MFA evaluation alongside the current 'MFA-Enforce-2025' policy, producing conflicting challenge outcomes.

Disabled the legacy Azure AD conditional access policy 'Legacy-MFA-Bypass' (CAS-legacy-001) in the Azure AD conditional access blade and aligned affected access flows for Finance-SaaS-Access and Sales-SaaS-Access groups to the current 'MFA-Enforce-2025' policy exclusively. Change approved by Marcus Webb and documented under CHG-2026-0412.

Reset MFA enrollment state for impacted user accounts (lnguyen, dholloway, pkapoor, and 14 additional affected users identified in the Charlotte office) in Okta where recent authenticator re-enrollment during the March 2026 factor migration had left stale factor mappings referencing the deprecated mfaEnrollmentLegacy attribute.

Forced affected users to re-register their current Okta Verify authenticator and verified device clock and timezone synchronization (UTC offset confirmed correct) on workstations WORKSTATION-LN2041 and WORKSTATION-DH3319 before retesting sign-in. All re-enrolled users completed MFA successfully on first attempt.

Validated successful SSO access for a pilot group of 5 users including lnguyen and dholloway across the SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) and downstream applications (Salesforce, Office365, Concur), then confirmed broader login recovery for all 17 affected Charlotte users before closing the incident.
agent_questions: Hi Lisa — can you confirm whether the MFA prompt loops across multiple SaaS apps (Salesforce, Office365, Concur) from the SSO portal at https://sso.corplabs.com, and whether this began after the 06:30 UTC morning deployment window? Also, please let us know whether you're seeing this on your workstation WORKSTATION-LN2041 or on other devices as well. We're checking whether this is isolated to your team or broader. — Marcus Webb, Identity Support

title: Internal hostname resolves to stale IP
description: Multiple internal clients and dependent services were trying to reach api.internal.corp by hostname, but name resolution intermittently returned an outdated address (10.0.1.23) or NXDOMAIN while the service remained reachable directly by IP at 10.0.2.47. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) on the Platform Engineering team around 2026-01-11 09:12 UTC, and subsequently confirmed by additional users across the Austin and Charlotte offices. It affected internal DNS resolution across multiple subnets (10.0.1.0/24, 10.0.3.0/24, 10.0.5.0/24) and blocked application-to-application connectivity for services relying on the internal resolver dns-resolver01.internal.corp, including the Internal API and Service Registry.
observed_errors: nslookup returned stale A record 10.0.1.23 for api.internal.corp
DNS lookup timeouts 100-200ms observed in monitoring probes
root_cause: Primary internal DNS resolver cached a stale A record for api.internal.corp while the internal DNS zone still contained an outdated record/TTL combination, causing clients to receive old or inconsistent answers until the resolver cache and zone data were corrected.
resolution_steps: Flushed the DNS cache on dns-resolver01.internal.corp using 'rndc flushname api.internal.corp' to remove the stale cached A record (10.0.1.23) being served to internal clients across the Austin and Charlotte offices.

Removed the outdated A record (10.0.1.23) for api.internal.corp from the Internal DNS Zone on ns-auth01.internal.corp, updated it to the current address 10.0.2.47, and reloaded the zone via rndc reload so authoritative data matched the current service address.

Validated name resolution by querying the resolver and authoritative path from multiple subnets (10.0.3.0/24, 10.0.5.0/24) with nslookup from WORKSTATION-PC-MD and WORKSTATION-LT-PN to confirm the hostname api.internal.corp returned the current address 10.0.2.47 consistently.

Temporarily lowered the record TTL from 86400 to 300 seconds in the zone file on ns-auth01.internal.corp to reduce cache persistence during stabilization and future record updates, with a plan to raise to 3600 after one week.

Monitored network DNS probes via Network Monitoring dashboards and service reachability checks for 2 hours after the change, with Kevin Marsh confirming lookup stability from all monitored subnets and no further stale responses for api.internal.corp.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please test api.internal.corp from an affected client (e.g. your workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD) with nslookup against dns-resolver01.internal.corp and confirm whether the service works by direct IP at 10.0.2.47 at the same time. Also, can you confirm if colleagues in your subnet are seeing the same behavior? Please send results to dns-ops@corplabs.com.

title: BitLocker protection not enabled
description: User Elisa Marchetti (emp ID EMP-40821) reported that her corporate Windows 10 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-EM) was showing noncompliant in Intune for required disk encryption. BitLocker protection was off, no recovery key was visible in Azure AD for the device, and the endpoint remained in a pending compliance state, blocking fulfillment of the organization's encryption requirement for the managed endpoint. The user is based in the Frankfurt office and contacted the service desk after receiving a Company Portal notification about the noncompliance.
root_cause: BitLocker could not complete enablement because the TPM protector was not initialized, preventing encryption startup and recovery key escrow to Azure AD.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the device TPM state on WORKSTATION-DELL-EM using Get-Tpm and initialized the TPM protector via Initialize-Tpm and manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm so BitLocker could create the required hardware-backed protector.

Started BitLocker encryption on the C: drive of WORKSTATION-DELL-EM using manage-bde -on C: after TPM readiness was established, and verified protection status began transitioning from Off to On (EncryptionPercentage climbing).

Forced Intune policy assignment refresh on WORKSTATION-DELL-EM and initiated a device sync via Company Portal so the active disk encryption configuration 'Corp Endpoint BitLocker - EMEA' was reapplied without delay.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key using manage-bde -protectors -delete C: -type RecoveryPassword followed by manage-bde -protectors -add C: -rp, then escrowed the current recovery key to Azure AD via BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector. Verified the key was present for support retrieval under emarchetti's device record.

Validated that BitLocker protection reported On for WORKSTATION-DELL-EM (manage-bde -status C: showing FullyEncrypted, Protection On) and that the device compliance state in Intune updated to compliant for disk encryption. Notified Elisa Marchetti at emarchetti@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Elisa, I confirmed that Intune shows your device WORKSTATION-DELL-EM (IP 10.47.83.112) as pending for encryption compliance and BitLocker protection is currently off. The device is enrolled under your account emarchetti@corplabs.com. Please reboot the laptop and let me know when you are back in so I can retry TPM and encryption checks. — Tobias Richter, Endpoint Support

title: BitLocker not enabling and recovery key not escrowed on sales laptop
description: User Marcus Delgado (emp ID: E-40291) reported that his corporate Windows 10 Enterprise sales laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD) was flagged noncompliant for device encryption in Intune. BitLocker showed the C: system drive as not encrypted, and the Azure AD device record for the machine did not contain an escrowed recovery key. The device, located at the Charlotte office, had synced recently from IP 10.42.18.77, but local BitLocker and TPM-related events indicated encryption could not start because the TPM protector was not provisioned, blocking both encryption enablement and recovery key backup.
observed_errors: TPM owner not found - protector initialization failed
Intune compliance: Encryption requirement not met
Azure AD: No recovery key found for device
root_cause: The device TPM protector was not initialized/provisioned, so BitLocker could not create its startup protector, encryption never began, and the recovery key could not be escrowed to Azure AD during initial policy application.
resolution_steps: Verified the laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (user: mdelgado, IP 10.42.18.77) had a TPM chip present and available in Device Manager, then confirmed BitLocker initialization was failing because no TPM-based protector had been successfully provisioned — 'manage-bde -protectors -get C:' returned no protectors.

Initialized and provisioned the TPM protector on the device by running 'Initialize-Tpm' via elevated PowerShell and then 'manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm', then rechecked BitLocker status to confirm the prerequisite for encryption was now healthy. Agent Priya Nair (pnair) performed this step remotely.

Started BitLocker encryption on the C: operating system volume using the TPM protector ('manage-bde -on C:') and monitored the device until encryption status moved from NotEncrypted to 'Encryption in Progress' and then to 'Fully Encrypted' on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD.

Forced an Intune device sync via Company Portal on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD after encryption initialization so the current recovery key could be backed up to Azure AD and the latest compliance evaluation could run against the 'Sales-Encryption-Win10' policy.

Confirmed the 48-digit recovery key was visible in Azure AD under the device record for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD and verified the Intune compliance state for user mdelgado (E-40291) updated to 'Compliant' reflecting the encryption requirement was now met.

Reapplied the assigned BitLocker policy 'Sales-Encryption-Win10' to ensure the endpoint WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD remained aligned with the required encryption configuration going forward. Notified Marcus Delgado at mdelgado@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, please open Company Portal on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD and trigger a manual sync from Settings > Device status, then confirm whether BitLocker still shows the C: drive as not encrypted on the laptop. Also, could you check under Device Security > Security Processor whether the TPM shows any warnings? You can reach me at x4418 or helpdesk-endpoint@corplabs.com if you have questions.

title: Users stuck in MFA prompt loop
description: Multiple users in the Sales group — initially reported by Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com) and confirmed by at least four other reps in the Dallas office — were trying to access Salesforce and Office365 through the Okta SSO portal (https://sso.corplabs.com), but after completing MFA via Okta Verify they were returned to the login page and prompted again instead of reaching the application. root_cause: Okta sign-on policy was still referencing deprecated 'Legacy MFA Policy v1', which caused a mismatch between current user MFA enrollments and the policy-required factor flow, resulting in repeated MFA_REQUIRED events followed by rejected sign-in assertions.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the affected Okta sign-on rule and removed the stale reference to 'Legacy MFA Policy v1', replacing it with the active 'MFA Policy v2' mapping. Change executed by Marcus Webb (mwebb) and verified in the Okta admin console.

title: Integration Gateway - Nightly sync API timeouts (Billing API)
description: Nightly data synchronization from the Integration Gateway to the external Billing API began failing around 02:30 UTC on 2025-12-12 in us-east-1. The integration service account (svc-billing-sync) running on gateway node intgw-prod-east-04 reported multiple jobs receiving 504 Gateway Timeout responses and 30-second request timeouts, causing retries to accumulate and some sync jobs to fail outright. Reported by Marcus Delgado (emp ID EMP-40821) from the Denver application support team. This blocked completion of the scheduled billing data sync until the downstream service recovered and the retry backlog was cleared.
observed_errors: Request to billing API timed out after 30s
root_cause: Elevated latency and upstream instability in the external Billing API caused repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses during the nightly sync window, which exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout and exhausted the configured retry/backoff policy.
resolution_steps: Correlated Integration Gateway failures on intgw-prod-east-04 with Monitoring System alerts (alert ID MON-88412) showing repeated 504 responses and increased downstream billing-service latency (p99 spiking to 45–60s) between approximately 02:28 and 02:40 UTC. Cross-referenced X-Request-Id values req-a83f21c4, req-b90e55d7, req-c12d88a1 to confirm the correlation.

Collected gateway log evidence from intgw-prod-east-04, including timestamped request identifiers and upstream timeout behavior, and Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) escalated the incident to the external Billing API provider contact at billing-ops@externalpay.io for remediation, attaching the evidence package and Monitoring System snapshots.

Coordinated with the downstream provider on a service restart/recovery action to restore normal responsiveness on the billing side. Provider confirmed recovery at approximately 02:52 UTC and attributed the degradation to an internal database connection pool exhaustion.

Adjusted Integration Gateway retry settings on intgw-prod-east-04 by increasing retry attempts from 3 to 5 and extending backoff windows from 10s/20s/30s to 15s/30s/60s/90s/120s so transient upstream latency would be tolerated during recovery. Change approved by team lead Raj Venkatesh (rvenkatesh, EMP-30195).

Validated that API calls from svc-billing-sync were succeeding again with sub-3-second response times, reran the 47 queued nightly sync jobs, and confirmed the retry backlog cleared without further 504 timeout failures by 03:15 UTC.

Documented the escalation path (internal → Priya Nair → billing-ops@externalpay.io), log-correlation approach using X-Request-Id tracing, and revised retry/backoff settings for future nightly sync timeout events. Added runbook entry RB-INT-0064 for the Denver application support team.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether gateway logs on intgw-prod-east-04 around 02:30 UTC show upstream 504 responses from the Billing API endpoint and share any request IDs or X-Request-Id values (e.g., from the svc-billing-sync service account logs) so we can correlate with the downstream billing alerts. Also, can you verify whether the issue is isolated to your workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD or visible across the monitoring dashboard? — Priya Nair, Integration Support

title: Users experience MFA prompt loop during SSO (Okta/Azure AD)
description: Multiple external contractor users were trying to sign in through the SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) to access Salesforce and Office365, but after completing Okta MFA they were returned to the MFA challenge again instead of reaching the application landing page. Corrected the Azure AD Conditional Access group mapping so the recently synced contractor access group 'CG-External-East' supplied the expected group claim during SSO evaluation, ensuring Okta could properly validate contractor group membership for application access policies.

Resynced Azure AD group membership to Okta via Azure AD Connect to refresh policy scope and ensure all 12 affected contractor users in the Arlington office were associated with the proper access group and claim configuration.

Reset MFA enrollment and cleared stale session state for two impacted users — rdelgado (EMP-40821) and kchan (EMP-40837) — to remove invalid challenge loops created before the mapping correction. Both users re-enrolled via Okta Verify successfully.

Validated the fix with test user mwilliams (EMP-40845) from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MW and then confirmed all 12 impacted contractor accounts, verifying successful SSO completion and restored access to Salesforce and Office365 without repeated MFA prompts. title: BitLocker not enabling
description: My corporate Windows 10 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, asset tag SLS-4821) remained noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune. root_cause: BitLocker enablement was initiated before TPM protection was fully initialized, so the device entered a partial or conflicting encryption state and the recovery key escrow operation to the management service timed out. Intune policy assignment was present, but compliance remained noncompliant until TPM protector initialization, encryption start, and recovery key escrow were completed and verified.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM readiness on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and initialized the TPM-based BitLocker protector so the device had a valid hardware-backed protector before retrying encryption. Confirmed via manage-bde -protectors -get C: that the TPM protector was active.

Started BitLocker encryption again on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR after TPM initialization to move the endpoint out of the prior conflicting state where policy had applied but encryption and escrow were incomplete. manage-bde -on C: completed without error.

Forced an Intune device sync for mreeves (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, IP 10.22.47.115) and re-applied the assigned disk encryption policy 'Corp-BitLocker-Encrypt-v3' so the endpoint could process the current BitLocker configuration and compliance evaluation.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and retried escrow to the management service, then verified that the recovery key record became visible to support under the mreeves device object in Azure AD.

Confirmed the endpoint WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR reported encrypted status and allowed time for compliance evaluation to refresh until Intune no longer showed EncryptionNotEnabled or missing escrow for user mreeves. Notified Marcus Reeves at mreeves@corplabs.com that the device is now compliant.

title: Internal hostname resolving to stale address from DNS resolver
description: Multiple internal users in the Austin office were trying to reach service.internal.example.com from the internal application path, but the hostname resolved to an outdated IP address (172.16.10.45) instead of the current internal service endpoint (172.16.10.78). This was initially reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) via the Network Monitoring dashboard after the internal-frontend application began throwing connection timeouts. The issue caused name-based connectivity failures for the affected application and prevented normal access to the internal service from corp-dc-1. Network investigation by the on-call engineer confirmed a mismatch between the internal resolver cache on dns-resolver-01.corp.internal and the authoritative internal DNS zone hosted on ns-auth-01.corp.internal.
observed_errors: resolver returned stale A record (172.16.10.45) while authoritative answer is 172.16.10.78
mismatched DNS responses between resolver and authoritative zone
root_cause: Internal DNS resolver cache retained and served a stale A record for service.internal.example.com (172.16.10.45) instead of the authoritative current address (172.16.10.78).
resolution_steps: Queried service.internal.example.com on the internal resolver dns-resolver-01.corp.internal from client WORKSTATION-PC-RN (10.42.16.93, Rachel Nguyen) and confirmed it was returning the stale cached A record 172.16.10.45 rather than the current authoritative address.

Verified the authoritative internal DNS zone record on ns-auth-01.corp.internal for service.internal.example.com was correctly set to 172.16.10.78 (serial 2026010401) and reviewed TTL guidance for the record (currently 86400s).

Cleared the stale cached entry on the internal DNS resolver dns-resolver-01.corp.internal using rndc flush to force fresh resolution from the authoritative source. Executed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado).

Retested DNS lookups against the internal resolver from both WORKSTATION-PC-RN (10.42.16.93) and WORKSTATION-LT-KP (10.42.16.107) and confirmed subsequent responses returned the authoritative A record 172.16.10.78.

Validated that the dependent internal-frontend application could again reach the internal endpoint by hostname — Rachel Nguyen and Kevin Park both confirmed restored access. Recommended lowering TTL to 3600s and enabling Network Monitoring alerts for resolver-authoritative mismatches on critical internal zones to reduce recurrence.

Retested name resolution for svc-db.corp.internal from multiple affected application servers including WORKSTATION-BKND-MD (mdelgado) and WORKSTATION-BKND-RL (rlewis) and confirmed consistent return of the current IP 10.22.9.140.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: Multiple users in the Sales team at the Frankfurt office, working on corporate-managed Windows 10 laptops, reported being unable to maintain GlobalProtect VPN connectivity while working remotely. The VPN session established successfully and Okta MFA push approval completed without error, but the tunnel disconnected within approximately 20-40 seconds post-authentication. Internal applications including Salesforce, Confluence, and the corporate intranet (intranet.corplabs.com) became unreachable immediately after disconnection. The issue was initially reported by Elena Richter (emp ID E-40291) and confirmed across several other Sales endpoints. Investigation traced the failure to post-authentication TLS teardown on endpoints with expired device certificates issued by the Device Certificate Service, affecting certificate-based conditional access validation on the GlobalProtect gateway gw-emea-01.corplabs.net.
observed_errors: TLS session teardown after successful MFA
Device certificate validation failed: certificate expired
root_cause: Expired device certificate on managed endpoints caused certificate validation failure during post-MFA TLS validation, which triggered GlobalProtect tunnel teardown shortly after successful Okta authentication.
resolution_steps: Issue and deploy replacement device certificates to affected managed endpoints (starting with WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-ER for erichter and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH for mhahn) through the Device Certificate Service, coordinated by Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) on the certificate team.

Verify the renewed device certificate is present on each endpoint (e.g., confirm CN=WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-ER in the local machine certificate store), confirm it is not expired, and ensure it is correctly associated with the active machine identity used for VPN conditional access on gw-emea-01.corplabs.net.

Refresh or republish the GlobalProtect VPN profile on affected devices so the client picks up the current certificate and policy configuration. Network Support (Tomasz Kowalski, tkowalski) to push updated profiles to all impacted Sales EMEA endpoints in the Frankfurt region.

Have impacted users (erichter, mhahn, and other affected Sales team members) reconnect to GlobalProtect and, where needed, re-enroll the device certificate through the Device Certificate Service portal before retrying VPN access.

Validate Conditional Access group assignments for the Sales EMEA user group and confirm the VPN tunnel remains established after Okta MFA on representative affected devices including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-ER (erichter) and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH (mhahn). Monitor gw-emea-01.corplabs.net logs for 24 hours to ensure no further session_end code 0x2A events.

title: Account locked after repeated failed sign-ins
description: I (Marcus Delgado, employee ID EMP-90214) was trying to sign in to corporate resources through the SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com from my personal iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) while working from the Austin office, but repeated failed sign-ins caused my Active Directory account (mdelgado) to become locked. I then could not access either SSO or the Password Reset Portal and received an "Account locked due to failed logins" message, blocking account recovery and normal access.
observed_errors: Account locked due to failed logins
root_cause: Active Directory lockout policy was triggered by repeated authentication failures from an iOS mobile device that continued submitting cached or expired credentials to SSO-connected services.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the account lockout details in Active Directory on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and confirmed 11 recent failed sign-in attempts (Event ID 4740) for account mdelgado were originating from the user's iOS device WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD at IP 10.47.83.112.
Unlocked the user's AD account (CN=mdelgado,OU=Corp Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) and cleared the lockout condition so authentication could proceed again.
Issued a fresh password reset token (PRX-881204) through the Password Reset Portal and confirmed user Marcus Delgado could complete the password reset flow successfully.
Instructed the user to remove cached credentials from WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD and re-authenticate on the mobile SSO client and related apps to stop stale password submissions from IP 10.47.83.112.

Documented the originating device IP 10.47.83.112 (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) for follow-up monitoring and advised Marcus Delgado to contact Identity Support at identity-support@corplabs.com if additional lockouts occur.

title: Print jobs stuck on server PS-PRINT01
description: Multiple office users in the Columbus branch were trying to print to the shared main office HP LaserJet 4250 printer through print server PS-PRINT01, but submitted jobs remained stuck in the queue and the printer appeared offline. Client systems reported driver unavailable or spooler timeout behavior, preventing normal document printing. The issue was first reported by Karen Ostrowski (kostrowski, EMP-40218) from her workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-KO at 10.47.22.85. The issue was isolated to the server-hosted printer queue and driver package on Windows Server 2019, with queue processing hanging during spooler activity.
observed_errors: EventID 7011: Service timeout while waiting for Print Spooler
root_cause: Corrupt HP printer driver package on PS-PRINT01 caused Print Spooler instability, queue processing failures, and client driver unavailable errors.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the affected shared printer queues on PS-PRINT01 and confirmed 23 jobs were accumulating in a spooling state while the printer showed offline to clients across the Columbus office, including submissions from kostrowski, mjennings, and dpham.
Removed the corrupted HP driver package (v5.6.0.2341) from the Windows Server 2019 print server and reinstalled the approved HP Universal Print Driver v5.8 package per the standard driver catalog.

Cleared all stuck jobs from the impacted print queues and restarted the Print Spooler service after the driver refresh. Notified affected users Karen Ostrowski and Marcus Jennings that their pending jobs would need to be resubmitted.

Remapped the affected printer queues to the refreshed HP Universal Print Driver v5.8 package to ensure the queues were bound to the correct server driver. Confirmed queue binding via Printer Management Console.

Validated successful test prints from multiple client machines including WORKSTATION-DELL-KO (kostrowski) and WORKSTATION-HP-MJ (mjennings), and confirmed the spooler remained responsive with no further queue hang behavior. Diane Pham (dpham) also confirmed printing restored at 20:05 UTC.
agent_questions: Hi Karen — please confirm whether all users printing through PS-PRINT01 are seeing jobs stuck in queue or driver unavailable errors, and whether the printer appears offline from their PCs. Can you also verify if users on the 3rd floor like Marcus Jennings (mjennings) are affected as well?

title: Corporate laptop not showing BitLocker enabled
description: User Marcus Delgado (EMP-40291) reported that his recently Autopilot-provisioned corporate Windows 10 Enterprise 21H2 laptop (hostname LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7) showed BitLocker as Off and was marked noncompliant in Microsoft Intune for device encryption. The device (IP 10.42.17.83) had no recovery key escrowed in Azure AD, so the endpoint could not reach required encryption compliance after provisioning. A manual Intune sync had already been attempted by Marcus without creating a recovery key or changing compliance state. The user is based in the Charlotte office and needs the laptop compliant for an upcoming client engagement.
observed_errors: No recovery key found in Azure AD for device
root_cause: BitLocker could not complete enablement because the TPM protector was not initialized on the device after provisioning, which prevented creation of a valid protector and blocked recovery key escrow to Azure AD.
resolution_steps: Validated that the TPM was present and available on LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 (IP 10.42.17.83) via tpm.msc and Get-Tpm, then reviewed BitLocker state with manage-bde -status C: to confirm encryption was still off and no usable protector had been established for user mdelgado's device.

Cleared residual or incomplete protector state using manage-bde -protectors -delete C: and initialized the TPM-based BitLocker protector locally on LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 by running Initialize-Tpm followed by manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm. Desktop support engineer Diana Kwan (dkwan) performed this step remotely.

Re-applied the corporate BitLocker configuration (Corp-Encryption-Win10-Standard) from Intune so LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 received the expected TPM protector and encryption settings, including the recovery key escrow directive targeting Azure AD.

Forced an Intune device sync on LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 via Company Portal and verified that BitLocker started properly on the C: drive and generated a recovery key for the endpoint. manage-bde -status C: confirmed 'Encryption in Progress' with TPM protector active.

Confirmed the recovery key was escrowed to Azure AD under the device record for LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 and then verified Intune compliance updated from 'Encryption not enabled' to Compliant. Notified Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) at the Charlotte office that the device was now fully compliant and the ticket could be closed.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, please confirm whether BitLocker shows Off locally on LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 and whether this device was recently Autopilot-provisioned. We also need to know if a recovery key appears in Azure AD for the device. Could you also verify the device is connected to the corporate network so we can run remote diagnostics? You can reach me at x4418 or dkwan@corplabs.com if you need to follow up offline.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: I was trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from my managed Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-LT-MKOVACS) while working remotely from Budapest. Okta MFA approval succeeded using my account mkovacs@corplabs.com, but the VPN tunnel disconnected immediately afterward, leaving internal applications such as the HR Portal, Confluence, and Jira unreachable. I tried re-authentication, client restart, full reboot, and a local VPN profile refresh — none of these restored access. My employee ID is E-40291 and my username is mkovacs. My direct manager Petra Lindgren suggested I open a ticket.
root_cause: Expired device client certificate on the endpoint caused the GlobalProtect TLS tunnel to terminate immediately after successful Okta MFA.
resolution_steps: Verified the endpoint device certificate (CN=mkovacs,OU=Corp Devices,DC=corplabs,DC=internal, serial 4A:7C:91:E3:00:2B) used for GlobalProtect authentication on WORKSTATION-LT-MKOVACS was expired as of 2026-03-18 and no longer valid for tunnel establishment.

Renewed the device certificate through the Device Certificate Service for user mkovacs (employee ID E-40291) and marked the renewed certificate (new expiry 2027-04-18) as the active client certificate in the corplabs device enrollment portal.

Pushed the updated certificate to the managed Windows endpoint WORKSTATION-LT-MKOVACS at IP 86.101.44.17 and completed re-enrollment to ensure the client received the valid certificate chain. Confirmed certificate installation via certlm.msc on the device.

Refreshed the GlobalProtect VPN profile on WORKSTATION-LT-MKOVACS and cleared stale profile state from %ProgramData%\Palo Alto Networks\GlobalProtect so the client would present the renewed certificate on next connection attempt.

Retested the VPN connection for mkovacs after Okta MFA approval and confirmed the tunnel remained established with a stable session to gp-emea.corplabs.com. Internal applications including Jira, Confluence, and the HR Portal were all reachable. Márton Kovács confirmed full access restored.
agent_questions: Hi Márton, thanks for reaching out. Please retry the GlobalProtect connection from your device at IP 86.101.44.17 and confirm whether the disconnect happens before MFA, during MFA, or immediately after the Okta approval completes. Also, can you confirm you're connecting to the gp-emea.corplabs.com gateway?

title: VPN disconnects immediately

My username is mkowalski and after approving the Okta MFA push notification, the VPN session established briefly but disconnected within about 30 seconds, leaving internal applications such as the HR Portal, Jira, and Confluence completely unreachable. title: Print jobs stuck on PS-PRINT-02 — driver unavailable
description: Multiple users were trying to print to the shared Office-Color-34 queue on print server PS-PRINT-02, but jobs remained stuck at 0% and some workstations showed the printer as Offline. The issue was first reported by Diana Kowalski (emp ID EMP-40821) at the Columbus office, who called the service desk at (614) 555-0193 after her print jobs failed. The issue began shortly after a morning driver push, blocking normal office printing for shared users. Print Management on PS-PRINT-02 showed the queue paused and the driver unavailable, indicating the server could not load the assigned HP Universal driver package.
observed_errors: Driver failed to load for queue 'Office-Color-34'
Jobs stuck at 0% and queue paused
root_cause: A corrupt or failed HP Universal driver update on PS-PRINT-02 left the Office-Color-34 queue mapped to a driver package that could not load, causing Print Spooler instability, paused queue state, and stale queued jobs.
resolution_steps: Removed the failed or unavailable HP Universal driver association from the Office-Color-34 queue on PS-PRINT-02 and installed the approved driver package (v6.8.4) from the central repository. Verified by agent Nathan Carr (ncarr).
Cleared 14 stuck and corrupted print jobs from the Office-Color-34 queue so pending jobs would not continue to reference the bad driver state. Notified affected users including dkowalski and bholt.
Restarted the Print Spooler service on PS-PRINT-02 and confirmed the service remained stable after the driver package was corrected. Monitored for 15 minutes with no further crashes.

Remapped the Office-Color-34 queue to the reinstalled approved HP Universal driver and verified the queue returned from paused/offline behavior to normal availability. Workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MR and WORKSTATION-DT-BH both showed the printer as Online.
Submitted multiple test print jobs from dkowalski (10.42.18.77) and mreeves (WORKSTATION-PC-MR) and confirmed they progressed beyond 0% and completed successfully for affected users.
agent_questions: Please confirm whether all jobs to Office-Color-34 are stuck at 0% and whether the printer shows Offline on affected PCs after this morning's driver push. Diana Kowalski (dkowalski) reported the issue from the Columbus office — can you verify if other users on the same floor are impacted as well?

title: Internal hostname service.example.local intermittent DNS failures — resolved
description: Users and the internal application team were trying to reach the internal service at service.example.local from application instances in the Newark data center, but beginning around 08:30 UTC on 2026-01-10 name-based access became intermittent. Some clients received NXDOMAIN responses while others resolved an outdated A record (10.42.8.17 instead of the current 10.42.12.55), even though direct connectivity to the service IP 10.42.12.55 still worked. The issue affected a subset of internal application hosts (including APPHOST-NWK-04 and APPHOST-NWK-07) and disrupted application communication that depended on DNS rather than hard-coded IP access. Reported initially by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, E-40291) from the application operations team.
observed_errors: dig +short service.example.local returned stale A record (old IP)
application DNS lookup timeout and name resolution failure
root_cause: A delayed update in the internal DNS zone left ResolverA serving a stale cached A record with an elevated TTL, causing intermittent responses of either an outdated IP or NXDOMAIN for service.example.local until the cache and zone data were corrected.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone entry for service.example.local on DNS-ZONE-EAST.corplabs.internal and identified that the published record state (10.42.8.17, TTL 7200s) did not match the address expected by affected application clients (10.42.12.55).

Updated the A record in the internal DNS zone on DNS-ZONE-EAST.corplabs.internal to the correct current IP address 10.42.12.55 and reduced the record TTL from 7200 seconds to 300 seconds to limit stale cache persistence.
Flushed the cached entry on DNS-RES-01.corplabs.internal (ResolverA) via rndc flush so the resolver would stop serving the outdated response (10.42.8.17) immediately.

Verified that resolver cluster members (DNS-RES-01.corplabs.internal and DNS-RES-02.corplabs.internal) were returning the corrected record (10.42.12.55) consistently after the zone update and cache flush. Priya Nair (pnair) confirmed via dig queries from the Newark NOC.

Tested name resolution from affected application hosts APPHOST-NWK-04 and APPHOST-NWK-07 and confirmed that service.example.local resolved to the current IP 10.42.12.55 without further NXDOMAIN or stale-record responses. Kevin Ortiz (kortiz) validated application connectivity was fully restored.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failure for internal service
description: Developers on the platform engineering team (reported by Marcus Delgado, emp ID E-20487) were trying to reach service.internal.corp for internal-service-api and the developer portal from the Austin and Raleigh office locations, but name resolution from internal resolver 10.1.1.10 intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or timed out. Direct queries to the authoritative DNS server dns-auth-01.internal.corp returned the expected A record (10.40.16.55), so users were blocked by inconsistent internal DNS responses rather than a missing service record. Impact was cross-site and intermittent, affecting access to internal endpoints and application connectivity. Initial report came in via Slack from mdelgado@corplabs.com.
root_cause: Resolver 10.1.1.10 had an internal DNS forwarding/cache issue for the internal zone: the authoritative server held the correct A record for service.internal.corp, but the resolver intermittently served NXDOMAIN or timed-out responses until conditional forwarder behavior and cached zone data were corrected.
resolution_steps: Validated that the authoritative DNS server dns-auth-01.internal.corp (10.1.1.30) for the internal zone returned the expected A record for service.internal.corp (10.40.16.55, TTL 300) and confirmed the issue was isolated to recursive resolver 10.1.1.10 behavior rather than a missing zone record. Verification performed by Raj Venkatesh from the Raleigh network monitoring host.

Reviewed and corrected the conditional forwarder path for the internal zone on resolver 10.1.1.10 — removed stale secondary forwarder target 10.1.1.22 (decommissioned) so queries for service.internal.corp consistently routed only to the valid authoritative DNS server dns-auth-01.internal.corp (10.1.1.30).

Cleared stale cached entries and negative cache data (rndc flush) on the affected internal resolver 10.1.1.10 after the forwarder configuration was corrected, ensuring no residual NXDOMAIN responses persisted from the decommissioned target.

Retested repeated lookups for service.internal.corp from the affected resolver and from multiple client locations — including Marcus Delgado's workstation WORKSTATION-MBP-MD (10.22.4.117, Austin) and Priya Nair's machine WORKSTATION-LNX-PN (Raleigh) — to confirm the resolver now returned 10.40.16.55 consistently without NXDOMAIN or timeout responses. 100/100 queries succeeded.

Monitored resolver and DNS query behavior via Network Monitoring dashboards for 2 hours after the change to verify timeout spikes stopped and internal applications (internal-service-api, developer-portal) could consistently resolve the service endpoint. Confirmed with Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) that CI/CD pipeline and portal access were fully restored.

title: Software Center installation blocked by Endpoint Protection policy
description: I was trying to install Adobe Acrobat Pro DC from Software Center on my corporate Windows 10 21H2 laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR), but the installer was blocked during deployment with error 0x87D00324 and a policy check failure. The application briefly appeared and then disappeared from Software Center after the failed attempt, preventing me from completing the required software installation for a client presentation. Review of the managed device in Intune indicated the installer had been flagged by Endpoint Protection. My employee ID is E50823 and I'm based out of the Portland office. Please advise — I need this resolved before end of day.
observed_errors: Installation blocked by Endpoint Protection policy
root_cause: Endpoint Protection policy flagged and blocked the approved application installer on the managed endpoint, causing Software Center policy validation to fail and the deployment to disappear after the failed attempt.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the managed device record for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (user mreeves, IP 10.42.17.89) in Intune and confirmed the Software Center deployment of Adobe Acrobat Pro DC was failing with behavior consistent with an Endpoint Protection enforcement block (error 0x87D00324).

Checked the security status for the endpoint WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and identified that the application installer AcroProDC_2300120093.msi had been flagged by Endpoint Protection during the install attempt initiated by mreeves.

Updated the Endpoint Protection allowlist/approval entry for the Adobe Acrobat Pro DC installer (AcroProDC_2300120093.msi) so the approved package was no longer blocked by policy on the device. Change approved by security analyst Priya Desai.

Triggered a manual Intune device inventory and policy refresh for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR so the endpoint received the updated security and application management state. Confirmed policy sync completed at approximately 09:42 UTC.

Had Marcus Reeves retry the installation of Adobe Acrobat Pro DC from Software Center after policy refresh and verified the application remained visible and completed installation successfully on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR without further Endpoint Protection blocks.

title: Print jobs stuck on print-server-02 after driver update
description: Corporate Office users in the Newark location were trying to print to the shared queue PrinterQueue-Corp on print-server-02 after an overnight printer driver deployment pushed by the Workplace Services team. Submitted jobs from multiple users, including Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40291) in Accounting and Derek Huang (dhuang) in Legal, remained stuck in a printing state for over three hours. Users received a 'driver unavailable' message when attempting to print, preventing normal printing to shared office printers across multiple departments on the 4th and 5th floors.
root_cause: A corrupted HP Universal PCL6 driver package deployed to print-server-02 caused the Windows Print Spooler to fail loading the driver for PrinterQueue-Corp, leaving submitted jobs stuck in the queue.
resolution_steps: Reviewed PrinterQueue-Corp on print-server-02 and cleared the backlog of 47 stuck print jobs submitted by users including mgonzalez, dhuang, and pnair so the queue could be reset cleanly.
Restarted the Windows Print Spooler service on print-server-02 to release locked queue entries and reset driver load state. Confirmed spooler PID recycled and service returned to running status.

Removed the corrupted HP Universal PCL6 driver package (v7.1.0.25054) from the server driver store on print-server-02 after spooler logs showed 312 repeated driver load failures with error 0x80070643 since the overnight deployment.

Installed the approved HP Universal PCL6 driver package (v7.0.0.24980) from the internal repository at \\pkg-repo-east\drivers\hp-upcl6 and re-associated PrinterQueue-Corp with the restored driver. Verified driver load succeeded without errors in the spooler log.

Submitted validation print jobs through the shared queue from WORKSTATION-PC-MG (mgonzalez, 10.42.16.88) and WORKSTATION-PC-DH (dhuang, 10.42.16.92) and confirmed jobs completed successfully within seconds without further 'driver unavailable' errors. Notified affected users Maria Gonzalez, Derek Huang, and Priya Nair via email that printing services were restored.

title: Laptop slow after login
description: My Windows 10 Dell Latitude 5490 (hostname WORKSTATION-DL5490-MR, IP 10.47.83.112) becomes very slow within 5-10 minutes after login. I'm logged in as mramirez (employee ID EMP-20418) and the issue started around Monday morning. File Explorer, Outlook, and Chrome take roughly 20-40 seconds to open, and CPU usage rises to 80-100% in Task Manager, preventing normal post-login work. The issue is isolated to my laptop and was traced to endpoint protection activity starting multiple queued scans and pending definition update tasks at login. I'm based out of the Portland office in the Sales group.
root_cause: endpoint protection scan backlog
resolution_steps: Reviewed active endpoint protection tasks on WORKSTATION-DL5490-MR for user mramirez and identified multiple queued scans (4 deferred quick scans from 2026-01-28 to 2026-01-31 and 1 full scan) plus pending definition update activity all starting immediately after user login.

Cleared the queued endpoint protection scan backlog on WORKSTATION-DL5490-MR via the Endpoint Management console to stop repeated scan launches consuming CPU during the login period. Confirmed MsMpEng.exe CPU usage dropped below 5% after clearing.

Updated endpoint protection scan scheduling in Endpoint Management for the Portland Sales group policy so full or heavy scans no longer begin during peak user login times (08:00-10:00 PST) and are staggered to off-peak hours (12:00-14:00 PST) to reduce contention.

Refreshed the device policy from the Endpoint Management console (initiated by agent pnair) so the revised scan schedule and protection settings applied to WORKSTATION-DL5490-MR. Policy sync confirmed at 2026-02-02T00:15:00Z.

Validated post-remediation performance by monitoring CPU on WORKSTATION-DL5490-MR after login and confirming File Explorer, Outlook, and Chrome opened normally (under 3 seconds each) without sustained resource spikes. User mramirez confirmed the laptop was performing as expected. Ticket closed and follow-up email sent to marco.ramirez@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Marco — thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether the slowdown starts shortly after you sign in to WORKSTATION-DL5490-MR and whether common apps like Outlook or Chrome take much longer than normal to open. Also, can you let us know if you've noticed any Windows Defender popups or scan notifications around the time the CPU spikes? I've pulled up your device record under mramirez in Endpoint Management.

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failing for api.internal.corp
description: Internal users and monitoring were trying to reach the service at api.internal.corp, but name resolution intermittently returned a stale A record (10.40.2.15) instead of the current service IP (10.40.5.80). The issue was first reported by Priya Nambiar from the Portland development team, who noticed API calls from her workstation WORKSTATION-DEV-PN were timing out. The authoritative internal zone already contained the updated record, yet some internal DNS resolvers and probes continued to answer with the previous address, causing intermittent failures for applications that connect to the API by hostname from corp-datacenter-1. Additional reports came in from dev team members Raj Menon and Lisa Cheng, confirming the issue was not isolated to a single client.
observed_errors: stale A record returned by resolver
inconsistent dig responses between authoritative server and resolver
root_cause: A stale cached A record remained on one or more internal recursive resolvers/forwarders after the DNS record change, so clients querying different resolver paths intermittently received the previous IP even though the authoritative zone had the updated address.
resolution_steps: Queried api.internal.corp against the authoritative DNS server (AUTH-DNS-01) and internal recursive resolvers (RSLV-INT-02, RSLV-INT-03) to confirm the authoritative zone served the new IP (10.40.5.80) while some resolver paths—particularly RSLV-INT-03 in Portland—still returned the previous address (10.40.2.15).

Flushed cache entries for api.internal.corp on the affected internal resolvers RSLV-INT-02 and RSLV-INT-03 and reloaded the resolver service so recursive nodes stopped serving the stale A record. Verified with user pnambiar that her workstation WORKSTATION-DEV-PN began resolving correctly after the flush.

Reviewed and corrected internal forwarder/cache behavior on FWD-ZONE-01 for the zone to ensure requests for the internal domain were routed to the proper authoritative source (AUTH-DNS-01) instead of reusing outdated cached data. Agent dkovalenko confirmed forwarder configuration was consistent with the expected zone delegation.

Kept the record TTL at 300 seconds to shorten cache persistence during the change window and verified the authoritative zone serial and A record data were current on the internal DNS infrastructure. DNS admin mforrester confirmed no further zone changes were pending.

Re-tested name resolution from multiple internal resolver paths and monitoring locations—including workstations belonging to pnambiar (10.22.17.44), rmenon, and lcheng—until dig responses consistently returned the updated IP (10.40.5.80) and the service was reachable by hostname without recurrence.

title: Installation blocked in Software Center for FinanceApp (entitlement missing)
