Verify the new group membership for rmorales has synchronized to Intune and SCCM (allow up to 30 minutes for AAD Connect delta sync) so the FinanceApp application becomes targeted to the user's managed device WORKSTATION-FIN-RMORALES.

Review Endpoint Protection or application control status for FinanceApp on WORKSTATION-FIN-RMORALES and approve or allowlist the installer if a security approval is pending in the Endpoint Protection console.

Trigger a device sync and policy evaluation cycle from Intune or Software Center on WORKSTATION-FIN-RMORALES (IP 10.42.18.97), then refresh Software Center application inventory on the endpoint to pull the updated targeting.

Retry the FinanceApp installation on WORKSTATION-FIN-RMORALES after policy refresh and confirm the application is visible in Software Center and no longer returns the entitlement error 0x80180014. Notify rmorales at rmorales@corplabs.com upon completion.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts
description: CustomerDataSync scheduled sync jobs through the Integration Gateway began failing during the 02:00 UTC processing window on 2025-12-02. The affected integration, managed by backend engineer Priya Nair (EMP-40291), could not complete authenticated calls to the external CRM API endpoint from gateway worker pods running on host WORKSTATION-GWPOD-PN in the us-east-1 EKS environment. Monitoring dashboards showed repeated 401 Unauthorized token_expired responses for service account svc-custsync followed by 504 Gateway Timeout errors as retries accumulated. This blocked timely customer data synchronization and increased backlog in the gateway worker queue, with over 1,200 pending sync jobs reported by 02:30 UTC. The issue was initially flagged by Monitoring System alert ALERT-SYNC-7744 and escalated to the integration operations team at ext 4085.
root_cause: The Integration Gateway service account token expired, causing 401 Unauthorized token_expired responses from the external API. The gateway continued retrying failed authentication attempts until jobs exhausted retries and surfaced as 504 timeouts, which created a processing backlog for scheduled syncs.
resolution_steps: Validated that the external CRM API itself was healthy via Monitoring System synthetic probes and direct latency checks from 10.42.17.88, and confirmed the primary failure pattern was authentication-related 401 token_expired responses for service account svc-custsync rather than a downstream service outage.

Rotated the expired Integration Gateway service account token for svc-custsync via Vault (new token issued 2025-12-02T02:48:00Z) and updated the active secret used by the gateway worker pods igw-worker-01 through igw-worker-04 for outbound API authentication.

Restarted the Integration Gateway worker pods (igw-worker-01 through igw-worker-04) on node 10.42.17.88 so they would load the new svc-custsync token and clear stuck retry state from previously failed sync attempts. Restart completed by 02:52 UTC.

Verified successful authenticated API calls after the token update by reviewing gateway response logs, and monitored backlog processing with Marcus Ellison until the 1,450+ delayed sync jobs drained normally by approximately 03:40 UTC.

Added token-expiry alerting in Monitoring System to notify the backend-syncers group (priya.nair@corplabs.com, mellison@corplabs.com) 14 days before TTL expiration, scheduled automatic token rotation at 60-day intervals for svc-custsync, then adjusted retry and backoff behavior (max retries reduced to 3, exponential backoff ceiling set to 30s) to reduce cascading timeout conditions if authentication fails again.
agent_questions: We are seeing 401 Unauthorized and 504 timeout errors during the scheduled sync window on the Integration Gateway pods in us-east-1. Reviewing logs from gateway node igw-worker-04 (10.42.17.88) confirms the failures are tied to service account svc-custsync. Priya, please confirm whether there was any recent token or secret rotation change for the Integration Gateway service account, and whether the credentials stored in Vault path secret/integrations/custsync were updated in the last 90 days.

title: Internal hostname svc-inventory.corp fails to resolve
description: Users and dependent internal applications at the Charlotte office were trying to reach the Inventory Service by the internal hostname svc-inventory.corp, but DNS lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN from multiple subnets while direct connections to the service IP (10.42.16.55) still worked. The issue was first reported by Marcus Ellison (mellison, EMP-40821) and affected internal name resolution for the service, causing application connectivity failures until the stale DNS record was corrected and caches were cleared.
root_cause: A stale A record for svc-inventory.corp remained cached on the primary resolver and was associated with a decommissioned host, and the long TTL allowed the incorrect data to persist and be served during internal DNS lookups.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone corp.internal for svc-inventory.corp and corrected the A record so it pointed to the current service IP 10.42.16.55 instead of the decommissioned host reference 10.42.16.12.
Reduced the TTL on the affected DNS record from 86400 seconds to 300 seconds to shorten persistence of incorrect cached data during propagation of the corrected entry.
Flushed DNS cache entries on the primary resolver DNS-PRI-EAST.corp.internal and secondary resolver DNS-SEC-EAST.corp.internal to remove the stale record immediately.

Validated name resolution for svc-inventory.corp from multiple client subnets (10.42.16.0/24 and 10.42.20.0/24) and confirmed the hostname consistently returned the expected address 10.42.16.55. Reporter mellison and application owner rtorres both confirmed service restoration.

Updated DNS monitoring logic in Network Monitoring and operational guidance for the Charlotte network team to better detect stale-record and elevated NXDOMAIN patterns for internal service names, including automated alerting thresholds for NXDOMAIN spikes.

title: Software Center installation blocked by policy for Acme Tools
description: I was trying to install Acme Tools v4.2 from Software Center on my Windows 10 21H2 managed device (WORKSTATION-DT-MREEVES), but the install was blocked with the message 'Installation blocked by policy.' The application was also not visible in Intune for the device even though the endpoint was enrolled and compliant. My username is mreeves (employee ID EMP-40821) and I need this software to complete a project deliverable for the Portland engineering team. I've confirmed my device IP is 10.22.47.118 and it shows as compliant in the Company Portal.
observed_errors: Application not listed in Intune assignments
root_cause: The user was not a member of the Intune entitlement group assigned to Acme Tools, so the application policy was not targeted to the user/device and Software Center blocked the installation.
resolution_steps: Verified that device WORKSTATION-DT-MREEVES (IP 10.22.47.118) was properly enrolled in Intune and reporting compliant status, confirming the issue was not caused by enrollment or general device health problems.

Reviewed the Acme Tools v4.2 application assignment in Intune and confirmed that user mreeves@corplabs.com (Marcus Reeves, EMP-40821) was missing from the required 'AcmeTools-Entitled' Azure AD entitlement group.
Added user mreeves to the 'AcmeTools-Entitled' group in Azure AD to restore application targeting and entitlement for Acme Tools v4.2 on the Portland engineering team's devices.
Triggered a device inventory and policy refresh on WORKSTATION-DT-MREEVES so updated group membership and app assignments would synchronize to the endpoint via Intune.

Had user Marcus Reeves retry the installation from Software Center after the Intune sync completed, then verified the application became visible and Acme Tools v4.2 installed successfully on WORKSTATION-DT-MREEVES.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: denied access to department shared drive (mapped drive prompts for credentials)
description: I was trying to open the department shared drive (\\FS-CORP-02.corplabs.internal\Shared\Dept) from a mapped SMB network drive (S:) on my Windows 10 workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, but the drive repeatedly prompted for credentials and returned "Access Denied" (0x80070005) when opening \\FS-CORP-02.corplabs.internal\Shared\Dept starting Monday morning. My username is mreynolds (employee ID FIN-40218) and I reported a recent Active Directory group change — I was removed from the ProjectAlpha_Team group last Friday, and I believe this may have inadvertently dropped my Finance_Department share entitlement. I was blocked from accessing department files on the Windows Server 2019 file server. Follow-up review also found inconsistent permissions on several subfolders under \Shared\Dept\Reports and \Shared\Dept\Budgets, indicating the issue may affect more than one user in the Arlington office.
root_cause: Primary access failure for the reported user was caused by missing membership in the approved AD security group for the shared drive, with access restored after group re-add and token refresh. A secondary file server issue was also identified: broken ACL inheritance on multiple subfolders, which explains continued denials for other users and should be treated as a separate permissions remediation item rather than the cause of the restored user's immediate session failure.
resolution_steps: Verified mreynolds' required AD security group for the department shared drive by running Get-ADPrincipalGroupMembership and confirmed FIN_SharedDrive_RW was missing; re-added the account CN=mreynolds,OU=Finance,DC=corplabs,DC=internal to the approved access group FIN_SharedDrive_RW.

Forced an access token refresh by instructing Monica Reynolds to sign out and back in on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR so the updated FIN_SharedDrive_RW group membership would be included in the Kerberos logon token for the current session.

Removed the stale S: drive mapping and remapped the shared network drive using 'net use S: \\FS-CORP-02.corplabs.internal\Shared\Dept /persistent:yes' to ensure the client used the current SMB path and refreshed credentials.

Confirmed mreynolds could open the \\FS-CORP-02.corplabs.internal\Shared\Dept location successfully from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (10.22.47.115) after the membership and session refresh changes — no further credential prompts or 0x80070005 errors observed.

Documented findings and scheduled follow-up remediation task CHG-REQ-1187 (assigned to file server admin Raj Patel, rpatel@corplabs.com) for broken NTFS permission inheritance on affected subfolders (\Shared\Dept\Reports\Q1-2026, \Shared\Dept\Budgets\FY2026) so broader file server ACL inconsistencies can be corrected for other impacted Arlington Finance users.

title: Device noncompliant: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key not escrowed
description: A managed Windows 10 Enterprise 21H2 corporate laptop (hostname LAPTOP-SALES-MR, asset tag SLS-4821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (mreeves, employee ID EMP-90274) in the Dallas office was marked noncompliant in Intune because device encryption was not enabled and no BitLocker recovery key was visible in Azure AD. The device IP at the time of the compliance check was 10.42.18.97. In Company Portal, encryption showed as failed, blocking Marcus from meeting compliance requirements needed to access corporate data and Sales team SharePoint resources. Investigation focused on BitLocker status, TPM readiness, Intune policy delivery, and recovery key escrow.
root_cause: BitLocker could not start because the device TPM protector was not initialized, and the assigned Intune disk encryption policy had not yet applied successfully. As a result, encryption did not begin and the recovery key was not escrowed to Azure AD.
resolution_steps: Validated local BitLocker and TPM state on LAPTOP-SALES-MR (Windows 10 Enterprise 21H2, IP 10.42.18.97, user mreeves) and confirmed via tpm.msc and Get-Tpm that TPM ownership was not initialized (error 0x80070057), which prevented creation of the required BitLocker protector.

Initialized TPM ownership on LAPTOP-SALES-MR using elevated PowerShell command Initialize-Tpm and ensured TPM 2.0 was enabled and ready in firmware (confirmed via tpm.msc showing 'The TPM is ready for use') so BitLocker prerequisites were satisfied.

Reviewed the Intune Windows disk encryption policy assignment ('Corp-BitLocker-Win10-Encrypt') for the affected device scope (Sales device group) and re-applied/enforced the BitLocker policy to LAPTOP-SALES-MR via Endpoint Manager.

Forced an Intune device sync from Company Portal on LAPTOP-SALES-MR so the updated encryption policy was received immediately by the laptop. Confirmed sync completed successfully at approximately 22:30 UTC.

Started BitLocker encryption on the C: drive after TPM and policy prerequisites were met on LAPTOP-SALES-MR, then verified via manage-bde -status that encryption progressed successfully (XTS-AES 256-bit) on the endpoint.

Confirmed the BitLocker recovery key (ID 8A3F2B**) escrowed to Azure AD for device LAPTOP-SALES-MR under user mreeves@corplabs.com, and that Intune compliance updated from 'Encryption - Failed' to compliant. Notified Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com) that the device is now fully compliant.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm the laptop model (we show a Dell Latitude 5520 under hostname LAPTOP-SALES-MR), whether TPM is enabled in firmware, and run a Company Portal sync so we can check if the encryption policy is reaching the device. You can trigger the sync from Company Portal > Settings > Sync. Also, could you verify you're signed in as mreeves@corplabs.com? I've assigned this to myself — Priya Nair, Desktop Support. You can reach me at pnair@corplabs.com or ext. 214-555-0183 if needed.

title: Device noncompliant (missing encryption signal) — Conditional Access blocked VPN
description: I (Rachel Nguyen, emp ID EMP-40291) on a Windows 11 22H2 company laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-RN) was trying to connect to the corporate VPN from the Arlington office, but Conditional Access blocked access because the device appeared noncompliant in Company Portal. Intune showed the device (IP 10.42.17.88) had not checked in for about 72 hours and the required encryption/BitLocker compliance signal was reporting as unknown after a recent update, preventing remote work access until compliance status refreshed.
observed_errors: Access blocked by Conditional Access policy
root_cause: Device compliance evaluation failed because the Intune-managed laptop had a stale check-in and was not reporting the required BitLocker/encryption state, causing Conditional Access to treat the device as noncompliant and block VPN access.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the Intune device record for WORKSTATION-DELL-RN (user rnguyen, EMP-40291) to confirm the last check-in was stale (2026-01-01T14:22:00Z) and that the failing compliance condition was the missing encryption/BitLocker signal.
Triggered a remote device sync from Intune to force a fresh management check-in and compliance re-evaluation on WORKSTATION-DELL-RN, initiated by agent Derek Morris (dmorris).

Reapplied or pushed the BitLocker/encryption compliance profile (Finance-US-East-Win11-Compliance) to the affected device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN so the required encryption state could be reported correctly after the forced sync.
Had the user Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen) reboot the laptop and complete pending operating system updates so the management agent and encryption status could refresh; confirmed via phone at 571-309-4482.

Verified the device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN reported current check-in (2026-01-04T11:38:00Z) and healthy encryption status in Intune, after which compliance returned to a healthy state and Conditional Access allowed VPN access again for rnguyen.

Scheduled follow-up monitoring for similarly affected devices in the Arlington Finance group and noted escalation to the endpoint team (endpoint-support@corplabs.com) if encryption reporting remains stale on repeat occurrences.
agent_questions: I checked the Intune record for user rnguyen (Rachel Nguyen, EMP-40291) and the device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN has not checked in for roughly 72 hours. Can you confirm whether Company Portal still shows encryption as unknown and whether the laptop recently installed updates? You can reach me at dmorris@corplabs.com or ext 4-7823 if you need to discuss further.

title: Print jobs stuck on PrintServer-01
description: Multiple users in the Frankfurt office were trying to print through shared queues hosted on PrintServer-01 (\\PrintServer-01\HP-CLJ-4525-3F), but jobs remained stuck in the server queue and clients showed "driver unavailable" with some printers intermittently appearing offline. The issue was first reported by Maria Engel (EMP-40821) around 23:10 UTC and quickly confirmed by at least four other desktops on the same floor. The affected printer model (HP Color LaserJet 4525) in the EMEA environment was completely blocked for normal printing.
root_cause: A corrupt printer driver package on PrintServer-01 for the affected printer model caused the shared queue to stall and repeatedly present "driver unavailable" to clients.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the affected shared printer queues on PrintServer-01 (specifically \\PrintServer-01\HP-CLJ-4525-3F) and confirmed 14 repeated queue stalls associated with the HP Color LaserJet 4525 printer model, impacting users including Maria Engel (EMP-40821) and Ralf Becker in the Frankfurt office.

Removed the corrupt driver package reference (HP Color LaserJet 4525 PCL6 v61.180.2.24989) by reinstalling the approved printer driver package (v61.180.2.25100) for the HP Color LaserJet 4525 model on PrintServer-01. Agent Thomas Richter (trichter@corplabs.com) performed the reinstallation.
Remapped the affected printer queue \\PrintServer-01\HP-CLJ-4525-3F to the newly installed approved driver so the queue no longer referenced the damaged driver package.
Cleared 11 remaining stale print jobs from the impacted queue and restarted the Print Spooler service on PrintServer-01 to reset queue processing.

Validated successful test prints from three client workstations — WORKSTATION-MENGEL (Maria Engel), WORKSTATION-RBECKER (Ralf Becker), and WORKSTATION-PNAIR (Priya Nair) — and monitored the queue for 30 minutes to confirm jobs processed normally without recurring "driver unavailable" errors.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — can you confirm which printer queues on PrintServer-01 are stuck? Specifically, is it \\PrintServer-01\HP-CLJ-4525-3F or other queues as well? Also, are the clients (e.g. your workstation WORKSTATION-MENGEL) showing the exact message "driver unavailable", or do some show an offline status instead? I want to narrow down whether this is isolated to the HP 4525 driver or a broader spooler problem.

title: Outlook mail not syncing on desktop and mobile
description: I am unable to receive current mailbox updates in Outlook Desktop on Windows 10 (hostname WORKSTATION-DT-RGARCIA) and Outlook Mobile on iOS 15 for the Exchange Online mailbox belonging to Rosa Garcia (rgarcia@corplabs.com, employee ID EMP-40291). Since yesterday morning, desktop Outlook has shown a disconnected state and mobile shows the last sync from 2026-02-12 around 08:15, while OWA at https://outlook.office365.com continues to display current messages. The issue appears limited to client synchronization rather than mailbox availability, preventing normal email access from installed Outlook clients for a Sales I user based in the Dallas office, NA region.
observed_errors: Mobile Outlook reports last sync yesterday despite new mail in OWA
No server errors observed in OWA for this mailbox
root_cause: Client-side Exchange synchronization failure affecting both Outlook desktop and mobile access paths, most consistent with stale or corrupted Outlook profile/cache on desktop combined with an unhealthy mobile sync partnership or Intune/MDM compliance-related block. Server-side mailbox availability is unlikely because OWA shows current mail successfully.
resolution_steps: Validated that the Exchange Online mailbox for rgarcia@corplabs.com was current in OWA, confirming the mailbox itself was available and narrowing the issue to Outlook client synchronization on WORKSTATION-DT-RGARCIA and IPHONE-RGARCIA rather than a server-side mail flow outage.

Compared Outlook connection behavior on WORKSTATION-DT-RGARCIA (IP 10.42.18.77) and isolated the desktop symptom to a client sync/connectivity issue after Outlook remained disconnected while OWA continued to update normally for rgarcia@corplabs.com.

Rebuilt the Outlook desktop profile for rgarcia on WORKSTATION-DT-RGARCIA by removing the existing mail profile via Control Panel > Mail > Show Profiles, deleting the stale OST cache file, and creating a fresh profile pointing to rgarcia@corplabs.com so the client could establish a clean Exchange synchronization session.

Reset the affected mobile mail sync relationship for IPHONE-RGARCIA by removing the existing mobile device partnership in Exchange Online admin center (Remove-MobileDevice) and instructing Rosa Garcia to re-establish the mailbox connection in Outlook Mobile after verifying device access prerequisites and Intune enrollment.

Confirmed the mobile device IPHONE-RGARCIA needed to be compliant with Intune management policy for Exchange Online mail access; Kevin Tran (ktran) verified the device compliance state in the Intune portal and instructed remediation of a pending OS update compliance alert before retrying sync.

After profile and partnership remediation, verified that new messages appeared in Outlook desktop on WORKSTATION-DT-RGARCIA and Outlook Mobile on IPHONE-RGARCIA within 10 minutes, and confirmed with Rosa Garcia (rgarcia@corplabs.com) that the disconnected and stale-sync symptoms no longer occurred. Ticket closed by Kevin Tran.
agent_questions: Hi Rosa — please confirm whether the mailbox for rgarcia@corplabs.com is current in OWA and whether your mobile device (iPhone managed via Intune) is showing any compliance warning or enrollment issue in the Company Portal app, so we can distinguish a client sync failure from an Exchange Online outage. Also, can you confirm the IP address your desktop is connecting from? This will help us rule out any network-level block.

title: BitLocker encryption failed: TPM protector not initialized and recovery key not escrowed
description: Windows BitLocker was not enabled on a managed Windows 10 21H2 device (hostname WORKSTATION-SALES-MR, asset tag WS-4417) assigned to Marcus Reeves (emp ID EMP-90234) in the Portland office. Control Panel showed the C: drive as not protected, and Intune marked the device noncompliant for the required disk encryption policy ('EP-Win10-Encryption-v3'). No recovery key was visible in the Intune management portal for this endpoint. This prevented the device from meeting encryption compliance requirements and indicated the initial BitLocker encryption workflow did not complete successfully during provisioning.
observed_errors: Intune: No recovery key on record
Device Compliance: Noncompliant for 'Require disk encryption'
root_cause: BitLocker encryption could not complete because the TPM was in an unowned or cleared state and no TPM protector was initialized. Without a valid protector, BitLocker did not generate a usable recovery key, so Intune had no key to escrow and the device remained noncompliant for disk encryption.
resolution_steps: Initialize and verify TPM readiness on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR by running 'Initialize-Tpm' in an elevated PowerShell session, then confirm Get-Tpm returns TpmReady: True so the device can support a TPM-based BitLocker protector.

Add the BitLocker TPM protector for the C: system drive after TPM initialization is complete by running 'Add-BitLockerKeyProtector -MountPoint C: -TpmProtector' and verify the protector is listed via 'manage-bde -protectors -get C:'.

Enable BitLocker encryption on the C: volume using 'Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -RecoveryPasswordProtector' and confirm that a 48-digit numerical recovery key is generated locally as part of the protection setup. Verify encryption progress with 'manage-bde -status C:'.

Force an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR via Company Portal or 'Start-IntuneSync' so updated BitLocker state and the recovery key can be reported to the management service. Confirm sync completes successfully in the Intune portal.

Validate that the recovery key is escrowed in Intune (Devices > WORKSTATION-SALES-MR > Recovery keys) and confirm the device changes from noncompliant to compliant for the 'Require disk encryption' policy. Notify Marcus Reeves (mreeves, marcus.reeves@corplabs.com) that encryption is active and the device is now compliant.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failure for internal host srv-app.internal.corp
description: Multiple internal teams were trying to reach the internal application endpoint using the hostname srv-app.internal.corp, but name resolution was inconsistent across the corporate network. The issue was first reported by Tanya Reyes (emp ID EMP-40821) from the Portland office, and subsequently confirmed by engineers in the Austin office. Some clients received NXDOMAIN responses while others experienced DNS timeouts, preventing the application from being reached by name and suggesting resolver-specific or subnet-specific DNS path issues rather than a full application outage.
observed_errors: NXDOMAIN for srv-app.internal.corp from some resolvers
DNS lookup timed out from other clients
root_cause: Inconsistent internal DNS resolution was caused by resolver path divergence for the internal.corp zone: one or more resolvers or network segments were not consistently forwarding or serving the current zone data, and stale cached responses on affected resolvers contributed to intermittent NXDOMAIN and timeout behavior for srv-app.internal.corp.
resolution_steps: Validated srv-app.internal.corp against a known-good internal resolver (10.20.2.10 in Austin) and compared results with affected resolver paths (10.20.1.5 in Portland) to confirm that failures were isolated to specific resolvers or segments rather than the application host itself. Tanya Reyes and Marcus Okonkwo confirmed the failures from their respective workstations.

Reviewed the internal DNS zone record and authoritative server consistency for srv-app.internal.corp on DNS-AUTH-01.internal.corp, confirming the correct A record was present and available from the expected authoritative source. Network engineer David Liang verified the zone file was intact.

Corrected DNS forwarding or resolver path configuration on resolver 10.20.1.5 for the affected internal.corp lookup path so impacted resolvers in the Portland segment queried the proper authoritative source for the zone.

Flushed stale DNS cache entries on affected resolvers (10.20.1.5) after the configuration correction so previously cached NXDOMAIN or outdated responses were cleared. Confirmed cache flush completed successfully.

Retested name resolution for srv-app.internal.corp from impacted and known-good paths to verify that lookups returned the same current answer consistently across subnets. Tanya Reyes confirmed resolution from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-TR (10.42.17.88) and Marcus Okonkwo confirmed from WORKSTATION-DESK-MO (10.42.18.22) in the Portland office; Austin hosts continued resolving normally.
agent_questions: Hi Tanya — please confirm whether the failure is limited to certain subnets or office locations and provide nslookup or dig output for srv-app.internal.corp from one impacted host, including the resolver IP and approximate test time. If possible, run the test from your workstation (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-TR) and share the output along with your client IP so we can correlate with resolver logs.

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: A company Windows 10 Pro laptop assigned to Rachel Nguyen (employee ID EMP-40291) in the Dallas office was showing disk encryption as disabled and was marked noncompliant in the Intune Device Compliance Service portal. Checks in manage-bde and Azure AD showed no BitLocker recovery key escrowed for the device (hostname LAPTOP-RNGUYEN-7), which prevented it from meeting required encryption compliance. The device was reported via Company Portal on 2026-01-19.
observed_errors: No recovery key escrowed to Azure AD
root_cause: BitLocker could not enable because the TPM protector was not initialized on the endpoint, and the Intune BitLocker policy had not successfully applied, leaving encryption off and the recovery key unescrowed.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM presence and readiness on LAPTOP-RNGUYEN-7 via tpm.msc, confirmed the TPM chip was ready (version 2.0), then initialized the TPM protector required for BitLocker startup protection using manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm.
Added a TPM-based BitLocker protector and enabled BitLocker on the OS volume (C:) of LAPTOP-RNGUYEN-7 using local remediation commands: manage-bde -on C: -RecoveryPassword.

Started disk encryption on LAPTOP-RNGUYEN-7 and confirmed BitLocker protection state changed from Off to 'Encryption in Progress' via manage-bde -status C:, with full encryption completing within the hour.

Added LAPTOP-RNGUYEN-7 (ranguyen) to the Sales-Encryption-Required assignment group, forced Intune BitLocker policy assignment (profile BL-Compliance-Sales-NA), and triggered a device sync from Company Portal so the endpoint received the expected encryption configuration.

Escrowed the BitLocker recovery key to Azure AD using manage-bde -protectors -adbackup C: -id {recovery-protector-id}, verified the 48-digit recovery key was present in the Azure AD device blade for support retrieval, and confirmed LAPTOP-RNGUYEN-7 returned to a compliant state in the Device Compliance Service. Notified Rachel Nguyen (ranguyen@corplabs.com) that the device was now compliant.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel, please confirm whether the device LAPTOP-RNGUYEN-7 (IP 10.42.18.103) is still showing BitLocker as Off locally and whether you recently reimaged or replaced the laptop, as we do not see a recovery key escrowed in Azure AD for your device. You can verify by opening manage-bde -status in an elevated prompt. — Kevin Marsh, Endpoint Support

title: Users encounter MFA prompt loop on Okta SSO affecting SaaS access
description: Multiple Sales users (including Rachel Nguyen, emp ID SE-40218, and Derek Holloway) were trying to access Salesforce and Confluence through the internal SSO portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) from the Charlotte office, but after entering credentials in Okta they were sent back to the MFA challenge repeatedly and were ultimately denied access. The issue began after a recent Azure AD group sync on 2026-04-08, affected users associated with the Sales-External access path, and blocked normal SaaS access needed for daily sales operations. Rachel first reported the problem at approximately 15:45 UTC on 2026-04-09 after being unable to log into Salesforce from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN.
observed_errors: Repeated MFA challenge followed by sign-in rejection
Okta log entries: 'MFA challenge' and 'assertion_rejected' for affected users
root_cause: A subset of affected users had stale Okta MFA enrollments while a recent Azure AD to Okta group sync introduced an incorrect Sales-External group mapping, causing repeated MFA challenges and rejected SSO assertions during application sign-in.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Okta sign-on activity for affected users (rnguyen, dholloway, mparker) and confirmed repeated MFA challenge behavior followed by rejected assertions during Salesforce and Confluence launches — rnguyen alone had 7 failed MFA cycles logged between 15:45–16:10 UTC on 2026-04-09.

Cleared active Okta sessions for impacted accounts (rnguyen, dholloway, mparker, and 3 additional Sales-External users identified in the Charlotte office) to remove stale authentication state before retesting sign-in.

Reset MFA enrollment for confirmed affected users so they could re-register a valid active factor and complete a clean challenge flow — rnguyen re-enrolled successfully from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN at 16:48 UTC and confirmed Salesforce access.

Corrected the Azure AD group-to-Okta assignment for the Sales-External mapping (reconciling the 14-member Azure AD group with Okta's 9-member assignment) so users were evaluated against the intended access policy and application assignment. Kevin Marsh (kmarsh@corplabs.com) confirmed the sync configuration has been updated to prevent future drift.

Validated successful SSO access with test accounts rnguyen and dholloway after MFA re-enrollment and mapping correction, then monitored sign-on logs for one business day to confirm no recurrence across all Sales-External users in the Charlotte region.
agent_questions: Please confirm whether the affected users are in the Sales-External Azure AD group and whether their authenticator app time is correct. Also send one recent username so we can review the Okta sign-on log entries — ideally the account for rnguyen or dholloway so we can cross-reference the sign-on policy evaluation in the Okta admin console.

title: Multiple users: print jobs stuck and 'Driver unavailable' on central print server
description: Multiple users in the Building 3 Finance wing at our Charlotte office were trying to print daily reporting documents to the Finance-Color shared queue on the central print server (psrv01.printinfra.corplabs.internal), but color print jobs remained stuck at 0% and displayed "Driver unavailable." The issue was first reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed by at least four other users on the same floor. Restarting the Windows Print Spooler service and clearing the queue did not restore service, and new jobs immediately failed again. Event logs on the Windows Server 2019 print server showed repeated printer driver load failures (Event ID 372 — driver load error), indicating a server-side driver issue affecting shared printing for all office users mapped to that queue.
observed_errors: Print job stuck at 0% with status 'Driver unavailable' in Finance-Color queue
Event Log: Print spooler error - driver load failure (print driver load error recorded multiple times)
Print spooler restart did not clear persistent job entries
root_cause: Corrupt or invalid printer driver package on the primary print server prevented the Finance-Color shared queue driver from loading, causing new jobs to remain stuck and report 'Driver unavailable' even after spooler restart and queue clearing.
resolution_steps: Escalated the incident to the Print Infrastructure Team (Rajesh Patel, r.patel@corplabs.com, ext. 4417) with the affected server name (psrv01.printinfra.corplabs.internal), Finance-Color queue details, list of confirmed affected users (mgonzalez, dchen, pkapoor, ltran), and server log bundle showing 47 repeated driver load failures (Event ID 372).

Removed the faulty Finance-Color printer driver package from psrv01 via the Printer Management Console and reinstalled the approved driver package (v6.4.2) from the authorized repository (\\driverstore.corplabs.internal\approved\print) after validating package signature and SHA-256 checksum.

Reassociated the Finance-Color shared queue with the reinstalled v6.4.2 driver and cleared residual spooler files and 12 pending queue entries on psrv01.printinfra.corplabs.internal, including stuck jobs from mgonzalez (EMP-40821) and dchen.

Restarted the Print Spooler service on psrv01 after driver reinstallation and confirmed the Finance-Color queue initialized cleanly without recurring driver load errors (Event ID 372) in the event logs. Queue status changed to 'Ready' within 8 seconds of spooler start.

Completed validation prints from multiple sample users — Maria Gonzalez (WORKSTATION-PC-MG, 10.42.18.55), David Chen (WORKSTATION-PC-DC, 10.42.18.61), and Priya Kapoor (pkapoor) — and monitored spooler and queue behavior for 24 hours to confirm normal job processing and no repeat 'Driver unavailable' condition. All test pages printed successfully within expected timeframes.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — thanks for reporting this. Can you confirm whether all affected users (yourself, and the others you mentioned on the Finance floor) are printing to the same Finance-Color shared queue on psrv01? Also, after the spooler restart performed earlier, do jobs still remain at 0% or do they now show a different driver-related message? If possible, please have one of the other affected users — perhaps David Chen or whoever is nearby — attempt a test print so we can confirm the scope. You can reach me at ext. 4417 or at r.patel@corplabs.com if it's easier.

title: Internal hostname resolution failures traced to stale DNS record and resolver cache
description: Internal users in the Arlington office were trying to reach an internal application endpoint by hostname, service.corp.local, from the on-premises corp-dc1 environment. During the incident window (approximately 04:00–05:30 UTC on 2026-01-12), the application intermittently could not connect because DNS lookups returned NXDOMAIN responses or timed out, and some resolver responses referenced an outdated address (10.40.12.55) after a host IP change to 10.40.14.20. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40821) and confirmed by several colleagues on the 10.40.0.0/16 network. Name resolution for the internal service was affected across multiple subnets (VLAN 120, VLAN 135, VLAN 140) until DNS data and resolver cache were corrected.
root_cause: An outdated A record remained in the internal DNS zone after the service host IP changed, and the internal resolver cluster continued serving stale cached data due to the long TTL, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN responses, lookup timeouts, and resolution to an old address.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the authoritative internal DNS zone on dns-auth1.corp.local for service.corp.local and identified that the A record (10.40.12.55) did not reflect the current service IP (10.40.14.20) following the migration documented in CHG-8842.

Updated the A record in the internal DNS zone to the correct current IP 10.40.14.20 and confirmed the intended TTL configuration was reduced from 86400 to 3600 seconds for the record to prevent prolonged stale caching in the future.
Flushed the DNS cache across the internal resolver cluster (dns-res1, dns-res2, dns-res3) so clients on all VLANs would stop receiving the stale cached address 10.40.12.55.

Validated resolution with nslookup service.corp.local from multiple subnets — VLAN 120 (10.40.120.47, WORKSTATION-PC-MD), VLAN 135 (10.40.135.19, WORKSTATION-LT-RO), and VLAN 140 — and compared results to the authoritative record to confirm consistent answers of 10.40.14.20.

Verified the application could again reach the internal service by name from affected users (mdelgado, rokonkwo) and monitored Network Monitoring alerts until NXDOMAIN spikes and DNS timeout symptoms cleared. Confirmed with Marcus Delgado at ext. 4-7193 that connectivity was fully restored.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether service.corp.local fails from all affected subnets and whether lookups are returning NXDOMAIN, timing out, or resolving to an unexpected IP. Can you run nslookup service.corp.local from your workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD and share the output? Also, are other users such as those on VLAN 135 or VLAN 140 seeing the same behavior? Please send results to dns-ops@corplabs.com so we can correlate.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to Finance shared drive for user j.smith
description: Newly onboarded user j.smith (Employee ID: EMP-40291) in the London office was trying to open the Finance shared drive at \\fs01\Finance from a mapped network drive (F:) on their Windows 10 workstation WORKSTATION-PC-JS (IP 10.42.17.88). The drive prompted for credentials and then returned Access Denied (NT STATUS C0000022), preventing access to Finance department files needed for normal work. The ticket was raised by the user's manager, Rebecca Thornton (r.thornton@corplabs.com), who noted that j.smith may not have received the required shared drive entitlement during onboarding. The user can be reached at ext. +44 20 7946 3182 or via email at james.smith@corplabs.com.
root_cause: User j.smith was not added to the Finance_Read Active Directory security group during onboarding, so the ACL on \\fs01\Finance correctly denied access until membership was added and the user's session token was refreshed.
resolution_steps: Verified the share and folder ACL on \\fs01\Finance granted access through the Finance_Read security group by reviewing the NTFS permissions and share-level permissions on the file server.

Added user j.smith (EMP-40291, CN=j.smith,OU=Finance,OU=Corp Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) to the Finance_Read Active Directory security group required for read access to the Finance shared drive. Updated the onboarding checklist and notified manager Rebecca Thornton (r.thornton@corplabs.com) of the correction.
Cleared cached credentials on the user's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-JS via Windows Credential Manager to remove the repeated credential prompt against the mapped drive (F:) to \\fs01\Finance.

Had the user sign out and sign back in on WORKSTATION-PC-JS so the updated Finance_Read group membership was included in a new Kerberos access token. Verified with 'klist' that the refreshed token contained the correct group SID.

Remapped the network drive (F:) to the current \\fs01\Finance path on WORKSTATION-PC-JS and confirmed that user j.smith could open the Finance folder successfully. Priya Kapoor (p.kapoor) from the same team verified shared access was unaffected.
agent_questions: Hi James, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether you are opening the Finance drive from the mapped drive (F:) or directly via \\fs01\Finance, and whether the prompt returns Access Denied after you enter your domain credentials (CORPLABS\j.smith). Also, can you confirm you're working from your usual workstation WORKSTATION-PC-JS at the London office? This will help us narrow down the issue.

title: Laptop slow after login
description: I reported that my Windows 10 laptop (hostname LAPTOP-SALES-MK, IP 10.42.17.88) became very slow immediately after login following a recent policy push. CPU usage spiked to about 90%, applications such as Microsoft Office and Google Chrome took several minutes to open, and normal work was delayed during the post-login period. The device is assigned to user mkaplan (employee ID EMP-40291) in the Frankfurt office. Investigation focused on login-time resource usage, recent endpoint policy activity, and local disk capacity on the affected managed laptop.
root_cause: Endpoint Protection backlog scans triggered after a recent policy push, combined with critically low local disk space and several non-essential startup items, caused sustained high CPU usage after login and delayed application launch.
resolution_steps: Reviewed login-time resource consumption on LAPTOP-SALES-MK (user mkaplan, IP 10.42.17.88) and confirmed MsMpEng.exe was driving sustained CPU spikes (approximately 85-90% for over 6 minutes) during backlog endpoint protection scans.
Cleared the endpoint protection scan backlog on LAPTOP-SALES-MK and verified the active scan queue returned to a normal state with zero pending backlog items in the Endpoint Protection console.

Adjusted scan scheduling through endpoint management so background or full scans run outside business hours (set to 01:00-05:00 CET window) for the device assigned to mkaplan in the Frankfurt Sales group.
Disabled three non-essential startup applications (OneDrive sync, Adobe Updater, legacy CRM agent) on LAPTOP-SALES-MK to reduce post-login contention for CPU and disk resources.
Ran Disk Cleanup on LAPTOP-SALES-MK to remove temporary files and reclaim disk capacity from the device's low free-space state, recovering approximately 18 GB and bringing free space to roughly 13%.

Refreshed device policy on LAPTOP-SALES-MK via Endpoint Management console and validated that CPU usage normalized (below 15% post-login) and application launch performance returned to expected levels. User Marcus Kaplan (mkaplan) confirmed Office and Chrome open within seconds.

title: Multiple users cannot connect to Corporate Wi‑Fi
description: Multiple employees on the 3rd and 4th floors of the Portland office were trying to connect to the Corporate Wi-Fi (SSID: CorpNet-Secure) and could complete authentication, but after joining they received no usable network access and saw a NAC access denied message. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed by at least 14 other users across both floors. The issue began shortly after the scheduled certificate rotation performed by Kevin Driscoll at approximately 03:45 UTC and affected EAP-TLS wireless authentication, blocking normal internet and corporate network access from managed devices.
root_cause: Expired TLS/RADIUS certificate on the wireless controller after the scheduled certificate rotation caused EAP-TLS validation failures and NAC access denials; some endpoints also retained stale or corrupt Wi-Fi profiles that required re-enrollment after the certificate was corrected.
resolution_steps: Renewed the TLS/RADIUS certificate on the wireless controller WLC-PDX-01.corp.internal (replacing expired cert serial 7A:3F:02:CB) and validated that the certificate chain and assigned identity matched the Corporate Wi-Fi (CorpNet-Secure) authentication configuration. Renewal was performed by kdriscoll and verified by network lead Sandra Liu.

Restarted the RADIUS authentication service on the controller and refreshed controller services so the new certificate was actively presented during EAP-TLS handshakes. Verified successful TLS negotiation with a test client at 10.42.3.205.

Updated the Network Access Control configuration to reference the renewed certificate and re-evaluated wireless access policy decisions for affected clients. Confirmed NAC policy 'CorpWiFi-FullAccess' was correctly applied post-renewal for users mchen, rpatel, and others.

Had impacted users forget the Corporate SSID (CorpNet-Secure) and reconnect; for devices that continued to fail — including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (mchen), and endpoints for rpatel and jmartinez — removed the stale wireless profile and re-enrolled the device into the corporate Wi-Fi configuration via the MDM portal.

Monitored post-change authentication attempts across floors 3 and 4 in Portland and confirmed successful NAC authorization and restored network access across the affected user population. Final confirmation received from Maria Chen (EMP-40821) and Raj Patel at 05:45 UTC. No further NAC denials observed in the subsequent 2-hour monitoring window.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether affected users can join the Corporate SSID (CorpNet-Secure) but then receive a NAC access denied message, and whether this started after today's certificate rotation around 03:45 UTC. Could you also let me know the hostnames or IPs of a few affected devices so we can trace them in the NAC logs? My colleague Kevin Driscoll who performed the rotation is also looking into this on the controller side.

title: Expired TLS Certificate Caused Internal Web Service TLS Outage
description: Internal consumers were trying to connect to the internal web service at https://portal.internal.corplabs.com over TLS, but the service endpoints presented an expired certificate (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com, issued by CorpLabs Internal CA) and dependent integrations began failing certificate validation. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (EMP-40821) from the Denver office, who noticed API calls from her application returning TLS errors. Load balancer LB-CENTRAL-04 logs showed certificate date invalid and chain validation errors starting at 15:02 UTC, and the outage affected internal application access until the renewed leaf certificate and correct intermediate chain were deployed.
observed_errors: TLS handshake failure: received fatal alert: certificate_unknown
root_cause: The internal web service outage was caused by an expired CA-issued leaf TLS certificate, combined with a missing certificate renewal alert and an outdated intermediate certificate chain still configured on the load balancer.
resolution_steps: Requested and issued a renewed CA-signed leaf certificate (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com, SAN: portal.internal.corplabs.com) from the CorpLabs Internal CA for the affected internal web service endpoint, with approval expedited by Jake Norton (jnorton).

Replaced the expired leaf certificate (serial 4A:7C:9E:01) and updated the full certificate chain on load balancer LB-CENTRAL-04 to use the current CorpLabs Intermediate CA G3 certificate, removing the stale G2 intermediate.

Deployed the renewed certificate bundle to the internal web service endpoints on svc-deploy-07.internal.corplabs.com and rotated or reloaded affected instances so the new certificate was actively served. Deployment coordinated by Kevin Briggs (kbriggs, EMP-30294).
Performed a staged load balancer configuration reload on LB-CENTRAL-04 and LB-CENTRAL-05 to ensure the updated chain was presented consistently across the us-central-1 region and all backend nodes.

Restored and corrected certificate expiration monitoring rule cert-renew-portal-001 (owner reassigned to dmorales and lhwang) so alerts trigger 30 days before expiry, then validated successful TLS handshakes from internal clients including WORKSTATION-MCHEN-D4 (10.42.18.97) and the Austin office without certificate warnings.
agent_questions: We are seeing TLS handshake failures at load balancer LB-CENTRAL-04 for the portal.internal.corplabs.com endpoint. Can you confirm whether internal clients are receiving certificate date warnings or name mismatch errors when connecting to the service endpoint? Please also confirm the client hostname and IP you're testing from so we can correlate with the LB access logs. — Kevin Briggs, Infrastructure Support

title: Unable to connect to Corporate Wi-Fi - EMEA sales
description: Multiple EMEA sales users in the Frankfurt office were trying to connect managed laptops to Corporate Wi-Fi after weekend maintenance, but devices failed during 802.1X authentication and showed authentication failed or Access denied messages in the Wi-Fi client. The issue was first reported by Andrea Brandt (emp ID: EMP-40291) from her workstation WORKSTATION-THINKPAD-AB (IP 10.42.17.88). Users could not obtain network access needed for normal work. The issue affected the Corporate Wi-Fi service path involving the wireless controller, NAC, and device Wi-Fi profile/certificate enrollment.
root_cause: The EAP-TLS certificate presented by the Corporate Wi-Fi service had expired on the wireless controller, causing 802.1X authentication failures and NAC access denials for affected devices; some legacy clients also required profile refresh or manual reprovisioning after certificate replacement.
resolution_steps: Renewed the expired EAP-TLS certificate for Corp-WiFi and installed the replacement certificate and chain on the wireless controller certificate store. Certificate renewal was coordinated by network engineer Priya Nair (pnair).
Restarted the 802.1X/authentication service on the wireless controller so the new certificate was actively presented to connecting clients across the Frankfurt site.

Validated that NAC authentication requests were succeeding again after certificate deployment for users abrandt, leriksson, and moliveira, and that Access Denied responses tied to the expired certificate condition had stopped.

Directed affected users including Andrea Brandt and Lars Eriksson to forget the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID and re-enroll through the CorpConnect enrollment process so devices received the refreshed wireless profile and trust chain. Instructions were also emailed to rmehta@corplabs.com for distribution to the wider Frankfurt sales team.

Completed follow-up remediation for older clients that did not automatically consume the updated profile, including Marta Oliveira's device, using manual profile updates where needed to restore connectivity. Priya Nair confirmed all affected endpoints were back online by 2026-04-29T19:15:00Z.
agent_questions: Hi Andrea — please confirm whether affected users are all failing at the authentication stage with Access denied and whether the issue began after the weekend maintenance window. Also, can you share the hostnames or asset tags of any other impacted devices besides your own (WORKSTATION-THINKPAD-AB)?

title: Device marked noncompliant
description: I'm Rachel Nguyen (employee ID EMP-40291) with a corporate Surface Laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-SURFACE-RN) running Windows 11 21H2. On January 1st, the device was marked as noncompliant in Company Portal and I was immediately blocked from accessing Exchange Online by Conditional Access. The compliance details in Company Portal showed 'Encryption not enabled' even though I had previously enabled BitLocker on the device weeks ago. The device had not checked in to Intune recently — I suspect because I was working remotely from Portland over the holidays — so I could not restore compliant access until Intune re-evaluated the encryption state. This is blocking my ability to send and receive email for Sales team activities.
observed_errors: PolicyEval: referenced policy 'Require device encryption v1' stale
root_cause: A stale Intune compliance policy reference to 'Require device encryption v1', combined with a device check-in older than 48 hours, prevented the current BitLocker encryption signal from being re-evaluated and caused the device to remain in a noncompliant state.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the device WORKSTATION-SURFACE-RN (user rng_nguyen, EMP-40291) had a stale compliance state with last check-in on 2025-12-29T14:22:00Z, and triggered a remote Intune device check-in plus Company Portal sync to force policy and signal refresh.

Reviewed the compliance evaluation details in the Intune admin console and identified that WORKSTATION-SURFACE-RN was still referencing the retired 'Require device encryption v1' policy (policyId: 8a3f-comp-enc-v1) instead of the current encryption requirement 'Require device encryption v2' deployed to Sales-West-Devices.

Updated the Device Compliance policy mapping for the Sales-West-Devices group so WORKSTATION-SURFACE-RN evaluated against 'Require device encryption v2' (policyId: 9b4g-comp-enc-v2) rather than the stale policy reference, and confirmed the assignment propagated in the Intune console.

Allowed the device to complete a fresh compliance re-evaluation cycle and verified the encryption status for WORKSTATION-SURFACE-RN moved from 'EncryptionMissing/pending' to 'Compliant' after sync; Conditional Access block on Exchange Online was lifted and Rachel Nguyen confirmed email access was restored.

Advised Rachel Nguyen (rng_nguyen) to verify BitLocker remained enabled locally via manage-bde -status and to install any pending Windows updates on the Surface Laptop to avoid delayed compliance reporting on the next evaluation cycle. Also recommended periodic manual Company Portal syncs if working remotely from Portland for extended periods to prevent stale check-in issues.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel, thanks for reporting this. Can you confirm whether you've attempted a Company Portal sync recently and whether BitLocker still shows as enabled locally under Settings > Privacy & Security > Device Encryption? In the meantime, I'm pulling up the Intune device record for WORKSTATION-SURFACE-RN (IP 10.47.83.112) to check the last check-in timestamp and compliance evaluation details. I'll also verify the policy assignment under your user object (rng_nguyen) in the Device Compliance Service.

title: Intermittent failure resolving app.internal.corp from internal network
description: Multiple internal users and services were trying to reach the internal application endpoint app.internal.corp from different office subnets (primarily the Newark and Richmond offices), but DNS resolution intermittently failed. Reports were initially filed by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40821) and confirmed by additional users on the 10.16.0.0/16 and 10.18.0.0/16 segments. Some lookups returned NXDOMAIN while others resolved to an outdated IP address (10.20.30.40), preventing dependent services and users from consistently connecting to the application by hostname across the internal network. The issue was first noticed around 05:50 UTC when automated health checks from WORKSTATION-PC-MCHEN began failing.
observed_errors: NXDOMAIN for app.internal.corp from site-A resolvers
Resolver returned stale A record 10.20.30.40 for app.internal.corp despite recent change
root_cause: Stale DNS data for app.internal.corp was being served by internal resolvers, causing intermittent responses between NXDOMAIN and an outdated A record after a record change.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone for app.internal.corp on DNS-AUTH-01 and corrected the A record to the current intended IP address 10.20.31.15 (previously pointing to deprecated 10.20.30.40, last modified by rgarcia on 2026-01-16).

Compared resolver responses from DNS-RES-01 (10.16.0.5, Newark) and DNS-RES-02 (10.18.0.5, Richmond) against the authoritative zone data on DNS-AUTH-01 to confirm that internal resolvers were serving stale or inconsistent results — NXDOMAIN from DNS-RES-01 and 10.20.30.40 from DNS-RES-02.

Flushed DNS caches on the primary (DNS-RES-01) and secondary (DNS-RES-02) internal resolvers and triggered a zone reload on DNS-AUTH-01 so current data would be served immediately across all internal segments.

Retested name resolution for app.internal.corp from previously affected network segments in Newark and Richmond — Maria Chen confirmed from WORKSTATION-PC-MCHEN (10.16.4.87) and David Okafor confirmed from 10.18.2.33 that the hostname consistently returned the correct address 10.20.31.15.

Lowered the TTL for the affected zone record from 3600s to 300s to reduce propagation delay for future DNS changes and documented the update in the DNS change log. Notified rgarcia of the TTL policy adjustment for the internal.corp zone.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts during nightly sync
description: The nightly sync job running under service account svc-nightlysync in us-east-1 began failing around 2025-12-10 09:05 UTC when calls from host WORKSTATION-SYNC-MR to the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corpsys.internal) started returning 504 Gateway Timeout and intermittent 401 Unauthorized responses. The sync workflow orchestrated by the data-integration namespace on Kubernetes stalled, downstream jobs were delayed, and retry activity increased traffic against the API Service endpoint /api/v2/data-sync. The issue was first reported by Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com) from the Atlanta integration engineering team and affected the Integration Gateway path used by the nightly data synchronization process. Approximately 1,400 records queued for sync to the downstream CRM pipeline were blocked.
root_cause: Expired API token on the Integration Gateway caused authentication failures during token refresh, producing 401 responses and triggering aggressive retries that amplified load and led to 504 timeouts during the nightly sync.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token (last valid rotation: 2025-11-09) used by the Integration Gateway service account svc-nightlysync and dependent API clients on igw-prod-east.corpsys.internal so authenticated calls could succeed again. Rotation performed by Marcus Reeves at 14:02 UTC.

Forced a token refresh on the affected integration path (/api/v2/data-sync) and validated that subsequent sync requests from pod IP 10.42.17.88 were accepted without 401 Unauthorized responses. Priya Nair confirmed OAuth handshake success in gateway logs.

Updated the Integration Gateway retry policy for the data-integration namespace to use exponential backoff (initial 2s, max 60s, jitter enabled) with reduced immediate retry pressure to prevent another retry storm during auth failures. Configuration change applied by Priya Nair and reviewed by Daniel Cho (dcho@corplabs.com).

Monitored gateway timeout rate, authentication errors, and downstream job completion on the Monitoring System dashboard for the Atlanta region pipeline after the change to confirm nightly sync processing returned to normal. All 1,400 queued records processed successfully by 15:18 UTC.

Scheduled automated token rotation verification for the svc-nightlysync nightly sync workflow (every 25 days, 5-day buffer before expiry) and added Monitoring System alerting for token refresh failures before the next sync window. Alert notifications configured to route to mreeves@corplabs.com and pnair@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — can you confirm whether a token rotation happened recently for the svc-nightlysync service account and share Integration Gateway log entries from igw-prod-east.corpsys.internal for the 401 and 504 responses between 09:00–09:30 UTC so we can align them with token refresh activity? Also, please verify whether the client IP 10.42.17.88 matches the expected pod source. I'm assigning this to Priya Nair on the platform side for parallel review.

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: Corporate Windows 10 21H2 laptop (hostname LAPTOP-FIN-MREEVES, asset tag FIN-4821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (emp ID EMP-90274) in the Finance group is being flagged noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune. Marcus reports he previously accepted the BitLocker enablement prompt approximately two weeks ago, but encryption never completed. Intune still shows the device as Not encrypted under his enrollment (mreeves@corplabs.com), and no recovery key is visible in Azure AD/Intune for this device. The device remains out of compliance for endpoint encryption requirements, with missing TPM/protector confirmation and no attached device logs to verify whether encryption failed to start or failed before key escrow. Device last checked in from IP 10.22.47.88 at the Philadelphia office.
observed_errors: Device shows as 'Not encrypted' in Intune
No recovery key present in Azure AD / Intune recovery keys
root_cause: BitLocker encryption was not successfully initialized on the endpoint, leaving the device unencrypted and preventing any recovery key from being escrowed to Azure AD/Intune. Available evidence points to an incomplete endpoint-side BitLocker start condition, with TPM/protector readiness and policy application not yet fully confirmed from the device.
resolution_steps: Validated that LAPTOP-FIN-MREEVES (user: Marcus Reeves, EMP-90274) was reporting Not encrypted in Intune and that no recovery key was present in Azure AD/Intune, confirming the compliance failure was due to BitLocker not being active rather than a stale portal display. Checked Device Compliance Service history for the device from IP 10.22.47.88.

Directed collection of endpoint BitLocker state using `manage-bde -status C:` and TPM readiness verification (`Get-Tpm` in PowerShell) on LAPTOP-FIN-MREEVES so the device-side blocker could be identified before retrying enforcement. Remote session initiated by Natasha Williams (nwilliams) with assistance from David Cho.

Confirmed the device must receive the active Intune encryption requirement (policy 'Finance-Encryption-Required') and then forced a policy sync via `Sync-IntuneDevice` so LAPTOP-FIN-MREEVES could re-evaluate BitLocker settings and compliance state under mreeves's enrollment.

Remediated by re-initiating BitLocker enablement on LAPTOP-FIN-MREEVES with a valid TPM-backed protector configuration using `manage-bde -on C: -RecoveryPassword -SkipHardwareTest` so encryption could begin successfully. Confirmed TPM was present and ready but protector had not been properly initialized during the original prompt acceptance.

Ensured the recovery key was escrowed to Azure AD/Intune after BitLocker initialization using `BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector` and then rechecked device compliance in Intune until the encryption requirement reported healthy for LAPTOP-FIN-MREEVES. Final compliance state confirmed as Compliant at 2026-01-28T00:14:00Z. Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com) notified of resolution.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether a TPM is present and ready in Device Manager on LAPTOP-FIN-MREEVES, then run `manage-bde -status C:` from an elevated command prompt and share the Conversion Status, Encryption Percentage, and Key Protectors sections. Also confirm the time of the last Intune sync shown in Company Portal (Settings > Sync). You can reach me at ext. 4417 or email nwilliams@corplabs.com if you need help running the commands. — Natasha Williams, Endpoint Support

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service outage via Load Balancer
description: Internal users and dependent integrations were trying to reach internal-web.internal.example.com over TLS through the internal load balancer (lb-internal-01.infra.example.com), but the endpoint began presenting an expired certificate. Reports were first filed by developer Maria Chen (mchen@example.com, EMP-40821) from the Denver office, who noticed browsers showed certificate warnings and clients encountered TLS handshake failures, with 502/523 errors observed at the load balancer. Additional reports came from integration service account svc-deploy on host WORKSTATION-DEVOPS-MC (10.42.16.88). The outage started when the service certificate expired and prevented normal access to the internal web service until the certificate and chain were corrected on the load balancer.
observed_errors: TLS handshake failure: certificate has expired
502 Bad Gateway via internal load balancer
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal-web.internal.example.com expired on the load balancer, and certificate renewal alerting did not trigger before expiration. The load balancer was also serving an outdated certificate chain, which caused TLS handshake failures and made the internal web service unavailable over HTTPS.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the presented certificate for internal-web.internal.example.com was expired (notAfter: 2025-12-22T23:59:59Z, serial 4A:3F:9C:01) and that the load balancer configuration on lb-internal-01 still referenced the outdated certificate bundle. Verification performed by Raj Patel (rpatel, EMP-55193) using OpenSSL s_client from 10.50.3.22.

Issued a replacement TLS certificate for internal-web.internal.example.com from the internal CA (ca-root-01.infra.example.com) with new validity through 2026-12-22 and prepared the correct full certificate chain including renewed intermediate CN=Example Internal CA G2 for deployment.

Installed the renewed certificate and updated intermediate chain on lb-internal-01 so the load balancer presented the current certificate path to clients. Deployment was executed by rpatel and confirmed via configuration diff on the lb-internal-01 certificate store.

Restarted or reloaded the affected service and load balancer processes on lb-internal-01 to ensure the new certificate bundle was actively served on the endpoint. Service reload was initiated by rpatel at 03:35 UTC and confirmed by Maria Chen (mchen) testing from WORKSTATION-DEVOPS-MC (10.42.16.88).

Validated successful TLS handshakes and health checks against the service endpoint from multiple client IPs (10.42.16.88, 10.50.3.22), confirming certificate warnings and 502/523 load balancer errors were cleared. Full chain verification passed with OpenSSL and browser-based tests by mchen.

Restored and corrected certificate expiry monitoring and renewal alerting (cert-renew-30d policy) so future renewals generate actionable alerts before expiration. Alert re-enabled by Lisa Nguyen (lnguyen) with notifications routed to infra-alerts@example.com and validated with a test fire.

title: Reopened: Print jobs stuck in Finance-Color queue on PS-PRINT-01
description: Finance users in the Charlotte office were trying to print to the shared Finance-Color queue on PS-PRINT-01, but multiple print jobs submitted by team members including Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen, EMP-40821) remained stuck in the queue showing "driver unavailable" or "printer offline" after a driver reinstall performed earlier in the week by technician Marcus Bell. The issue affected several Finance workstations (including WORKSTATION-FIN-RN and WORKSTATION-FIN-DK) and blocked normal color printing until the queue-to-driver mapping on the print server was corrected.
root_cause: The Finance-Color queue on PS-PRINT-01 remained mapped to a stale or incorrect driver instance after a partial driver reinstall, causing the print spooler to treat queued jobs as driver unavailable and leave new submissions stuck.

title: Windows laptop slow after login
description: My company-issued Windows 10 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LPT-MCHEN) becomes extremely slow immediately after login. I'm logged in as mchen (employee ID EMP-90274) and working from the Denver office. Task Manager shows Microsoft Defender Antivirus (MsMpEng.exe) consuming roughly 80-95% CPU with sustained disk activity from svchost, causing delayed application launches and poor interactive performance. Telemetry from the Endpoint Management Agent indicates queued endpoint protection scans are starting at my login while the system also has low free disk space on C: (about 8%), increasing I/O contention and extending scan impact. This is severely affecting my ability to work — Visual Studio and other engineering tools take 5+ minutes to become responsive.
observed_errors: Sustained high disk I/O by svchost
root_cause: Queued Microsoft Defender endpoint protection scans were starting at user login and competing for CPU and disk on a device with only 8% free disk space, causing prolonged performance degradation after sign-in.
resolution_steps: Cleared the 14 queued endpoint protection scan backlog on the affected laptop WORKSTATION-LPT-MCHEN (user mchen) to stop repeated high-CPU post-login scan activity. Kevin Ortiz performed the backlog flush via the Endpoint Protection console.

Changed endpoint protection scan scheduling for the Denver Engineering device group so full or prioritized scans run during off-hours (after 22:00 local) instead of at user login, preventing future catch-up scan storms.

Adjusted scan policy to stagger scan start times across devices in the Denver Engineering group and enforce a 30% CPU throttle cap during active user sessions, reducing CPU impact when scans do overlap with interactive use.

Reclaimed approximately 28 GB of local disk space on WORKSTATION-LPT-MCHEN by removing temporary files from C:\Users\mchen\AppData\Local\Temp, clearing Windows Update cache, and purging other unneeded data so the system maintains more than 15% free space and reduces scan-related disk contention.

Validated after policy and cleanup changes that CPU and disk utilization on WORKSTATION-LPT-MCHEN normalize within 3 minutes after login for user mchen and application launch performance (Visual Studio, browser, Teams) returns to expected levels — confirmed by mchen on 2026-02-09.

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failures for service1.corp.local
description: Multiple internal application owners, including Raj Patel (DevOps lead) and members of the platform engineering team, were trying to reach service1.corp.local from several private subnets (10.20.0.0/16 and 10.30.0.0/16), but DNS lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or timed out, causing application timeouts for service1 and the internal-api-gateway. The issue was first reported from workstations in the Arlington datacenter and began after a recent internal A record update on 2026-01-11; authoritative DNS servers (ns1.corp.local, ns2.corp.local) returned the new IP 10.50.12.40, but some recursive resolvers—specifically dns-resolver-01.corp.local and dns-resolver-02.corp.local—continued serving stale or negative responses, creating inconsistent name resolution across the environment. Raj initially opened the ticket after receiving alerts from Network Monitoring on his workstation WORKSTATION-RPL-4417.
root_cause: A recent update to the service1.corp.local A record was not being resolved consistently because one internal resolver cluster lacked the required conditional forwarder for the corp.local zone, and affected resolvers retained stale negative and outdated cached responses. This caused some clients to receive the correct authoritative answer while others received NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or timeouts until forwarding and cache state were corrected.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the authoritative DNS zone on ns1.corp.local and ns2.corp.local for service1.corp.local contained the intended current A record (10.50.12.40) and verified the low TTL (300s) and recent record change by kliu on 2026-01-11T21:47Z were correct.

Compared responses from authoritative servers (ns1.corp.local, ns2.corp.local), known-good recursive resolver dns-resolver-03.corp.local, and the affected resolver cluster (dns-resolver-01.corp.local, dns-resolver-02.corp.local) to isolate inconsistent behavior to internal recursive resolution in the Arlington datacenter rather than the zone itself.

Added the missing conditional forwarder configuration for the corp.local zone on dns-resolver-02.corp.local (10.50.1.11) so requests for the internal zone were routed to the correct authoritative path (ns1.corp.local, ns2.corp.local). Change performed by Marcus Webb (mwebb) and verified by Karen Liu.

Flushed caches on dns-resolver-01.corp.local (10.50.1.10) and dns-resolver-02.corp.local (10.50.1.11) using rndc flush to remove stale positive and negative cached entries that were continuing to return NXDOMAIN and timeouts after the record change. Verified cache clear via rndc dumpdb on both nodes.

Validated successful resolution of service1.corp.local from all monitored subnets — confirmed from rpatel's workstation at 10.20.5.88, pnair's host at 10.30.4.62, and additional test clients on 10.40.0.0/16 that all clients now received the same current address (10.50.12.40) consistently.

Continued monitoring via Network Monitoring dashboards after the change and performed staggered follow-up cache clearing on secondary caching layers where residual historical cache entries still produced intermittent lookup failures. Marcus Webb confirmed full resolution stability at 2026-01-12T14:30Z and notified rpatel and pnair via email.
agent_questions: Hi Raj — we are comparing DNS results across internal subnets. Could you confirm whether failures are limited to specific networks (e.g., 10.20.0.0/16 vs 10.30.0.0/16) and whether any clients can still resolve service1.corp.local successfully? Also, please let us know if the issue is observed from your workstation WORKSTATION-RPL-4417 at 10.20.5.88 or from other hosts as well. We've looped in Karen Liu (karen.liu@corplabs.com) from the DNS infrastructure team to assist. — Marcus Webb, Network Operations

title: Outlook mailboxes not syncing (desktop and mobile) — Exchange Online
description: Multiple users in the Sales - Mobile Users group (primarily based out of the Charlotte office) reported that Outlook Desktop and Outlook Mobile stopped syncing email for their Exchange Online mailboxes following the February 15 profile update rollout. The issue was first escalated by Rachel Dominguez (rdominguez@corplabs.com) who noticed her desktop Outlook showed a Disconnected state and her iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RD) had not received new messages in over 6 hours. Additional reports came from Marcus Yee (emp ID: EMP-40821) and at least three other sales reps on both Windows 10 and iOS 15 devices. Tenant service health dashboard showed no Exchange Online outage, pointing to a client/profile sync problem rather than a platform-wide issue.
observed_errors: Mobile client: mailbox last sync 6+ hours ago
root_cause: Stale and corrupted Outlook client profile state after the recent profile update rollout caused invalid cached mailbox settings and offline sync data, preventing a clean Exchange Online sync session; some affected mobile partnerships also required reset before full mailbox synchronization resumed.
resolution_steps: Verified Exchange Online tenant health via the Microsoft 365 admin center and confirmed no platform-wide outage or service advisory for the us-east-1 region before focusing on affected user endpoints (DESKTOP-RDOMINGUEZ, DESKTOP-MYEE) and their profile state.

Created new Outlook desktop profiles for impacted users — Rachel Dominguez (rdominguez@corplabs.com) and Marcus Yee (myee@corplabs.com) — and re-added their Exchange Online mailboxes to replace stale profile configuration and corrupted local OST sync state. Old .ost files were renamed for reference.

Validated Autodiscover responses (Test-OutlookConnectivity) and refreshed cached mailbox settings on both DESKTOP-RDOMINGUEZ and DESKTOP-MYEE so the rebuilt profiles established a healthy connection to Exchange Online without residual stale endpoint data.

Cleared existing mobile sync partnerships for affected devices — including WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RD (Rachel Dominguez) and Marcus Yee's managed iPhone — using Remove-MobileDevicePartnership in Exchange Online PowerShell, then forced re-enrollment and re-sync so mobile mail clients could establish a clean mailbox partnership.

Confirmed mailbox updates resumed on desktop and mobile clients for all affected Sales - Mobile Users in the Charlotte office. Provided support guidance authored by Kevin Pratt (kpratt@corplabs.com) to recreate the Outlook profile and refresh Autodiscover again if the disconnected state recurs after future profile update rollouts.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether Outlook shows Disconnected on your desktop (hostname DESKTOP-RDOMINGUEZ) and whether the same mailbox (rdominguez@corplabs.com) is also delayed on your mobile device. Can you also advise whether this started immediately after the February 15 profile update rollout? We'd like to verify the same behavior on Marcus Yee's devices as well before proceeding.

My employee ID is EMP-40821 and I can be reached at mreeves@corplabs.com or +49-170-448-2913 if further info is needed.
observed_errors: TLS handshake failed; session tear down observed ~10s post-auth
client presented device certificate with expiry date 2026-02-14
GlobalProtect log: tunnel tear-down reason 118 (auth failed)
