Have Marcus Reeves complete Okta MFA again and verify the VPN tunnel remains established beyond the prior 8-15 second failure window; confirm stable connectivity from source IP 85.214.67.103 for at least 5 minutes.

Confirm access to required internal applications such as the HR Portal, Confluence, and JIRA from WORKSTATION-LT-MREEVES, and document the renewed certificate (new serial and expiry) and profile refresh as the corrective action in the CMDB record for EMP-40821.

title: BitLocker encryption not enabled
description: Managed Windows 10 21H2 Azure AD joined device (hostname: WORKSTATION-SALES-MR) assigned to Marcus Reeves (emp ID: EMP-40218) in the Portland office was flagged noncompliant for disk encryption shortly after provisioning on 2026-01-20. BitLocker never started on the endpoint (IP: 10.42.17.83), Intune showed the encryption policy was not applied, and the recovery key was not visible in Azure AD/Intune escrow. This blocked the device from meeting security compliance requirements for user mreeves@corplabs.com, who needs access to Sales resources by end of week.
root_cause: BitLocker did not start because the TPM protector was not initialized on the endpoint, and the assigned Intune disk encryption policy had not successfully applied. Without an active protector and policy enforcement, recovery key escrow to Azure AD failed.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM state on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR (assigned to Marcus Reeves, mreeves, EMP-40218) using Get-Tpm and Initialize-Tpm, then initialized a TPM protector via manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm so BitLocker could use hardware-backed protection.

Started BitLocker encryption on the C: system drive of WORKSTATION-SALES-MR using manage-bde -on C: and monitored the device via Get-BitLockerVolume until encryption percentage began increasing successfully.

Reviewed the Intune disk encryption policy 'BL-Win10-Sales-West' assignment and added WORKSTATION-SALES-MR to AAD security group 'SG-Encryption-Sales', reapplying/re-scoping the policy to ensure the device received the required encryption configuration.

Forced an Intune device sync from the Endpoint Manager portal for WORKSTATION-SALES-MR after the policy correction so the endpoint could process the updated encryption settings and report compliance status.

Verified the recovery key was successfully escrowed to Azure AD/Intune for WORKSTATION-SALES-MR (user mreeves@corplabs.com) and confirmed the device returned to an encryption-compliant state in the Device Compliance Service dashboard. Notified Marcus Reeves at ext. 4-7193 that the device is now compliant.
agent_questions: Checking the encryption failure on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR for user mreeves (Marcus Reeves, EMP-40218): please confirm whether BitLocker ever started on the device and whether the recovery key appears in Intune or Azure AD. I can see the device was enrolled on 2026-01-20 but the compliance dashboard currently shows it as noncompliant for encryption. Also verifying whether the Intune disk encryption policy 'BL-Win10-Sales-West' was targeted to the correct device group.

title: Unable to connect to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: I'm Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) on a Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) in Engineering at the Durham office. I was trying to reconnect to the Corporate Wi-Fi after a scheduled wireless profile update this morning. The Corporate SSID was visible and the device associated briefly, but then showed "Connected, no network access" and disconnected within about a minute. I could not reach internal resources such as the Engineering wiki or source repos, and a reboot did not resolve the issue. Re-enrollment improved service, but intermittent drops continued when connecting through specific access points on the 3rd floor.
root_cause: Corrupt client-side Corporate Wi-Fi profile entries and cached supplicant state on the endpoint caused repeated 802.1X re-authentication after the profile push; a subset of access points continued to trigger intermittent disconnect behavior until controller-side stability was verified.
resolution_steps: Removed the stale and corrupt Corporate Wi-Fi profile from the affected Windows 10 endpoint (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN, user rnguyen, EMP-40821) and cleared cached supplicant entries tied to the old profile, including residual certificate references from the prior enrollment cycle.

Re-enrolled the laptop to Corporate Wi-Fi using the current standard wireless profile template and verified the endpoint received a valid IP lease (10.42.18.97) after reconnecting to the Durham office network.

Confirmed the device wireless certificate and authentication state were valid after profile re-registration so 802.1X authentication could complete normally; Kevin Marsh validated the certificate chain on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN matched the current CA trust anchor.

Applied a temporary connectivity stabilization policy during recovery for rnguyen's device, then validated that the device maintained association without repeated re-authentication loops across multiple access points on the Durham 3rd floor.

Reviewed controller behavior for the access points involved in the user session (including AP-DURHAM-3F-07) and confirmed stable connectivity after remediation, closing the incident once internal resource access was restored for Rachel Nguyen per verification by Priya Desai.

title: Users unable to join Corporate Wi‑Fi
description: Multiple corporate staff at the Frankfurt office were trying to join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-5G) on managed devices starting around 06:30 UTC. 802.1X authentication via EAP-TLS completed successfully, but affected endpoints were immediately placed into NAC quarantine or showed limited connectivity with repeated disconnects. Users such as Elena Richter (e.richter@corplabs.com) and Markus Hahn reported they could associate to the SSID but could not obtain normal network access needed for routine work. Initial reports were gathered by service desk analyst Priya Nair (EMP-40821). Evidence from ClearPass Policy Manager (cppm-emea-01.corplabs.internal) and the wireless controller (WLC-FRA-02) pointed to a policy assignment mismatch affecting the Corporate device group rather than a credential failure.
observed_errors: Client placed in NAC quarantine with no network access
WLC reports frequent client disconnects post-association
root_cause: ClearPass NAC policy assignment for the Corporate device group was misconfigured, causing successfully authenticated endpoints to be evaluated against a deny/quarantine policy instead of the intended allow policy.
resolution_steps: Updated the ClearPass enforcement and role-mapping policy on cppm-emea-01.corplabs.internal so the Corporate device group (Role: Corp-Managed) matched the correct Corp-Allow enforcement profile instead of the Quarantine-Deny policy after successful 802.1X EAP-TLS authentication. Change performed by Anil Kapoor (akapoor, EMP-60193).

Validated and corrected SSID-to-policy mapping with the Wireless Controller team on WLC-FRA-02 to ensure the Corporate SSID (CorpNet-5G) was sending the expected RADIUS attributes (including NAS-Identifier and Called-Station-Id) used by ClearPass policy evaluation.

Removed affected endpoints — including WORKSTATION-ERICHTER (10.47.12.88) and WORKSTATION-MHAHN (10.47.13.41) — from NAC quarantine and re-enrolled devices that had stale or mismatched posture/group state so they could be re-evaluated under the corrected Corp-Allow policy.

Retested representative affected clients on the Corporate SSID, including Elena Richter's and Markus Hahn's devices, and confirmed they received normal network access (correct VLAN, full connectivity) without repeated disconnects or quarantine placement.

Monitored ClearPass Access Tracker and WLC-FRA-02 client events for 48 hours after the change to verify policy decisions remained consistent and no new deny mismatches were occurring for the Corporate device group. Priya Nair (EMP-40821) confirmed no further user reports were received.
agent_questions: Hi — please confirm whether affected users (e.g., erichter, mhahn) can complete the Corporate SSID sign-in and then immediately lose access, or whether the failure occurs before authentication. Also advise if the issue affects multiple managed devices and whether it is limited to the Frankfurt site or spans other EMEA locations. If possible, share the MAC address or hostname of one affected device so we can trace the ClearPass session.

title: Nightly integration timeouts via Integration Gateway (03:00 UTC)
description: Nightly batch data sync jobs sent through the Integration Gateway to the downstream partner (Acme Data Services) are failing around 03:00 UTC in us-east-1. The gateway returns 504 Gateway Timeout for POST /sync during the scheduled run window, and monitoring shows a matching latency spike at the same time. This is delaying the partner data synchronization workflow for batch-sync-users. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Dallas integration operations team. Current telemetry is incomplete because request correlation IDs and token rotation history were not available in the original evidence. The affected API client ID is intg-client-batch-7741, and the integration service account username is svc_batchsync. Requests originate from host WORKSTATION-INTGOPS-MD (10.42.18.97).
root_cause: Downstream API latency during the 03:00 UTC batch window exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout window, producing 504 Gateway Timeout responses for POST /sync. Token expiry was considered but not supported by available evidence because gateway and API log review found no authentication failures or 401 errors.
resolution_steps: Correlated the nightly failure window (03:00–03:12 UTC on 2025-12-04) with Monitoring System data (alert group intg-latency-critical) and confirmed that elevated downstream latency (p95 of 45s) aligned with the Integration Gateway 504 responses for POST /sync around 03:00 UTC on gateway node gw-east-01. Analysis performed by Kevin Ortiz (kortiz) using source IP 10.42.18.97 request logs.

Reviewed Integration Gateway (gw-east-01) and API Service logs for authentication failures and token-related errors for service account svc_batchsync / client ID intg-client-batch-7741; no 401 responses or explicit token rejection events were present, reducing likelihood of expired credentials as the primary cause. Confirmed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Classified the incident as downstream latency (Acme Data Services partner endpoint) exceeding the 15-second gateway timeout window rather than an authentication failure and prepared evidence package for service owner escalation. Rachel Simmons (rsimmons, EMP-41503) approved the classification.

Escalated the recurring 03:00 UTC latency condition to the downstream service owners/vendor (Acme Data Services, vendor ticket ref: ACME-INC-2291) for remediation of the partner-side performance issue during the batch sync window. Escalation contact: Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) designated as corplabs liaison.

Recommended increasing retry/backoff tolerance (from 2 retries with 5s backoff to 4 retries with exponential backoff up to 60s) or adjusting the gateway timeout window from 15s to 45s for the nightly sync path as an operational mitigation until the downstream latency issue is corrected. Change request to be submitted by Kevin Ortiz (kortiz) pending approval from the Dallas integration operations team.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please provide the API client ID (confirmed intg-client-batch-7741), last token rotation date for svc_batchsync, and a sample request ID or precise failure timestamp so we can correlate gateway events with monitoring traces and rule out credential issues. Also looping in Priya Nair (pnair) from the API platform team to assist with downstream trace analysis. You can reach her at pnair@corplabs.com. — Kevin Ortiz, Integration Support (EMP-60738)

title: Cannot connect to Corporate Wi‑Fi — authentication fails

Validated that controller WLC-PDX-01 and RADIUS authentication flows on ISE-WEST-02 no longer returned certificate-expiration failures during EAP negotiation for test user mreynolds.
Had the user Marcus Reynolds forget and re-add the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) on LAPTOP-SALES-MR so the endpoint would refresh the wireless profile association and trust state.

Re-enrolled the affected device credentials/profile for mreynolds (E-20841) on LAPTOP-SALES-MR and confirmed the laptop received normal network access (DHCP-assigned IP 10.31.44.112) after reconnecting to Corporate Wi-Fi at the Portland office.

title: Device reported noncompliant: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key missing
description: A corporate Dell Latitude 5520 (hostname LAPTOP-DL5520-MR) assigned to Marcus Reeves (emp ID E-40287) in the Columbus office was showing as not encrypted in Intune and marked noncompliant by the Device Compliance Service for disk encryption. Verified that the BitLocker recovery key successfully escrowed to Azure AD (key ID visible under device record for mreeves) and confirmed the device LAPTOP-DL5520-MR returned to compliant status in the Device Compliance Service. Notified Marcus Reeves at marcus.reeves@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.

title: Print jobs stuck on ps-nyc-print01
description: Multiple users in the NYC office reported by floor coordinator Maria Chen were trying to print to shared queue HP-Color-01 on print server ps-nyc-print01, but jobs remained held in the queue and reported driver unavailable errors instead of completing. The issue was initially reported by user dkumar (employee ID EMP-40821) from workstation WORKSTATION-PC-DK at IP 10.22.17.45, who submitted a print job at approximately 08:15 and noticed it never reached the physical printer. Restarting the Print Spooler temporarily cleared blocked jobs, but new print attempts failed again within minutes. The issue affected office printing for all users in the Manhattan office relying on the shared server-hosted queue until the server driver package was validated and corrected.
observed_errors: Spooler log: Failed to bind driver - checksum mismatch
root_cause: Corrupted printer driver package HP-Color-Driver-v5.2 on ps-nyc-print01 caused checksum mismatch and prevented the queue from binding the correct driver, leaving jobs stuck in Held status.
resolution_steps: Removed the corrupted HP-Color-Driver-v5.2 package from print server ps-nyc-print01 using the Print Management console, clearing all cached driver files from the C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\x64 directory.
Installed the approved HP-Color-Driver-v5.2 package from the central repository (\\repo-nyc-fs01\PrintDrivers\HP-Color-v5.2) after validating it against the approved SHA256 checksum (9a3f...c7b1).
Cleared all 14 stuck jobs from queue HP-Color-01 and restarted the Print Spooler service on ps-nyc-print01 to reload the corrected driver files into memory.
Remapped queue HP-Color-01 to the newly installed driver package on ps-nyc-print01 to restore proper driver binding, and confirmed the queue status returned to Ready.

Ran validation test prints from workstations of dkumar (WORKSTATION-PC-DK), jpark, and tnguyen through the shared queue and confirmed all jobs processed successfully without recurring driver unavailable errors. Notified floor coordinator Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) that printing was restored.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether all affected users are printing through shared queue HP-Color-01 on ps-nyc-print01 and whether jobs are staying in the queue with a driver unavailable message. Can you also verify if user dkumar and the other reporters (jpark, tnguyen) are all connecting via the same mapped printer path? I'm checking from my end as well. — Agent R. Hoffman

title: account locked
description: I (Danielle Moreau, emp ID EMP-40291) was trying to sign in to the SSO Portal from my iPhone on the morning of 2025-11-21 but received an AccountLockedException after repeated failed authentication attempts. I also attempted a self-service password reset through the Password Reset Portal using the link sent to d.moreau@corplabs.com, but the reset token/link was already expired, preventing completion of the reset. The lockout blocked access to SSO-connected applications including Outlook Mobile until the account was unlocked and stale mobile credentials were removed. My device was connecting from IP 74.112.46.88.
observed_errors: Multiple failed authentication attempts (AD lockout event)
root_cause: Cached stale credentials on the user's iPhone continued submitting failed authentication attempts to Active Directory, triggering the account lockout policy. A separate expired self-service password reset token prevented the user from completing recovery until a new token was issued.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Active Directory lockout activity on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and confirmed 14 repeated failed sign-in attempts (Event ID 4740) were originating from the user's iPhone (IPHONE-DM-SALES, IP 74.112.46.88) for account dmoreau.
Unlocked dmoreau's Active Directory account on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal to restore access after the lockout threshold of 10 failed attempts had been reached.
Issued a new password reset token through the Password Reset Portal to d.moreau@corplabs.com and confirmed user Danielle Moreau could complete the password reset with the current token at 17:24 UTC.

Instructed the user to remove or clear saved account credentials for dmoreau on the mobile device IPHONE-DM-SALES (Outlook Mobile and SSO Portal apps) and re-add the account with the newly reset password.

Monitored post-reset authentication activity for account dmoreau on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal for approximately 2 hours (until ~19:30 UTC) and confirmed no additional failed sign-in bursts or repeat lockouts occurred.
agent_questions: Hi Danielle — I reviewed the lockout activity for your account (username: dmoreau) and it appears repeated failed sign-ins are coming from your iPhone (device hostname IPHONE-DM-SALES). The authentication logs on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal show 14 failed attempts between 07:42 and 08:11 UTC from source IP 74.112.46.88. Please confirm whether your mobile mail or SSO apps were still trying to sign in this morning.

title: Users unable to authenticate to Corporate Wi‑Fi
description: Multiple Engineering users in the Frankfurt office (EMEA Building 3) were trying to connect managed Windows 10 and macOS 12 laptops to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure), but 802.1X authentication failed and devices received no usable network access after joining. The issue was first reported by Elena Vasquez (emp ID ENG-4821) at approximately 08:15 local time and quickly confirmed by several teammates on the same floor. Affected devices included hostnames such as LAPTOP-EVASQUEZ and LAPTOP-MKORNER. The issue impacted access to internal resources during the morning and persisted for a subset of laptops after the initial controller-side fix because those endpoints retained bad cached wireless profiles.
root_cause: Expired RADIUS certificate on the Wireless Controller caused 802.1X authentication failures, and some affected laptops continued to fail after certificate renewal due to cached or corrupt corporate Wi-Fi profiles that required removal and MDM re-enrollment.
resolution_steps: Renewed the Wireless Controller (WLC-FRA-01) RADIUS certificate — replacing expired serial 4A:7C:03:EE — and verified the certificate chain presented for 802.1X EAP-TLS authentication was valid again. Renewal was performed by network engineer Priya Nair (pnair).

Validated controller and authentication behavior after renewal to confirm clients could successfully associate and complete 802.1X authentication. Spot-checked RADIUS session logs for users evasquez and mkorner to verify successful handshake completion.

Identified laptops still failing after the controller fix — LAPTOP-EVASQUEZ, LAPTOP-MKORNER, and LAPTOP-JLINDGREN — as having cached or corrupt corporate Wi-Fi profiles referencing the old certificate thumbprint rather than an active controller certificate issue.

Removed the affected CorpNet-Secure wireless profiles from impacted endpoints and re-enrolled those devices through MDM to push a clean corporate Wi-Fi profile and certificate configuration. Desktop support technician Amir Haddad (ahaddad) coordinated remotely with each user to complete the process.

Reviewed and normalized the temporary NAC policy adjustment (remediation VLAN assignment) so successfully authenticated devices received the intended Engineering access policy after remediation. Confirmed with Priya Nair that no stale policy overrides remained.

Monitored rejoin and authentication results for affected users — Elena Vasquez, Marcus Korner, and Jonas Lindgren — over the following 24 hours to confirm stable Corporate Wi-Fi access was restored. All three devices maintained persistent connectivity with no further 802.1X failures.

title: Print jobs stuck — driver unavailable on Print Server PS-PRINT01
description: Finance users in the Charlotte office were trying to print to shared printers through print server PS-PRINT01 after a recent maintenance window on 2026-02-24, but jobs remained stuck in the server queue (PRN-Queue) and client systems showed 'printer offline' and 'driver unavailable' messages. The issue was initially reported by Maria Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40291) and subsequently confirmed by at least five other Finance team members. The problem affected multiple shared printers mapped via PS-PRINT01 and blocked normal document printing—including time-sensitive month-end financial reports—until the print queue and driver package on the server were corrected.
root_cause: Corruption in printer driver package DriverPkg_v3.2 on PS-PRINT01 caused spooler DLL load failures, preventing driver initialization and leaving shared printer queues in a stale offline state.
resolution_steps: Cleared all 37 stuck jobs from the affected shared queues (PRN-Queue) on PS-PRINT01 to remove the backlog created while the driver was failing. Notified affected users including Maria Delgado (mdelgado) and James Okafor (jokafor) that their pending jobs would need to be resubmitted.

Restarted the Print Spooler service on PS-PRINT01 via services.msc and confirmed the service returned to a stable running state (PID verified) before further changes. Monitored for 60 seconds to ensure no immediate crash-loop behavior.

Removed the corrupt DriverPkg_v3.2 package from PS-PRINT01 using Print Management and installed the approved replacement package DriverPkg_v3.2.1 from the Workplace Services driver repository (\\fs-workplace01\drivers\approved\DriverPkg_v3.2.1). Verified DLL integrity of pcldrv32.dll post-installation.

Re-associated the affected printer queues on PS-PRINT01 with DriverPkg_v3.2.1 so that client workstations in the Charlotte Finance group no longer referenced the failed driver package. Confirmed queue-to-driver mapping via Print Management snap-in.

Validated successful test prints from multiple client machines—WORKSTATION-PC-MD (mdelgado, 10.42.18.77) and WORKSTATION-PC-JO (jokafor, 10.42.18.83)—and asked Linda Pratt (lpratt) to confirm printing from her workstation. Monitored spooler and Event Viewer logs on PS-PRINT01 for 2 hours with no repeat 'driver unavailable' or DLL load failure events. Sent confirmation to the Finance team via r.nakamura@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — thanks for reporting this. Can you confirm whether all affected Finance users in Charlotte are printing through PS-PRINT01, and whether the issue started after the maintenance window that ran on the evening of 2026-02-24? Also, could you let me know the hostnames of any client machines experiencing the problem so we can cross-reference spooler logs? You can reach me at ext. 4718 or at r.nakamura@corplabs.com if it's easier to send screenshots.

title: account locked after password reset
description: User Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40291) from the Phoenix office reset their password through the Password Reset Portal after multiple failed sign-in attempts, but remained unable to access the SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) or email because the account was still showing as locked. AD security evidence on DC-EAST-02.corplabs.internal indicates repeated authentication failures (Event ID 4625) continued from an iOS mobile device at IP 10.47.83.112 using stale cached credentials, preventing the new password from taking effect and blocking normal account access.
observed_errors: AD lockout entry observed in security logs
Repeated 4625 failed logon events from device IP (mobile)
root_cause: Active Directory lockout policy was triggered by repeated failed authentication attempts from a mobile device holding cached or expired credentials. After the user reset the password, the failing mobile authentication source continued submitting stale credentials, and the prior reset token state did not successfully restore access before the account relocked.
resolution_steps: Identity Tier 2 agent Priya Nair unlocked the AD account for mdelgado (CN=mdelgado,OU=Sales,OU=Corp Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) on DC-EAST-02.corplabs.internal and cleared the active lockout condition so new authentication attempts could be evaluated normally.

A fresh password reset token was issued via the Password Reset Portal for mdelgado and the user was contacted at mdelgado@corplabs.com with instructions to complete the reset again to ensure a current valid credential was written to directory-backed authentication services.

Marcus Delgado was directed to remove and re-enter saved credentials on the affected iOS mail client on device IPHONE-MD-SALES, including removing the Exchange ActiveSync profile and re-adding it with the new password, to stop stale password submissions from the mobile device.

The repeated failed authentication source from mobile device IPHONE-MD-SALES at IP 10.47.83.112 was reviewed and contained by temporarily blocking the device partnership in Exchange ActiveSync so it no longer triggered additional AD lockouts for mdelgado.

Post-change monitoring was performed by Priya Nair on lockout activity (Event ID 4740) and failed sign-in events (Event ID 4625) for mdelgado over a 2-hour window to confirm the account stopped relocking and Marcus Delgado could resume access to SSO Portal and email from both WORKSTATION-MBPRO-MD and IPHONE-MD-SALES.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Users and internal monitoring were trying to reach the internal web service at portal.corplabs.internal over HTTPS, but browser sessions showed certificate warnings and dependent connections failed TLS validation. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40821) from the Austin office. The load balancer LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal logged TLS handshake failures after the service certificate passed its expiration date, which blocked normal access to the internal-portal and auth-service for internal developers. Additional reports came in from developers connecting from workstations including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC and IP 10.22.47.115.
root_cause: The TLS certificate deployed for the internal web service expired on 2025-12-24, and the load balancer continued serving the old certificate chain, resulting in TLS handshake failures and client certificate warnings.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the production service certificate for portal.corplabs.internal had expired and requested a renewed certificate from the internal Certificate Authority CA-INT-01.corplabs.internal. CSR was generated by Ryan Jackson (rjackson) and submitted via the cert-request portal.
Uploaded the renewed server certificate (serial 7B:22:AE:05:DC) and complete certificate chain to the load balancer LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal, replacing the expired PEM bundle in /etc/ssl/portal/.

Updated the load balancer listener or TLS proxy configuration on LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal so the service presented the renewed certificate instead of the expired chain. Listener on port 443 was rebound to the new PEM bundle by rjackson.
Restarted or reloaded the load balancer TLS process on LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal to apply the certificate change cleanly. Service reload was performed by Ryan Jackson at 03:12 UTC.

Validated successful HTTPS connectivity and confirmed the served certificate chain and handshake behavior were healthy from the client side. Maria Chen (mchen) and David Okonkwo (dokonkwo) verified access from their workstations at IPs 10.22.47.115 and 10.22.48.203 respectively, confirming no further certificate warnings.

Restored and tested certificate renewal alerting on MON-EAST-01.corplabs.internal so future expiration conditions are detected before service impact. Alerts now route to rjackson@corplabs.com and infra-alerts@corplabs.com with a 30-day advance window.
agent_questions: We are checking whether the issue is caused by an expired endpoint certificate or an incomplete chain on the load balancer LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal. Please confirm whether users are seeing browser certificate warnings or only generic connection failures. This was escalated by rjackson@corplabs.com from the network operations team. You can also reach me at ext 4-7823 if needed.

title: Cannot connect to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Several managed laptops on the 4th floor of the Birmingham office could see and join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-5G), but users including Rachel Whitfield (r.whitfield@corplabs.com) and Marcus Okonkwo were either denied access during EAP-TLS sign-in or left without usable network connectivity after attempting to connect. The issue appeared on a subset of corporate devices (approximately 6 endpoints) rather than across the whole wireless environment and prevented affected users from working normally on office Wi-Fi. Ticket raised by network liaison Priya Nair (EMP-40821).
observed_errors: RADIUS: Access-Reject due to certificate validation failure
root_cause: A subset of managed endpoints had stale or missing corporate Wi-Fi profile and trust settings, causing NAC policy rejection during 802.1X authentication.
resolution_steps: Re-enroll the current corporate Wi-Fi profile on all six affected devices (including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RW and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MO) via Intune forced sync to restore the expected CorpNet-5G SSID, trust chain, and renewed EAP-TLS client certificate configuration.

Force device compliance check-in for each endpoint and confirm the endpoints meet the NAC posture requirements for corporate wireless access; verify updated status in the Intune compliance dashboard and clear any 'Non-Compliant' flags for the Birmingham 4th-floor device group.

Validate successful 802.1X authentication and correct VLAN 120 network policy assignment by reconnecting test devices (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RW — user r.whitfield, and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MO — user m.okonkwo) to Corporate Wi-Fi and confirming full network connectivity with Priya Nair and affected users.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please confirm whether the Wi-Fi failure is affecting multiple users on the Birmingham 4th-floor area and whether devices connect to the CorpNet-5G SSID but fail during 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentication rather than showing no signal. Could you also share the hostnames or MAC addresses of two or three affected machines so we can cross-reference RADIUS logs?

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to Finance shared drive
description: I was trying to open the Finance department folder from my mapped shared drive (F:\Finance) on my workstation WORKSTATION-PC-LM while connected to the corporate network at the Charlotte office, but received Access Denied (0x80070005) and intermittent credential prompts after my Active Directory group membership was updated by our IT admin earlier the same day. My username is lmorales and I had been able to access the Finance files without issue prior to the group change. The issue blocked access to all Finance files on \\FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal\Finance$, with evidence pointing to both permission inconsistency on the file server and delayed recognition of updated AD entitlements.
observed_errors: The requested operation requires elevation (ACL mismatch observed)
root_cause: Access was denied because the user's effective permissions were inconsistent across identity and file-server layers: the user was not currently reflected in the expected FINANCE_USERS access path at first check, the file server had not yet refreshed group membership data after the AD change, and a legacy explicit per-user ACE on the Finance folder introduced contradictory ACL evidence. Standardizing access back to group-based permissions and refreshing server/user security context resolved the mismatch.
resolution_steps: Verified the intended access model for the Finance share on FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal and confirmed that lmorales (Laura Morales, EMP-90234) should receive access through the FINANCE_USERS security group rather than through a manual per-user ACL entry.

Added and confirmed lmorales in FINANCE_USERS via Active Directory (change originally initiated by rjensen) and validated that the membership change had replicated across domain controllers in us-east-1 before retesting access.

Forced FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal to refresh its view of AD-backed security context using klist purge on the server and refreshed SMB/Netlogon dependency services where operationally safe to clear stale group evaluation for lmorales's SID.

Removed the unexpected explicit allow ACE for lmorales's individual SID from the Finance folder on FS-EAST-02 after review with the Finance team lead, and re-applied inherited permissions according to the standard Finance share ACL policy granting access via FINANCE_USERS.

Cleared Laura Morales's cached credentials in Windows Credential Manager on WORKSTATION-PC-LM (10.22.47.88), disconnected and remapped the F: drive to \\FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal\Finance$, and had the user establish a fresh Kerberos session token before validation.

Retested the current Finance shared-drive path (F:\Finance) from WORKSTATION-PC-LM and confirmed the folder opened successfully without Access Denied. Laura confirmed she could read and write files as expected. Ticket closed and notification sent to lmorales at laura.morales@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Laura, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether you are opening the current mapped Finance drive path (F:\Finance → \\FS-EAST-02.corplabs.internal\Finance$) and whether the access issue started after today's AD group change processed by admin rjensen. If possible, sign out of your session on WORKSTATION-PC-LM or reconnect the drive and tell us whether the same Access Denied message appears. You can reach me at ext. 4127 or helpdesk@corplabs.com if you need assistance with the steps.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: I was trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from my managed Windows 10 22H2 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LP-MREEVES) at the Charlotte office. After approving the Okta MFA prompt on my phone, the VPN tunnel established briefly for about 10 seconds and then disconnected, preventing access to internal applications including the Intranet Portal, ExpenseApp, and the Internal HR Portal. My username is mreeves and my employee ID is EMP-40821. The issue started the same morning after a Windows security update (KB5036892), and repeated re-authentication did not keep the tunnel active. I reached out to my manager, Denise Whitfield, who confirmed no one else on our team was affected.
observed_errors: AUTH_ERROR_401: authentication token rejected after MFA
VPN tunnel teardown observed immediately post-MFA
root_cause: Expired device certificate on the endpoint caused GlobalProtect to complete MFA but fail device-based validation shortly afterward, triggering VPN tunnel teardown.
resolution_steps: Validated that the endpoint device certificate used for VPN authentication on WORKSTATION-LP-MREEVES (user mreeves, EMP-40821) was expired (expiry date 2026-04-10) and no longer aligned with the active GlobalProtect device profile.

Renewed the device certificate through Device Certificate Service for host WORKSTATION-LP-MREEVES and confirmed the updated certificate (valid through 2027-04-23) was present on the affected endpoint.
Cleared and refreshed the GlobalProtect client profile on WORKSTATION-LP-MREEVES so the VPN client would use the renewed device certificate during connection to the US-East gateway.

Had the user mreeves re-initiate Okta MFA and reconnect to GlobalProtect from the Charlotte office, then confirmed the VPN tunnel remained established and internal applications (Intranet Portal, ExpenseApp, Internal HR Portal) were reachable.
Verified conditional access group membership for mreeves in the Sales user group and related VPN policy assignment to rule out post-authentication policy rejection.

Monitored the connection for mreeves on WORKSTATION-LP-MREEVES (IP 10.42.18.97) through an extended validation period and closed the ticket after 24-hour stability confirmation. Sent confirmation email to mreeves@corplabs.com.

title: Devices marked noncompliant by Intune
description: Multiple managed Windows 10 Sales Laptops assigned to users in the Charlotte office were blocked by Conditional Access after Intune marked them noncompliant for missing encryption. Users including Maria Castillo (mcastillo, emp ID EMP-40291) reported BitLocker was already enabled locally, but Intune continued to show encryption not detected and compliance did not refresh after reboot. The issue affected access to corporate resources from devices such as WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (IP 10.42.18.77) and was traced to stale device check-ins together with an outdated compliance policy revision still referenced by some devices.
root_cause: Affected devices had stale Intune check-in status, so current BitLocker encryption telemetry was not being reported back to the compliance service. Several of those devices were also still evaluating against the deprecated EnforceEncryption_v1 compliance policy reference, which lacked the current BitLocker signal mapping and caused encryption to be interpreted as missing.
resolution_steps: Triggered remote device sync for impacted endpoints (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC, WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-DH, and pnair's device) and forced a fresh compliance evaluation to recover devices that were only delayed by stale check-in data.
Validated that the failing compliance condition was the encryption signal and confirmed affected users mcastillo, dhines, and pnair reported BitLocker enabled on the devices.

Replaced the deprecated EnforceEncryption_v1 compliance policy reference with EnforceEncryption_v2 so the current BitLocker telemetry mapping is used during evaluation. Change implemented by endpoint admin krobles.

Published the updated compliance policy to the Sales Laptops group in the Charlotte office and initiated a policy refresh so devices would pull the corrected assignment and reprocess compliance state.

Monitored post-refresh check-in and compliance results until impacted devices (mcastillo, dhines, pnair) updated from noncompliant to compliant and Conditional Access blocks cleared. Confirmed with Maria Castillo at mcastillo@corplabs.com that access to corporate resources was restored.

title: Device marked noncompliant by Conditional Access despite Intune reporting compliant
description: User Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) on a Windows 10 21H2 managed laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) was blocked from accessing Microsoft 365 because Azure AD Conditional Access evaluated the device as noncompliant for missing encryption, while the Microsoft Intune portal continued to show the same device as Compliant. The issue intermittently prevented sign-in for a remote worker based in Charlotte and indicated conflicting compliance telemetry between Intune and Conditional Access during access evaluation. The user's client IP at the time of the blocked sign-in was 74.112.56.203.
observed_errors: Access denied by Conditional Access - device noncompliant: missing encryption
Intune console shows 'Compliant' while CA logs indicate 'Encryption missing'
Conditional Access evaluation returned noncompliant for encryption attribute
root_cause: Conditional Access consumed a stale or delayed encryption compliance signal for the device while Intune still showed the last successful compliant state, creating a mismatch between endpoint compliance telemetry and real-time access evaluation.
resolution_steps: Forced an Intune device check-in on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and initiated a remote sync via the Intune admin center so the endpoint could submit a fresh compliance evaluation for user rnguyen (EMP-40821).

Triggered re-evaluation of the encryption compliance state on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and had Rachel Nguyen reboot the device to refresh local BitLocker protection status reporting to the Device Compliance Service.

Reviewed Conditional Access sign-in results for rnguyen@corplabs.com after the new compliance sync to confirm the encryption attribute no longer evaluated as missing. Azure AD sign-in logs from client IP 74.112.56.203 showed successful authentication post-sync.

Validated that WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN returned to an allowed sign-in state for Microsoft 365 after the refreshed compliance signal propagated. Rachel confirmed full access to Exchange Online, Teams, and SharePoint from her Charlotte location.

Advised follow-up OS updating from Windows 10 21H2 to a supported release and monitoring for recurrence because the condition was tied to delayed compliance telemetry rather than a confirmed encryption configuration failure. Ticket details shared with endpoint team lead Marcus Webb (mwebb) for awareness.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: denied access to department shared drive (mapped drive prompts for credentials)
description: I was trying to open the department shared drive at \\fs-prod-east.corplabs.internal\FinanceDept from Windows Explorer on my Windows 10 workstation (WORKSTATION-PC-MR). The mapped drive (F:) now prompts for credentials and then returns "Access is denied" (0x80070005), preventing me from opening department files that other team members on the Finance Operations team can still access. The drive previously worked fine until last Thursday. Clearing cached credentials via `cmdkey /delete:fs-prod-east.corplabs.internal` plus remapping with `net use F: \\fs-prod-east.corplabs.internal\FinanceDept /persistent:yes` did not restore access, indicating a user-specific permissions or entitlement issue rather than a general file server outage. My username is mreeves and my employee ID is EMP-40821.
root_cause: User-specific access to \\fileserver\Dept was lost because the user's effective entitlement to the shared folder was no longer present in the current logon token, most likely due to missing or changed Active Directory security group membership for the department share. Cached credentials were not the cause because the prompt persisted after credential cleanup and remapping.
resolution_steps: Verify mreeves' Active Directory group membership against the security group SG-FinanceDept-RW assigned to the \\fs-prod-east.corplabs.internal\FinanceDept share and add the user back to the approved access group if missing. AD admin Raj Kapoor (rkapoor) confirmed mreeves was not a member and re-added the account.

Confirm the FinanceDept folder and share ACL on fs-prod-east.corplabs.internal still grant Read/Write access to SG-FinanceDept-RW and that NTFS permission inheritance on the department folder is intact where expected. Verified via `icacls \\fs-prod-east.corplabs.internal\FinanceDept` — inheritance was enabled and SG-FinanceDept-RW had Modify permissions.
Have Marcus Reeves sign out of WORKSTATION-PC-MR and sign back in with CORPLABS\mreeves to obtain a refreshed Windows access token that includes the corrected SG-FinanceDept-RW group membership.

Remove any stale mapping to \\fs-prod-east.corplabs.internal\FinanceDept via `net use F: /delete`, clear any remaining stored credentials for the file server using `cmdkey /delete:fs-prod-east.corplabs.internal`, and remap the drive using `net use F: \\fs-prod-east.corplabs.internal\FinanceDept /persistent:yes` under the user's current domain account CORPLABS\mreeves.

Test direct access to \\fs-prod-east.corplabs.internal\FinanceDept in Windows Explorer on WORKSTATION-PC-MR and confirm the folder opens without a credential prompt or access denied error. Marcus confirmed the F: drive and direct UNC path both opened successfully. Ticket closed.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reaching out. Please confirm the Windows username returned by `whoami` on your machine WORKSTATION-PC-MR and test the direct UNC path \\fs-prod-east.corplabs.internal\FinanceDept (rather than the F: mapped drive) so we can rule out a stale mapping or alternate account issue. Also, can you confirm whether you're connecting from the Arlington office or remotely? I'm assigning this to myself — Priya Nair, Service Desk. You can also reach me at pnair@corplabs.com or ext. 4417 if needed.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: denied access to Finance shared drive (\CorpFiles\Finance)
description: I was trying to open the Finance shared drive at \\CorpFiles\\Finance from my Windows 10 workstation (WORKSTATION-PC-RMORALES) at the Arlington office. I had been accessing the same share without issues the previous day using my domain account rmorales@corplabs.com. Opening the mapped drive (F:) prompted for credentials, and navigating directly to the department folder returned "Access Denied," preventing me from reaching the quarterly close spreadsheets and Finance files needed for normal department work. I cleared saved network credentials via Credential Manager but that did not restore access, indicating a likely entitlement or server-side permission issue rather than a local credential cache problem. My employee ID is FIN-20418 — please let me know what additional info you need.
root_cause: The user was missing membership in the FINANCE_Share_Access Active Directory security group. Because access to \\CorpFiles\\Finance is granted through that group, the file server denied access even after local saved credentials were cleared.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the effective access requirements for \\CorpFiles\\Finance and confirmed that user rmorales (Rosa Morales, employee ID FIN-20418) was not a member of the FINANCE_Share_Access Active Directory security group by querying CN=rmorales,OU=Finance,DC=corplabs,DC=internal.

Added rmorales to the FINANCE_Share_Access group via Active Directory Users and Computers to restore the required share and NTFS entitlement for the Finance folder. Change approved by manager David Cho (dcho@corplabs.com).

Had Rosa Morales sign out of the Windows domain session on WORKSTATION-PC-RMORALES and sign back in so the refreshed Kerberos logon token would include the updated FINANCE_Share_Access group membership.

Verified NTFS permissions and inheritance on \\CorpFiles\\Finance to confirm the FINANCE_Share_Access group retained the expected Modify access level; icacls output showed the correct ACE propagating to child objects.

Retested access with Rosa Morales from WORKSTATION-PC-RMORALES (10.40.17.83) and confirmed the Finance shared drive (F: mapped to \\CorpFiles\\Finance) opened successfully without additional credential prompts or access denied errors.

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: Managed Windows 10 Enterprise 21H2 laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (asset tag W10-123) assigned to Marcus Reeves (emp ID EMP-40821) in the Portland office was reported noncompliant for Disk Encryption in Microsoft Intune. BitLocker showed as not enabled on the device (IP 10.47.82.115), and no recovery key was visible in Azure AD or Intune escrow, preventing the device from meeting endpoint compliance requirements for the Sales mobile user group. Ticket raised by Marcus's manager, Dana Whitfield (dwhitfield@corplabs.com).
observed_errors: No recovery key found in Azure AD / Intune escrow
Device compliance: Noncompliant for Disk Encryption
root_cause: The device was not receiving the required Intune BitLocker encryption policy, and the TPM protector was in a NotInitialized state. Together these conditions prevented BitLocker from starting and blocked recovery key escrow to Azure AD/Intune.
resolution_steps: Assigned the correct Intune BitLocker encryption policy 'BL-Sales-Mobile-West' to device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (W10-123, user mreeves) by adding the device to the 'Sales - Mobile Devices' Intune group so the endpoint could receive the required disk encryption settings.

Initialized the TPM protector on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR by running Initialize-Tpm in an elevated PowerShell session after confirming the TPM chip was present (TpmPresent: True) but not ready for BitLocker use (TpmReady: False). Post-initialization, Get-Tpm confirmed TpmReady: True.

Forced an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR via Sync-IntuneDevice to refresh policy application and update the endpoint with the current encryption configuration. Sync completed successfully within 90 seconds.

Initiated BitLocker encryption on the device using Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -EncryptionMethod XtsAes256 -RecoveryPasswordProtector and verified the status changed from not enabled to encryption pending and then enabled. Full volume encryption completed in approximately 18 minutes.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key via BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector, confirmed escrow to Azure AD/Intune (recovery key ID 7F2A91xx visible under mreeves's device record), and verified the device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR returned to a compliant encryption state in the Device Compliance Service. Notified Marcus Reeves at mreeves@corplabs.com that the device is now fully compliant.

title: Print jobs stuck
description: Marketing users in the Portland office were trying to print to shared network printers (HP LaserJet 4250 series) through print server PRNT-SRV-01, but after the scheduled driver deployment (Change CR-2026-0187) the printer queues showed printers as offline and submitted jobs remained stuck with a 'Driver unavailable' status. Initial report came from Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) who noticed the issue at approximately 08:45 local time. Users were blocked from normal printing following the overnight change on Windows Server 2019. Approximately 14 Marketing team members were affected, including users printing from workstations such as WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN.
observed_errors: Printer driver load failure (INF parse error)
root_cause: A corrupt printer driver package deployed to PRNT-SRV-01 contained an INF corruption and checksum mismatch, causing the Windows Print Spooler to fail driver loading and leaving affected printer queues in stale mappings that prevented job processing.
resolution_steps: Rolled back PRNT-SRV-01 from the faulty driver deployment (v6.8.1.4020, CR-2026-0187) to the previously approved printer driver version v6.7.2.3850 to restore a known-good baseline. Rollback performed by Marcus Bell (EMP-30254) and verified against the approved checksum in the Driver Package repository.

Removed the corrupted v6.8.1.4020 driver package from PRNT-SRV-01 and reinstalled a verified signed printer driver package (v6.8.1.4020-r2) after checksum validation against the updated manifest. Package integrity confirmed by Priya Deshmukh before deployment.

Cleared 22 stuck jobs from affected print queues (MKT-CLR-Q1, MKT-CLR-Q2, MKT-BW-Q3) and restarted the Print Spooler service on PRNT-SRV-01 so the server could reload the corrected driver files. Notified affected users including Rachel Nguyen (r.nguyen@corplabs.com) and David Kowalski to resubmit their print jobs.

Remapped affected printer queues MKT-CLR-Q1, MKT-CLR-Q2, and MKT-BW-Q3 on PRNT-SRV-01 to remove stale queue-to-driver associations created during the failed deployment, and confirmed correct driver binding to each queue using the v6.8.1.4020-r2 package.

Updated the Printer Driver Whitelist Policy to include the validated signed driver version v6.8.1.4020-r2 and documented the approved checksum (SHA256: 9b2d...a804) for future deployments. Added a pre-deployment checksum validation gate to the change management process per recommendation from Priya Deshmukh (p.deshmukh@corplabs.com).

title: Sales users stuck in MFA prompt loop
description: Multiple users in the Sales group were unable to complete SSO sign-in to SaaS applications through the SSO Portal after a recent conditional access policy change pushed by the Identity team on 2026-04-06. After entering credentials at https://sso.corplabs.com, they were repeatedly returned to the MFA prompt instead of reaching applications such as Sales CRM, Email, and HR SaaS. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed by at least four other Sales team members in the Charlotte office. Reported symptoms included repeated MFA challenges, 401 MFA_REQUIRED, and authentication failures that blocked normal access to business applications. Users were working on Windows 10 machines and accessing the portal via Chrome and Edge browsers.
observed_errors: Browser shows repeated MFA challenge without success
root_cause: A stale conditional access policy reference to MFA-Policy-2020, combined with stale MFA enrollments for affected Sales users, created a mismatch between current group-based access rules and the users' enrolled MFA state. This caused the identity flow to repeatedly challenge for MFA and fail application sign-in.
resolution_steps: Identify impacted Sales users (including rnguyen, dpatel, msorenson, and 20 additional members in the Charlotte office Sales group) and reset their MFA enrollments in the Okta admin console so they can complete fresh factor registration against the current MFA-Policy-2024 requirements.

Update the conditional access configuration in Azure AD to replace deprecated MFA-Policy-2020 references with MFA-Policy-2024, ensuring the Sales group GUID is correctly bound to the active policy. Change performed by identity admin jkrasinski and verified via Azure AD audit log.

Review and correct Sales group membership mappings and policy scoping in Azure AD so the intended 23 users (verified against HR roster for the Charlotte office) match the active MFA-Policy-2024 assignment.

Validate the fix with test Sales user rnguyen by confirming a single MFA prompt via Okta Verify leads to successful access through the SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com to affected SaaS applications (Sales CRM, Email, HR SaaS). Rachel confirmed access restored at 18:45 UTC.

Monitor Okta and Azure AD authentication logs for recurring MFA loop behavior or token mismatch errors for 24 hours, filtering on the Sales group and Charlotte office IP range (10.22.47.0/24), and confirm normal sign-in across the impacted apps. Escalation contact: identity team lead Marcus Webb (mwebb@corplabs.com, ext. 4417).

description: I completed a corporate password reset through the Password Reset Portal on 2025-11-18 at approximately 07:45 UTC, but sign-in to the SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com continued to fail with a locked-account error and my Active Directory account (username: mcarson) became locked again within minutes. Guided Monica Carson to remove and re-add the corporate account on her iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MC) and clear saved browser credentials in Safari so the old password would no longer be retried by iOS Mail or the browser against Active Directory.

Revoked stale SSO sessions and tokens associated with mcarson's prior sign-in state on the SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com to ensure all subsequent authentication used the new password exclusively.

Validated successful sign-in to the SSO Portal for mcarson at 08:14 UTC from IP 10.22.47.88 after mobile credential cleanup and documented WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MC as the lockout source in the incident record for follow-up monitoring by Kevin Briggs on the identity team.

title: Intermittent internal hostname lookup failing
description: Multiple users and monitoring in corp-dc-1 reported intermittent failures resolving service.corp.internal for internal-portal and service.backend. The issue was initially flagged by Rajesh Patel (emp ID EMP-40291) from the Engineering team at the Denver office, who noticed that the hostname sometimes returned NXDOMAIN, sometimes an old decommissioned IP (10.20.5.47), and sometimes timed out. This prevented the applications from reaching the internal service endpoint by name from affected subnets. Additional reports came in from Maria Chen on the same floor.
root_cause: An internal DNS resolver retained and served a stale cached A record for service.corp.internal that pointed to a decommissioned IP, while some lookups also returned NXDOMAIN during inconsistent cache state, causing intermittent internal name resolution failures.
resolution_steps: Verified the authoritative internal DNS zone for service.corp.internal and corrected the A record to the current production IP 10.20.8.130, replacing the decommissioned entry 10.20.5.47.

Flushed cache on all internal DNS resolvers (dns-res-01, dns-res-02) serving the affected Denver clients and restarted the resolver service on dns-res-02 where cache purge did not fully clear stale entries.

Confirmed conditional forwarding and resolver path behavior for the corp.internal zone so subsequent queries were answered from the correct authoritative source; verified from WORKSTATION-LP-RPATEL and WORKSTATION-DT-MCHEN.

Validated fresh DNS responses for service.corp.internal from multiple subnets including 10.20.3.0/24 and 10.20.4.0/24, and compared results against authoritative lookups to confirm the stale (10.20.5.47) and NXDOMAIN responses were eliminated. Rajesh Patel and Maria Chen confirmed applications internal-portal and service.backend were functioning normally.

Reviewed and adjusted the record TTL from 86400s to 3600s to align with internal DNS policy and documented the zone correction in the Denver network runbook to reduce recurrence after future service IP changes.
agent_questions: Hi Rajesh — thanks for the detailed report. Please compare DNS results for service.corp.internal from an affected subnet and a known-good resolver so we can determine whether the issue is client-side or resolver-side. Can you run nslookup from your workstation WORKSTATION-LP-RPATEL and share the output? Also loop in your teammate Maria if she can test from her machine WORKSTATION-DT-MCHEN on the same VLAN. — Kevin Briggs, Network Operations

title: Laptop slow after login
description: User reports their Windows 10 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, asset tag EP-PC-04821) became very slow immediately after morning login at approximately 08:15 EST. Applications including Windows Explorer, Microsoft Edge, and Microsoft Office were taking roughly 20-40 seconds to open, CPU utilization was spiking to 85-95%, and the system fan was running loudly. The user, Marcus Reeves (employee ID EMP-20947), is based in the Charlotte office and relies on the laptop for daily Sales operations. The slowdown affected normal work after sign-in, and available disk space was low at about 12% on the 256 GB SSD, worsening startup and application launch performance.
root_cause: Endpoint protection scans were backlogged and running heavily at user login, driving sustained CPU usage from MsMpEng.exe; non-critical startup items and low free disk space amplified the post-login performance degradation.
resolution_steps: Reviewed startup performance evidence on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (asset EP-PC-04821, user mreeves) and confirmed MsMpEng.exe (PID 4728) was consuming sustained CPU at 93% during login because of 14 pending endpoint protection scan activities queued at sign-in.

Cleared the endpoint protection scan backlog (14 queued scans) on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and adjusted the full scan schedule to run at 02:00 EST during off-hours instead of user login periods, reducing peak login CPU load.

Disabled non-essential startup items (Adobe Updater, Cisco Jabber auto-launch, HP Support Assistant, and OneDrive sync pre-login trigger) to reduce competing CPU and disk activity during sign-in and first application launch.

Ran Disk Cleanup and removed 8.4 GB of temporary files from C:\Users\mreeves\AppData\Local\Temp and Windows Update cache to reclaim local storage (free space increased from 12% to approximately 15.3%) and improve application launch responsiveness.

Refreshed device policy from Endpoint Management so the updated scan schedule and startup-related settings were applied consistently on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR; confirmed policy sync completed and post-reboot login time dropped to under 45 seconds with CPU stabilizing below 30% within one minute.

title: Outlook mail not syncing
description: Multiple users in the Sales group at the Charlotte office were unable to receive new email in Outlook on desktop and mobile for approximately 90 minutes starting around 21:00 UTC. Outlook on affected Windows 10 desktops (including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR used by Marcus Rivera and WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-KP used by Karen Phelps) showed a "Disconnected" state, and mobile clients displayed stale mailbox content. Users could not reliably read current mail or confirm recent messages, impacting normal sales communication and time-sensitive deal correspondence. Exchange Online service health dashboard (https://admin.microsoft.com) appeared normal, indicating the issue was localized to affected Outlook profiles and device sync state rather than a tenant-wide outage. Initial report submitted by Marcus Rivera (mrivera@corplabs.com, EMP-40287).
root_cause: Stale Outlook profiles with corrupted local OST cache caused mailbox sync token mismatch on affected desktop clients, and some impacted mobile devices also had stale or non-compliant sync partnerships that prevented current mailbox synchronization.
resolution_steps: Confirmed Exchange Online service health was normal via the Microsoft 365 admin center and isolated the issue to affected client profiles and mobile device sync state for users mrivera, kphelps, and jokafor in the Charlotte Sales group.

Created new Outlook profiles on impacted desktop clients (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR for Marcus Rivera, WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-KP for Karen Phelps, and Jason Okafor's workstation) and allowed full mailbox resynchronization instead of reusing the corrupted OST cache. Old OST files were renamed to .old for reference.

Removed stale mobile sync partnerships for affected phones belonging to mrivera, kphelps, and jokafor, and re-added the mailbox accounts to establish fresh device synchronization via Exchange ActiveSync.

Remediated Intune compliance issues on Karen Phelps's non-compliant iPhone device (policy version mismatch) and re-enrolled affected mobile endpoints where required, ensuring all devices met current compliance policy before re-establishing sync.

Forced mailbox resynchronization from Exchange Online for impacted users (mrivera, kphelps, jokafor) and verified Outlook returned to a connected state with current mail flowing normally on both desktop and mobile. Derek Kwan confirmed resolution with all three users and closed the ticket.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether Outlook on the affected desktops shows Connected, Trying to connect, or Disconnected in the status bar. Also, can you verify whether mobile mail is stale for the same users (yourself, Karen Phelps, and anyone else on the Sales team at Charlotte)? If possible, note the last successful sync timestamp shown on each device. You can reach me at ext. 4418 or dkwan@corplabs.com if it's easier to call in.

title: Intune shows devices as NonCompliant causing Conditional Access blocks
description: Multiple corporate-managed Windows 10/11 laptops assigned to the Richmond US-East Sales and Field Engineer population began showing as NonCompliant in Intune after a compliance policy push on the evening of 2025-12-25. As a result, Azure AD Conditional Access blocked affected users—including Rachel Simmons (rsimmons@corplabs.com), Derek Huang, and others—from SharePoint Online, GlobalProtect VPN, and other corporate resources. The issue affected approximately 12 devices, appeared intermittent, and was tied to stale device check-ins and missing encryption status reporting following the updated compliance policy (CP-WIN-ENCRYPT-v3). Initial reports were filed by Rachel Simmons (EMP-40821) from her laptop WORKSTATION-RSIMMONS after repeated Conditional Access denials.
observed_errors: Device shows NonCompliant status in Intune
Missing encryption signal reported for device
root_cause: Devices had stale Intune check-in/compliance evaluation data after the policy push, and a subset of endpoints was not reporting the required BitLocker encryption compliance signal, causing Conditional Access to treat them as noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Forced Intune device sync for all 12 affected endpoints from the admin console (initiated by Kevin Marsh, EMP-30294) to refresh management check-in and trigger a new compliance evaluation against the updated CP-WIN-ENCRYPT-v3 policy.

Reviewed the failing compliance state on the three remaining noncompliant devices (WORKSTATION-DHUANG / dhuang, mreyes, lchoi) and confirmed the missing signal was the BitLocker encryption status rather than a broad policy assignment failure.

Instructed affected users—Derek Huang (dhuang@corplabs.com, 571-555-0148), Marco Reyes (mreyes@corplabs.com), and Lisa Choi (lchoi@corplabs.com)—to reboot their laptops, complete BitLocker enablement where required, and open Company Portal to allow the device to finish reporting updated compliance data to Intune.

Reran compliance evaluation for the three remaining devices after user-side BitLocker remediation and verified their status changed back to Compliant in Intune. WORKSTATION-DHUANG was the last to clear at 2025-12-26T15:42Z.

Monitored Conditional Access access restoration and confirmed previously blocked users—including Rachel Simmons, Derek Huang, Priya Nair, Marco Reyes, and Lisa Choi—could again reach SharePoint Online, GlobalProtect VPN, and other corporate resources once device compliance was updated.

Added temporary nightly automated check-ins via Intune remediation script and follow-up monitoring by Kevin Marsh to ensure all 12 impacted endpoints in the Richmond region continued reporting current compliance status after the CP-WIN-ENCRYPT-v3 policy change.

title: Intermittent API timeouts from Integration Gateway
description: Batch integrations from the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-04.corplabs.internal) to the downstream API Service began failing intermittently starting 2025-12-09 09:38 UTC. Users in the Application Support group, initially reported by Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821), observed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and occasional 401 Unauthorized errors on integration jobs running under service account svc_intgateway. Retries did not clear the backlog, and the issue affected all API integration jobs routed through the us-east-1 cluster, delaying data synchronization for the Charlotte office until authentication and gateway configuration were corrected.
root_cause: An expired API token combined with a stale Integration Gateway configuration reference to TokenRotationPolicy_v1 caused token validation failures against the downstream API. The resulting authentication failures increased retry activity and contributed to intermittent 504 timeout behavior.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token for service account svc_intgateway used by the Integration Gateway and updated the downstream token store on api-svc-east-02.corplabs.internal with the new valid secret. Rotation was executed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Updated the Integration Gateway configuration on igw-prod-east-04.corplabs.internal to replace the stale TokenRotationPolicy_v1 reference with TokenRotationPolicy_v2, ensuring future automatic rotations align with the 60-day credential lifecycle.

Redeployed the integration connector pods in the us-east-1 Kubernetes cluster so the new token and updated TokenRotationPolicy_v2 reference were loaded into the running service. Rolling restart completed at 10:14 UTC with zero dropped connections.

Adjusted retry and backoff behavior on the Integration Gateway to use safer exponential backoff (initial interval 2s, max 60s, multiplier 2×) and applied temporary timeout tuning (raised to 25s) to reduce repeated failures during token propagation across the connector fleet.

Validated successful authenticated API calls for svc_intgateway and monitored 401 and 504 error rates via the Monitoring System until integration processing returned to baseline. Confirmation sign-off provided by Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) at 11:02 UTC.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please pull the latest Integration Gateway error log from igw-prod-east-04.corplabs.internal and confirm when the API token for service account svc_intgateway was last rotated. We need to verify token age against the TokenRotationPolicy_v1 reference currently configured. Also, can you check whether Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) made any recent credential changes on the API Service side? That will help us rule out a manual rotation mismatch.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Customers were trying to sync data through the Integration Gateway (gateway-prod-us-east-1.corplabs.internal) to the downstream API Service, but requests began timing out with intermittent HTTP 504 errors over roughly the last 90 minutes starting around 11:15 UTC. This caused delayed data sync completion for integration jobs owned by the Application Support team, some failed batch runs reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com), and impact to nightly batch processing on the Data Sync Worker cluster. Gateway logs from pod igw-worker-7b on host WORKSTATION-IGWNODE-MD showed sustained downstream response time spikes above the normal 5-second timeout window along with some auth retries against the /v2/token endpoint; token rotation by engineer Priya Nair reduced auth-related noise briefly, but the main customer-visible issue remained downstream latency from the API Service side. Reported from workstation 10.42.18.77 in the Arlington office.
root_cause: Elevated downstream API Service latency exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout window, causing intermittent HTTP 504 responses during sync traffic; token-related auth retries were secondary noise and not the primary failure driver.
resolution_steps: Validated and retained the rotated API token (client_id: igw-sync-prod-01) after confirming authentication errors were reduced from ~12% to <1%, separating auth noise from the primary timeout condition. Priya Nair (pnair) verified the token via manual endpoint test from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN.

Restarted Integration Gateway pods (igw-worker-7a through -7d) in the igw-prod namespace on EKS to clear transient session and connection state while confirming the timeout pattern persisted after restart, ruling out stale connection pooling as a contributing factor.

Temporarily increased retry and backoff behavior on integration jobs — retry count raised from 3 to 5, exponential backoff ceiling increased from 10s to 30s — to reduce immediate job failure rates while downstream latency was being addressed. Change applied by Priya Nair and confirmed in the Integration Job Runner configuration.

Enabled additional timeout and request tracing on the Integration Gateway (X-Trace-Enabled header, extended access log format) to capture evidence of elevated downstream response times and repeated HTTP 504 behavior. Trace samples (trace-a4f8c1, trace-b7d902) were exported for the escalation package.

Escalated the incident to the downstream API Service owners — team lead Raj Venkatesh (rvenkatesh@corplabs.com) in Dallas — with evidence of sustained latency (avg 6.2s, p99 8.4s), request impact across 247 timed-out calls, and a request to review recent deploy api-svc-v3.14.2 (rolled out 10:30 UTC), capacity, and scaling health in us-east-1. Escalation filed by Carlos Medina (cmedina, emp ID E-22814).

Continued monitoring after escalation via the Monitoring System igw-prod-latency dashboard and treated the service as resolved from the gateway side once mitigation (adjusted retry/backoff) and ownership transfer to Raj Venkatesh's team were in place for the downstream latency issue. title: Expired TLS certificate from internal CA causing TLS failures on Load Balancer
description: Internal employees at the Denver office were trying to access the Internal Web Service at https://portal.internal.corplabs.com, but browsers and monitoring began reporting certificate warnings and failed TLS validation. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID: E-40291) via email to the service desk. TLS captures from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (IP 10.42.17.88) showed the Kubernetes ingress/load balancer presenting a certificate issued by the internal CA that expired on 2025-12-13, causing ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and blocked HTTPS access to the service until the certificate and full chain were updated on the load balancer.
root_cause: The load balancer continued presenting an expired TLS certificate issued by the internal Certificate Authority because the renewed certificate and full trust chain were available in the CA store but were not deployed and referenced in the load balancer configuration before the prior certificate expired.
resolution_steps: Retrieve the renewed server certificate and complete intermediate/root chain from the internal Certificate Authority for the Internal Web Service endpoint (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com). Kevin Orozco (korozco) downloaded the renewed bundle portal-2025.pem and full chain from the CA portal.

Replace the expired certificate bundle in the load balancer certificate store and update the load balancer configuration to reference the new certificate and full chain instead of the old file/path. Specifically, the ingress TLS secret was updated to point from /etc/tls/certs/portal-2024.pem to /etc/tls/certs/portal-2025.pem by korozco.

Reload or restart the load balancer/ingress process so the active listener begins presenting the renewed certificate. Kevin Orozco (korozco) performed a rolling restart of the ingress controller pods in us-east-1 at 2025-12-13T23:15:00Z to pick up the new TLS secret.

Validate from a client and from the load balancer side that the presented certificate is unexpired, matches the service hostname, and the full chain validates without missing or expired intermediates. Maria Chen (mchen) and Raj Patel (rpatel) confirmed from their workstations (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC and WORKSTATION-DESK-RP) that the certificate warning was resolved and HTTPS access to https://portal.internal.corplabs.com was restored.

Restore and tune certificate expiry monitoring and renewal reminders so alerts fire before expiration and deployment tasks are tracked through completion. Lisa Nguyen (lnguyen) re-enabled the cert-expiry-30d alert subscription and added a new cert-expiry-7d critical alert. Deployment tracking was added to the runbook so that certificate renewal is not marked complete until the load balancer configuration is verified by the infrastructure team.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution for internal-service.example.com
description: Users and monitoring systems across multiple offices were trying to resolve internal-service.example.com for access to the internal-service endpoint, but DNS responses were intermittent across locations. Reports originated from users in the Charlotte and Raleigh offices, as well as automated health checks from the Network Monitoring platform. Some client lookups (e.g., from workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES, IP 10.50.12.88) and resolver checks returned the current internal A record 10.2.3.50, while other resolvers—particularly those serving the Raleigh site—continued to return the old IP 10.1.2.45 or timed out, causing applications to intermittently fail to reach the service by hostname after a recent DNS record update. Ticket raised by Marcus Reeves (mreeves, EMP-40821) on behalf of the internal-users group.
observed_errors: nslookup returned old IP 10.1.2.45 from some resolvers
timeout resolving internal-service.example.com from select locations
NXDOMAIN not observed; inconsistent A record responses
root_cause: Stale cached A record data on downstream/internal resolvers and conditional forwarding path inconsistency caused some clients to receive the previous address 10.1.2.45 after the authoritative zone had already been updated to 10.2.3.50.
resolution_steps: Validated that the authoritative internal DNS zone on ns1-internal.corplabs.net for internal-service.example.com contained the intended A record value 10.2.3.50 and confirmed the change (originally made by admin jmartinez at 2026-01-10T10:30:00Z) was present on authoritative servers with correct SOA serial.

Flushed caches on primary internal DNS resolvers dns-resolver-east-01 and dns-resolver-east-02 using rndc flush and reloaded DNS services to remove stale entries serving the previous address 10.1.2.45. Verified immediate improvement for clients in the Raleigh office.

Coordinated cache clears on downstream resolvers dns-resolver-east-04 and dns-resolver-south-01 involved in conditional forwarding, with assistance from network engineer David Cho (dcho, EMP-40955), so clients in Charlotte and other affected sites no longer received mixed responses from different resolution paths.

Temporarily reduced the DNS TTL for the affected record from 3600s to 300s to shorten cache persistence during propagation and future address changes. Change documented in the Internal DNS Zone change log.

Reviewed and corrected conditional forwarder behavior on dns-resolver-east-04 for the internal zone (ensured direct forwarding to ns1-internal.corplabs.net rather than through intermediate resolver dns-resolver-south-01), then verified from multiple locations—Charlotte (Marcus Reeves, WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES), Raleigh (Priya Nair, WORKSTATION-LT-PNAIR), and us-east-1 monitoring probes—that resolvers consistently returned 10.2.3.50 without timeouts or old-address responses.
