title: Integration Gateway timeouts during data sync — expired API token
description: Scheduled data sync jobs from the application to the downstream API began failing in Kubernetes in us-east-1, triggering monitoring alerts at 2025-12-06 02:14 UTC. The Integration Gateway (host: INTGW-NODE-04) showed repeated request timeouts and 504 Gateway Timeout responses, with accompanying 401 Unauthorized errors. This blocked normal DataSync Service processing for the Chicago data center and caused delayed data synchronization for affected users and dependent systems. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Jennings (emp ID: EMP-40821) via email at mjennings@corplabs.com.
root_cause: The Integration Gateway was using an expired API token while still referencing stale Integration API Policy v1.2, causing authentication failures against the downstream API; repeated retries then manifested as 504 timeout symptoms during scheduled sync processing.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token (client_id: datasync-prod-east) and updated the downstream API credential used by the Integration Gateway. New token issued by Derek Whitfield (dwhitfield) with a 180-day expiry and stored in the secure token vault.

Changed the gateway policy reference from Integration API Policy v1.2 to Integration API Policy v2.0 to align with the current authentication requirements, as confirmed by the platform engineering team in Chicago.

Redeployed the Integration Gateway configuration in Kubernetes (us-east-1 cluster) so the new token and policy settings were loaded by running gateway instances on INTGW-NODE-04 and peer nodes. Rollout completed at 11:08 UTC.

Adjusted retry and backoff settings from a fixed 3-second interval to exponential backoff (initial 5s, max 30s, jitter enabled) to reduce immediate repeat attempts that were amplifying downstream latency and masking the primary authorization failure.

Validated successful authenticated calls and confirmed scheduled data sync jobs completed without new 401 or 504 errors. Priya Nair (pnair) verified from the Houston operations center that all pending sync batches cleared by 11:15 UTC, then continued monitoring for recurrence via the Monitoring System alerting dashboard.
agent_questions: We are seeing both 504 timeout errors and 401 Unauthorized responses from the Integration Gateway. Hi Marcus, can you please confirm whether any token or policy change was pending for the downstream API integration? We're also checking with Derek Whitfield (dwhitfield) from the platform engineering team to verify recent credential rotation schedules. Please respond to this thread or reach out at 512-884-3091 if you have additional context.

title: Laptop slow after login
description: My Windows 10 21H2 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-SALES-MR, asset tag LAP-513) becomes extremely slow immediately after sign-in. Outlook and Chrome take several minutes to open, CPU remains around 80-95% for several minutes, and Task Manager shows disk usage near 92% during the slowdown. The issue started after a recent endpoint policy change pushed over the weekend. My username is mreeves and I'm based out of the Charlotte office on the Sales team. This is blocking my normal post-login workflow — I can barely get anything done for the first 10-15 minutes after booting up. Please advise. — Marcus Reeves, EMP-40821
root_cause: Recent application of the 'Corp-Startup-Heavy' endpoint startup policy queued excessive startup tasks and contributed to endpoint protection scan backlog, causing sustained post-login CPU saturation and high disk I/O.
resolution_steps: Reviewed endpoint startup behavior on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR (LAP-513, user mreeves) and confirmed multiple policy-driven startup tasks — including software inventory collection, compliance baseline evaluation, and font cache rebuild — were launching concurrently after user login, creating sustained CPU and disk contention for 10-15 minutes.

Disabled unnecessary startup items associated with the heavy startup sequence (deferred non-critical inventory and font cache tasks to off-peak hours) and initiated a device policy refresh via Endpoint Management console so WORKSTATION-SALES-MR could receive the corrected policy state immediately.

Performed temporary rollback of the 'Corp-Startup-Heavy' startup policy (GPO revision 2026-01-27) on the affected device LAP-513 to reduce concurrent post-login processing, reverting to the previous 'Corp-Startup-Standard' baseline pending a revised policy from the endpoint engineering team.

Cleared the CrowdStrike Falcon endpoint protection scan backlog (14 deferred scans) on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR so real-time protection activity no longer overlapped heavily with login startup tasks, and rescheduled full scans to run during the 12:00-13:00 maintenance window.

Removed temporary files and reclaimed local disk space on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR (recovered an additional 5.4 GB beyond the user's earlier Disk Cleanup, bringing total free space to approximately 16.7 GB on the 256 GB SSD) to reduce disk queue pressure and improve application launch performance after sign-in.

Validated that post-login CPU and disk usage on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR returned closer to normal (CPU below 40% within 2 minutes of login, disk usage under 60%) and that Outlook and Chrome opened within expected time (under 15 seconds each) after remediation. Confirmed with Marcus Reeves that morning login workflow was restored to acceptable performance.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether the slowdown starts right after sign-in on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR and whether Task Manager shows high CPU or disk usage while Outlook and Chrome are opening. Also, can you confirm your current IP address so we can pull the latest endpoint telemetry for your device? — Agent Priya Nair

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failures for db.internal.example.com
description: Internal services were trying to resolve and connect to db.internal.example.com, but multiple hosts across at least two racks (Rack 14A and Rack 14B) in the Arlington datacenter began intermittently failing name resolution around 08:30 on 2026-01-07. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40821) from the platform engineering team after deployment pipelines on WORKSTATION-MDELGADO started failing database connectivity checks. Affected clients reported a mix of NXDOMAIN responses and DNS lookup timeouts, and some resolver checks returned an older A record pointing to 10.22.4.17 instead of the expected 10.22.6.50. The issue impacted name-based access to the internal database endpoint across multiple subnets (10.22.4.0/24 and 10.22.6.0/24) in the on-premises us-east-1 datacenter. Additional reports came in from Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) on the observability team, confirming the same symptoms from hosts in Rack 14B.
root_cause: Intermittent internal DNS resolution was caused by stale or inconsistent resolver data for db.internal.example.com, likely due to an incorrect or outdated internal zone record and/or resolver forwarder/cache state serving old answers across subnets.
resolution_steps: Verify the authoritative internal DNS zone entry for db.internal.example.com, confirm the correct A record value (10.22.6.50) and TTL (300s), and correct the record where it differs from the intended database endpoint address. The stale record pointing to 10.22.4.17 was updated by jlin on the primary zone server.

Clear cache on the affected internal DNS resolvers (dns-resolver-1.internal.example.com and dns-resolver-2.internal.example.com) so stale responses and negative cache entries for db.internal.example.com are removed and new queries return fresh zone data reflecting the corrected 10.22.6.50 address.

Flush DNS cache on representative affected clients — including WORKSTATION-MDELGADO (10.22.4.103) and WORKSTATION-PNAIR (10.22.6.88) — and retest name resolution from multiple subnets (10.22.4.0/24 and 10.22.6.0/24) to confirm the hostname consistently resolves to the current address 10.22.6.50 without NXDOMAIN or timeout behavior.

Review and correct any conditional forwarder or delegation path used for the internal.example.com zone on dns-resolver-1.internal.example.com so queries are routed to the proper authoritative source. The stale conditional forwarder entry was updated and validated by the network team.

Validate steady-state resolution by repeating lookups from impacted racks (Rack 14A and Rack 14B in Arlington) and monitoring via Network Monitoring dashboards for consistent answers (10.22.6.50) and elimination of intermittent lookup failures. Marcus Delgado and Priya Nair confirmed resolution from their respective hosts.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether all affected hosts use the same internal DNS resolver path (e.g., are they all pointed at dns-resolver-1.internal.example.com and dns-resolver-2.internal.example.com?) and whether failed lookups return NXDOMAIN, timeout, or an unexpected IP when querying db.internal.example.com. Also, can you verify from WORKSTATION-MDELGADO whether nslookup db.internal.example.com returns the stale 10.22.4.17 address or the correct 10.22.6.50? Please include output from both resolver paths if possible.

title: Internal DNS resolution failure for app-service.internal (stale A record)

Monitoring on Network Monitoring dashboard showed bursts of NXDOMAIN responses and some lookups returning the retired IP 192.0.2.45 (previously assigned to decommissioned host WORKSTATION-APPOLD-MD), which prevented the application from consistently reaching its internal endpoint from multiple client subnets including 10.40.12.0/24. root_cause: A duplicate and stale A record for app-service.internal remained in the internal DNS zone, and resolver caches continued serving the retired address 192.0.2.45, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN responses and stale DNS answers.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone for app-service.internal (zone managed by dns-admin rchen) and identified the duplicate stale A record pointing to retired host IP 192.0.2.45, originally associated with decommissioned host WORKSTATION-APPOLD-MD.
Removed the stale DNS entry (performed by rchen via Internal DNS Zone console) and confirmed the authoritative zone retained only the correct A record 10.40.8.20 for app-service.internal.
Lowered the DNS TTL temporarily from 3600 to 300 seconds to speed propagation of the corrected record across internal resolvers and clients in the Ashburn prod-east environment.

Flushed DNS cache entries on dns-resolver-01.corplabs.internal and dns-resolver-02.corplabs.internal so cached stale responses (192.0.2.45) would no longer be served to clients such as WORKSTATION-DEV-KP (10.40.12.87).

Validated that monitoring and representative client hosts in prod-east (including WORKSTATION-DEV-KP at 10.40.12.87, user kpatel) resolved app-service.internal to the correct address 10.40.8.20 without further NXDOMAIN or stale-IP responses. Confirmed resolution with Marcus Delgado (m.delgado@corplabs.com).

title: Finance users unable to join Corporate Wi-Fi — certificate authentication failures (escalated)
description: Multiple Finance users on Windows 10 laptops in the Philadelphia office were unable to join the Corporate Wi-Fi starting around 07:30 on April 25. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed by at least four other Finance team members including David Kowalski. Users could not obtain normal network access for business work — affected machines such as WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-DK were stuck on limited connectivity. Profile re-adds and device reboots did not restore connectivity.
root_cause: The corporate wireless authentication certificate on the Wireless Controller expired, causing EAP-TLS validation failures between endpoints, the controller, and NAC trust policy for the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID.
resolution_steps: Renew the expired corp-wlan-cert on the Wireless Controller (WLC-PHILA-01) with the correct server certificate and verified intermediate CA chain, ensuring the new certificate validity extends through April 2027.

Update Network Access Control trust settings and policy bindings on the NAC authentication service so the renewed wireless certificate is accepted for Corporate Wi-Fi 802.1X authentication across the Philadelphia office infrastructure.

Validate successful EAP-TLS handshakes on WLC-PHILA-01 and NAC by confirming new authentication attempts from test users rnguyen and dkowalski no longer fail with certificate expired or certificate validation errors.

Have affected users (Rachel Nguyen, David Kowalski, Priya Mehta, Jennifer Olson, and others) forget and reconnect to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID so devices establish a fresh trust path and complete authentication with the renewed certificate.

Monitor Finance user authentication attempts in the Philadelphia office after rollout to confirm normal access policy assignment and no recurring certificate-related failures; Anil Prasad (EMP-55034) to review NAC logs at 24-hour and 72-hour checkpoints.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether all affected Finance users are connecting to Corporate Wi-Fi with the standard wireless profile (CorpWLAN-Finance) and whether reconnect attempts after reboot still show certificate-related 802.1X errors. title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Internal users and automated health checks were unable to reach the internal dashboard at https://internal.example.com starting around 02:00 UTC on 2025-12-16. Browsers displayed an expired certificate warning (ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and dependent API clients from the DevOps team failed TLS handshakes. Automated Nagios checks from host MONITOR-EAST-01 also flagged the endpoint. The service was completely unavailable over TLS for internal teams, blocking normal dashboard access, CI/CD pipeline status views, and deployment tracking until the expired service certificate and load balancer certificate chain were corrected.
observed_errors: upstream TLS handshake failed on load balancer
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal.example.com expired, and although a renewed certificate was available from the internal Certificate Authority, it was not deployed with the full updated chain on the Load Balancer serving the internal web service.
resolution_steps: Requested and obtained a renewed TLS certificate for internal.example.com (CN=internal.example.com, SAN: internal.example.com) from the internal Certificate Authority at ca.pki.corplabs.internal, verified by Raj Patel (E-40291). New certificate serial: 3A:F7:C2:91:00:5C, valid through 2026-12-16.

Uploaded the renewed server certificate and full intermediate chain (including CorpLabs Internal Issuing CA G2) to the Load Balancer LB-EAST-PROD-02 TLS configuration at /etc/ssl/certs/internal-example-com.pem, replacing the expired certificate material. Upload performed by Raj Patel from WORKSTATION-RPT-4021.

Reloaded the Load Balancer TLS configuration on LB-EAST-PROD-02 (nginx -s reload) so new client connections presented the updated certificate chain. Reload confirmed successful at 09:12 UTC by Lisa Nguyen.

Validated successful HTTPS access to https://internal.example.com and confirmed TLS handshakes completed without certificate warnings from client (Maria Chen, mchen@corplabs.com, Arlington office) and service monitoring perspectives (MONITOR-EAST-01). openssl s_client verification from WORKSTATION-LN-7744 showed valid chain with correct expiry date.

Re-enabled and verified certificate expiration monitoring on MONITOR-EAST-01 with 30-day and 7-day advance alerts. Updated the SSH key for service account svc-certdeploy to restore the automated cert-renew-deploy pipeline. Added a renewal reminder calendar entry for the infrastructure team (infra-ops@corplabs.com) to reduce the risk of future missed deployments.

Re-evaluate the AppX deployment in Software Center on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KB and confirm the application is visible to the target device after policy refresh. Katrin Bauer confirmed the app now appears in her Software Center catalog.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Overnight integration jobs for DataSyncApp were delayed or failed when the Integration Gateway in Kubernetes (us-east-1) experienced repeated HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses while calling the downstream API Service. The issue was first reported by platform engineer Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) at approximately 06:15 UTC after reviewing the nightly batch run from the Arlington data center. Monitoring and traces showed sustained downstream response time increases above the gateway timeout window, which created retries, backlog growth, and delayed customer data synchronization. Affected gateway pods were running on nodes WORKSTATION-GWNODE-MD in the integration namespace. The incident impacted sync jobs servicing accounts managed by the platform-engineering user group.
root_cause: Sustained downstream API Service latency exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout window, causing HTTP 504 responses, retries, and overnight job backlog.
resolution_steps: Validated that the failure pattern aligned with elevated downstream API latency rather than gateway pod instability by reviewing timeout errors, trace latency, and job failure correlation. Agent Priya Nair (pnair) cross-referenced Monitoring System trace spans with DataSyncApp job scheduler logs from the Arlington cluster to confirm that all 847 failed jobs mapped to downstream latency spikes exceeding the 10-second timeout.

Applied a temporary mitigation on the Integration Gateway by increasing the request timeout from 10 seconds to 30 seconds and tuning retry/backoff behavior to reduce immediate job failures during transient latency spikes. Configuration change was committed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) and deployed via the platform-engineering CI/CD pipeline at 12:08 UTC.

Scaled the Integration Gateway deployment by two pods to reduce queueing pressure and restarted a limited subset of pods to clear transient worker errors while preserving service availability. The additional pods were scheduled on nodes in the Arlington availability zone and confirmed healthy by Priya Nair via the Monitoring System pod readiness dashboard at 12:15 UTC.

Escalated the confirmed downstream latency issue to the API Service owning team for remediation of the slow response condition that was driving 504s. Escalation ticket INC-AIT-0025-ESC was assigned to Jonathan Reeves (jreeves) at the Columbus service center, with Gold SLA priority and a 4-hour response commitment.

Updated alerting and correlation logging so downstream latency spikes, 504 rates, and integration backlog growth can be identified together and acted on earlier. New composite alert rules were configured in the Monitoring System by Marcus Delgado to trigger when p50 downstream latency exceeds 8 seconds concurrently with 504 error rate above 5% over a 5-minute window.

Monitored the environment for 4 hours after mitigation and confirmed a reduction in HTTP 504 occurrences and stabilization of integration job completion. Priya Nair verified via the Monitoring System that p50 latency returned to 1.8 seconds and the DataSyncApp backlog cleared by 16:30 UTC, with zero additional job failures observed from gateway pod IP 10.42.17.93.

Refresh and reapply the device startup policy to stagger resource-intensive startup tasks introduced by the recent January 30th policy change on LAPTOP-SALES-MK, ensuring no more than two background services initialize concurrently at login.

Free sufficient space on the C: drive by removing temporary files (~18 GB under C:\Users\mkaplan\AppData\Local\Temp) and other non-essential local data including Windows Update cache to reduce disk contention during startup and scan activity, targeting at least 25 GB free.

Reboot the laptop LAPTOP-SALES-MK after policy and remediation changes, then validate that CPU utilization settles below 30% within 5 minutes after login and Outlook and Chrome open within normal time (under 10 seconds). title: Print jobs stuck on FIN-PRQ-01
description: Finance users (reported initially by Priya Deshmukh, emp ID FIN-4821) were trying to print to shared queue FIN-PRQ-01 on print server PS-PRINT-01, but jobs remained stuck or the queue showed paused/offline. Cleared all 14 stuck print jobs from FIN-PRQ-01 (submitted by users p.deshmukh, mvitelli, sokonkwo) and remapped the queue to FIN-Printer-01 to restore the correct port binding.
Restarted the Print Spooler service on PS-PRINT-01 to reload the corrected driver and restore queue processing; verified spooler event log was clean post-restart.

Validated successful test prints from affected Finance user endpoints — WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PD (Priya Deshmukh, 10.42.17.65) and Marco Vitelli's workstation (10.42.17.88) — and monitored the queue for 30 minutes to confirm jobs processed normally with no recurrence.

title: VPN disconnects immediately
description: Several users in the Engineering group at the Frankfurt office were trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from managed Windows 10 21H2 endpoints. Affected users include Marcus Reinhardt (m.reinhardt@corplabs.com, EMP-40821), Priya Dasgupta (p.dasgupta@corplabs.com), and Leon Schäfer. observed_errors: TLS peer certificate expired during handshake
root_cause: Expired endpoint device certificate caused GlobalProtect TLS validation to fail immediately after successful Okta MFA approval, resulting in tunnel teardown during session establishment.
resolution_steps: Verified the affected endpoints (WORKSTATION-MR-4082 for m.reinhardt, WORKSTATION-PD-7731 for p.dasgupta, and l.schaefer's device) had expired device certificates issued 2025-04-18 and confirmed the certificate validation failure matched the VPN disconnect timing after MFA approval.

Renewed the expired device certificates for m.reinhardt (EMP-40821), p.dasgupta, and l.schaefer through the Device Certificate Service portal and confirmed successful issuance of replacement certificates with new 12-month validity periods.

Refreshed the GlobalProtect VPN profile on affected endpoints (WORKSTATION-MR-4082, WORKSTATION-PD-7731) and pushed the renewed certificate enrollment state via endpoint management to ensure the new certs were bound to the active VPN configuration.

Reconnected test sessions for m.reinhardt from WORKSTATION-MR-4082 (IP 10.47.83.112) and p.dasgupta from WORKSTATION-PD-7731 to validate that Okta MFA completed successfully, the VPN tunnel remained established through gateway vpn-gw-emea-01.corplabs.internal, and internal applications (Intranet Portal, Jira, Confluence) became reachable.

Updated certificate expiration monitoring in Device Certificate Service to alert the Frankfurt desktop support team 30 days before device certificate expiry, and added support notes to the Engineering group's runbook to reduce recurrence of device-certificate-driven VPN disconnects.

title: Multiple users cannot join Corporate Wi‑Fi; authentication failing
description: Multiple employees in the Denver HQ building were trying to connect managed laptops and mobile devices to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) starting around 08:00 on April 26. Devices could associate to the SSID but then showed no network access and disconnected repeatedly across Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android, blocking normal internet and corporate network use for staff on the affected floors (primarily floors 2–4). The issue was first reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez@corplabs.com) and subsequently confirmed by at least 40 additional users. Affected hostnames included WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG and several other managed endpoints.
observed_errors: NAC: device denied network access after association
root_cause: The 802.1X/RADIUS server certificate used for Corporate Wi-Fi authentication expired, causing EAP-TLS certificate validation failures and NAC denial after association.
resolution_steps: Renew and install a valid 802.1X/RADIUS server certificate on the wireless authentication infrastructure (radius-auth01.corplabs.internal) with the correct subject, validity period, and full certificate chain. Diane Choi (dchoi) submitted the CSR to the internal CA and received the renewed certificate with a new expiry of 2028-04-25.

Update the Network Access Control and related trust configuration to recognize the renewed certificate chain and ensure EAP-TLS validation succeeds. The NAC console was updated by kliu to reference the new certificate thumbprint and intermediate CA, and trust was verified against the CorpNet-Secure authentication policy.

Apply the updated certificate configuration on the wireless controller and authentication path, then restart or reload affected authentication services as required to clear the expired certificate state. Diane Choi (dchoi) deployed the renewed certificate to radius-auth01.corplabs.internal and performed a rolling restart of the RADIUS service at 15:32 to activate the new certificate.

Validate successful client authentication by testing managed Windows and macOS devices on the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID and confirming successful EAP-TLS handshakes, policy assignment, and network access. Verification was performed with mgonzalez on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG (IP 10.42.3.117) and rpatel's MacBook — both authenticated successfully and received full corporate network access within seconds of reconnecting.

Keep the temporary limited PSK guest SSID available only until production authentication is confirmed stable, then remove the workaround and notify users to reconnect if they cached failed sessions. Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez@corplabs.com) and other affected users on floors 2–4 in Denver were notified via email at 16:00 that Corporate Wi-Fi was restored and the guest SSID workaround would be disabled at 18:00.

title: BitLocker not enabling
description: I was trying to bring a company-managed Windows 11 laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-DELL-MR) into encryption compliance, but Company Portal continued to show the device as noncompliant for disk encryption. The device is assigned to me (Marcus Reeves, emp ID EMP-40821) and is located at our Portland office. I contacted our desktop team at endpoint-support@corplabs.com but the device remained blocked from meeting corporate security requirements because the encryption policy appeared targeted but was not applying successfully to complete compliant BitLocker protection.
observed_errors: Intune: No recovery key found for device
TPM initialization error during protector creation (reported during enablement step)
root_cause: Intune disk encryption policy assignment/applicability failure prevented the endpoint from receiving and enforcing the required BitLocker configuration, leaving recovery key escrow unavailable and the device noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the device's Intune policy targeting and applicability details for WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (enrolled user: mreeves). Identified that the assignment filter on the 'Corp-BitLocker-Win11' encryption profile excluded the device's enrollment category. Corrected the assignment filter to include the 'Corporate Laptops - Portland' device group, resolving the conflict preventing the encryption profile from applying.

Triggered a fresh device sync on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR after the policy assignment change (initiated via Intune portal at 2026-05-12T07:28:00Z) and confirmed the endpoint received the active disk encryption configuration 'Corp-BitLocker-Win11' without assignment errors. Profile status for mreeves updated to 'Succeeded'.

Forced BitLocker policy evaluation on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR using Invoke-GPUpdate and a manual Intune sync cycle, verified recovery key escrow became visible to support in the Intune BitLocker recovery keys blade under mreeves, and confirmed the device returned to compliant status in both Company Portal and the Intune Device Compliance dashboard. Marcus Reeves (EMP-40821) was notified at mreeves@corplabs.com that the device is now fully compliant.

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: My corporate Windows 10 22H2 laptop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MR, hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-MR) assigned to me (Marcus Reilly, emp ID EMP-40291) showed "Encryption Off" in Company Portal and was marked noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune. BitLocker was not enabled on the OS drive (C:), and no recovery key was visible in my Intune/Azure AD record, blocking compliance with the endpoint encryption policy on the managed device. I'm based in the Frankfurt office and need this resolved so I can access Sales resources again. My username is m.reilly and I can be reached at marcus.reilly@corplabs.com or +49 170 448 2913.
observed_errors: TPM state: No owner / Not initialized
Intune error: Recovery key escrow failed
root_cause: The device TPM was present but not initialized/owned, so a TPM-based BitLocker protector could not be created. This prevented BitLocker from starting on the OS drive and caused Intune recovery key escrow to fail during encryption policy application.
resolution_steps: Validated local BitLocker and TPM state on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (user m.reilly, IP 10.42.17.88) using manage-bde -status C: and Get-Tpm, confirming the OS drive had Protection Off with no usable TPM protector configured and TpmReady was False.

Initialized TPM ownership on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR via Initialize-Tpm and brought the TPM to a ready state (TpmReady: True, TpmOwned: True) so a valid BitLocker TPM protector could be created on the endpoint.

Enabled BitLocker on the operating system drive C: using Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -TpmProtector -RecoveryPasswordProtector and started disk encryption successfully. manage-bde -status C: confirmed Encryption In Progress.

Forced an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR so the active encryption policy "EMEA-Endpoint-Encryption-v3" reapplied and recovery key escrow retried after the TPM protector was in place. Sync completed without errors.

Verified the recovery key was escrowed to the Azure AD tenant record for WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and confirmed the device compliance state updated from noncompliant to compliant in Intune. Notified Marcus Reilly (marcus.reilly@corplabs.com) that encryption is active and compliance is restored.

title: Expired TLS certificate resurfaced on internal web service
description: Users were trying to reach the internal HTTPS service at https://internal-api.corp and related internal applications, but browsers displayed certificate warnings and TLS connections failed starting this morning. Certificate bundle was pulled by Rafael Simmons (rsimmons) from the internal CA portal and validated against the expected CN and SAN entries.

Updated the load balancer (LB-EAST-02.corp.internal) listener TLS configuration to replace the expired certificate and attach the full renewed chain instead of the stale LB certificate bundle. Configuration change was applied by Danielle Ortiz with change ticket CHG-88412.

Reloaded the load balancer configuration on LB-EAST-02.corp.internal so new TLS handshakes began serving the renewed certificate path to clients. Service was confirmed live within 2 minutes of the reload.

Validated the endpoint certificate subject, expiration date, and trust chain from multiple client perspectives — including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (Marcus Chen, Portland) and WORKSTATION-DESK-PN (Priya Nair, Seattle) — and confirmed the TLS handshake completed successfully without certificate warnings.

Reviewed and restored certificate monitoring and renewal alert coverage so future renewals include the load balancer deployment step and trigger notification before expiration. Added LB-fronted endpoint checks and assigned renewal verification ownership to rsimmons with escalation notifications to dortiz.

title: Device marked noncompliant after policy update

The issue was initially reported by Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen, emp ID EMP-40821) from the Arlington office, whose device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (IP 10.42.17.88) was among the first flagged. The Intune portal showed the encryption-related signal as missing ("EncryptionMissing") and compliance state remained stale even after same-day device check-ins and successful remote sync attempts. The issue affected access controlled by Conditional Access because devices that were already encrypted were still evaluated against an older policy reference and blocked from normal access until compliance re-evaluated. Additional reports came from Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) and Priya Kapoor (pkapoor) in the same Mobile Workforce group.
observed_errors: Compliance evaluation shows stale policy id
root_cause: A stale compliance policy reference remained attached during Intune compliance evaluation, so the current encryption state was not read correctly and devices were assessed against an older policy revision, producing the EncryptionMissing result and stale noncompliant status.
resolution_steps: Verified the affected devices (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN for rnguyen, WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-MD for mdelgado, WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PK for pkapoor) were still referencing an older compliance policy revision (CompliancePolicy-Encryption-Check-v1) during evaluation and identified the stale encryption compliance assignment in the Arlington Mobile Workforce group.

Updated affected assignments to use the current policy reference, CompliancePolicy-Encryption-Check-v2, in place of the stale policy revision CompliancePolicy-Encryption-Check-v1. Change was executed by Tom Briggs (tbriggs) and confirmed in the Intune admin console.

Triggered remote sync and device check-in for impacted endpoints (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN, WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-MD, WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PK) so the updated compliance policy and fresh compliance evaluation were pulled from Intune.

Validated that the encryption attribute (BitLocker) was present after re-evaluation and confirmed devices with active encryption transitioned back to Compliant status. All three devices showed Compliant within 15 minutes of the forced re-evaluation.

Provided user guidance to Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com), Marcus Delgado, and Priya Kapoor for the remaining edge cases to confirm local encryption state via the Company Portal app and reboot the device, then rechecked compliance until status updated successfully. Users were advised to contact the service desk at ext 4-7193 if issues recurred.

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: User Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) on a corporate Surface Pro 7 running Windows 10 22H2, hostname WORKSTATION-SURFPRO-RN, reported BitLocker showing Off in Windows Settings while Microsoft Intune marked the device noncompliant for encryption. The device TPM was present and a BitLocker policy had recently applied, but no recovery key was visible in Azure AD for the device, blocking compliant encryption state and creating a risk that the device could not be recovered if encryption started without successful key backup. Rachel reported the issue from the Portland office and noted she needed the laptop compliant before an upcoming client visit.
observed_errors: Intune compliance check: Encryption not present
root_cause: BitLocker enablement was blocked from reaching a compliant managed state because the recovery key failed to escrow to Azure AD/Intune with access denied error 0x80070005 after TPM protector initialization, leaving local encryption status and cloud compliance state out of sync.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the TPM was present on WORKSTATION-SURFPRO-RN and initialized a TPM-based BitLocker protector on the device so encryption could be started with supported hardware protection. Verified TPM version 2.0 readiness via Get-Tpm cmdlet.

Started BitLocker locally on the C: volume and verified the volume entered encryption after the protector was added, establishing that the endpoint could encrypt even though Intune compliance for r.nguyen's device had not yet updated.

Forced an Intune policy sync on WORKSTATION-SURFPRO-RN (IP 10.42.17.88) and re-applied the encryption policy so the device could retry recovery key backup and compliance evaluation against the current assignment.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key and retried backup of the current recovery password to Azure AD after the initial escrow attempt failed with 0x80070005, then verified that a recovery Key ID became available in the Intune cloud management view under Rachel Nguyen's device record (EMP-40821).

Validated that Intune compliance refreshed after successful key escrow and that WORKSTATION-SURFPRO-RN no longer reported encryption noncompliance. Notified r.nguyen@corplabs.com that the device is now fully compliant and the recovery key is safely escrowed.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel, this is Kevin Marsh from the endpoint support team. Could you please confirm whether BitLocker still shows Off in Windows Settings on WORKSTATION-SURFPRO-RN and whether any recovery key is visible for this device in Azure AD after the recent policy push? Also, can you verify you're logged in with your corporate account r.nguyen@corplabs.com so we can cross-reference the device enrollment status in Intune?

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Nightly integration jobs from the Integration Gateway (pod ig-prod-worker-07 on cluster k8s-east-prod) to the downstream API Service were delayed between 23:50–00:15 UTC on 2025-12-04 in us-east-1. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Dallas application support team after the overnight data synchronization workflow failed to complete on schedule. Monitoring System dashboards showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and 401 token_expired errors originating from service account svc-ig-sync, causing queued sync jobs to fail and data ingestion to lag by over 25 minutes. The blocked task was the overnight data synchronization workflow feeding the Ingestion Worker pipeline, with impact to downstream application data freshness for the finance and analytics consumers until authentication and retry behavior were corrected.
root_cause: Expired API credential on the Integration Gateway caused token refresh failures, leading to 401 token_expired responses and subsequent downstream call timeouts during the nightly sync window.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token for service account svc-ig-sync configured on the Integration Gateway pod ig-prod-worker-07 and confirmed the gateway could successfully authenticate to the downstream API Service at https://api.corplabs.internal/v2/ingest. Rotation performed by Rachel Nguyen (rng0042) at approximately 00:18 UTC.

Validated that token refresh operations for svc-ig-sync completed successfully after the credential update by reviewing gateway logs on ig-prod-worker-07 and confirming that new API requests no longer returned 401 token_expired errors.

Cleared and reprocessed 14 affected integration queue items so delayed nightly sync jobs could resume with valid authentication; Marcus Delgado (E-50821) confirmed data freshness was restored for downstream finance and analytics consumers by 00:32 UTC.

Updated the token_refresh_policy for svc-ig-sync to enforce automated renewal checks 7 days before credential expiry and configured a Monitoring System alert to notify the Dallas application support team (appsupp-dallas@corplabs.com) before credential expiration to prevent recurrence.

Adjusted the integration retry and backoff configuration on ig-prod-worker-07 from a fixed 5s interval to exponential backoff (initial 2s, max 120s, jitter enabled) to better tolerate transient downstream latency without exhausting jobs during the nightly sync window.

Monitored logs and Monitoring System metrics for 24 hours after remediation to confirm normal API latency on the /v2/ingest endpoint, successful sync completion for all scheduled jobs, and no further 401 or 504 spikes. Rachel Nguyen signed off on the 24-hour observation at 2025-12-05T13:00:00Z.

title: Intermittent internal DNS resolution failures for app.payments.corp
description: Internal applications were trying to resolve the backend hostname app.payments.corp, but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or timed out against internal DNS after the prior night's DNS maintenance. The issue was reported by engineer Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com, EMP-40821) and observed from multiple clients and regions including the Chicago and Austin offices, preventing the payments service from reliably reaching its internal dependency by name and causing intermittent application failures across the corp-net environment.
root_cause: DNS maintenance left inconsistent internal resolver state for the app.payments.corp zone path, with stale or incorrect cached data and/or forwarder handling causing intermittent negative responses and timeouts despite the zone record needing to resolve internally. The incident behavior across multiple hosts and regions points to resolver-side cache/forwarder inconsistency rather than a single client issue.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal zone record and recent maintenance changes for app.payments.corp to confirm the expected target value (10.30.5.120) and TTL (300s) after the DNS work performed during change CHG-90412 by mreeves on 2026-01-07.

Validated resolution from affected clients (WORKSTATION-PN-7241 at 10.44.12.87 for pnair in Chicago, WORKSTATION-DLEE-3390 at 10.44.18.22 for dlee in Austin) against the internal resolver and compared results with the authoritative or known-good internal DNS path to confirm inconsistent resolver behavior.

Cleared positive and negative caches on the impacted internal caching resolvers (DNS-CACHE-01.corplabs.internal and DNS-CACHE-03.corplabs.internal) and verified conditional forwarder or zone routing configuration for the payments.corp namespace, ensuring the forwarder pointed to DNS-AUTH-02.corplabs.internal.

Corrected the resolver-side DNS path so app.payments.corp returned the current internal record (10.30.5.120) consistently, then restarted or refreshed the caching service where required on DNS-CACHE-01 and DNS-CACHE-03.

Had affected clients (pnair on WORKSTATION-PN-7241, dlee on WORKSTATION-DLEE-3390) flush local DNS cache and retest name resolution, confirming the hostname resolved consistently without NXDOMAIN or timeout responses.

Monitored resolver metrics and incident symptoms via Network Monitoring after the change window to verify the spikes in NXDOMAIN and timeouts did not recur, with mreeves confirming stable resolution across Chicago and Austin regions for 4 hours post-fix.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please confirm whether app.payments.corp fails only through the standard internal resolver (DNS-CACHE-01.corplabs.internal, 10.20.1.53) or also when tested against another known-good internal DNS path such as DNS-AUTH-02.corplabs.internal, and whether the issue started immediately after last night's DNS maintenance. Also, can you let us know which client hostnames or IPs you tested from?

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts to Billing API causing delayed data sync
description: Automated monitoring detected that Integration Gateway requests to the Billing API in us-east-1 began timing out around 2025-12-12T09:40:00Z. Outbound calls from integration node INTGW-PROD-04 (10.22.18.97) returned repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and some requests exceeded the 30 second timeout window, causing integration jobs to fail and delaying customer billing data synchronization. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the AppIntegrationTeam in Charlotte. The issue affected API-based sync processing on Kubernetes (EKS) and created downstream data freshness impact until Billing API latency was reduced. Ticket opened on behalf of the integration operations group by agent Priya Nair (EMP-40821).
root_cause: Elevated downstream Billing API response latency caused Integration Gateway requests to exceed the configured timeout window, resulting in 504 Gateway Timeout errors and failed sync jobs.
resolution_steps: Correlated the Integration Gateway alert window on INTGW-PROD-04 (source IP 10.22.18.97) with downstream Billing API latency metrics in the Monitoring System and confirmed timeout failures were aligned with increased response times (p99 ~48s) from the dependent service between 09:40 and 11:52 UTC. Analysis performed by Priya Nair (pnair, EMP-40821).

Applied a temporary mitigation by increasing the Integration Gateway request timeout from 30 seconds to 60 seconds on INTGW-PROD-04 to reduce immediate job failures while the dependency issue was investigated. Change logged under CR-20251212-0041 and approved by pnair.

Adjusted the gateway retry and backoff policy on INTGW-PROD-04 (max retries increased from 3 to 5, exponential backoff base set to 2 seconds) to better tolerate transient downstream slowness and allow delayed requests to complete successfully.

Escalated the incident to the Billing API team lead Tomás Reyes (treyes) with evidence of repeated 504 responses and elevated latency observed from Integration Gateway transactions on INTGW-PROD-04. Escalation included distributed trace samples and latency percentile charts from the Monitoring System covering the 09:40–11:52 UTC window.

Validated recovery after the Billing API team reduced service latency (connection pool fix deployed by treyes) by monitoring end-to-end requests from INTGW-PROD-04 and confirming timeout rates dropped to 0% and billing data sync jobs completed successfully. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) in Charlotte confirmed data freshness restored in the operations dashboard.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: Multiple remote users on managed Windows 10 and macOS 12 devices—including reports from jmarquez (emp ID: EMP-40291) in the Raleigh office and kpatel in the Charlotte office—were trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN gateway (vpn-east.corplabs.com) to reach internal applications including CRM, Confluence, and JIRA. observed_errors: VPN tunnel closed immediately after successful authentication
root_cause: Expired device certificates on managed corporate endpoints caused GlobalProtect device certificate validation to fail during post-authentication tunnel establishment, resulting in immediate VPN teardown after successful Okta MFA approval.
resolution_steps: Renew the expired device certificates (serial range 7A:3F:91:xx, issued April 2025) for the affected enrollment cohort of 37 devices through the Device Certificate Service admin console, prioritizing users jmarquez and kpatel who reported the issue.

Push refreshed device certificates to impacted Windows and macOS corporate devices (including WORKSTATION-JMARQ and WORKSTATION-KPATEL) using the MDM enrollment profile, confirming delivery via MDM compliance dashboard.
Deploy updated GlobalProtect VPN profiles (profile version 2026-04-R2) so the client uses the current enrolled device certificate during tunnel establishment on gateway vpn-east.corplabs.com.

Have affected users (jmarquez, kpatel, and others in the US-East cohort) remove any stale local GlobalProtect profile from C:\ProgramData\Palo Alto Networks\GlobalProtect or ~/Library/Application Support/PaloAltoNetworks/GlobalProtect, or re-enroll the device via the Device Certificate Service portal if the old certificate continues to be presented.

Validate successful VPN connection after Okta MFA approval on representative affected devices (WORKSTATION-JMARQ at IP 10.42.19.103 and WORKSTATION-KPATEL at IP 10.42.18.77) and confirm internal application access to CRM, Confluence, and JIRA is restored. Sandra Whitfield to coordinate user confirmation.

Monitor GlobalProtect gateway logs and Device Certificate Service enrollment alerts for recurrence of certificate expiration or validation failures after rollout; set a calendar reminder for the next renewal window (April 2027) to proactively renew certificates before expiry.

title: BitLocker encryption not enabled
description: I have a corporate Windows 10 21H2 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, asset tag SLS-4821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (employee ID E-50274) showing "Encryption not enabled" in Windows Settings and noncompliant status in Intune after a recent BitLocker policy deployment. The device at IP 10.28.44.113 was not encrypting the system drive (C:), the BitLocker recovery key was not visible in Azure AD/Intune, and Marcus was blocked by endpoint compliance requirements until disk encryption and key escrow were restored. The user reached out from the Charlotte office and needs this resolved urgently for an upcoming client visit.
root_cause: The device TPM was not in a ready state to initialize a BitLocker TPM protector, so BitLocker could not create the required protector on C: or escrow the recovery key to Azure AD, causing Intune compliance to continue reporting encryption failure.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM status on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR via Get-Tpm and tpm.msc, cleared stale TPM ownership state using Clear-Tpm, rebooted the device, and initialized the TPM so it was ready for BitLocker protector creation. Performed remotely by agent Priya Nandakumar (pnandakumar).

Added a TPM-based protector to the C: volume on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and enabled BitLocker with a recovery password using 'manage-bde -on C: -RecoveryPassword -TpmProtector' after confirming the protector could be created successfully. Encryption began at approximately 2026-01-24T01:20:00Z.

Forced an Intune/MDM sync from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR via Company Portal so the active disk encryption policy and updated encryption state for user mreeves were reported back to management. Sync completed and device check-in timestamp updated in Intune admin console.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR using 'Invoke-MgDeviceManagementManagedDeviceRotateBitLockerKey' and confirmed the current recovery password escrowed successfully to Azure AD for support retrieval. Recovery key ID 7A3F2B visible under the device record for Marcus Reeves (E-50274).

Verified the endpoint WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR showed BitLocker protection active locally (manage-bde -status C: returned 'Protection On', 'Encryption Method: XTS-AES 256') and that Intune Device Compliance updated the device to compliant for encryption. Notified Marcus Reeves at mreeves@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved and the device is cleared for travel to the Raleigh branch.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether the laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR shows BitLocker as off in Windows Settings and whether any TPM or device security warnings appear locally after the recent encryption policy rollout. title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures for svc-api.internal.corp with conflicting remediation evidence
description: Internal users in the Newark office were trying to reach svc-api through the hostname svc-api.internal.corp, but name resolution was intermittent across the on-prem DNS environment. The issue was first reported by developer Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40821) at approximately 08:30 UTC on 2026-01-14. Some clients received NXDOMAIN while others were returned a stale A record pointing to the old IP 10.2.3.4, which prevented dependent applications such as svc-api and the internal dashboard from consistently reaching the internal endpoint. Resolver logs on dns-res-01.internal.corp and dns-res-02.internal.corp, along with Network Monitoring alerts, indicated mixed responses across DNS servers, with SERVFAIL spikes during the incident window and inconsistent resolver configuration contributing to impact. Workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC belonging to mchen was among the first to exhibit the failure.
observed_errors: stale A record (old IP 10.2.3.4) served by some resolvers
root_cause: Inconsistent DNS resolver state caused intermittent failures: the authoritative record had been stale, some resolvers continued serving cached old data, and two domain controller resolvers were missing the required conditional forwarder for the corp-ad path, resulting in mixed NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, and stale-address responses depending on which resolver answered the query.
resolution_steps: Updated the authoritative A record for svc-api.internal.corp on dns-auth-01.internal.corp from the stale 10.2.3.4 to the correct current IP 10.2.7.15, and verified the Internal DNS Zone data reflected the intended value and a TTL of 300s. Change performed by Tomás Rivera (trivera).

Flushed DNS caches on the primary and secondary internal resolvers (dns-res-01.internal.corp and dns-res-02.internal.corp) using dnscmd /clearcache so they would stop serving the previously cached 10.2.3.4 address.

Added and standardized the missing conditional forwarder configuration on the two domain controller resolvers DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and DC-EAST-04.corplabs.internal so all resolvers used the same resolution path for the internal.corp zone via corp-ad.

Validated resolution from multiple resolver paths and client perspectives — confirmed correct 10.2.7.15 response from mchen's workstation (10.14.22.87), rpatel's endpoint (10.14.23.41), and three additional Newark developer machines to confirm the hostname no longer returned mixed NXDOMAIN or stale-address results.

Requested affected teams in Newark to clear local DNS caches on impacted endpoints (ipconfig /flushdns) and monitored Network Monitoring dashboards for recurrence until lookup failures and stale responses subsided. Final confirmation received from Maria Chen at 10:15 UTC.

title: Multiple users cannot connect to Corporate Wi-Fi — expired certificate
description: Multiple employees in the Charlotte office were trying to join the Corp-Enterprise wireless network but devices either failed 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentication or associated without receiving usable network access. The issue was first reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed by at least six other users on the 4th floor. root_cause: Wireless controller server certificate expired on 2026-04-30, causing EAP-TLS authentication failures and RADIUS rejects; after renewal, a subset of endpoints still had stale Wi-Fi profile or certificate trust state that required re-enrollment.
resolution_steps: Renewed the wireless controller server certificate (CN=wlc-east-01.corp.netinfra.local) and verified the certificate chain presented for Corp-Enterprise authentication; new certificate valid through 2028-04-30, uploaded by Raj Anand (ranand).

Restarted the AAA/RADIUS integration on the authentication server so the controller and authentication services began using the renewed certificate for 802.1X transactions; restart performed at 2026-05-02T15:24Z.

Validated successful authentication and network access with a pilot device (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG, user mgonzalez, IP 10.42.18.97) after the certificate replacement and AAA restart — full connectivity confirmed at 15:25Z.

Remediated affected endpoints by having users (dpham, krusso, and four others in Charlotte) forget the Corp-Enterprise SSID and re-enroll the wireless profile, with updated certificate trust delivered through MDM for managed devices such as WORKSTATION-PC-DP.

Reviewed authentication and NAC logs after remediation to confirm failed certificate-expired rejects cleared and devices were again receiving normal access policy; final verification completed by Raj Anand (ranand) at 2026-05-02T16:10Z with zero outstanding rejects for the Charlotte site.

title: Multiple users fail to connect to Corporate Wi-Fi — NAC rejects devices

Initial reports were filed by floor warden Kevin Pratt (kpratt@corpnet.com) who noted at least 30 affected staff members.
root_cause: An early-morning NAC configuration change introduced incorrect policy mapping for the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID, causing valid 802.1X/EAP-TLS device authentications to miss the intended access policy and be rejected by NAC/RADIUS.
resolution_steps: Identify and remove or roll back the NAC policy change introduced by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) at 06:45 that altered Corporate Wi-Fi policy matching on Cisco ISE. The misconfigured policy set condition in the 'CorpWiFi-Managed-Devices' authorization rule was reverted to the previous known-good configuration snapshot from 2026-04-28.

Correct the NAC policy assignments for the CorpWiFi-Secure SSID on Cisco ISE, including restoring the intended authentication rule, the 'CorpWiFi-FullAccess' authorization profile, and the RADIUS profile mapping used for corporate-managed endpoints. Priya Vasquez (pvasquez) validated the corrected policy set against the change management baseline.

Validate that affected device classes receive the correct network access result after authentication by testing a pilot set across Windows, iOS, and Android devices. Pilot devices included WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP (kpratt, floor 4), WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RN (rnguyen, floor 6), and Tom Brierly's Android device (tbrierly, floor 8) — all three received 'CorpWiFi-FullAccess' authorization successfully.

Clear or refresh any stale session state for impacted wireless authentications on Cisco ISE as needed, then have affected users reconnect or refresh their wireless profile/certificate enrollment if their device remained in a rejected state. Kevin Pratt (kpratt@corpnet.com) coordinated with floor wardens to notify approximately 30 affected staff to toggle Wi-Fi or reconnect.

Monitor NAC and wireless controller logs after the change to confirm RADIUS rejects return to normal baseline and users can associate and obtain network access across floors 4, 6, and 8 in the Denver North Tower. Priya Vasquez confirmed RADIUS reject rate dropped to baseline within 20 minutes of the policy rollback, and no further reports were received by 14:00.

Can you also verify whether your own device (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KP) is experiencing the same rejection? We need to rule out a localized AP issue versus a broader NAC policy problem.
