description: I, Jane Doe (jane.doe@corplabs.com, employee ID FIN-20418), am based in the Chicago office in Finance. I was trying to open the Finance shared drive from mapped drive Z: and the UNC path \\fileserver.corplabs.internal\Finance on my Windows 10 workstation (WORKSTATION-FDESK-JD, IP 10.22.14.87). Access attempts intermittently prompted for credentials and then returned "Access is denied" (0x80070005), preventing access to department folders needed for normal Finance file work. Issue was isolated to my access entitlement rather than a general shared drive outage.
observed_errors: Mapped drive repeatedly prompts for credentials
root_cause: User account was missing membership in the FINANCE_SHARE Active Directory security group required by the file server ACL for \\fileserver\Finance.
resolution_steps: Validated that the NTFS/share permissions on \\fileserver.corplabs.internal\Finance allow access only to FINANCE_SHARE and Finance_Admins, confirming the access model was functioning as designed. Colleague Marcus Reeves (marcus.reeves@corplabs.com) in Finance verified no general outage.

Added jane.doe to the FINANCE_SHARE Active Directory security group on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal to grant the required shared drive entitlement. Change performed by Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) from the Service Desk.
Had the user sign out of workstation WORKSTATION-FDESK-JD and sign back in to refresh the Windows Kerberos logon token so the updated FINANCE_SHARE group membership would be included in the session.

Retested access using the current Finance path and confirmed \\fileserver.corplabs.internal\Finance and mapped drive Z: opened successfully without credential prompts from workstation WORKSTATION-FDESK-JD (10.22.14.87).
Confirmed the user Jane Doe could open Finance department folders after the entitlement update, closing the incident as resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Jane, this is Priya Nair from the Service Desk. Please confirm whether the access denied message appears on both mapped drive Z: and when opening \\fileserver.corplabs.internal\Finance directly from Explorer, and whether other Finance team members (for example, your colleague Marcus Reeves) can still access the same folders from their workstations.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data syncs
description: Scheduled data sync jobs through the Integration Gateway (namespace: intg-gateway-prod, cluster: k8s-east-prod-04) began failing or queuing at approximately 09:12 UTC on 2025-12-08 because POST requests to the downstream API Service endpoint https://api-svc.corplabs.internal/v2/sync were returning repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Application Support team in the Charlotte office, noting that data lag for the integration workflow in the Kubernetes environment in us-east-1 had exceeded 45 minutes and was blocking timely completion of routine sync processing for the customer-data pipeline. Investigation focused on whether the failures were caused by expired authentication tokens, API rate limiting, or elevated downstream response latency. Ticket was assigned to senior integration engineer Priya Nair (emp ID: EMP-40821) for triage.
root_cause: Sustained elevated latency in the downstream API Service caused Integration Gateway requests to exceed the configured upstream timeout threshold, producing 504 Gateway Timeout responses and causing scheduled sync jobs to fail or backlog.
resolution_steps: Validated that authentication was not the trigger by confirming there was no matching pattern of 401 or 403 failures for service account svc-intg-sync during the timeout window (09:12–09:24 UTC); token expiry date verified as 2026-03-15.

Confirmed the timeout condition was latency-driven by correlating 14 failed integration jobs with downstream API latency spikes (p95: 48s vs. 1.2s baseline) and repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses on pod intg-gw-worker-7b4d9, as identified by Priya Nair.

Temporarily increased the Integration Gateway request timeout from 30 seconds to 90 seconds in the intg-gateway-prod namespace ConfigMap so in-flight downstream calls could complete during the latency event; change applied at 09:31 UTC.

Adjusted retry and exponential backoff settings on upstream calls (max retries: 5, initial backoff: 2s, multiplier: 2x) to reduce immediate job failure rates and avoid excessive retry pressure while the downstream service remained slow.

Cleared 14 queued integration jobs and monitored processing throughput via the Monitoring System until the sync backlog returned to acceptable levels at 09:48 UTC; confirmed with Marcus Delgado in Charlotte that data lag was resolved.

Escalated the incident to the downstream API service team lead Robert Cheng (rcheng) via ESC-7841 with supporting latency trends, Grafana snapshots, and request traces (trx-8a3f29c), and updated Monitoring System alert thresholds to detect future 95th-percentile latency spikes above 10 seconds earlier.

title: Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service — load balancer chain not
description: Internal users across the Chicago office were trying to access the internal web service at https://portal.internal.corpinfra.net, but browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID certificate warnings and Nagios monitoring reported TLS handshake failures starting around 07:45 UTC on 2025-12-24. The outage was initially reported by Maria Gonzalez (emp ID E-40291) and escalated by the on-call infrastructure engineer David Chen. The outage continued after the certificate was renewed at the internal Certificate Authority (ca01.pki.corpinfra.net) because the load balancer cluster (lb-frontend-01 through lb-frontend-04) kept presenting the old expired certificate chain, so users and dependent clients — including the payroll integration service — could not complete trusted TLS connections until the load balancer deployment was corrected across all four nodes.
root_cause: The internal web service certificate expired, the renewal alerting did not prevent the lapse, and the renewed full certificate chain was not deployed to all load balancer nodes after CA renewal. As a result, the load balancer continued presenting an expired chain to clients and caused TLS validation failures.
resolution_steps: Verified the renewed certificate at the internal Certificate Authority (ca01.pki.corpinfra.net), confirming serial 4A:7C:3E:91 with validity 2025-12-24 through 2026-12-24 and SAN coverage for portal.internal.corpinfra.net, to confirm the replacement certificate itself was usable. Verification performed by David Chen (dchen, emp ID E-50184).

Updated the full certificate chain on the load balancer cluster (lb-frontend-01 through lb-frontend-04) so the HAProxy frontend listener presented the renewed certificate and required intermediate CA instead of the expired chain (serial 2F:8B:01:AA). New bundle deployed to /etc/ssl/certs/portal-chain.pem by Priya Sharma (psharma).

Redeployed the certificate bundle to all four load balancer nodes (lb-frontend-01, lb-frontend-02, lb-frontend-03, lb-frontend-04) via Ansible playbook and restarted HAProxy worker processes on each node so every node loaded the updated chain consistently. Deployment confirmed by psharma at 09:22 UTC.

Validated TLS handshakes and certificate presentation from multiple regions (us-east-1 and us-west-2) and client perspectives — including from Maria Gonzalez's workstation (10.22.14.87) and Raj Patel's workstation (10.22.14.92) — to confirm the expired certificate warning was cleared and openssl s_client returned 'Verify return code: 0 (ok)'.

Restored and tuned Nagios certificate renewal monitoring for portal.internal.corpinfra.net so alerting triggers at 30 days and 7 days before expiration (--warning 30 --critical 7), and configured a deployment verification check so failed or incomplete certificate deployments to load balancer nodes are visible earlier. Alert recipients updated to include dchen@corpinfra.net and psharma@corpinfra.net.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — this is David Chen from Infrastructure. Please confirm whether the browser warning (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) still appears after the CA renewal completed at 08:15 UTC, and whether the same error is seen from multiple regions or only from the Chicago endpoint. Also, can you share the hostname or IP you're connecting from so we can correlate with load balancer logs?

title: account locked
description: I was trying to regain access to the Corporate SSO portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) but was blocked after repeated failed sign-in attempts locked my Active Directory account (username: j.smith, Employee ID: EMP-20418). A password reset was attempted through the Password Reset Portal, but the reset token was reported as expired and SSO continued to deny access. The issue affected account access across AD, the reset service, and SSO, with likely continued failed authentication coming from my iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-JS) using cached credentials. Activity was noted from IP 10.4.32.18. I'm based in the Raleigh office and need access restored urgently for sprint work. — Jordan Smith, jordan.smith@corplabs.com, ext. 4738.
observed_errors: Account locked due to too many failed attempts
root_cause: Active Directory domain lockout policy was triggered by repeated failed authentication attempts from a mobile device with stale cached credentials, preventing SSO access; the user's reset attempt did not complete recovery because the password reset token had already expired.
resolution_steps: Unlock the user's Active Directory account for j.smith (CN=j.smith,OU=Engineering,DC=corplabs,DC=internal, Employee ID EMP-20418) and verify the lockout state has cleared in directory services on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal.

Invalidate the expired password reset token (issued at 22:15 UTC, TTL exceeded) and issue a new reset token via the Password Reset Portal so Jordan Smith can complete a fresh password reset at https://sso.corplabs.com/reset.

Have Jordan remove and re-enter saved credentials on mobile mail and Teams applications on device WORKSTATION-IPHONE-JS, and confirm stale credentials are no longer stored on the affected iOS device. Jordan can be reached at 919-555-0147 or jordan.smith@corplabs.com if walkthrough assistance is needed.

Review lockout events (Event ID 4740) and repeated authentication attempts associated with IP 10.4.32.18 on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal to confirm the mobile device WORKSTATION-IPHONE-JS was the active source of the failed sign-ins and that the attempts stopped after cache removal.

Validate that the new password has propagated to AD-backed authentication across domain controllers and confirm Jordan Smith (j.smith) can successfully sign in to the Corporate SSO portal at https://sso.corplabs.com from both laptop and mobile device.

title: Corporate Wi-Fi: Devices show 'No network access'
description: Users in the London office were able to join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpWiFi-5G) and complete 802.1X authentication via ClearPass NAC, but devices then showed "No network access" and could not reach internal resources. The issue started after an overnight configuration push at approximately 02:30 UTC on 2026-04-27 and affected both laptops and mobile devices across floors 3–5 of the London building. Staff member Rachel Nguyen (emp ID EMP-40821) first reported the problem at 08:15 local time, and multiple other users including contractor David Kowalski confirmed the same symptoms. The issue blocked normal corporate network access for staff and contractors, preventing access to intranet portals and shared drives.
observed_errors: 802.1X authentication succeeded but NAC denies network access
root_cause: An incorrect AD group-to-NAC policy mapping introduced during the overnight configuration push assigned valid authenticated users to the Quarantined access role instead of the normal corporate access policy.
resolution_steps: Reviewed ClearPass/NAC and wireless controller policy decisions to confirm authenticated users were being mapped to the Quarantined role because of an incorrect AD group association. Network engineer James Thornton (j.thornton, EMP-55193) examined the ClearPass Access Tracker entries for users r.nguyen, d.kowalski, and p.mehta, verifying that the enforcement profile 'Quarantine-Restricted' was incorrectly applied following change CHG-88214.

Applied a temporary allow rule on the NAC platform to restore production access for impacted users while the permanent policy correction was prepared. The rule was scoped to the London wireless VLANs (VLAN 142, 143) and activated at 13:58 UTC by j.thornton.

Corrected the AD group-to-NAC policy mapping so valid corporate users and contractors were assigned the appropriate production access role instead of Quarantined. The mapping for AD group CN=CorpWiFi-Users,OU=Wireless Groups,DC=corplabs,DC=internal was updated to reference the Corp-Wireless-Access enforcement profile, and the contractor group mapping was similarly corrected.

Pushed the corrected policy mapping to the NAC environment and wireless controller, then validated that newly connecting devices received the expected access role and network access. Validation was performed by having r.nguyen and d.kowalski reconnect their devices (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and WORKSTATION-SURFACE-DK respectively), confirming role=Corp-Employee assignment in ClearPass.

Instructed affected users to forget and rejoin the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID, and re-enroll the wireless profile on devices that continued to present stale policy or profile state. Rachel Nguyen (r.nguyen@corplabs.com, phone +44 20 7946 3128) and Priya Mehta (p.mehta@corplabs.com) were contacted directly with step-by-step instructions.

Monitored post-change authentication and role-assignment logs to confirm the misassignment no longer recurred after the corrected policy deployment. James Thornton reviewed ClearPass logs for a 4-hour window following the fix and confirmed all London wireless authentications received the correct Corp-Employee or Contractor-Access roles with no Quarantined assignments.

title: VPN disconnects immediately after Okta MFA approval
description: I was trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN from my managed Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-LT-MREEVES) while working remotely from Frankfurt. After approving the Okta MFA push notification on my phone, the VPN session established briefly — I could see the 'Connected' status for about 2–3 seconds — and then disconnected almost immediately, preventing access to internal applications including the intranet portal, CRM, and file shares. My username is mreeves and my employee ID is EMP-40821. I've been experiencing this consistently since this morning. My current IP is 85.214.47.103.
root_cause: Expired device certificate on the endpoint caused the GlobalProtect TLS handshake to fail after successful Okta MFA approval, which terminated the VPN tunnel immediately after authentication.
resolution_steps: Verified the endpoint device certificate on WORKSTATION-LT-MREEVES (serial 4A:7C:91:DE:03) had expired on 2026-04-19 and matched the TLS handshake failure ('TLS handshake failed: certificate expired') seen in GlobalProtect session logs on gp-emea.corplabs.internal for user mreeves.

Renewed the device certificate for WORKSTATION-LT-MREEVES through the Device Certificate Service enrollment portal and deployed the updated certificate (new expiry 2027-04-22) to the affected laptop used by Marcus Reeves (EMP-40821) in the Frankfurt office.

Refreshed the enrolled certificate profile and GlobalProtect VPN profile on the client WORKSTATION-LT-MREEVES to ensure the renewed certificate was presented during tunnel establishment. Cleared the stale cached profile from %ProgramData%\Palo Alto Networks\GlobalProtect and triggered a re-enrollment.

Forced a new GlobalProtect connection from WORKSTATION-LT-MREEVES (IP 85.214.47.103) after profile refresh and confirmed the VPN tunnel to gp-emea.corplabs.internal remained established after Okta MFA approval by mreeves. Tunnel uptime exceeded 15 minutes with no drops.

Validated access to internal applications over the VPN — confirmed mreeves could reach the Intranet Portal (https://intranet.corplabs.com), CRM, and file shares (\\fs-emea-01.corplabs.internal) — and monitored the session for 30 minutes for recurrence to confirm the disconnect issue was fully resolved. Advised Marcus Reeves to contact the service desk at ext. 4400 if the issue recurs.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. I'm Agent Priya Nair from the Network Support team. Please confirm whether the VPN disconnect happens before MFA approval or only after you approve the Okta prompt, and whether internal apps become unreachable immediately after the tunnel drops. Also, could you confirm the hostname of the laptop you're connecting from and whether you've seen any certificate warning popups in the GlobalProtect client?

title: Outlook/ActiveSync: Mobile and desktop email not syncing (device compliance block)
description: I was trying to receive current email in Outlook Desktop on my Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MR) but messages were not updating as expected after recent sign-in prompts and account changes on my mailbox (marcus.reeves@corplabs.com). Outlook did not remain fully disconnected, yet sync behavior was inconsistent enough to interrupt normal mailbox use. I also reported uncertainty about whether mobile mail access on my iPhone was still functioning normally. I'm based in the Charlotte office and need email working for client meetings this week. My employee ID is E-50831 for reference.
observed_errors: Outlook desktop disconnected; no active sync session
root_cause: Corrupted or invalid stored Microsoft 365 authentication tokens caused Outlook to repeatedly fail reauthentication, preventing stable mailbox synchronization despite a healthy profile and compliant mobile partnership.
resolution_steps: Cleared stored Office credentials and invalid authentication tokens from Windows Credential Manager on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR for user mreeves, including cached entries for marcus.reeves@corplabs.com in the Office sign-in cache under the user's Windows profile.

Forced a fresh Microsoft 365 sign-in for marcus.reeves@corplabs.com and completed the required modern authentication and MFA prompt to re-establish the mailbox session on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR from client IP 10.42.17.88.

Relaunched Outlook on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and verified send/receive completed without new authentication prompts and that current email and calendar items for marcus.reeves@corplabs.com began syncing normally on both desktop and the user's managed iPhone. Confirmed with Marcus Reeves that mail flow was restored.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, please confirm whether the sync failure is happening only on the iPhone or also in Outlook on your Windows laptop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MR), and whether messages have been missing since roughly two days ago. Also, can you verify the account affected is marcus.reeves@corplabs.com? — Agent Priya Nair

title: Print jobs stuck for 3rdFloor-Laser
description: Multiple users on HQ Building A Floor 3 were trying to print to the shared queue 3rdFloor-Laser, but jobs remained pending and client systems showed "Driver unavailable." The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (r.nguyen, EMP-40218) from the Engineering group. Reprints and a reboot did not clear the backlog, preventing Engineering users from completing normal printing from the shared print server queue on printsrv-01.
root_cause: The 3rdFloor-Laser queue on printsrv-01 was still mapped to an outdated or missing printer driver package, causing Windows clients to report "Driver unavailable" and leaving submitted jobs stuck in the shared queue.
resolution_steps: Verified that the 3rdFloor-Laser queue on printsrv-01 was associated with an older driver package (HP Universal v1.8.0) that was no longer fully present on the server. Confirmed affected users included r.nguyen (EMP-40218), d.cho, and m.pratt from the Arlington Engineering group.

Installed the approved manufacturer printer driver package version 2.3.1 on printsrv-01 to restore a valid server-side driver for the shared queue. Installation performed by k.marsh from the Workplace Services team.
Updated the 3rdFloor-Laser queue configuration to use the newly installed approved driver (Manufacturer v2.3.1) instead of the stale HP Universal v1.8.0 driver mapping.

Cleared 27 residual stuck print jobs from the affected queue — including jobs from r.nguyen, d.cho, and m.pratt — and restarted the Print Spooler service on printsrv-01 to remove cached driver and job state.

Performed validation prints from three user workstations (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN at 10.40.3.87, WORKSTATION-PC-DC at 10.40.3.92, WORKSTATION-PC-MP at 10.40.3.105) and confirmed jobs processed normally without the "Driver unavailable" message. Users r.nguyen, d.cho, and m.pratt all confirmed resolution.

title: Installation blocked: VPNClientPro via Software Center
description: I was trying to install VPNClientPro from Software Center on my managed Windows 10 21H2 device (WORKSTATION-FIN-RCHEN), but the install failed with policy check error 0x87D13B3. Endpoint Protection had quarantined the installer, and the application was also not appearing for other Finance users in our Portland office, indicating both a security block and possible entitlement or policy targeting visibility issue. I need the VPN client installed urgently to access corporate resources for quarter-end reporting. My employee ID is E-50274 and my username is rchen. Please contact me at rachel.chen@corplabs.com or ext 503-555-4182 if you need remote access to my machine (IP 10.42.17.89).
root_cause: Endpoint Protection quarantined the VPNClientPro installer, which caused the Software Center/Intune installer policy validation to fail with 0x87D13B3. The missing app visibility for other Finance users also indicated entitlement or policy targeting needed verification and refresh.
resolution_steps: Endpoint Support (Priya Nair, pnair) approved the VPNClientPro installer in Endpoint Protection by whitelisting the installer signature hash and releasing the quarantined file on WORKSTATION-FIN-RCHEN and across the Portland Finance endpoint group.

The affected device WORKSTATION-FIN-RCHEN (IP 10.42.17.89) was refreshed in Intune/Software Center so the application policy and inventory state could be reevaluated after the security block was removed; sync confirmed successful at 08:02Z.

Finance user entitlement and application targeting for the FIN-VPNClientPro-Deploy group were verified by agent Darren Okafor (dokafor) to confirm rchen, mwatkins, and jdelgado were included in the required deployment scope.

The installation was retried by rchen from Software Center on WORKSTATION-FIN-RCHEN after quarantine release and policy refresh, allowing the VPNClientPro installer to pass the policy check and complete successfully.

A follow-up check by pnair confirmed the VPNClientPro package was visible again through Software Center for rchen and peer Finance users (mwatkins, jdelgado) in Portland, and no active Endpoint Protection rule continued blocking the approved installer.

title: Print jobs stuck on PRN-SRV-01
description: Multiple users in the Finance department were trying to print to department printers through PRN-SRV-01, but jobs remained stuck in shared queues and the printers appeared offline to clients. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (rng4521) at approximately 22:10 UTC when she attempted to print month-end reconciliation reports from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN. Windows Server 2019 Event Logs on PRN-SRV-01 repeatedly reported 'Driver unavailable' for the HPUniversal_v6 package. Clearing queues and restarting the print spooler on the server and affected workstations did not restore service, leaving Finance users in the Arlington office unable to complete normal printing tasks. At least five additional users confirmed the same behavior, including Marcus Webb (mwebb03).
root_cause: Corruption or invalid registration of the approved HPUniversal_v6 printer driver on PRN-SRV-01 caused shared queues to lose a usable driver binding, resulting in stuck jobs and printers appearing offline.
resolution_steps: Remove the broken HPUniversal_v6 driver package from PRN-SRV-01 (including the corrupted hpuni6.inf in the driver store) and reinstall the approved HPUniversal_v6 driver version from the supported print driver repository. Performed by Kevin Ostrowski (kostrowski, EMP-90274).

Rebind or remap each affected printer queue on PRN-SRV-01 to the reinstalled approved driver so the queues no longer reference the unavailable driver instance. All three Arlington Finance printer queues were remapped and verified online.

Purge all 14 stuck print jobs from the affected queues and restart the Print Spooler service on PRN-SRV-01 after the driver reinstall is complete. Confirmed spooler running stable with no new 'Driver unavailable' events.

Run validation test prints from representative affected workstations to confirm queues return online and jobs process successfully end to end. Test prints completed from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (Rachel Nguyen), WORKSTATION-PC-MW (Marcus Webb), and WORKSTATION-PC-PD (Priya Desai) — all processed without error.

Review and update Print Queue Mapping Policy or queue deployment settings if any mappings still reference the old or invalid driver package name. GPO printer deployment for the Arlington Finance OU was verified and no stale driver references remained.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether all affected users are printing through PRN-SRV-01 and whether printers show offline after new jobs are submitted, even after local workstation restarts. Also, can you verify whether users on other floors or in other offices (e.g. the Raleigh branch) are experiencing the same issue, or if this is isolated to the Arlington Finance group? Please share the hostnames of any additional affected workstations if possible.

title: Laptop slow
description: My corporate Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, asset tag LPT-4821) became very slow immediately after login. CPU usage spiked during session startup — Outlook, Microsoft Edge, and our CRM line-of-business application took an unusually long time to open, and overall desktop responsiveness was poor. I'm logged in as mreeves on the domain. The issue affected normal post-login work on this single managed laptop and was most noticeable right after sign-in. My IP at the time was 10.42.17.88. I'm based out of the Charlotte office in the Sales group.
root_cause: A resource-heavy startup configuration caused multiple noncritical monitoring and updater agents to launch at user login at the same time an endpoint protection scan backlog was processing. With only about 30% free space on the C: drive, the device experienced elevated CPU and disk I/O contention during session startup, delaying application launches and degrading responsiveness.
resolution_steps: Reviewed startup processes on the affected laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (user: mreeves) and disabled unnecessary noncritical startup items, including AnalyticsAgent.exe and UpdaterSvc.exe, to reduce post-login CPU load from 98% sustained down to normal levels.

Refreshed endpoint management policy on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR via the Endpoint Management console so nonessential agents (AnalyticsAgent, UpdaterSvc) no longer auto-start during user logon, and confirmed the updated policy applied successfully for mreeves.

Cleared the queued endpoint protection scan backlog (14 pending scans dating back to 2026-01-19) and ran a manual full scan cycle on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR to return the Endpoint Protection client to a normal state with no outstanding scan queue.

Removed temporary files from C:\Users\mreeves\AppData\Local\Temp, Windows Update cache, and browser caches, and performed disk cleanup to reclaim approximately 26 GB of additional free space on the C: drive, reducing disk contention during login.

Validated after remediation that login CPU spikes on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR dropped to expected levels (below 60% within 90 seconds of login) and Outlook, Edge, and the CRM line-of-business application opened within normal timeframes for user mreeves. Confirmed with Marcus Reeves that the laptop was performing as expected.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. Can you confirm whether the slowness happens mainly right after login and whether Outlook, Edge, and the CRM app are all delayed when the desktop first loads? Also, is this occurring on your primary device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR? I'd like to pull up your endpoint profile under mreeves to check recent policy pushes. — Derek Huang, Desktop Support

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Finance user denied access to Shared Drive \Finance
description: Finance — I was trying to open the department shared folder at \\SharedDrive\\Finance from Windows Explorer on my Windows 10 workstation (WORKSTATION-FIN-TR, IP 10.42.17.88). The mapped drive repeatedly prompted for credentials and then returned "Access is denied (Error 5)," preventing access to Finance files needed for normal department work. I had already logged out, remapped the drive, and cleared saved Windows credentials without resolving the issue. My username is treeves and I'm based in the Arlington office. Please contact me at ext. 4127 if needed.
root_cause: User account was not a member of the FINANCE_RW Active Directory security group required by the \\SharedDrive\\Finance folder ACL, so SMB authentication succeeded but authorization to the folder was denied.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the \\SharedDrive\\Finance share and folder permissions on file server FS-CORP-02.corplabs.internal to confirm access is granted through the FINANCE_RW Active Directory security group.
Validated the affected user's Active Directory group membership for account treeves (Tanya Reeves, employee ID FIN-20418) and confirmed the account was missing from FINANCE_RW.
Added the user treeves to the FINANCE_RW security group to restore the required share and NTFS access entitlement. Change performed by service desk agent Raj Nguyen.

Refreshed policy and access context by forcing an update via gpupdate /force on WORKSTATION-FIN-TR and instructing the user to sign out or restart the workstation so a new logon token would include the new group membership.

Had the user reconnect to the current \\SharedDrive\\Finance path from workstation WORKSTATION-FIN-TR and verify the folder opened successfully without further credential prompts or access denied errors. Tanya Reeves confirmed full read/write access was restored.

title: Device marked noncompliant and blocked by Conditional Access
description: I (Marcus Delgado, emp ID E-40291) enrolled a corporate Windows 10 22H2 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD) into Intune the same morning from our Philadelphia office and was then marked noncompliant, causing Conditional Access to block Exchange Online email and SharePoint Online access. Intune showed the device (IP 10.42.17.83) in a compliance failure state with an older-than-expected check-in timestamp and no clear portal error beyond an encryption-related noncompliance signal. My goal was to regain access to Microsoft 365 resources from the newly enrolled managed device under my account mdelgado@corplabs.com.
observed_errors: ConditionalAccess: Blocked by device compliance policy
No explicit error code in Intune portal; stale check-in timestamp
root_cause: The device enrolled successfully but did not report a current encryption compliance signal back to Intune after enrollment. A stale post-enrollment check-in prevented Device Compliance Service from re-evaluating BitLocker status, so the device remained in an EncryptionMissing noncompliant state and Conditional Access continued to block access.
resolution_steps: Validated that WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD's Intune check-in was stale (last seen 2025-12-27T05:32:00Z) and that the active compliance failure for mdelgado (E-40291) was tied to the missing BitLocker encryption signal rather than a broader enrollment failure.

Had Marcus Delgado run a manual Company Portal sync on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD and reboot the device to trigger a fresh management check-in and compliance evaluation cycle against the 'Sales-Win10-Standard' policy.

Verified BitLocker status on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD via the manage-bde -status command and confirmed full disk encryption was enabled on the OS drive (C:), so the required encryption compliance signal could be reported back to Intune's Device Compliance Service.

Triggered a follow-up Intune sync on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD after encryption status was confirmed active, allowing the device record to refresh and the compliance state to be recalculated by Device Compliance Service. Agent Priya Kapoor monitored the sync from the Intune admin console.

Confirmed WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD returned to compliant status in Intune at approximately 06:45 UTC and that Conditional Access no longer blocked mdelgado@corplabs.com access to Exchange Online email and SharePoint Online. Marcus verified he could open Outlook and SharePoint successfully.

Used the documented temporary access exception (applied by Priya Kapoor for mdelgado's account) only during the remediation window and removed reliance on the workaround once compliant reporting was restored on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD.

title: Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service caused TLS outages behind load
description: Internal users and dependent services were trying to access internal.example.corp, but the endpoint began presenting an expired TLS certificate and browser certificate warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) while integrations failed TLS handshakes. The outage was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, noting that the Internal Web Service behind load balancer LB-EAST-02 was unreachable over HTTPS. The certificate expiration window had passed as of 2025-12-15 03:14 UTC, blocking normal internal application access for all users in the us-east-1 region until the deployed certificate chain on the load balancer was corrected.
root_cause: The renewed certificate had been issued by the internal Certificate Authority, but the load balancer continued serving the expired certificate and old chain for internal.example.corp. Certificate expiry monitoring and renewal alerting were not active, so the stale load balancer certificate was not corrected before expiration.

Alert rule restored and validated by Derek Holloway (dholloway, EMP-90234).

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: Corporate Windows 10 Azure AD joined laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-DELL-MR, asset tag FIN-4821) assigned to Maria Reyes (mreyes, employee ID E-90274) in the Chicago office was reported as noncompliant for disk encryption by the Device Compliance Service. The user contacted the helpdesk at ext. 312-555-0148 after receiving the noncompliance notification.
observed_errors: BitLocker not enabled on OS volume
Recovery key not escrowed to Azure AD
Device compliance check failed for encryption requirement
root_cause: The device TPM was present but not initialized for BitLocker use, which prevented creation of the TPM protector on the OS volume. Because the protector was missing, the Intune disk encryption policy could not complete successfully and the recovery key was not escrowed to Azure AD.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM readiness on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and initialized the TPM protector using Initialize-Tpm so the device could support BitLocker on the OS volume C:. Technician Priya Nair (pnair) performed the on-site steps in the Chicago office.

Enabled BitLocker on the operating system drive C: using the TPM protector (manage-bde -on C: -RecoveryPassword) and confirmed encryption began successfully — manage-bde -status showed Encryption Percentage: 1.2% and climbing on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR.
Reassigned the Intune disk encryption policy 'FIN-Encryption-Win10' to the affected device WORKSTATION-DELL-MR to clear the failed policy application state that occurred during initial enrollment.

Forced a device sync with Intune on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Sync) so updated encryption configuration and compliance evaluation were applied immediately for user mreyes.

Rotated the recovery protector on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and confirmed the current 48-digit BitLocker recovery key was escrowed to Azure AD under mreyes@corplabs.com and visible for support recovery in the Azure AD portal.

Verified the device WORKSTATION-DELL-MR returned to a compliant encryption state in the Device Compliance Service after protector creation, policy application, and key escrow completion. Notified Maria Reyes and her manager David Liang (dliang) that the laptop now meets Finance team encryption requirements.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing nightly data sync failures
description: The nightly Sales Data Sync integration job (job ID: sync-sales-nightly-0312) failed at 03:12 UTC on 2025-12-10 when the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-07) could not complete authenticated calls to the API Service endpoint https://api.corplabs.com/v2/sales-ingest. During the failure window, monitoring on the Monitoring System dashboard showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses, spikes of 429 Too Many Requests from the rate limiter, and a token refresh failure (AuthFailure: TokenRefreshFailed) on service account svc-salessync, which prevented the scheduled sync from completing. The backlog in the downstream data load queue grew to approximately 14,200 pending records. Reported by Marcus Delgado (Platform Integrations team, emp ID EMP-40821) from the Austin office.
root_cause: Expired API token on the Integration Gateway caused authentication refresh failure; repeated retries against the API Service then contributed to 504 timeout and 429 rate-limit responses during the nightly sync window.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token for service account svc-salessync used by the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-07) to authenticate to the API Service at https://api.corplabs.com/v2/sales-ingest. Rotation performed by Priya Nair at 03:45 UTC.

Validated successful authentication with the new token by issuing test calls from igw-prod-east-07 to the API Service and confirmed the endpoint was accepting authenticated requests for svc-salessync with <200ms response times.

Temporarily increased retry delay from 2s to 10s and adjusted exponential backoff ceiling from 30s to 120s on the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-07) to reduce rapid retry bursts during recovery, as approved by team lead Raj Mehta.

Retried the failed nightly synchronization (job sync-sales-nightly-0312) at 04:15 UTC and processed the accumulated backlog of ~14,200 records successfully; completion confirmed at 04:38 UTC by Marcus Delgado.

Reviewed rate-limit behavior with the downstream vendor (contact: vendor-support@databridge.io) and scheduled permanent tuning for retry handling. Added Monitoring System alerts for token refresh failures on svc-salessync and threshold-based alerting for 429/504 spikes exceeding 10 events per 5-minute window. Follow-up review scheduled by Raj Mehta for 2025-12-17.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — we confirmed repeated 504 and 429 responses during the 03:12 UTC run on gateway node igw-prod-east-07. Logs from the Monitoring System show the first 504 at 03:12:04 UTC and 429 bursts starting at 03:12:18 UTC. Can you verify whether the token rotation job for service account svc-salessync reported any refresh or authentication failures around the same window? Also, please confirm whether the client host WORKSTATION-INTG-MD was used to trigger any manual retries. — Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com)

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts affecting daily data sync
description: Daily customer data synchronization through the Integration Gateway began failing around 2025-12-09 03:20 UTC with repeated HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses. The affected workflow — managed by the Application Support team under Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) — could not complete customer data sync jobs on time, causing delayed downstream updates to the Billing API Integration pipeline. Monitoring dashboards on host INTGW-MON-01 and distributed traces from the us-east-1 cluster showed elevated upstream response times from the downstream CRM API while no recent Integration Gateway configuration changes were identified. Initial report was filed by Priya Nair (priya.nair@corplabs.com) from the Charlotte office.
root_cause: Downstream API latency increased enough for Integration Gateway requests to exceed configured timeout thresholds, which produced repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and caused daily sync job failures.
resolution_steps: Validated monitoring alerts on INTGW-MON-01 and distributed traces to confirm the timeout failures were correlated with elevated downstream CRM API response times (1200–1800ms) rather than a new gateway deployment or configuration change. Verification performed by Raj Okonkwo (rokonkwo) from the Charlotte office.

Escalated the latency issue to the downstream CRM API provider (contact: Lisa Fernandez, lfernandez@partnerservices.net) with supporting trace evidence showing sustained slow upstream responses during the failed sync window (03:20–04:50 UTC on 2025-12-09).

Temporarily increased the Integration Gateway timeout from 30 seconds to 60 seconds for the affected integration path (/v2/customer-sync) so in-flight requests from client IP 10.42.17.88 could complete while the downstream service stabilized. Change implemented by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado).

Adjusted the integration retry and backoff policy (initial delay 2s→10s, max retries 5→3) to reduce immediate retry pressure and limit cascading retries during periods of elevated upstream latency. Configuration updated in the Kubernetes ConfigMap for the intgw-worker deployment.

Monitored post-change gateway 504 rates on INTGW-MON-01, upstream latency, and daily sync execution results over the following 48 hours, then verified that timeout volume dropped to zero and scheduled customer data sync jobs completed successfully by 2025-12-10 03:25 UTC. Final confirmation provided by Priya Nair.
agent_questions: We are seeing recurring 504 Gateway Timeout errors on the Integration Gateway during the daily sync window (starting approximately 03:20 UTC). Requests originating from integration pod intgw-worker-7b4c on the Kubernetes cluster in us-east-1 are timing out against the downstream CRM API endpoint. Can you confirm whether any gateway configuration changed recently, or if downstream API latency is elevated at the same time? Assigning initial triage to Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) on the Application Support team.

title: Print jobs stuck on Finance-Printer queue after driver update
description: Finance users reported by Maria Chen (emp ID FIN-20481) were unable to print to the shared Finance-Printer queue hosted on PS-PRINT01. Submitted jobs remained stuck in the queue with 'Driver unavailable' errors, and attached printers appeared offline. The issue began shortly after the approved HP Universal Print Driver package v7.2.1 was deployed to the central Windows Server 2019 print server at approximately 04:30 UTC on 2026-02-24. Cleared all 14 stuck jobs from the Finance-Printer queue so previously failed spool files from mchen (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC), rliu, and jgarcia (WORKSTATION-DESK-JG) would not continue referencing the bad driver state.

Restarted the Print Spooler service on PS-PRINT01 to reload the freshly installed HP Universal Print Driver v7.2.1 package and reset queue processing. Confirmed no Event ID 372 warnings reappeared in the System log.

Remapped the Finance-Printer queue to the newly reinstalled HP Universal Print Driver v7.2.1 and verified that new test jobs from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (mchen, 10.22.14.87) and WORKSTATION-DESK-JG (jgarcia, 10.22.14.92) processed successfully for Newark office finance-area printing. Notified affected users via jgarcia@corplabs.com that printing was restored.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — can you confirm whether other queues on PS-PRINT01 (e.g., HR-Printer, Legal-Printer) are still processing jobs normally, and whether the approved HP Universal Print Driver package v7.2.1 was deployed to that server before the Finance-Printer failures began? Also, could you check from your workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC whether the queue shows as offline in Devices and Printers? I've asked jgarcia@corplabs.com to gather affected user names as well.

title: stuck in MFA prompt loop when signing into SSO Portal (Okta)
description: I was trying to sign in to the Okta-based SSO Portal from Chrome on Windows 10 to reach SaaS applications including Salesforce, Confluence, and Google Workspace. My username is cmorales and I'm logging in from my workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-CM at IP 10.42.17.88. observed_errors: MFA prompt loop observed in browser

resolution_steps: Reviewed the user's Okta factor enrollments and removed duplicate or stale TOTP factor records associated with the account cmorales, specifically deleting the stale factor opf3x9a1 (enrolled 2025-11-03) that was causing authentication conflicts.
Reset the user's MFA enrollment in Okta to clear the invalid factor state that was causing the prompt loop, performed by identity engineer dkhan via the Okta Admin Console.

Had the user re-enroll their authenticator app with a fresh MFA registration and complete a new approval test. Carlos Morales confirmed successful TOTP setup from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-CM and verified the new factor generated valid codes.

Validated that the user could sign in through the SSO Portal without repeated MFA prompts and successfully open the affected SaaS applications (Salesforce, Confluence, and Google Workspace). Sign-in completed in a single MFA challenge from IP 10.42.17.88.

Confirmed that group-based access and application assignment for the user remained unchanged after the MFA cleanup. cmorales retains Engineering - contractors group membership and all three application assignments are intact in Okta.

title: Expired TLS certificate causing internal web service TLS outages
description: Users in the Arlington office were trying to access the Internal Web Service (internalapp.corplabs.internal) through the load balancer LB-EAST-01, but browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and automated clients failed TLS validation. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MC at 10.42.18.97. The service became unavailable over HTTPS after the service certificate expired on 2025-12-22 and the load balancer continued presenting the old or incomplete chain, blocking normal internal application access for the internal_services user group.
root_cause: The Internal Web Service TLS certificate issued by the internal CA expired on 2025-12-22, and the load balancer was still configured with the old certificate chain. Certificate renewal alerting did not trigger in time, so the expired certificate and stale chain remained in service until clients began rejecting the endpoint.
resolution_steps: Requested and obtained a renewed certificate from the internal Certificate Authority (CA-INT-EAST-01.corplabs.internal), submitted by Kevin Briggs (kbriggs, EMP-40821), then validated the CN=internalapp.corplabs.internal, SAN entries (DNS:internalapp.corplabs.internal), and certificate validity dates (2025-12-22 to 2026-12-22) against the Internal Web Service endpoint.

Deployed the renewed server certificate and full trust chain (leaf + CorpLabs Internal Issuing CA G2 intermediate) to the Internal Web Service backend at /etc/ssl/certs/internalapp/ on the Ubuntu 20.04 host so the backend presented the current certificate materials.

Updated the load balancer LB-EAST-01 certificate store with the renewed certificate and complete chain in the correct order (leaf → intermediate → root), replacing the expired chain reference under the internalapp.corplabs.internal virtual server binding.
Restarted the load balancer LB-EAST-01 HTTPS listener so the active TLS listener began serving the updated certificate chain; confirmed reload completed without errors at 2025-12-22T22:05:00Z.

Verified successful TLS handshakes from client perspectives — Maria Chen (mchen) from WORKSTATION-PC-MC (10.42.18.97) and Raj Patel (rpatel) from WORKSTATION-LT-RP (10.42.19.33) — and from the load balancer side; confirmed that certificate warnings and handshake failures no longer occurred. openssl s_client showed 'Verify return code: 0 (ok)' with the new expiry date.

Re-enabled and tested certificate renewal monitoring in Nagios for internalapp.corplabs.internal with 30/14/7-day expiration thresholds alerting cert-owners@corplabs.com and kbriggs@corplabs.com. Documented certificate ownership (team lead: Danielle Okafor, dokafor) and rotation steps in the runbook to prevent recurrence.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether all clients are seeing certificate warnings or only a subset (e.g., only users on the Arlington network), and whether the affected endpoint is only the Internal Web Service at internalapp.corplabs.internal behind load balancer LB-EAST-01. Also, can you check if the issue reproduces from your workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MC as well as from other machines? — Kevin Briggs, Infrastructure Support (EMP-40821)

title: Laptop slow
description: I'm Marcus Reeves (employee ID EMP-40291) from the Philadelphia office. My corporate Windows 10 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, IP 10.32.18.77) becomes extremely slow immediately after login. The desktop is responsive only after a long delay, and common applications like Outlook and Excel take 30-120 seconds to open. The impact is limited to the endpoint but blocks normal work right after sign-in. Telemetry indicates high CPU during startup and critically low free space on the system drive.
observed_errors: CPU usage peaked at 85% after login
Free disk space reported <5% on C:
root_cause: A backlog of endpoint protection scans combined with multiple resource-heavy startup items and critically low disk space on C: caused sustained post-login CPU contention and delayed application launches.
resolution_steps: Reviewed endpoint telemetry for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (user mreeves, IP 10.32.18.77) after login and confirmed CPU spikes to 85% were driven by a 14-day queued Defender scan backlog and multiple startup processes launching simultaneously under the Sales group policy.
Cleared the Defender scan backlog on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and allowed scan queues to drain so endpoint protection activity no longer consumed excessive CPU during user sign-in for mreeves.

Disabled non-essential startup items tied to the heavy Sales login profile on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and pushed a device policy refresh via Endpoint Management to apply the lighter startup configuration for mreeves.

Removed approximately 38 GB of temporary files using Windows Disk Cleanup and Storage Sense on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR to reclaim disk space and restore the system drive to a healthier free-space level (16%) above the critical threshold.

title: Multiple users unable to join Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple users in Building A (Denver) and the Portland remote office were trying to connect to the Corp-Employee wireless network but were blocked during 802.1X authentication. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (EMP-40291) from Engineering and escalated by helpdesk after additional reports from Sales. Windows 10 laptops, iOS 15 iPhones, and Android 12 devices showed authentication failed or certificate trust errors immediately after selecting the SSID, preventing users from getting normal corporate network access. Review of the wireless controller (WLC-BLDGA-01.corp.netops.local) and NAC authentication path indicated the outage aligned with an expired server-side RADIUS certificate used for EAP-PEAP authentication. Affected devices included WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC and several personal mobile devices.
region: North America - Building A and Remote Office
observed_errors: NAC deny: device not authorized due to certificate validation failure
root_cause: Expired RADIUS/server certificate in the 802.1X authentication chain on the wireless controller/NAC, causing endpoints to reject the server certificate and fail NAC authorization.
resolution_steps: Renewed the expired RADIUS/server certificate (CN=radius.corp.netops.local) used for Corp-Employee 802.1X EAP-PEAP authentication; new certificate valid through 2028-04-27.

Kevin Orosco (korosco, EMP-55187) installed the renewed certificate on the wireless controller WLC-BLDGA-01.corp.netops.local and NAC appliance NAC-CORE-01.corp.netops.local and bound it to the active EAP-PEAP authentication chain.

Validated successful 802.1X/EAP-PEAP authentication with test clients — Maria Chen's WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (IP 10.20.14.88) and Raj Patel's iPhone — and confirmed affected devices were no longer denied by NAC policy Corp-Standard-Access for certificate expiry.

Used a temporary NAC grace policy ('Cert-Recovery-Grace') during recovery so impacted endpoints across Denver and Portland could re-enroll and obtain updated trust material without remaining fully blocked.

Instructed users (via email to affected groups Engineering and Sales) to forget the Corp-Employee SSID and reconnect so devices would renegotiate authentication against the updated certificate chain. Contact korosco@corplabs.com or helpdesk ext 4-9100 for assistance.

Scheduled MDM distribution of updated trust anchors/client certificate dependencies via Workspace ONE and added the RADIUS certificate expiry date (2028-04-27) to the network_team's certificate rotation tracking calendar to prevent recurrence.

Validated that the compliance state updated to Compliant for WORKSTATION-DELL-ME after the fresh sync path completed and Conditional Access restored SharePoint Online access for mellingham. Documented Endpoint Support escalation path (contact: Ravi Chandran, rchandran@corplabs.com) only if the device failed to report again, requiring re-enrollment or OS remediation.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing failed sync jobs
description: Customers were trying to run scheduled data synchronization through the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-01), but starting around 2025-12-02 03:10 UTC the gateway began returning repeated 504 Gateway Timeout errors on downstream API calls to the Order Fulfillment API Service. Two scheduled sync jobs (sync-job-4417 and sync-job-4418, owned by svc-integrations) failed, data delivery to the Application was delayed by over 3 hours, and monitoring reported elevated latency and timeout alerts in us-east-1. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Chicago operations team, who noticed the failed jobs in the morning dashboard review.
root_cause: The Integration Gateway was using an expired API token to authenticate to the downstream API Service. Authentication failures on downstream calls led to repeated retries and eventual upstream 504 timeout responses, which caused scheduled sync jobs to fail.
resolution_steps: Validated that the token configured on the Integration Gateway (secret ref: vault/igw/downstream-api-token, associated with service account svc-integrations) had expired on 2025-12-01T23:59:59Z and no longer authenticated successfully to the downstream Order Fulfillment API Service.

Rotated the expired API token via Vault and updated the stored secret (vault/igw/downstream-api-token) used by the Integration Gateway for downstream API authentication. Rotation was performed by Raj Venkatesh (rvenkatesh, emp ID E-90274) at 2025-12-02T14:42:00Z.

Confirmed authenticated API requests from igw-prod-east-01 (10.42.17.88) completed successfully after the secret update, with response times returning to baseline ~200ms, and removed reliance on the temporary timeout increase as the primary mitigation.

Re-ran queued sync jobs (sync-job-4417 and sync-job-4418) and verified previously failed synchronization jobs completed successfully without further 504 errors. Marcus Delgado confirmed data delivery to the Application was restored and consistent.

Updated the token rotation policy to enforce automated renewal 14 days before expiry via Vault auto-rotate and reviewed secret management ownership for the integration path, assigning Raj Venkatesh as the designated secret owner for the igw-prod-east-01 integration credentials.

Adjusted retry and backoff behavior on igw-prod-east-01 from linear (5s fixed interval, 10 retries) to exponential backoff (initial 2s, max 60s, 5 retries) so future transient downstream issues are less likely to surface as repeated gateway timeouts. Configuration change reviewed by Priya Nair.
agent_questions: We are correlating the 504 errors with downstream API behavior on igw-prod-east-01. Please confirm whether the failures began at the same time for all scheduled syncs (sync-job-4417 and sync-job-4418) and whether any recent token or secret changes were made for the Integration Gateway. Also, can you verify whether the service account svc-integrations was modified recently? — Priya Nair, Integration Support

title: Laptop slow

My name is Marcus Reeves (employee ID EMP-40291) and I'm based in the Denver office on the Sales floor. resolution_steps: Paused the immediate endpoint protection scan schedule on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and cleared the queued scan backlog (7 pending quick scans accumulated over the prior week) so multiple scan processes would not start concurrently after login for user mreeves.

Disabled two identified non-essential startup items (OneDrive auto-sync and a legacy CRM agent) that were contributing to post-login CPU load on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and verified the change locally via Task Manager for mreeves.

Refreshed the device startup policy from endpoint management for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (asset assigned to Marcus Reeves, EMP-40291) so the updated startup configuration applied consistently across the Denver office Sales group.

Removed temporary files and performed disk cleanup on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR to increase free disk space from the low starting threshold of approximately 12% to above a healthier operating level of roughly 32%, reclaiming about 18 GB from browser caches, Windows temp directories, and old update files.

Scheduled the remaining antivirus quick/full scan activity outside business hours (daily quick scan at 01:00, weekly full scan Saturday 03:00) on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and validated on the next login by mreeves that CPU usage normalized below 30% within 90 seconds and Outlook and Chrome launched within expected time.

title: Multiple users fail to authenticate to Corporate Wi‑Fi
description: Multiple users on floors 4 and 7 of the Arlington office were unable to connect to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) after the scheduled overnight certificate rollover. Updated the active certificate binding on RADIUS-EAST-01.corplabs.internal (10.22.1.50) so the authentication services presented the new certificate instead of the expired rollover artifact. Verified the new cert thumbprint matched the PKI-issued renewal.

Restarted the FreeRADIUS listener on RADIUS-EAST-01.corplabs.internal and wireless authentication services on WLC-HQ-01.corplabs.internal to load the new certificate chain and clear all failed EAP-TLS sessions queued since 00:15 UTC.

Validated in controller and RADIUS logs that new client authentication attempts completed successfully without 'certificate expired' errors or NAC denials. Confirmed successful 802.1X authentication for test devices belonging to Derek Huang (dhuang) and Maria Espinoza (mespinoza) on both floors.

Directed impacted users to forget and rejoin the Corporate Wi-Fi profile (CorpNet-Secure). Manually re-enrolled the small subset of devices (approximately 8) that retained stale wireless profile state, including WORKSTATION-IPHONE-JP belonging to James Parker (jparker). Sent confirmation email to mespinoza@corplabs.com and dhuang@corplabs.com with reconnection instructions for their teams.

title: Outlook clients failing to sync with Exchange Online
description: Multiple users in the Sales Division at the Charlotte office were trying to receive new email in Outlook for Windows and Outlook for iOS, but desktop clients showed "Disconnected" and mobile mailboxes stopped updating for several hours. The issue was first reported by Rachel Dominguez (rdominguez@corplabs.com) and subsequently confirmed by at least five other Sales team members. Cleared and re-established mobile sync partnerships for impacted mailboxes (rdominguez@corplabs.com, ktran@corplabs.com, jmartinez@corplabs.com) so ActiveSync could resume after device compliance was restored. Verified last sync timestamps updated to current time for all three.

Rebuilt Outlook cached profiles on the two tested desktops — WORKSTATION-RDOM-PC (rdominguez) and WORKSTATION-JMAR-PC (jmartinez) — where cache clearing alone did not restore normal mailbox synchronization, then verified inbox updates and mail flow were working again for both users.

Have a representative set of affected users — Claudia Reinhardt (creinhardt), Marco Bellini (mbellini), and Priya Nair (pnair) — complete fresh MFA enrollment and perform a new SSO Portal sign-in test to confirm access to Salesforce, Workday, and other target applications.

Monitor Okta and Azure AD sign-in activity for the SG-EMEA-SalesMktg group for 48 hours for repeat MFA validation failures or renewed prompt looping, and hand off to Identity Support (identity-support@corplabs.com) if recurrence appears.

title: Laptop running slowly
description: My Windows 10 company laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, asset tag LPT-4821) became very slow starting this morning. After logging in with my account mreeves, CPU remained around 80-90% and common applications such as Microsoft Word and Edge took 30-60 seconds to open, severely impacting my normal work in the Columbus office. Diagnostics indicated sustained login-time resource pressure from a queued endpoint protection scan, critically low disk free space (under 5% on a 256GB drive), and several unnecessary startup applications increasing post-login load.
observed_errors: High CPU usage (~80-90%) after user login
Endpoint protection scan queue length > 20 pending items
root_cause: Queued endpoint protection scans and critically low local disk space caused sustained post-login CPU and storage pressure, with additional delay introduced by unnecessary startup applications and a recently applied startup policy.
resolution_steps: Paused and cleared the Endpoint Protection Client scan backlog on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (23 pending items), then verified the pending scan queue drained and CPU utilization dropped from sustained 80-90% post-login peaks to under 15% idle.

Rescheduled full Endpoint Protection Client scans on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR to off-business hours (daily at 01:00 AM EST) via the endpoint management console to prevent repeated login-time resource contention on the device.

Reclaimed approximately 28 GB of local storage on C: drive by removing temporary files, Windows Update caches, and stale user temp data using Disk Cleanup, restoring free disk space to 16.4% (above the low-space threshold) and reducing disk-related slowdown and swap thrashing.

Disabled unnecessary startup applications on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, including nonessential user startup items (Adobe Updater, Slack auto-launch), to reduce resource contention immediately after sign-in for user mreeves.

Refreshed the device startup policy via gpupdate /force on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and verified post-login performance with user Marcus Reeves, confirming normal application launch times (Word: ~4s, Edge: ~3s) and stable CPU behavior under 20% at idle.

title: Multiple users stuck in MFA prompt loop
description: Multiple users in the Sales group at the Chicago office were trying to access cloud applications through the SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com), including Salesforce and G Suite, but were returned to the MFA step repeatedly instead of completing sign-in. Users approved or attempted Okta Verify authentication, yet the session looped back to another MFA challenge and blocked access to business applications after the morning identity sync change at approximately 04:50 UTC. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com) and quickly confirmed by five additional Sales team members. Okta logs showed repeated MFA challenge issuance for accounts in the CN=Sales,OU=Corp Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal group, and admins correlated the start of impact with Azure AD group attribute changes pushed in the prior AD sync window by identity engineer Marcus Delgado.
observed_errors: Repeated MFA prompt without token acceptance
Okta authentication events: MFA_CHALLENGE issued repeatedly
root_cause: Azure AD group attribute changes during the recent identity sync caused affected Sales users to retain stale Okta MFA factor enrollments that no longer aligned with current group-to-policy mapping, resulting in repeated MFA challenges without successful verification.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Okta authentication logs for the affected Sales users (rnguyen, kmarsh, psethuraman, tbarlow, jfernandez, dwilliams) and confirmed repeated MFA challenge events with no successful verification completion after the 04:48 UTC identity sync committed by mdelgado.

Reset MFA enrollments in Okta for the six affected users whose factor state was identified as stale or mismatched after the Azure AD group attribute change. Resets were performed by identity engineer Anil Kapoor (akapoor, EMP-70584) via the Okta Admin Console.

Assisted affected users with re-enrolling Okta Verify — Rachel Nguyen re-enrolled on WORKSTATION-IPHONE-RN and Kevin Marsh on WORKSTATION-IPHONE-KM — and validated that new push challenges were received and approved successfully for all six accounts.

Tested SSO access for re-enrolled users to Salesforce and G Suite to confirm that authentication completed without returning to the MFA prompt. Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen) and Priya Sethuraman (psethuraman) verified successful end-to-end login from the Chicago office.
