title: API integration timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Overnight integration jobs for customer data synchronization (namespace: igw-custsync-prod, cluster: k8s-east-prod-07) intermittently failed through the Integration Gateway between approximately 02:00–03:30 UTC on 2026-05-14, delaying downstream application updates before business hours. The incident was reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Denver operations team. The primary user-visible symptom remained timeout and job failure behavior across the /api/v2/customer-sync endpoint, but the available diagnostics did not point cleanly to expired credentials, sustained API slowness, or a consistent throttling pattern across the full incident window. Affected sync jobs included batch IDs SYNC-20260514-0200 through SYNC-20260514-0330.
root_cause: Unknown; available diagnostics were insufficient to distinguish between intermittent downstream latency, burst-based throttling, or another transient external integration condition during the overnight batch window.
resolution_steps: Captured additional gateway debug logging (log level set to DEBUG on igw-gw-east-01.corplabs.internal, namespace igw-custsync-prod) and enabled 100% request tracing for subsequent overnight runs to improve visibility into authentication, latency, and throttle responses. Configuration change applied by Priya Nair (pnair) at 06:05 UTC.

Applied a temporary workaround by increasing the API timeout from 30s to 45s and reducing batch concurrency from 20 to 8 parallel workers on igw-worker-node-04 to limit repeat failures while evidence collection continued. Changes deployed via Helm values override in the igw-custsync-prod namespace.

Escalated the ambiguous findings to the downstream API owner at PartnerData (contact: Lena Kowalski, lkowalski@partnerdata.io) and internal integration engineering team lead Rafael Tomescu (rtomescu@corplabs.com, EMP-51934) for joint review of the next occurrence. Escalation ticket XREF-AIT-0033 created.

Verified partial recovery by re-running the 38 failed sync jobs (batch IDs SYNC-20260514-0200 through SYNC-20260514-0330) at 06:20 UTC and monitoring whether the backlog of ~14,000 customer records drained without recurring timeout spikes. All re-run jobs completed successfully within 12 minutes; no 504 or ETIMEDOUT errors observed. Confirmed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) that downstream CRM data was current by 06:45 UTC.

title: API timeouts during data sync — conflicting evidence between expired token and
description: Overnight API Integration data sync jobs running on Kubernetes us-east-1 (namespace: api-sync-prod) began failing or completing late starting around 02:15 UTC on 2025-12-08, leaving users in the Columbus office with delayed record updates and failed integration runs. The issue was first flagged by integration lead Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) after the morning handoff review. Monitoring detected repeated 504 Gateway Timeout events against the API Service endpoint api-gw.corpsvc.internal:8443 during the same period that Integration Gateway logs on host INTGW-PROD-04 recorded 401 Unauthorized errors for an expired token tied to service account svc_apisync. The overlapping authentication and latency symptoms blocked normal scheduled synchronization and created uncertainty about whether the primary failure was credential expiry, downstream slowness, or retry amplification. Ticket raised by r.nakamura@corplabs.com on behalf of the Application Support group.
root_cause: Primary cause was an expired API token on the Integration Gateway, which generated 401 authentication failures and triggered repeated retry behavior. The increased retry volume overlapped with elevated downstream API latency and intermittent rate-limit pressure, producing correlated 504 timeout spikes. Rotating the token and tuning retry/backoff removed the recurring failure pattern and restored sync stability, while downstream latency remained an external contributing factor monitored through escalation.
resolution_steps: Validated the Integration Gateway authentication path on INTGW-PROD-04 and rotated the expired API token for service account svc_apisync used by the API Integration; new token issued with a 90-day expiry and registered in the secrets vault by Priya Venkatesh.

Restarted the affected Integration Gateway pods (3 replicas in namespace api-sync-prod on Kubernetes us-east-1) so the updated secret was loaded consistently by all running instances; confirmed new token active via health-check endpoint.

Adjusted the API Integration retry and backoff policy from 5 retries at 2-second intervals to 3 retries with 10-second exponential backoff, to reduce immediate retry storms that were amplifying latency and timeout conditions against api-gw.corpsvc.internal:8443.

Verified post-change behavior by reviewing gateway logs on INTGW-PROD-04 and the Monitoring System dashboard to confirm the 401 expired-token errors stopped and all five sync profiles (customer-records, inventory-delta, order-fulfillment, billing-extract, compliance-audit) resumed without recurring timeout spikes; Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) confirmed records were current by 05:10 UTC.

Escalated the observed downstream latency to the external service owner under REF INC-DOWNSTREAM-987 and kept correlation alerts in place for any future overlap between authentication failures and 504 events; escalation contact notified via r.nakamura@corplabs.com with Priya Venkatesh as the internal point of contact.
agent_questions: We found overlapping 504 timeout alerts and 401 expired-token entries from the Integration Gateway (INTGW-PROD-04). Reviewing the logs for service account svc_apisync, the token expiration timestamp was 2025-12-08T01:59:00Z — roughly 15 minutes before the first failed sync job. Please confirm whether the overnight failures affected all scheduled sync jobs or only specific integrations, and whether any recent credential change was expected. Also, can Marcus Delgado or anyone on the Columbus team confirm if there was a planned token rotation window that may have been missed? — Agent: Priya Venkatesh

title: Print jobs stuck on HR queue
description: HR staff (reported initially by Maria Gonzalez, emp ID EMP-40291) were trying to print through the shared HR printer queue \\psrv01.corp.eastprint.local\HR-Color-Q1 on print server psrv01, but submitted jobs remained stuck in the queue in a 'printing' state and client devices showed 'driver unavailable' and 'printer offline' messages. The issue began after a scheduled driver push at approximately 08:45 EST this morning and affected multiple users in the Arlington office, including workstations WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG and WORKSTATION-PC-DL, preventing normal printing for the entire HR team.
root_cause: Approved HR printer driver on psrv01 was corrupted or replaced by a mismatched driver during the morning driver push, causing the shared queue to hold jobs in printing state and clients to report driver unavailable.
resolution_steps: On psrv01, remove the corrupted or mismatched driver package (HP Universal Driver v6.5.0.21457) associated with the HR shared printer queue HR-Color-Q1 and reinstall the approved HP Universal Driver v6.8.0.24100 package from the driver repository. Performed by Rachel Torres (ratorres).

Stop and restart the Print Spooler service on psrv01 after clearing pending spool files from C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS for the affected HR-Color-Q1 queue so stuck jobs do not continue retrying against the bad driver state. Verified spooler restarted cleanly with no errors in the System event log.

Purge the 14 existing stuck print jobs from the HR-Color-Q1 shared queue on psrv01 and verify the queue returns to an 'online ready' state in the Print Management console. Confirmed queue status changed from 'Error' to 'Ready' after purge.

Remap or reconnect the HR shared printer queue \\psrv01.corp.eastprint.local\HR-Color-Q1 for affected clients (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG for mgonzalez, WORKSTATION-PC-DL for dliu, and spatel's workstation at 10.22.14.105) where the previous queue mapping cached the invalid v6.5 driver reference, then validate print permissions remain correct for the HR security group.

Update the Printer Driver Approval Policy GPO (HR-Printer-Driver-Policy) so only the approved HP Universal Driver v6.8.0.24100 package is deployed to the HR-Color-Q1 queue and HR client workstations, preventing recurrence from future driver pushes. Change reviewed and approved by Rachel Torres.

Submit a test print through the HR-Color-Q1 queue from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MG (mgonzalez, IP 10.22.14.87) and confirm the job leaves the queue normally without 'driver unavailable' errors. Test page printed successfully at 16:42 EST and confirmed by Maria Gonzalez.

title: BitLocker recovery key not escrowed
description: A managed Windows 10 21H2 company laptop assigned to Marcus Delgado (employee ID EMP-40821) showed as Not encrypted in Microsoft Intune, and the Azure AD device record for hostname LAPTOP-SALES-MD did not contain a BitLocker recovery key. The missing escrowed recovery key caused the device to be marked noncompliant for encryption in the Device Compliance Service, blocking normal corporate compliance status for the user (mdelgado@corplabs.com) until BitLocker protection and key upload were corrected. The device was located at the Charlotte office and connected from IP 10.42.17.89.
observed_errors: No BitLocker recovery key found in Azure AD
root_cause: BitLocker recovery key escrow to Azure AD did not occur because the local TPM/protector state was not fully initialized for the managed encryption workflow, so Intune reported the device as not encrypted and noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Verified TPM readiness on LAPTOP-SALES-MD using tpm.msc and initialized the TPM-based BitLocker protector locally via manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tp so the device had a valid hardware-backed protection state for user Marcus Delgado (mdelgado).
Rotated the BitLocker recovery protector on LAPTOP-SALES-MD using manage-bde -protectors -add C: -rp to generate a current 48-digit recovery key tied to the active device protection configuration.

Triggered recovery key escrow via BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector and confirmed the new BitLocker recovery key uploaded successfully to Azure AD for support visibility under the device record of LAPTOP-SALES-MD.

Validated that the company BitLocker policy assignment (BL-ENCRYPT-SALES-01) in Intune was present for LAPTOP-SALES-MD and forced a device sync through Company Portal so updated encryption state would report back to the Device Compliance Service.

Confirmed the device LAPTOP-SALES-MD changed to Compliant in Intune for user mdelgado (EMP-40821) and that BitLocker encryption had started on the OS volume (C:). Notified Marcus Delgado at mdelgado@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to Finance shared drive - user cannot open department folder
description: I was trying to open the Finance shared drive on my Windows 10 workstation (WORKSTATION-PC-RMORALES) using mapped drive G: and the UNC path \\fileserver\finance\DeptFolder. The drive prompted for credentials and then returned Access Denied, preventing access to the department folder and blocking normal Finance file share usage. My username is rmorales (employee ID FIN-20418) and I'm based in the Charlotte office. I need access restored urgently as quarter-end reporting deadlines are approaching.
root_cause: User account was missing membership in the FINANCE-READ Active Directory security group required to access \\fileserver\finance\DeptFolder, so the SMB share returned Access Denied and prompted for credentials.
resolution_steps: Validated the user's effective access issue by reviewing the Finance share path and confirming the access denied behavior (0x80070005) against \\fileserver\finance\DeptFolder from Rosa Morales's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-RMORALES at IP 10.42.17.83.

Checked Active Directory group membership for rmorales (CN=rmorales,OU=Finance Users,DC=corp,DC=internal) and confirmed the user was not assigned to the FINANCE-READ security group required for the shared drive. Manager Derek Huang (dhuang@corpfinance.com) verified the user should have access.
Added rmorales to the approved FINANCE-READ security group in Active Directory to restore required read access to the Finance share at \\fileserver\finance\DeptFolder.
Refreshed the user's Kerberos sign-in token via klist purge on WORKSTATION-PC-RMORALES so the updated FINANCE-READ group membership would be applied to the current session.

Verified that rmorales could open \\fileserver\finance\DeptFolder successfully after the membership change and advised Rosa Morales to remap drive G: or clear cached credentials from Windows Credential Manager if any prompt persisted. User confirmed access restored via phone at 704-555-2198.

title: Multiple users unable to connect to Corporate Wi‑Fi
description: Multiple employees in the Raleigh office (Building A, 3rd and 4th floors) were trying to join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID 'CorpWiFi-Secure' on desktops and mobile devices, but 802.1X authentication failed during EAP-TLS and devices showed certificate-related errors. The issue was first reported by Karen Whitfield (EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed by at least seven other users on the same floor. Users could not obtain network access after attempting to connect, causing loss of wireless connectivity across the site. Investigation focused on the Cisco WLC (wlc-east-01.corp.netops.local) and NAC path because the issue affected multiple endpoints rather than a single device profile. Network team lead David Moreno was engaged to coordinate the infrastructure-side review.
root_cause: The Wireless Controller TLS certificate used during EAP-TLS authentication had expired, causing certificate validation failures on the controller/NAC path and preventing successful 802.1X authentication to the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID.
resolution_steps: Reissued the expired TLS certificate for the Wireless Controller (wlc-east-01.corp.netops.local) via the CorpCA-Intermediate CA and installed the renewed certificate (serial 5B:72:A0:DD:18, valid through 2028-05-01) on the controller. Performed by David Moreno (dmoreno).

Updated the NAC appliance (ise-east-02.corp.netops.local) trust configuration and refreshed policy so the new controller certificate thumbprint (5B:72:A0:DD:18) was recognized during EAP-TLS authentication.

Restarted or reloaded the relevant WLC services on wlc-east-01.corp.netops.local so the renewed certificate became active for new wireless authentication sessions. Confirmed service restart completed at 16:32 UTC.

Validated successful 802.1X and EAP-TLS handshakes in WLC and NAC logs after the certificate replacement. Confirmed clean authentication for kwhitfield (WORKSTATION-KW-4082, 10.42.16.55), jparikh (WORKSTATION-JP-3371, 10.42.16.88), and mdelgado from Raleigh Building A.

Advised affected users — including Karen Whitfield (kwhitfield), Jaya Parikh (jparikh), and Marco Delgado (mdelgado) — to forget and rejoin the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID 'CorpWiFi-Secure', and re-enroll device Wi-Fi profiles on legacy endpoints where cached profile trust still referenced the expired certificate.

title: BitLocker not enabling
description: A corporate-managed Windows 10 21H2 laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-DELL-MR) assigned to Marcus Reeves (emp ID: E-20841) in the Sales group completed Intune enrollment on 2026-01-19 but remained noncompliant for disk encryption. The device, registered under mreeves@corplabs.com in Azure AD, did not receive an active Intune Endpoint Encryption Policy assignment. BitLocker showed TPM protector readiness issues, and the recovery key was not escrowed to Azure AD. Remote sync and remote encryption attempts from the Intune console failed to bring the endpoint to an encrypted/compliant state, creating a policy compliance and recovery-key visibility gap for the endpoint at the Charlotte office.
root_cause: A deprecated Intune Endpoint Encryption Policy reference remained associated with the device, preventing the active encryption policy from applying. Without the correct policy, the TPM protector was not initialized properly, BitLocker encryption did not start, and recovery key escrow to Azure AD failed.
resolution_steps: Removed the stale Intune encryption policy reference (EEP-Legacy-2024) from WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and reassigned the device to the current Endpoint Encryption Policy v2.0 under the Charlotte Sales device group.

Forced an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (triggered by agent pnair) and confirmed the updated Endpoint Encryption Policy v2.0 assignment was successfully received without assignment errors in the Intune compliance dashboard.
Initialized the TPM protector on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR using manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm so BitLocker could create a valid protector set for OS drive encryption.

Started BitLocker encryption on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (manage-bde -on C:) and verified the protection status progressed from 'not enabled' to active encryption in progress, reaching full encryption within approximately 45 minutes.

Rotated the recovery key on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and confirmed the current key escrowed successfully to Azure AD under mreeves@corplabs.com's device record and became visible for support recovery operations.

Rechecked device compliance for WORKSTATION-DELL-MR in Intune/Device Compliance Service and verified the endpoint moved to a compliant encryption state. Confirmed with Marcus Reeves (mreeves) that BitLocker shows active protection in Windows Security.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether WORKSTATION-DELL-MR has completed an enrollment sync recently (check Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Info) and whether BitLocker or Windows Security shows any TPM or protection warnings on the laptop. Also, can you verify the device is connecting from your usual network? We see the last known IP as 10.42.18.77.

title: Software Center installation blocked by Endpoint Protection
description: Marketing user Diana Castillo (emp ID MKT-4821) on managed Windows 10 device WIN10-DBS-03 (IP 10.42.18.77) was trying to install AcmeApp from Software Center, but the installation failed with a policy check error (0x80070490) and the installer was quarantined by Endpoint Protection during execution. observed_errors: Endpoint Protection quarantine event during installer execution

Refreshed device policy and inventory synchronization in Intune/Software Center on WIN10-DBS-03 after approval and Endpoint Protection allowlist changes were applied by Priya Nair and the security team.

Retried the AcmeApp installation on WIN10-DBS-03 for user dcastillo after the policy and protection updates and confirmed the deployment path was ready; Diana Castillo verified successful installation and launched AcmeApp without further quarantine events.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data syncs
description: Scheduled integration jobs on the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-01) in us-east-1 began failing at approximately 06:15 UTC this morning while sending data to the downstream API Service endpoint https://api.corpsync.internal/v2/ingest on behalf of the Application. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corpnet.com) from the Atlanta office, who noticed missing ingest records during the daily reconciliation. The gateway returned elevated HTTP 504 timeout and HTTP 429 rate-limit responses on the /v2/ingest path, retry volume increased sharply across all scheduled jobs, and queue backpressure developed on the integration bus. This delayed daily data sync processing and caused missing records in the Application ingest until authenticated API access and retry behavior were corrected. The service account svc-igw-sync used for outbound calls was confirmed to be affected.
root_cause: A stale expired API token cached on the Integration Gateway caused failed or delayed authenticated requests, while concurrent downstream API rate limiting (HTTP 429) amplified retries and pushed requests past the gateway timeout window, resulting in job failures and sync delays.
resolution_steps: Rotated the Integration Gateway API token for service account svc-igw-sync via the credentials vault and validated that new outbound requests from igw-prod-east-01 (10.42.8.17) to the downstream API Service at https://api.corpsync.internal/v2/ingest were successfully authenticated with HTTP 200 responses.

Cleared the stale token cache on gateway node igw-prod-east-01 and changed token refresh cadence from the previous 24-hour interval to 15 minutes to prevent reuse of expired credentials beyond the 90-day TTL boundary.

Updated the integration retry policy from 2 fixed retries (5 s interval) to 5 attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (base 2 s, max 60 s) to reduce retry storms during transient throttling; configuration deployed to igw-prod-east-01 by Priya Nair.

Reprocessed the 14 affected scheduled integration jobs (job group daily-sync-east, run IDs 4401–4414) after the token and retry configuration changes to clear queue backpressure (queue depth returned from 4,200 to ~200) and restore delayed syncs for records reported missing by Marcus Delgado and the Atlanta and Denver office users.

Escalated persistent downstream rate-limit spikes (~40 429s/min post-fix) to the downstream service team contact Rafael Ochoa (rochoa@corpsync.com) under ticket DS-789 for follow-up capacity or throttling review; Priya Nair added as watcher on DS-789.
agent_questions: We are seeing elevated 504 and 429 responses from the downstream API Service at https://api.corpsync.internal/v2/ingest. Monitoring System dashboards for gateway node igw-prod-east-01 show a spike beginning around 06:15 UTC. Please confirm whether the missing records reported by Marcus Delgado align with this morning's scheduled sync window (06:00–07:00 UTC) and whether the issue is limited to data arriving through the Integration Gateway path rather than direct Application submissions. Also, can you verify whether the service account svc-igw-sync credentials were recently renewed? — Priya Nair, Application Support

title: Intermittent API timeouts on Integration Gateway causing delayed data sync
description: Users in the Finance and Operations group were trying to sync data through the Integration Gateway (gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal) to the API Service endpoint, but intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout responses and elevated request latency caused delayed synchronization and failed integration jobs. The issue was reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) and affects the Linux-hosted integration path in us-east-1, where jobs were timing out after 30 seconds and backlog had to be cleared manually. The affected client workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (IP 10.42.17.88) was used for initial troubleshooting. A gateway restart did not provide sustained improvement, and token validity plus downstream API health initially remained unconfirmed. Ticket escalated internally by Derek Owens (EMP-40291).
root_cause: Primary cause was downstream API latency periodically exceeding the Integration Gateway request timeout window, which produced intermittent 504 errors and delayed sync processing. Token expiration could not be confirmed from the original intake, but available evidence favored timeout sensitivity to elevated downstream response times rather than an authentication failure.
resolution_steps: Validated the integration path against gateway monitoring on gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal and confirmed that request latency spikes were breaching the original 30 second timeout window during affected sync periods (18:45–19:10 UTC on 2025-12-03), as reported by Maria Chen and Priya Nair.

Increased the Integration Gateway request timeout from the prior 30 second setting to 60 seconds on gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal so transient downstream latency no longer caused immediate 504 failures for normal sync traffic. Change applied by Raj Patel (rpatel).

Updated retry behavior for service account svc-integ-sync to use controlled exponential backoff (initial 2s, max 32s, jitter enabled) so repeated calls during latency spikes would not rapidly exhaust retries or compound queue congestion on the us-east-1 integration path.

Cleared and reprocessed the pending retry backlog (approximately 47 queued jobs) after the timeout and retry configuration changes were applied to restore delayed synchronization jobs. Confirmed completion with Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com).

Continued post-change monitoring of gateway latency and 504 volume on gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal via the Monitoring System and confirmed reduced failure frequency over the following 4-hour observation window, with guidance to escalate to downstream service owners if sustained latency again exceeds the adjusted 60-second timeout threshold. Derek Owens (EMP-40291) assigned as point of contact for any recurrence.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether the API client token associated with service account svc-integ-sync was recently rotated or expired, and provide any gateway request IDs tied to the 504 errors along with the latest latency graphs from the Monitoring System dashboard. Also, can you verify whether the issue is isolated to your workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC or if other team members in the Arlington office are also affected? Please loop in Derek Owens (dowens@corplabs.com) if he has additional context from the Operations side.

title: Software Center install blocked by Endpoint Protection policy
description: I was trying to install AppX from Software Center on my Windows 10 21H2 managed laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, IP 10.42.17.88), but the application was not visible and install attempts failed with a PolicyCheckFailed:EP-403 error. The issue persisted after a previous Endpoint Protection approval because the affected device had not completed an Intune inventory sync for approximately 30 days, preventing the approval and app targeting state from reaching the endpoint. This blocked my ability to self-install the required software through Software Center. I need AppX for an upcoming project deadline. — Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com), Employee ID E-20418, Portland office.
root_cause: The installer remained blocked because the original Endpoint Protection approval did not propagate to the affected device. The endpoint had stale Intune inventory and had not recently synchronized policy/application targeting, so the device did not receive the approved state for AppX and Endpoint Protection continued denying the install with PolicyCheckFailed:EP-403.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Software Center and installer logs on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (IP 10.42.17.88) to confirm the failure for user mreeves was tied to Endpoint Protection policy enforcement and matched the observed PolicyCheckFailed:EP-403 condition in AppControl.log.

Verified that WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (assigned to mreeves, emp ID E-20418) had stale Intune inventory (last sync 2026-02-23) and was not showing current application targeting data for AppX in Software Center.

Applied an explicit AppX approval in Endpoint Protection scoped to WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR so the endpoint had a direct allow decision instead of relying on the prior incomplete approval state from 2026-03-10. Approval applied by Danielle Okafor.

Triggered an immediate Intune device inventory and policy refresh on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR via the Intune portal, then validated that the sync completed successfully at 2026-03-25T18:52:00Z and updated the device's application and policy state for mreeves.

Reopened Software Center on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR after sync, confirmed AppX became visible to mreeves in the Available Applications catalog, and retried the installation successfully with no EP-403 blocks.

Confirmed the application installed correctly on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and that no further Endpoint Protection denial events were generated in AppControl.log after the remediation. Marcus Reeves confirmed the software is working as expected from the Portland office.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. Please reopen Software Center on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and confirm whether AppX is visible in the Available Applications list. If you try the install again from the installer path, let us know whether the same PolicyCheckFailed:EP-403 block appears. Also, can you confirm you're currently connected to the corporate network or VPN from your Portland location so we can validate connectivity to the management service? — Danielle Okafor, Endpoint Support

title: Software Center installation blocked for FinanceApp — reopened, inventory refresh resolved
description: I (Rachel Nguyen, emp ID EMP-40821) on a corporate-managed Windows 10 21H2 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN, IP 10.42.17.88) was trying to install FinanceApp from Software Center but the application was not visible for the device and installation attempts were blocked. Reviewed the Software Center and Intune management client status on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN after sync to confirm the FinanceApp deployment became visible to the device; IntuneManagementExtension.log showed successful policy receipt at 18:11 UTC.

Approved the FinanceApp installer (FinanceApp_v3.8.2_x64.msi) in Endpoint Protection via security analyst Tomas Reyes so the package was no longer blocked during policy evaluation and execution on the Philadelphia device group.

Initiated a redeploy/install retry from Software Center on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and verified FinanceApp appeared and completed installation successfully on the device; confirmed with Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com) that the application launched without errors.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel, this is Derek Holloway from the service desk. Please confirm whether FinanceApp is still missing from Software Center on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN after the entitlement update and whether the client still shows the installer failed policy check message. title: Device marked noncompliant in Intune
description: I am blocked from accessing Exchange Online on a Windows 10 21H2 Azure AD joined device (hostname: WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MK) because Intune reports the endpoint as Noncompliant and Conditional Access is enforcing the device compliance requirement. My user account is mkaplan@corplabs.com and the device is registered under employee ID EMP-20418. Company Portal shows the last successful check-in was 7 days ago and the encryption state is unknown. An admin-triggered remote sync did not refresh the compliance state, and no explicit error code is currently available from the endpoint. title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: Multiple remote users on managed Windows 10 corporate laptops in the Frankfurt office were trying to connect to GlobalProtect VPN to reach internal resources such as the intranet, Jira, and Confluence. After approving the Okta MFA prompt, the VPN session established briefly and then disconnected immediately, leaving internal services unreachable. The issue was initially reported by Maria Engström (mengstrom, EMP-40291) and confirmed by at least three other EMEA remote workers. The problem blocked normal remote work access after authentication completed and was escalated at 12:15 UTC.
root_cause: Expired device certificate on affected endpoints caused GlobalProtect TLS certificate validation to fail during VPN re-authentication immediately after Okta MFA approval, which dropped the tunnel.
resolution_steps: Identify affected endpoints presenting expired device certificates during GlobalProtect re-authentication — confirmed hosts include WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-ME (mengstrom, EMP-40291) and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-TK (tkowalski, EMP-40388) — and renew the device certificates through the managed Device Certificate Service enrollment process.

Force a refresh of the GlobalProtect VPN profile on impacted laptops by clearing the stale profile cache (C:\ProgramData\Palo Alto Networks\GlobalProtect\) and re-enrolling the managed VPN configuration where needed, as was required on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-TK.

Validate that the renewed certificate is present, current, and mapped to the active VPN profile on each endpoint before initiating a new connection test. Verified renewed certs for mengstrom (new expiry 2027-04-14) and tkowalski (new expiry 2027-04-14) via certlm.msc.

Confirm the affected users (mengstrom, tkowalski) remain in the required conditional access group 'EMEA-VPN-RemoteWorkers' so post-MFA access evaluation succeeds with the renewed certificate. Nikhil Kapoor verified group membership in Okta directory for both users.

Retest GlobalProtect sign-in with Okta MFA approval for mengstrom and tkowalski and verify the tunnel stays connected and internal applications (Corporate Intranet, Jira, Confluence) remain reachable. Both users confirmed stable sessions at 13:45 UTC. Monitor session stability across the Frankfurt remote worker group during the broader certificate rollout over the next 48 hours.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether the VPN disconnect happens immediately after you approve the Okta MFA prompt and whether any internal sites briefly load before the tunnel drops. Also, can you share the hostname of the laptop you're connecting from? We're checking whether this is isolated to specific endpoints or affecting the broader EMEA remote worker group. You can reach me at n.kapoor@corplabs.com if you need to send logs directly.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failure for internal-service.corp (near-duplicate)
description: Multiple internal services on the corporate network intermittently failed to resolve internal-service.corp starting around 2026-01-08 09:40 UTC. Affected applications, including internal-service and service-gateway, were blocked from reaching the internal endpoint by hostname. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, who noticed service-gateway connections timing out. Some clients received NXDOMAIN while others resolved the hostname to a stale IP address (192.0.2.50), creating inconsistent connectivity across recursive resolvers and client caches in us-east-1. Workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD was among the first endpoints observed exhibiting the failure.
observed_errors: stale DNS record present in resolver cache
root_cause: Stale and inconsistent DNS cache entries on recursive resolvers caused internal-service.corp to return NXDOMAIN or an outdated A record (192.0.2.50) instead of the authoritative value (192.0.2.75).
resolution_steps: Validated that the authoritative Internal DNS Zone on ns-auth.corplabs.internal for internal-service.corp was correct and publishing A record 192.0.2.75 (SOA serial 2026010802, updated 2026-01-07 22:15 UTC).

Compared responses from affected recursive resolvers ns-rec-01.corplabs.internal and ns-rec-02.corplabs.internal against the authoritative zone and confirmed cache divergence, including stale A record 192.0.2.50 and intermittent NXDOMAIN responses affecting clients such as 10.22.9.34 (mdelgado) and 10.22.14.88 (kcho).

Flushed DNS cache on the primary resolver ns-rec-01.corplabs.internal and affected recursive nodes ns-rec-02 and ns-rec-03 to remove stale and negative cached entries for internal-service.corp. Flush performed by Ramon Estrada (restrada, EMP-55190).

Cleared client-side DNS cache on impacted application nodes including WORKSTATION-PC-MD (Marcus Delgado, 10.22.9.34) and WORKSTATION-LT-KC (Kevin Cho, 10.22.14.88) and re-ran lookups to confirm consistent resolution to 192.0.2.75.

Temporarily reduced the record TTL from 3600s to 300s to accelerate propagation of the corrected answer and monitored resolver responses via Network Monitoring for 30 minutes to confirm stability after cache refresh. TTL will be restored to 3600s after 24-hour observation window.

title: Reopened: Laptop running slowly
description: I reopened the incident because my corporate Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, asset tag LPT-04821) again became very slow immediately after login. My username is mreeves and the issue started this morning around 8:45 AM EST. Applications including Windows Explorer, Microsoft Office, and Teams were taking 30-60 seconds to open while CPU usage spiked to about 95% during startup. The slowdown was affecting my normal post-login work at the Charlotte office and appeared to recur after a recent Defender definition update pushed overnight and the prior temporary fix applied under the original ticket.
root_cause: Windows Defender entered a queued scan backlog after a definition update, causing MsMpEng.exe to consume sustained CPU during user login. This startup contention delayed application launch and was aggravated by unnecessary startup items and temporary file buildup.
resolution_steps: Validated that MsMpEng.exe was the primary process driving CPU usage during login on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (user mreeves, IP 10.42.18.77) and confirmed the issue aligned with a Defender scan backlog of 14 queued tasks following definition update v1.407.215.0.

Cleared the queued Defender scan tasks on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR via the Endpoint Management console and forced an endpoint policy refresh through SCCM so the device could pick up current protection settings cleanly without residual scan queue entries.

Applied local endpoint cleanup by disabling unnecessary startup programs (OneDrive sync, Adobe Updater, Slack auto-launch) and removing 4.2 GB of temporary files through disk cleanup on C:\Users\mreeves\AppData\Local\Temp and the Windows Update cache to reduce login-time contention.

Rescheduled Defender definition updates and full scans to off-hours (daily at 01:00 EST) via Endpoint Management policy so scan activity would not compete with Marcus Reeves' normal login and application startup period. Coordinated with Danielle Okafor (dokafor@corplabs.com) to apply the updated schedule across the Sales user group.

Rebooted WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and monitored post-login performance for user mreeves, confirming CPU returned to normal startup levels (~12% within 90 seconds of login) and applications opened without the prior 30-60 second delay. Marcus confirmed normal operation at 2026-02-05T08:30Z.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, before we reapply the full fix, can you confirm whether the slowdown on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR starts immediately after you sign in with your mreeves account and whether apps like Teams or Office are delayed by 30-60 seconds? Also, can you confirm your current IP so I can pull the endpoint logs — should be your usual 10.42.18.77 address on the Charlotte VPN segment?

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Internal users and monitoring were trying to reach svc-internal-web through the ALB (alb-prod-east-01.corplabs.internal), but starting around 08:15 UTC on 2025-12-19 the service began failing TLS handshakes and showing certificate warnings. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, who noticed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID errors in Chrome when accessing https://svc-internal-web.corplabs.internal. Dependent internal clients including the internal-admin-portal could not establish secure connections, causing the internal web service to be unavailable over TLS in us-east-1. Additional reports came in from employees in the Raleigh office confirming the same behavior.
root_cause: The TLS leaf certificate issued by the internal Certificate Authority expired, and the renewed certificate chain was not deployed on the ALB, so the load balancer continued presenting the old expired chain. A misconfigured suppression filter on the certificate renewal alert also prevented timely notification before expiration.
resolution_steps: Requested and issued a renewed TLS certificate (new serial 6F:A1:22:D4:CC:18) for svc-internal-web.corplabs.internal from the internal Certificate Authority, coordinated by Sandra Okafor (sokafor@corplabs.com), before revalidating the certificate subject and intended endpoint coverage including SAN entries.

Uploaded and applied the renewed leaf certificate together with the full certificate chain to the ALB (alb-prod-east-01.corplabs.internal) so it no longer presented the expired chain to clients. Deployment performed by Raj Anand (ranand) and verified in the AWS ACM listener configuration.

Cleared the load balancer certificate cache on alb-prod-east-01.corplabs.internal and forced a fresh TLS presentation to remove the stale expired certificate (serial 4A:7C:3E:91:BB:02) from active handshakes.

Validated the service endpoint from multiple internal client paths — including WORKSTATION-PC-MCHEN (10.42.17.88) in Arlington and WORKSTATION-LT-DHOLL (10.42.23.115) in Raleigh — and through the load balancer to confirm the certificate expiration date (2026-12-19), chain trust, and successful TLS handshake behavior. Maria Chen and Derek Holloway confirmed service restoration.

Removed the suppression filter (rule ID CW-SUPP-0447, originally created by jparker) from the certificate renewal monitoring rule in CertWatch and tested alert delivery to sokafor@corplabs.com and the #infra-certs Slack channel so future certificate expiry conditions are detected before service impact.

title: Multiple users trapped in MFA prompt loop
description: Users in Engineering and some external contractor groups (primarily under the Apex Solutions contractor org) were trying to sign in to Salesforce and Workday through the SSO Portal, but after the Okta MFA challenge they were repeatedly returned to another verification prompt or redirected back to the sign-in page. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-4821) and escalated by team lead Marcus Whitfield. Some users saw a 'verification failed' message instead of receiving a session. The issue began shortly after an Okta group-based policy change pushed by identity admin dkrasinski around 2026-04-05 09:20 UTC and affected roughly 120 users across the Arlington and parts of Frankfurt regions, blocking normal access to SaaS applications.
observed_errors: Repeated MFA challenge with no successful token issuance
Redirect loop back to SSO Portal sign-in
root_cause: An Okta group-based conditional access policy change incorrectly scoped MFA requirements and application access for impacted Engineering and contractor users, creating an authentication loop where MFA challenges completed without successful session issuance. A secondary contributor was stale MFA factor enrollment on a subset of accounts, which caused continued prompt loops or verification failures until re-enrollment was completed.
resolution_steps: Reviewed recent Okta policy changes and identified the newly pushed group-based conditional access rule ('Eng-Contractor-MFA-Enforce-v2'), authored by dkrasinski at 09:20 UTC, as the common change preceding the MFA loop behavior for Engineering and Apex Solutions contractor groups.

Rolled back the affected Okta group-based access policy for impacted user groups (Eng-US-East, Contractors-Apex) to restore the prior authentication path and stop the repeated MFA challenge loop. Rollback performed by Tomasz Keller at approximately 09:55 UTC.

Validated group membership and application assignment for affected Engineering and contractor accounts — including rnguyen (EMP-4821), mwhitfield (EMP-5190), and pdeshmukh — to confirm they matched the intended policy scope for SSO Portal, Salesforce, and Workday access.

Forced MFA re-enrollment for 14 users who still experienced verification failures or redirect loops after the rollback, clearing stale factor enrollment state and re-establishing a valid active factor. Users were contacted via email (e.g., r.nguyen@corplabs.com) with re-enrollment instructions.

Monitored post-change authentication activity across Arlington and Frankfurt regions and confirmed successful sign-in restoration for the large majority of impacted users, then documented a permanent policy correction and planned cleanup of stale MFA enrollments. Follow-up review scheduled with dkrasinski and Tomasz Keller to prevent recurrence.

Also, can you let us know whether other members of your team (e.g., Marcus Whitfield or anyone in the contractor group) are seeing the same behavior? If possible, try from a different browser or device and note the result. You can also reach me at identsupport@corplabs.com.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: During the overnight CustomerSync batch window (scheduled 01:00–04:00 PST), the Integration Gateway in us-west-2 began returning repeated 504 Gateway Timeout errors and API call durations exceeding 30 seconds when calling the downstream CRM API endpoint at api.customersync.corplabs.com. This was first reported by Priya Nair (Application Support lead, Portland office) after the Reporting Dashboard failed to refresh overnight customer records. Gateway logs on host INTGW-WEST-01.corplabs.internal showed a token refresh job failure (job ID: tknrot-20251201-0130) in the same time window, indicating the sync process was blocked by downstream authentication issues rather than a general platform outage. Approximately 14,200 customer records were delayed, impacting dependent reporting and sync workflows used by the finance reconciliation team.
root_cause: An expired downstream API token was left in use after the automated token rotation job failed. The Integration Gateway could no longer complete authenticated calls, which manifested as repeated timeout behavior during batch sync processing and delayed customer data updates.
resolution_steps: Validated the downstream API authentication path for service account svc-custsync-prod and manually rotated the expired API token on the Integration Gateway (INTGW-WEST-01.corplabs.internal) via the admin console to restore successful authenticated requests to api.customersync.corplabs.com. Rotation performed by Melissa Williams (mwilliams) at 21:02 UTC.

Restarted the gateway worker process on INTGW-WEST-01.corplabs.internal (PID 28417) to clear any stale authentication cache and ensure the new token was actively used by batch sync jobs. Post-restart, confirmed HTTP 200 responses with avg latency of 280ms on downstream calls.

Applied temporary retry and exponential backoff tuning on the Integration Gateway (max_retries: 5, initial_backoff: 2s, backoff_multiplier: 2.0) to reduce immediate job failures while authentication was being stabilized. Configuration change deployed by Derek Hollis (dhollis, Platform Engineering, Seattle office).

Corrected the failed automated token rotation job (tknrot-20251201-0130) by updating the rotation script's credential store path and added pre-expiry validation checks so future rotations confirm token acceptance at least 24 hours before the previous credential expires. Fix committed by dhollis and reviewed by Priya Nair.

Added alerting and dashboard visibility for token rotation failures via the Monitoring System (alert rule: TOKEN_ROTATION_FAIL, notify: appsupport-oncall@corplabs.com, pnair@corplabs.com) and post-change monitoring confirmed API success rates returned to 99.97% and sync latency returned to normal levels (p95: 1.2s) within 30 minutes of remediation.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — we found repeated 504 timeouts during the overnight CustomerSync batch on INTGW-WEST-01.corplabs.internal and a failed token refresh event (job tknrot-20251201-0130) in the same window. The service account svc-custsync-prod was returning AUTH_EXPIRED on downstream calls starting around 01:32 UTC. Can you confirm whether any token rotation or downstream API credential change occurred before the sync delays started? Also, was anyone else on your team — perhaps Raj Menon or the on-call engineer — aware of a scheduled credential update?

title: Okta SSO MFA prompt loop prevents user access
description: I (Jorge Morales, emp ID EMP-90234) could not access SaaS applications through the corporate SSO Portal because Okta repeatedly prompted for MFA and rejected authentication instead of completing sign-in. The issue began after a recent device change from my old phone to a new iPhone, affected a single account (username: jmorales), and blocked access to applications including Salesforce and Google Workspace from Chrome on Windows 10. I was working from the Austin office at the time and my workstation hostname is WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-JM (IP 10.42.17.88).
root_cause: Stale MFA enrollment record in Okta after the user's device change caused factor verification to mismatch and loop the MFA challenge during SSO authentication.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the user's (jmorales / Jorge Morales, EMP-90234) recent sign-in behavior and account history in Okta, including the reported device change and repeated MFA challenge failures from client IP 10.42.17.88.

title: Print jobs stuck on Print Server PDQ-Print01
description: Multiple users in the Philadelphia office reported that printing to the shared HP LaserJet MFP M634 through PS-PRINT01 stopped working after recent maintenance changes on the print server. observed_errors: Print jobs stuck in queue (status: spooling)
Print spooler restart transiently clears jobs
Driver package checksum mismatch detected in event log
root_cause: The shared printer queue on PS-PRINT01 had been left in a paused state, preventing queued jobs from processing.
resolution_steps: Resume the paused shared printer queues \\PS-PRINT01\HP-Sales-3F and \\PS-PRINT01\HP-HR-2F on PS-PRINT01 using Set-Printer -Name <QueueName> -ComputerName PS-PRINT01 -PrinterStatus Normal, and clear any stale jobs that remained from the paused period (5 orphaned jobs were purged via Remove-PrintJob).

Review queue settings and recent administrative activity on PS-PRINT01 to determine why the queue entered or remained in a paused state — audit logs confirmed the pause was triggered by svc-printadmin during a scheduled maintenance window at 19:45 UTC but the resume step was missed. Anil Kapoor updated the maintenance runbook to include a mandatory post-maintenance queue status verification checklist.

Submit validation print jobs from affected users to confirm the queue accepts and completes jobs normally. Confirmed successful test prints from Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez) on \\PS-PRINT01\HP-Sales-3F and Rachel Stein (rstein) on \\PS-PRINT01\HP-HR-2F. Both users verified output at their respective printers in the Philadelphia office.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused Internal Web Service TLS outage — certificate renewed
description: Internal users and dependent integrations across the Portland datacenter were trying to reach the Internal Web Service at https://appportal.corp.internal, but the endpoint began failing TLS validation after the service certificate expired on 2025-12-20. Browsers showed certificate warnings and clients reported ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID, TLS handshake failures, and some 502 responses over TLS. The issue was initially reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40291) from the internal-dev team. The outage continued after the initial certificate renewal because the load balancer (LB-PROD-DC1) was still presenting an outdated certificate chain, blocking normal internal application access until the full chain was corrected and reloaded.
root_cause: The Internal Web Service outage was caused by an expired TLS certificate. The initial remediation renewed and deployed the leaf certificate, but the load balancer continued serving an outdated certificate chain, so clients still failed certificate validation. Certificate renewal monitoring/alerting was also not active enough to prevent expiration before impact.
resolution_steps: Renew the expired TLS certificate (CN=appportal.corp.internal) through the internal Certificate Authority for the Internal Web Service endpoint; renewal request submitted by Raj Patel (rpatel, EMP-50184) and approved via the CA portal.

Deploy the renewed service certificate to the Internal Web Service backend on appportal.corp.internal so the backend presents the current certificate (valid through 2026-12-20). Deployment confirmed by Raj Patel.

Replace the full certificate chain on the load balancer LB-PROD-DC1, including the correct intermediate chain issued by the internal CA, and restart or reload the load balancer service to apply the change. Chain replacement performed by Priya Nair (pnair) from the network team.

Validate the served certificate from client and load balancer paths to confirm the endpoint https://appportal.corp.internal now presents the renewed certificate and complete chain without expiration warnings. Verified by Maria Chen from WORKSTATION-PC-MCHEN (10.42.18.77) and Tomás Reyes from Austin.

Restore and test certificate renewal monitoring and alerting so future certificate expirations are detected before service impact. Kevin Briggs (kbriggs, EMP-30872) re-enabled the cert-expiry-monitor scheduled job and confirmed test alerts are delivered to infra-alerts@corp.internal at 30, 14, and 7 days before expiry.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — this is Kevin Briggs from the infrastructure team. Please confirm whether clients are still seeing certificate warnings after the certificate renewal performed yesterday evening, and if the error is the same across browser-based access and service-to-service calls (e.g., the CI/CD integration from WORKSTATION-BUILD-MC). Can you also verify whether the issue affects connections from both Portland and Austin offices?

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to \\fileserver\Dept folder for Finance user
description: Finance analyst Rachel Nguyen (employee ID FIN-20418) was trying to open the department shared folder \\fileserver\Dept from Windows Explorer on her Windows 10 endpoint WORKSTATION-RNGN-PC (IP 10.42.17.83) and received an "Access Denied" message. The issue blocks access to department files on the on-premises file server and may involve stale mapped-drive credentials, a stale shortcut/path, or missing share entitlement. Ticket submitted on behalf of the user by service desk agent Marcus Delgado.
root_cause: User access token or effective share entitlement was no longer matching the permissions required for \\fileserver\Dept, most likely due to missing or unapplied AD security group membership and/or stale cached SMB credentials on the existing mapped drive session.
resolution_steps: Validated that Rachel Nguyen (rnnguyen, FIN-20418) should have access to the Finance department share and reviewed the expected AD security group FS-Finance-RW used to grant access to \\fileserver\Dept. Confirmed membership was present in Active Directory.

Confirmed the access path in use on WORKSTATION-RNGN-PC (10.42.17.83) and had the user test the current UNC path \\fileserver\Dept directly rather than relying on the existing mapped drive (Z:) or a stale shortcut.

Removed stale network session state by having Rachel clear stored Windows credentials for the file server via Credential Manager, disconnecting the mapped drive/session (net use Z: /delete), and having her sign out and sign back in to refresh the Kerberos access token on WORKSTATION-RNGN-PC.

Reapplied the correct access model by ensuring rnnguyen was associated with the approved security group FS-Finance-RW (CN=FS-Finance-RW,OU=Security Groups,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) that grants read/write access to the department share.

Had Rachel reconnect to \\fileserver\Dept after the token refresh and verified the folder opened successfully without the access denied error. Re-mapped Z: drive via net use Z: \\fileserver\Dept /persistent:yes and confirmed all Finance subfolders were accessible.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please test the current UNC path \\fileserver\Dept directly from your workstation WORKSTATION-RNGN-PC instead of the mapped drive (Z:), then open Credential Manager and clear any saved Windows credentials for the file server. After that, sign out of your Windows session and sign back in so we can rule out a stale SMB session or token. Let me know the result. — Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com)

title: Laptop slow
description: I was trying to use my corporate Windows 10 laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-DELL-MR) after sign-in at around 2:00 PM, but the device became extremely slow immediately after login. My username is mreeves and I'm based out of the Portland office. Outlook and Chrome took upwards of 3–4 minutes to open, Task Manager showed CPU usage pinned near 90%, and Microsoft Defender activity (MsMpEng.exe) was consuming heavy CPU and disk IO. The issue impacted normal post-login productivity on a single managed laptop assigned to me (EMP-40821).
observed_errors: High CPU by MsMpEng.exe observed at login
Disk IO saturation during post-login full AV scan
root_cause: Microsoft Defender Antivirus had a backlog of queued scans and a policy condition that allowed full scans to trigger at user login, causing sustained CPU and disk IO contention immediately after sign-in.
resolution_steps: Reviewed active Microsoft Defender scan state on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (user: mreeves, IP: 10.42.17.88), cleared the queued scan backlog of 3 pending full scans (oldest from 2026-02-08), and stopped the stuck full-scan activity contributing to post-login resource spikes.

Restarted the Windows Defender Antivirus Service (WinDefend) on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and refreshed Defender signatures to the latest definitions so the endpoint returned to a normal scan state instead of resuming a repeated backlog at login.

Validated that MsMpEng.exe (PID 4812) was the primary resource consumer on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and confirmed CPU usage dropped from ~90% to under 12% and disk IO returned to normal levels within two minutes after backlog cleanup and service restart.

Refreshed and redistributed the endpoint protection policy (GPO: EP-ScanPolicy-West-v4) in coordination with security team member David Cho (dcho) to set ScanOnlyIfIdle=true and prevent full scans from being triggered during user logon on managed endpoints in the Portland group.

Rescheduled full antivirus scans to off-hours (2:00 AM–5:00 AM window) and staggered scan timing across the Portland endpoint group to reduce the chance of future simultaneous login-time scan contention.

Removed approximately 4.2 GB of temporary files from C:\Windows\Temp and user profile temp directories on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and reclaimed disk space (from 11 GB to 15.2 GB free) to reduce disk pressure during startup and scan operations.

title: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key not escrowed on Intune-managed laptop
description: Intune-managed laptop WORKSTATION-SLAPTOP-MR (asset tag LPT-4821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com, EMP-90274) in the Dallas office became noncompliant for disk encryption after a recent policy push on 2026-01-18. In the Intune portal, the device (IP 10.42.17.88) shows BitLocker not enabled and no recovery key escrowed to Azure AD, blocking my ability to restore compliance for endpoint encryption requirements. The issue affects BitLocker, Intune, and Device Compliance Service on Windows 10 21H2, and prior compliance history indicates the failure began after the latest policy/application cycle rather than initial enrollment.
root_cause: BitLocker encryption was initiated successfully after TPM protector initialization, but the device failed to escrow the current recovery key to Intune because the device key protection service returned error 0x80090010 during key upload. Compliance remained failed because the encryption policy requires successful recovery key escrow in addition to local BitLocker enablement.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM readiness on WORKSTATION-SLAPTOP-MR (Get-Tpm confirmed TpmReady: True, TpmPresent: True) and initialized the TPM-based BitLocker protector via manage-bde so the device assigned to Marcus Reeves (mreeves, EMP-90274) could proceed with encryption.

Started BitLocker encryption on the C: system volume of WORKSTATION-SLAPTOP-MR (IP 10.42.17.88) and confirmed that local encryption activity began on the device with encryption percentage progressing in manage-bde -status output.

Attempted recovery key rotation and escrow to Intune for WORKSTATION-SLAPTOP-MR, then forced an Intune device sync via Company Portal to trigger policy re-evaluation and key upload. Escrow failed with 0x80090010 on both attempts.

Reviewed BitLocker and MDM logging on WORKSTATION-SLAPTOP-MR (C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs and Event Viewer > BitLocker-API), which consistently showed recovery key upload failure with error 0x80090010 (NTE_PERM) during escrow rather than a local policy-assignment failure.

Documented the confirmed escrow failure and handed the incident to Endpoint Support engineer Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) for service-level investigation and remediation of the Intune/key protection upload path before re-running escrow and compliance evaluation for mreeves' device.

Confirmed the compliance state for rnguyen's device returned to compliant, which cleared the Conditional Access block and restored SharePoint access. Rachel Nguyen confirmed she could reach SharePoint from the Arlington office without further issues.

Final confirmation received from Maria Gonzalez at 2026-04-01T14:22:00Z.

title: Print jobs stuck on print server
description: Finance users in the Frankfurt office were trying to print to the shared HP-LaserJet-Dept queue on print server PRT-SRV-01, but jobs remained queued and did not complete. The issue was first reported by Maria Engel (EMP-40291) who noticed her month-end reports were not printing. Several other Finance team members, including Tobias Richter, confirmed the same behavior — some users also saw the printer appear offline on their workstations. The issue affected printing from the central Windows print server and blocked normal document output for the Finance team. Initial server checks showed Windows Print Spooler driver load failures tied to the HP-Universal-6.1 package.
observed_errors: Spooler log: Driver load failure referencing HP-Universal-6.1
Print job status: Stuck / Error - driver not found
EventID 8004 - Print Spooler error loading driver
root_cause: Corruption in the HP-Universal-6.1 printer driver package on PRT-SRV-01 caused Windows Print Spooler driver load failures, leaving jobs stuck in the HP-LaserJet-Dept queue and making the shared printer appear offline to users.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the HP-LaserJet-Dept queue and spooler event logs on PRT-SRV-01 (10.42.16.5) to confirm repeated driver load failures (EventID 8004) referencing HP-Universal-6.1. Identified 23 stuck jobs from Finance users including mengel and trichter.
Stopped the Print Spooler service on PRT-SRV-01 and cleared all 23 stuck jobs from the affected queue so the corrupted pending jobs would not continue retrying and consuming spool resources.

Removed the corrupted HP-Universal-6.1 driver references from the PRT-SRV-01 driver store (C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\x64) and reinstalled the approved HP Universal driver package from the central repository at \\filesrv-emea\drivers\hp-universal\approved, verified by file hash comparison.

Restarted the Print Spooler service on PRT-SRV-01 and verified that the HP-LaserJet-Dept queue returned to an online state without new driver load failures. Confirmed the driver loaded cleanly in the spooler logs.

Submitted validation prints from affected user workstations — WORKSTATION-ME-FIN (Maria Engel, 10.42.17.22) and WORKSTATION-TR-FIN (Tobias Richter, 10.42.17.31) — and monitored spooler behavior on PRT-SRV-01 for 30 minutes to confirm all jobs completed successfully with no recurrence of EventID 8004. Notified mengel@corplabs.com and trichter@corplabs.com that service was restored.

title: BitLocker not enabling
description: User Rachel Dominguez (rdominguez, EMP-40291) reported that her Windows 10 21H2 corporate laptop (WORKSTATION-DELL-RD) at the Phoenix office was showing Encryption: Not enabled in Intune Device Compliance and was marked noncompliant for the required disk encryption policy. BitLocker had not started on the endpoint (IP 10.42.17.88), and no recovery key was visible in Azure AD for the device, blocking compliance and leaving the machine out of encryption policy enforcement. Ticket escalated by her manager Kevin Tran (ktran@corplabs.com).
observed_errors: TPM protector missing / not initialized observed during manage-bde check
No BitLocker recovery key present in Azure AD device object
Intune device compliance flag: EncryptionRequired = false
root_cause: The device's TPM-based BitLocker protector was not initialized, so BitLocker could not start encryption and the recovery key could not be escrowed to Azure AD for Intune compliance reporting.
resolution_steps: Validated local BitLocker and TPM status on WORKSTATION-DELL-RD (IP 10.42.17.88, user rdominguez) using manage-bde -status C: and tpm.msc, and confirmed the TPM protector was missing or not initialized.
Initialized the TPM protector on WORKSTATION-DELL-RD via manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm and recreated the BitLocker protector required for TPM-based encryption on the OS volume.
Enabled BitLocker locally on WORKSTATION-DELL-RD (manage-bde -on C:) so disk encryption could begin using the newly initialized TPM protector.

Forced an Intune device sync from WORKSTATION-DELL-RD (Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Sync) and from the Intune admin console for rdominguez's device to trigger policy re-evaluation and recovery key escrow to Azure AD.

Verified the BitLocker recovery key appeared in Azure AD under the WORKSTATION-DELL-RD device object and confirmed the Intune encryption compliance state updated to compliant after policy reassignment. Notified Rachel Dominguez and Kevin Tran (ktran@corplabs.com) of resolution.

title: Intermittent disconnects from Corporate Wi-Fi
description: I was trying to stay connected to the Corporate Wi-Fi from my Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, IP 10.42.17.88), but the device would join the CorpWiFi-5G SSID and then lose network access within about a minute, showing "No network access." The issue started this morning around 8:15 AM EDT at the Raleigh office, appears limited to this single device, and blocked normal use of corporate network resources over wireless — I couldn't reach internal sites or pull code from our repos. Rebuilding the Wi-Fi profile and re-enrolling the device improved connectivity only temporarily, indicating a device-specific wireless authentication or session stability issue rather than a broader SSID outage. My username is mramirez (employee ID EMP-40821).
observed_errors: No network access after joining SSID
802.1X session drop observed in controller logs
root_cause: Corrupted endpoint wireless profile combined with a stale 802.1X/NAC session on the wireless infrastructure caused the device to authenticate inconsistently and drop network access shortly after joining the Corporate SSID.
resolution_steps: Removed the existing Corporate Wi-Fi profile from the affected laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, user mramirez) to clear corrupted supplicant settings and the outdated certificate thumbprint that was causing EAP-TLS negotiation failures.

Re-enrolled the device to the CorpWiFi-5G SSID using the standard Onboarding Client flow and confirmed the active corporate Wi-Fi profile and valid wireless certificate were present and matched the current issuing CA thumbprint.

Cleared the device's stale wireless/NAC session (MAC 4C:77:A3:1E:9D:02) on WLC-EAST-01 so the endpoint could establish a fresh authenticated 802.1X session and receive the correct Engineering VLAN (VLAN 142) assignment.

Reconnected the laptop to Corporate Wi-Fi and verified that network access remained available beyond the previous one-minute failure window — confirmed stable connectivity for over 15 minutes with successful pings to gateway 10.42.16.1 and internal resource access.

Advised the user (mramirez) to report recurrence immediately to the Wireless Team or contact agent Diana Chen at d.chen@corplabs.com / ext 4417 so the team can review roaming or controller-side behavior on WLC-EAST-01 if the issue returns.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether the issue affects only this laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR) and whether the connection consistently drops about a minute after joining Corporate Wi-Fi. Also, can you verify you're connecting from the Raleigh office and not over VPN or a remote site? I'd like to rule out AP-specific problems before digging into your endpoint profile.

title: unable to complete SSO login
description: I am unable to complete sign-in to SaaS applications through the web SSO portal at https://sso.corplabs.com. After entering my credentials (mwilson@corplabs.com), I am repeatedly prompted for MFA and the authentication flow either rejects the prompt or returns to the MFA challenge instead of completing login. The issue was observed when attempting access to Office 365, Salesforce, and the internal SSO portal from my Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-SURF-MW) and my iPhone. Browser cache clear and device reboot did not resolve the problem, and I remain blocked from normal application access. My employee ID is E-40821 for reference.
observed_errors: Continuous MFA prompt with no completion
No consistent numeric error code provided
root_cause: Likely stale or invalid MFA factor enrollment for the affected user in the identity provider, causing successful primary authentication but repeated MFA challenge failure/loop during SSO completion. Scope remains consistent with a user-specific identity configuration issue rather than a broad outage.
resolution_steps: Validated that the symptom matched an MFA challenge loop during SSO at https://sso.corplabs.com rather than a password failure or application-specific outage by reviewing Okta sign-on logs for mwilson@corplabs.com showing repeated factor verification failures from IP 10.42.18.97.

Reviewed the user's (mwilson) MFA enrollment state in the Okta admin console and identified the need for a targeted factor reset due to repeated challenge failure across multiple apps and devices. The enrolled TOTP factor dated 2025-11-14 was orphaned after the user's recent iPhone factory reset.
Reset the user's MFA enrollment in Okta and removed the stale TOTP factor association for mwilson. Performed by identity team member Priya Nair (pnair).

Had Marcus Wilson re-enroll the Microsoft Authenticator factor on his iPhone and confirm device time synchronization (Settings > General > Date & Time > Set Automatically) before retrying sign-in through the SSO portal.

Retested access through the SSO portal at https://sso.corplabs.com and confirmed mwilson could complete MFA once and reach Office 365, Salesforce, and the internal portal without being returned to the challenge screen. Successful sign-on event confirmed in Okta logs at 2026-04-08T12:38:00Z from WORKSTATION-SURF-MW.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, can you confirm whether the MFA loop happens on both your Windows laptop and iPhone, whether you recently changed or re-enrolled your Microsoft Authenticator app, and whether the same behavior occurs for both Office 365 and Salesforce? Also, could you let me know the IP address you're connecting from so I can check the Okta sign-on logs for your account (mwilson)?

title: account locked in AD
description: I (Marcus Delgado, emp ID E-40291) was trying to sign in after completing a self-service password reset on the Password Reset Portal, but subsequent authentication attempts against Active Directory returned an account locked message (AD error 532). The issue affected my AD account (mdelgado), the Password Reset Portal, and SSO sign-in at https://sso.corplabs.com. I reported repeated background sign-in attempts from my corporate iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) at IP 10.42.17.88 after the reset. This blocked normal account access because the initial reset token expired before the password change fully propagated to SSO, and stale mobile credentials cached on the iPhone continued to submit failed logons against DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal.
root_cause: Active Directory lockout policy was triggered by repeated failed sign-in attempts from a corporate iPhone using cached credentials after a self-service password reset token expired before the password change propagated to SSO.
resolution_steps: Reviewed AD lockout logs on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and Password Reset Portal activity to confirm the lockout source was the user's corporate iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD, IP 10.42.17.88) repeatedly attempting authentication with stale cached credentials for account mdelgado — 14 failed attempts between 14:42 and 14:58 UTC.
Unlocked the user's account (CN=mdelgado,OU=Corp Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) in Active Directory via DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal so new authentication attempts could proceed.

Instructed Marcus Delgado to clear the saved corporate account credentials on the iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) for Outlook and Teams mail and collaboration clients to stop additional failed background sign-in attempts from IP 10.42.17.88.
Issued a new password reset token (PRX-88435) through the Password Reset Portal for mdelgado and completed a fresh password reset workflow at 15:14 UTC.

Verified the updated credential for mdelgado successfully propagated to SSO at https://sso.corplabs.com via DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and confirmed Marcus Delgado could sign in normally from the Charlotte office after the mobile credential cache was cleared.

Documented the incident (INC-ALP-0065) for follow-up review by Rachel Nguyen and the identity team of reset token TTL (currently 15 min) and AD lockout threshold settings (currently 10 attempts) to reduce recurrence for mobile-heavy users.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reaching out. Please confirm whether any mobile mail or collaboration apps on your corporate iPhone (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) are still signed in or prompting for credentials in the background after the password reset. Specifically, check Outlook and Teams — we're seeing repeated failed authentication attempts from IP 10.42.17.88 against your AD account mdelgado. — Rachel Nguyen, Identity Support
