title: Integration Gateway - scheduled job timeouts
description: Overnight scheduled data sync jobs through the Integration Gateway in Kubernetes (namespace: intg-gateway-prod) began failing against the upstream partner API (partner: Meridian Data Services) in us-east-1. The issue was first flagged by the Monitoring System at 2025-12-02T03:14Z when engineer Priya Narayanan received PagerDuty alerts on repeated HTTP 401 Unauthorized responses with token expiration indicators from the gateway pod intg-gw-pod-7b4c running on host WORKSTATION-INTGW-PN. These were followed by HTTP 504 timeouts as the gateway retried until backoff limits were reached. The failures delayed expected partner data synchronization for internal API clients (service account: svc-datasync-east) during the 02:00–05:00 UTC scheduled job window. Reported by Marcus Ellison (emp ID: EMP-90274) from the Denver integration operations team.
root_cause: Expired API token for the upstream partner service caused authentication failures; gateway retries and backoff then extended requests until scheduled jobs timed out.
resolution_steps: Validated that the upstream Meridian partner credential (secret: intg-partner-token-secret) in use by the Integration Gateway service account svc-datasync-east was expired based on repeated 401 responses showing token expiration, cross-referenced with Vault TTL expiry at 2025-12-01T23:59Z.

Rotated the Meridian partner API token via the partner portal (coordinated with dmurphy@meridiandata.io) and updated the Kubernetes secret intg-partner-token-secret consumed by the Integration Gateway in namespace intg-gateway-prod. Rotation performed by Carlos Medina (cmedina, EMP-61038).
Redeployed and restarted the gateway pods (intg-gw-pod-7b4c and replicas) in namespace intg-gateway-prod so the running workloads loaded the new credential from the refreshed Kubernetes secret.

Confirmed authenticated calls from service account svc-datasync-east to the Meridian partner API (https://api.meridiandata.io/v2/sync) no longer returned 401 Unauthorized responses after the secret rollout — test call returned HTTP 200 at 2025-12-02T21:04Z.

Verified two consecutive scheduled integration job runs (02:00 UTC and 03:00 UTC cycle equivalents triggered manually) completed successfully without retry exhaustion or HTTP 504 timeouts; data sync payloads confirmed in downstream consumers.

Monitored gateway and job metrics via the Monitoring System dashboard for 2 hours after deployment (until 2025-12-02T23:15Z) to confirm stable processing, nominal latency, and no recurrence. Alert channel confirmed clear by Priya Narayanan.
agent_questions: Reviewing the overnight failures now — I can see the alert trail in the Monitoring System dashboard for namespace intg-gateway-prod. Can you confirm whether the gateway logs on pod intg-gw-pod-7b4c show authentication errors from the Meridian partner API before the timeout events, and whether any recent token rotation was expected? I'm checking the secret intg-partner-token-secret in Vault as well. — Agent: Priya Narayanan (pnarayanan@corplabs.com)

title: reports Windows laptop very slow after login
description: I have a corporate Windows 10 laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-DELL-MR, asset tag LPT-4821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (emp ID: E-20948) becoming extremely slow immediately after login for the past two days. The device is used at our Portland office and connects via IP 10.47.22.115. Outlook, Chrome, and File Explorer take roughly 20-60 seconds to open, preventing normal work. Task Manager showed sustained CPU spikes from Microsoft Defender (MsMpEng.exe) along with multiple startup processes, and the system drive (C:) had only about 4% free space remaining (~9.5 GB on a 256 GB SSD), indicating a post-login resource bottleneck affecting general application launch performance.
observed_errors: CPU usage spiking to 85-95% from MsMpEng.exe (Defender)
Multiple startup processes consuming sustained CPU
root_cause: A Microsoft Defender scan backlog running during user logon, combined with multiple resource-heavy startup items and critically low free space on C:, caused sustained CPU contention and delayed application launches.
resolution_steps: Reviewed endpoint resource usage on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (user: mreeves, IP 10.47.22.115) and confirmed Defender scan activity (3 queued full-scan jobs), heavy startup processes (OneDrive sync, Salesforce Agent, legacy CRM updater), and critically low free space (9.5 GB of 256 GB on C:) were occurring immediately after login.

Disabled two non-essential startup items (legacy CRM updater and redundant Salesforce background agent) on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and updated the applied startup configuration via Endpoint Management to reduce CPU load during logon for user mreeves.

Cleared user temporary files from C:\Users\mreeves\AppData\Local\Temp and ran Disk Cleanup to reclaim approximately 18 GB of space on C:, bringing free capacity to ~27.5 GB (roughly 11%) and reducing disk pressure contributing to slow application launches.

Paused the 3 queued Defender full-scan activities on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR, cleared the scan backlog dating back to 2026-02-05, and allowed a targeted quick scan to complete successfully with no threats detected.
Forced a device policy refresh through Endpoint Management so the revised startup and scan settings applied cleanly to WORKSTATION-DELL-MR, verified by technician Priya Nair (pnair).

Validated normal performance after remediation by confirming CPU spikes subsided to 12-18% at login and Outlook, Chrome, and File Explorer opened within 3-5 seconds on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR. Notified Marcus Reeves (marcus.reeves@corplabs.com) that the ticket is resolved.

title: Multiple users stuck in MFA prompt loop
description: Multiple users in the Sales group — including Rachel Dominguez (rdominguez), Marcus Hale (mhale), and at least four others — were trying to access Salesforce, Workday, and Concur through the Okta SSO portal from the Austin office, but after completing the password step they were returned to the MFA challenge page instead of reaching the application landing page. The issue began after overnight maintenance on 2026-04-05, affected users on both desktop (Windows 10) and mobile authenticator apps, and blocked access to core SaaS applications needed for normal sales operations. Browser and identity logs for the affected accounts showed rejected MFA challenges (MFA challenge rejected), invalid session behavior (Authentication failed: invalid_session), and TOTP validation failures across all three target apps.
root_cause: Stale MFA factor enrollment records in Okta for affected Sales users, combined with clock drift on some authenticator devices, caused TOTP validation mismatches and repeated MFA challenge rejection that returned users to the MFA prompt.
resolution_steps: Reviewed affected Sales user accounts in Okta (rdominguez, mhale, pnair, jfields, kmoreno, acooper) and reset MFA enrollment for users showing stale or inconsistent factor state via the Okta admin console.

Forced MFA re-enrollment at next sign-in for all six affected users so each could register a fresh authenticator factor and remove invalid prior enrollments. Confirmation emails were sent to each user's corporate address (e.g., rdominguez@corplabs.com) with re-enrollment instructions.

Instructed users — particularly mhale and pnair whose devices showed clock drift — to enable automatic time synchronization on their mobile devices and resync or re-register their authenticator app before retrying login. Tomas Garcia (tgarcia, emp ID E-50274) from the Sales team coordinated user communication.

Validated that conditional access and factor policy assignments for the Sales group were aligned after overnight maintenance and updated policy handling to enforce periodic factor re-enrollment, reducing recurrence risk from stale-device enrollments. Change reviewed by Naveen Kapoor on the identity team.

Tested sign-in with sampled affected users (rdominguez from WORKSTATION-RDOMINGUEZ and mhale from his mobile device) and confirmed successful access to Salesforce, Workday, and Concur without MFA looping, then monitored Okta authentication logs for 24 hours with no recurring spike in rejected challenges.
agent_questions: I can see repeated Okta MFA challenge rejections for the reported users, including rdominguez and mhale. Their sign-in attempts from IP range 10.42.16.x (Austin office VPN pool) are cycling through the MFA prompt without completing. Please confirm whether all affected users are in the Sales group and whether the issue started immediately after the overnight maintenance window on 2026-04-05.

title: Multiple users cannot connect to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple employees in the Building 4 Denver office were trying to join the Corporate Wi-Fi from managed laptops, but the connection prompted for credentials, attempted 802.1X authentication, then failed with an authentication error and no network access. The issue was first reported by Priya Nair (EMP-40821) around 08:45 local time and quickly confirmed by at least four other engineers on the same floor. The issue began the same morning, affected multiple nearby users, and blocked normal wireless connectivity needed to access internal resources. Controller and RADIUS-side evidence pointed to EAP-TLS failures caused by an expired wireless server certificate on WLC-BLDG4-01.corp.local.
root_cause: The wireless controller server certificate used for EAP-TLS authentication had expired, causing Cisco ISE/RADIUS authentication attempts to be rejected and preventing clients from receiving network access. Some endpoints also retained stale or corrupt Wi-Fi profiles after certificate renewal, requiring local profile remediation.
resolution_steps: Generated or imported a renewed wireless server certificate and deployed it to the Wireless Controller (WLC-BLDG4-01.corp.local) for EAP-TLS authentication. Deployment was coordinated by network engineer Kevin Marsh (kmarsh).

Validated the certificate chain and binding used by the controller and RADIUS authentication path to confirm the renewed certificate was presented correctly to connecting clients including pnair, mellison, rcho, and dokafor.
Restarted the RADIUS service on Cisco ISE to clear failed authentication sessions for all affected users and ensure the updated certificate was active for new connection attempts.

Had impacted users (pnair, mellison, rcho, dokafor) forget the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID and reconnect so devices would re-establish trust with the renewed server certificate. Priya Nair and Marcus Ellison reconnected successfully at this step.

For devices that still failed after reconnect — specifically WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RC (rcho, IP 10.22.4.87) and dokafor's endpoint — removed the stale wireless profile and re-enrolled the endpoint into the corporate WLAN profile via Cisco ISE to restore successful authentication. Confirmed all four users had stable connectivity before closing.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please confirm whether multiple users in Building 4 are affected and whether controller or RADIUS logs on WLC-BLDG4-01.corp.local show EAP-TLS, certificate expired, or Access-Reject messages during connection attempts. Can you also share the hostname of your laptop? I see your username is pnair in Active Directory — I'll check ISE logs for your account specifically.

title: Print jobs stuck on Sales-Printer01
description: Sales users reported by team lead Maria Chen were trying to print to the shared queue Sales-Printer01, but jobs remained stuck on print-server-01 with a visible 'driver unavailable' state and the printer appeared offline from multiple client workstations including WORKSTATION-MC-4021 and WORKSTATION-RP-7788. Temporary queue clearing and Print Spooler restart restored printing briefly, but the issue returned within about 30 minutes, blocking normal document printing for the Sales group based in the Charlotte office. Ticket originally submitted by rparker (employee ID EMP-40291).
root_cause: A corrupt printer driver package on print-server-01 caused shared queue mapping failures for Sales-Printer01 and intermittent Print Spooler instability. Clearing queued jobs temporarily reduced symptoms but did not remove the defective server-side driver package, so new jobs returned to a 'driver unavailable' state.
resolution_steps: Removed the corrupt printer driver package from print-server-01 for the affected Sales-Printer01 queue. Performed by kbriggs with change approval from team lead Maria Chen (EMP-30184).
Installed the approved printer driver package (HP Universal Print Driver v6.9.0) on print-server-01 in place of the defective driver, verified DLL hash against approved baseline.
Remapped Sales-Printer01 to the corrected shared queue so client connections on WORKSTATION-RP-7788, WORKSTATION-MC-4021, and other Charlotte Sales workstations used the approved server-side driver.
Cleared residual stuck print jobs from the queue (14 jobs total from rparker, mchen, dokonkwo, and others) and restarted the Print Spooler service to reload the corrected driver binding.

Submitted and observed follow-up print activity after the change — confirmed successful test prints from rparker (WORKSTATION-RP-7788) and mchen (WORKSTATION-MC-4021) — and monitored queue behavior for 48 hours with no recurrence of driver unavailable errors. Users notified via email by tflores.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed sync
description: Scheduled analytics integration jobs from the Integration Gateway (gateway-prod-analytics.corplabs.internal) to the downstream API service began failing over the last 2 hours with repeated HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses. The issue was first reported by Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) from the analytics team in Charlotte. Retries were exhausted and downstream data synchronization for the analytics application was delayed, affecting automated reporting pipelines. Gateway logs on host INTGW-NODE-04 and the Monitoring System showed upstream latency spikes above the normal 3-second timeout window in Kubernetes in us-east-1, impacting automated sync completion rather than a single I action. The integration service account analytics_sync_svc was used for all failing requests originating from pod IP 10.42.17.88.
root_cause: Downstream API service latency intermittently exceeded the Integration Gateway request timeout window, producing HTTP 504 timeouts and exhausting job retries. Token validity was verified by rotation and post-change behavior did not materially improve, ruling out expired credentials as the primary cause. The incident was mitigated by increasing gateway timeout and retry handling and restarting gateway pods, with ownership handed to the downstream service team for capacity and latency remediation.
resolution_steps: Validated the integration authentication path by rotating the API token for the analytics_sync_svc service account and confirming authenticated requests continued to succeed during low-latency windows, which ruled out token expiry as the primary driver of the failures. Rotation performed by Carlos Medina.

Adjusted the Integration Gateway request timeout from 3 seconds to 8 seconds plus retry/backoff policy (exponential base 2s, max 5 retries) on INTGW-NODE-04 so transient downstream latency spikes would not immediately exhaust scheduled integration jobs.

Restarted Integration Gateway pods (including intgw-analytics-7b4d9f at 10.42.17.88) in Kubernetes us-east-1 to clear transient connection state and ensure the updated timeout and retry configuration was active across the running instances.

Correlated gateway 504 errors with Monitoring System data showing downstream API latency spikes (p99 at 7.2s) above the prior 3-second request window and documented downstream service latency as the operational fault domain. Findings reviewed by Tomoko Ishida.

Escalated the incident to the downstream API service team under Raj Patel (rpatel) for service-side latency and capacity investigation while keeping enhanced Monitoring System alerting in place for 24 hours to confirm sync recovery and no further retry exhaustion on the analytics_sync_svc integration path.

title: Print jobs stuck on PrintServer01
description: Multiple users in the Frankfurt office were trying to print through shared queues hosted on PrintServer01 (\\PrintServer01.corpprint.internal), but submitted jobs remained stuck in the queue and showed driver-related failures, including 'driver unavailable'. The issue was first reported by Maria Engström (EMP-40821) who noticed her 15-page contract document had been sitting in the queue for over 40 minutes. Restarting the Windows Server 2019 print spooler service only provided temporary movement of queued jobs and did not restore normal printing. The issue affected shared printer queues using the HP Universal Print Driver v6.9.0 and blocked normal employee printing across floors 2–4 until Tier 2 rebuilt the affected driver package and queue mappings.
observed_errors: jobs stuck at spooler for >30 minutes
root_cause: Corruption of the HP Universal printer driver package on PrintServer01 caused shared queues to report 'driver unavailable' and left jobs stuck in the spooler until the driver package and associated queue mappings were rebuilt.
resolution_steps: Remove the corrupted HP Universal Print Driver v6.9.0 package from PrintServer01 using Print Management (printmanagement.msc) and install the currently approved printer driver package (HP Universal Print Driver v7.0.1) from \\corpprint.internal\DriverRepo\HP_UPD\approved for the affected queues. Performed by Dmitri Volkov (dvolkov).

Purge all 23 stuck print jobs from the five impacted queues (FRA-FL2-HP01, FRA-FL3-HP02, FRA-FL4-HP01, FRA-FL2-HP03, FRA-FL3-HP04) and validate that the spool directory (C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS) no longer contains orphaned .SPL/.SHD files tied to the failed driver state.

Reassociate or rebuild the five affected printer queues so they reference the reinstalled approved HP Universal Print Driver v7.0.1 package instead of the corrupted v6.9.0 driver instance. Queue driver bindings verified via PowerShell Get-Printer on PrintServer01.

Restart the Print Spooler service on PrintServer01 after the driver reinstall and queue cleanup, then submit test print jobs from workstations WORKSTATION-ME-3190 (mengstrom) and WORKSTATION-LP-4821 (lpetersen) through the shared queues to confirm normal processing. All five queues processed test jobs successfully within 10 seconds.

Remap affected printers to the rebuilt queues on impacted client machines via Group Policy printer deployment where required, and update the print server driver inventory with the confirmed approved driver version (HP Universal Print Driver v7.0.1) used for recovery. Notify affected users including Maria Engström (mengstrom), Lars Petersen (lpetersen), and Priya Nair (pnair) that printing has been restored.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether all affected printers are hosted on PrintServer01 and whether users see 'driver unavailable' on the shared queues (e.g. \\PrintServer01\FRA-FL2-HP01) or only after submitting a job. Also, can you check whether users on other floors such as Lars Petersen (lpetersen) or anyone else in your team have the same symptoms? You can reach me at x4417 or helpdesk-print@corpservices.net if it's easier.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures for svc-inventory.internal.corp
description: Users and monitoring reported intermittent DNS resolution failures for svc-inventory.internal.corp starting around 08:30 from some internal subnets in the Austin office. The issue was initially flagged by Rajesh Menon (r.menon, EMP-40821) from the platform engineering team. The service remained reachable by direct IP (10.42.16.55), but affected clients could not consistently reach the application by hostname because DNS queries intermittently timed out and sometimes returned NXDOMAIN for the internal zone. Affected workstations included WORKSTATION-RMENON-L1 on subnet 10.42.16.0/24.
root_cause: Intermittent name resolution was caused by an internal DNS resolver path issue affecting some subnets, most consistent with an incorrect or missing conditional forwarder and stale cached responses on one or more internal resolvers for the internal.corp zone.
resolution_steps: Validated that affected clients including WORKSTATION-RMENON-L1 (10.42.16.112, user r.menon) were using internal resolver 10.42.1.12 that intermittently returned timeouts and NXDOMAIN for svc-inventory.internal.corp while direct IP connectivity to the service at 10.42.16.55 remained healthy.

Reviewed the internal DNS zone on DNS-AUTH-02.internal.corp and confirmed the svc-inventory.internal.corp A record was present with the expected target 10.42.16.55, indicating the issue was in resolver pathing rather than service availability.

Corrected the conditional forwarder configuration on resolver 10.42.1.12 for the internal.corp zone — updated from the decommissioned server 10.42.1.5 to the active authoritative DNS server DNS-AUTH-02.internal.corp (10.42.1.20) — so queries for internal.corp were sent to the proper authoritative DNS servers. Change performed by Patricia Hwang (p.hwang).

Flushed DNS cache on the impacted internal resolver 10.42.1.12 to remove stale negative and outdated cached responses that were causing intermittent lookup failures for the Austin 10.42.16.0/24 subnet.

Retested name resolution from affected subnets — confirmed consistent successful lookups for svc-inventory.internal.corp from WORKSTATION-RMENON-L1 and other Austin hosts without further timeout or NXDOMAIN responses. Rajesh Menon (r.menon) confirmed the issue was resolved.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal service TLS outage
description: Internal users in the Arlington office were trying to access the Internal Web Service at https://portal.internal.corplabs.com over HTTPS, but browsers showed certificate warnings and TLS handshakes failed, preventing normal access to internal endpoints. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40291) via email to the infrastructure team. Investigation showed the load balancer LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal was presenting an expired service certificate (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com) and an outdated intermediate chain after the certificate passed its renewal window, causing an internal TLS outage in us-east-1.
root_cause: The Internal Web Service TLS certificate expired and the load balancer continued serving the old certificate chain, including an outdated intermediate certificate. Certificate renewal monitoring was not firing, so the expiration was not remediated before service impact occurred.
resolution_steps: Validated the certificate presented by load balancer LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal and confirmed the service certificate for CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com had expired on 2025-12-19 and the intermediate chain (CorpLabs Intermediate CA G2) was outdated.

Issued a renewed TLS certificate from the internal Certificate Authority for the Internal Web Service (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com, SAN: portal.internal.corplabs.com), performed by Rachel Simmons (rsimmons) on the PKI team with new serial and validity through 2026-12-19.

Deployed the renewed certificate to the Internal Web Service and updated the full certificate chain (including current CorpLabs Intermediate CA G3) on load balancer LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal. Deployment verified by David Okafor.
Reloaded the load balancer configuration on LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal so it stopped presenting the expired certificate and old chain. Reload completed at 2025-12-20T00:22:00Z.

Verified successful TLS handshakes from client hosts WORKSTATION-PC-MC (10.42.17.88) and WORKSTATION-LT-JP (10.55.3.22) and confirmed that users mchen and jparker no longer received certificate date warnings when accessing https://portal.internal.corplabs.com.

Restored and tested certificate renewal monitoring alerts to ensure future expirations are detected before impact. Alert rule re-enabled by rsimmons in the certificate lifecycle dashboard with a 30-day and 7-day pre-expiry notification schedule. Confirmation email sent to infra-alerts@corplabs.com.

title: Nightly API integration jobs timing out for Integration Gateway
description: Nightly data synchronization jobs from the Integration Gateway (namespace: intg-gateway-prod, cluster: eks-prod-east) to the downstream API Service in us-east-1 began failing at 02:00 UTC on 2025-12-05 with repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses. Gateway pod intg-gw-worker-7b4d9 logged requests timing out after 30 seconds against endpoint https://api-internal.corpsync.io/v2/data-ingest. The last known successful full sync completed at 03:10 UTC on 2025-12-04 (job ID sync-nightly-20251204-0300). This is blocking scheduled data delivery for internal integrations relied upon by the Finance and Analytics teams. Reporter: Darren Whitfield (dwhitfield@corpmail.com), Integration Platform team. Available monitoring in Datadog shows elevated API Service latency during the job window, while retained logs do not show clear 401/403 authentication failures, leaving backend latency and API-side throttling as the primary investigated causes.
root_cause: Downstream API Service latency during the nightly processing window caused Integration Gateway requests to exceed the 30-second client timeout, resulting in repeated 504 timeouts and failed sync jobs. Token expiration was investigated but not supported by available evidence because retained logs showed no explicit authentication failures and the configured token was still present.
resolution_steps: Validated that the integration credential for service account svc-intg-sync was present in Vault configuration (secret/intg-gateway/api-token) and found no supporting evidence of token rejection or 401/403 authentication failures during the incident window in logs from pod intg-gw-worker-7b4d9.

Correlated the nightly job failure window (02:00–02:45 UTC) with Datadog APM monitoring data and confirmed a sharp increase in downstream API Service latency on api-svc-node-east-03, with p95 response time rising from ~200ms to ~6s — well above normal baseline — during the affected sync-nightly runs.

Applied a mitigation on the Integration Gateway job path (namespace intg-gateway-prod, pod intg-gw-worker-7b4d9) by increasing the request timeout from 30s to 90s and configuring exponential retry with backoff (max 3 retries, initial delay 5s) so long-running downstream API calls could complete instead of failing at the prior 30-second limit. Change applied by Priya Nair.

Restarted the affected Integration Gateway pod intg-gw-worker-7b4d9 from workstation WORKSTATION-DW-PC12 to clear transient connection state and reran a validation job (sync-validate-20251206-0015) after the timeout adjustment; validation completed successfully in 74 seconds.

Escalated the latency finding to the API Service owner Marcus Tan (mtan@corpmail.com, phone +1-555-839-2104) for backend performance investigation on api-svc-node-east-03 during the nightly batch window and documented the dependency on their service health for permanent correction. Escalation ticket INC-AIT-0028-ESC created and assigned to the Austin platform engineering team.
agent_questions: Hi Darren — please confirm whether any token rotation or deployment change occurred on the intg-gateway-prod namespace before 02:00 UTC, and share a sample failed request timestamp (e.g., from the pod logs on intg-gw-worker-7b4d9) so we can compare gateway errors with backend latency telemetry in Datadog. Also, can you verify whether the service account svc-intg-sync still has valid credentials in Vault? — Priya Nair, Integration Support

title: Outlook desktop and mobile stopped syncing while Exchange Online shows new mail
description: I (Marcus Reeves, emp ID EMP-40821) was trying to access current mailbox content from Outlook Desktop on my workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (IP 10.42.17.88) running Windows 10 and Outlook Mobile on my iPhone for my corporate Microsoft 365 account (mreeves@corplabs.com), but both clients stopped syncing around 08:30 while Exchange Online webmail (OWA) continued to show new messages. Outlook Desktop displayed a disconnected state and I could not reliably receive recent email in either client, impacting normal email access from our Austin office until client sync was restored.
observed_errors: Sync error 0x8004010F observed in client logs
root_cause: Stale Outlook desktop profile and corrupted local folder sync state prevented the desktop client from maintaining an active Exchange Online session; mobile synchronization was also affected by a stale device sync partnership that required reset.
resolution_steps: Verified new mail was present in Exchange Online through OWA for mreeves@corplabs.com to confirm mailbox delivery and isolate the issue to Outlook client synchronization on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR rather than a server-side mail flow outage.

Reviewed Outlook client behavior and sync evidence on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (IP 10.42.17.88), including the disconnected state and sync error 0x8004010F, which indicated local profile and cached folder state corruption for user mreeves.

Recreated the Outlook desktop mail profile for mreeves on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and cleared the local OST cache so the client could establish a fresh Exchange Online connection and rebuild mailbox data. Performed by ktran from desktop support.

Reset the mobile sync partnership for WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MR through Mobile Device Management and re-initiated account synchronization on the mobile client to remove stale device-side sync state for Marcus Reeves (EMP-40821).

Validated that Outlook desktop on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR reconnected successfully, recent messages populated on both desktop and mobile clients for mreeves@corplabs.com, and mail synchronization remained stable during post-fix monitoring. Marcus Reeves confirmed full functionality at 512-555-0147.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus Reeves, please confirm whether Outlook Desktop on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR still shows Disconnected after restart and whether OWA continues to show current mail for your mailbox mreeves@corplabs.com. We are checking whether this is a client profile issue versus a mailbox service problem. I've assigned this to our desktop support analyst, Kevin Tran (ktran), for further investigation.

title: stuck in MFA prompt loop during SSO sign-in (Okta) — resolved
description: I was trying to sign in to the corporate SSO Portal from my workstation (WORKSTATION-LP-MCHEN) to access Salesforce and Slack. After primary credentials were accepted for my account (mchen@corplabs.com), Okta repeatedly prompted for MFA and then rejected the verification instead of completing sign-in. The issue began after I reinstalled their authenticator app earlier that day, blocking access to SaaS applications from the web on Windows 10. My employee ID is E-40821 and I'm based out of the Raleigh office.
observed_errors: Repeated MFA challenge followed by authentication rejection
Okta: user authentication denied due to inconsistent MFA enrollment
root_cause: Stale and duplicate MFA enrollment records remained on the user's Okta account after the authenticator app reinstall, causing the identity provider to challenge against an inconsistent factor state and loop MFA instead of completing authentication.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the user's Okta audit history and factor enrollment state for mchen (employee ID E-40821) to confirm duplicate or stale authenticator entries were present after the app reinstall on 2026-04-02.
Removed the stale MFA enrollment records and duplicate authenticator device tokens from the user's Okta profile for mchen, including the orphaned factor registration dating back to 2025-11-18.
Reset the user's MFA enrollment so a clean factor registration could be performed, clearing all prior Okta Verify factor state for mchen.
Guided the user through re-enrolling the authenticator app against the corrected Okta account factor state, confirming a single active Okta Verify registration for Monica Chen on her mobile device.
Validated successful SSO sign-in from WORKSTATION-LP-MCHEN (10.22.47.115) and confirmed the user could access the SSO Portal, Salesforce, and Slack without further MFA looping.

title: Device shows Compliant in Intune but blocked by Conditional Access
description: I (Marcus Delgado, emp ID E-40291) on a managed Windows 11 22H2 corporate laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD) was blocked from accessing Exchange, SharePoint, and related Microsoft 365 resources by a Conditional Access policy requiring a compliant device. Intune and Company Portal showed the device as Compliant, but sign-in attempts from my account mdelgado@corplabs.com were intermittently denied with a device not compliant result, preventing normal corporate resource access. I'm based in the Charlotte office and need access restored urgently for ongoing sprint work.
observed_errors: Access denied by Conditional Access policy 'Require compliant device'
Intune portal shows 'Compliant' while access is denied
root_cause: A stale and mismatched device compliance state existed between Intune Device Compliance Service and Conditional Access token evaluation. The endpoint had a compliant state in Intune, but Conditional Access continued using older compliance attributes until device sync and token state were refreshed and cache propagation completed.
resolution_steps: Triggered a manual device check-in and compliance sync from Intune and Company Portal on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD so the latest device state for mdelgado was submitted to the compliance service.

Validated that WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD remained in the intended compliance policy scope ('Corp-Win11-Baseline' under Engineering group) and that no stale assignment or group targeting issue was present for employee E-40291.

Cleared the local sign-in/token cache by signing mdelgado out of the device and restarting WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD so Conditional Access would request a fresh device compliance evaluation on next authentication.
Reinstalled Company Portal on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD and re-ran policy evaluation to refresh device registration and local MDM compliance reporting components for mdelgado@corplabs.com.

Allowed Conditional Access cache propagation time (~12 minutes), then Marcus Delgado re-tested access to Exchange and SharePoint from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD at IP 10.42.17.88 and confirmed sign-in succeeded without the DeviceNotCompliant denial.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether Company Portal shows the device as Compliant at the same time sign-in to Exchange or SharePoint is blocked from your laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD, and whether the issue continues after a manual sync and reboot. Also, can you verify the IP address you're connecting from — is it your usual office connection at 10.42.17.88? This will help us rule out network-based Conditional Access restrictions. — Priya Nair, Service Desk

title: account locked after password reset attempt
description: I (Rachel Nguyen, emp ID EMP-40821) attempted to reset their corporate password through the Password Reset Portal, but the account remained locked and sign-in to the SSO Portal was not restored. I continued receiving authentication prompts on an iOS mobile device (hostname IPHONE-RNGUYEN-7), and repeated failed sign-in attempts from that device triggered Active Directory lockout behavior. This blocked normal account access after the password reset and prevented successful use of the new credential. My workstation is normally based out of the Charlotte office, but I'm traveling and connecting from IP 10.47.83.112.
observed_errors: Account locked due to AD lockout (EventID 4740)
Password reset token shows as used but login fails
Multiple failed authentication attempts from mobile client IP
root_cause: Active Directory lockout policy was repeatedly triggered by stale cached credentials on the user's mobile device. Although the password reset token was consumed successfully, the mobile client continued retrying the old password, causing ongoing failed authentications and preventing successful use of the updated credential until the account was unlocked and cached credentials were cleared.
resolution_steps: Unlock the user's Active Directory account (rnguyen, CN=rnguyen,OU=Corp Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) and reset the lockout counters on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal so authentication attempts can proceed normally. Identity Tier 2 agent Marcus Delaney performed the unlock at 16:12 UTC.

Remove or clear saved credentials on the user's mobile mail and collaboration apps, including deleting the affected corporate account from the device if cached authentication continues. Rachel Nguyen was guided over the phone at 704-555-0193 to remove the rnguyen account from Outlook and Teams on IPHONE-RNGUYEN-7, then re-add it after the unlock was confirmed.

Have the user sign in again with the newly reset password after credential cache removal, and verify successful authentication through the SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) before re-enabling mobile access. Rachel confirmed successful SSO login from IPHONE-RNGUYEN-7 at 16:25 UTC.

Issue a fresh password reset token only if the user cannot confirm the current password or if the original reset session is no longer trusted after repeated lockouts. In this case, rnguyen confirmed the reset password worked after unlock, so no new token was required.

Review recent authentication logs and device identifiers to confirm failed attempts stop after mobile credential cleanup; if retries persist, isolate and remediate the offending client or app configuration. Post-resolution monitoring of IP 10.47.83.112 and device IPHONE-RNGUYEN-7 showed zero failed attempts in the 30 minutes following credential re-enrollment, confirming the issue is fully resolved for Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821).

title: Internal hostname resolution failure - missing forwarder
description: Multiple internal users and application monitoring were trying to reach services by hostname under corp.internal, but internal names were returning NXDOMAIN from the primary resolver (DNS-RESOLVER-01.corp.internal, 10.40.2.10). The affected application, internal-service-app, could not make name-based connections to internal endpoints such as api-gateway.corp.internal and inventory-svc.corp.internal, creating a service interruption for users in the on-prem us-east-dc1 environment. The issue was initially reported by Maria Sandoval (emp ID E-40821) from the Arlington office via the Network Operations bridge call, and was corroborated by automated alerts from Network Monitoring at 22:44 UTC.
root_cause: Conditional forwarder for the internal zone corp.internal was missing on the primary and secondary DNS resolvers, causing queries to return NXDOMAIN and leaving stale negative cache entries for affected names.
resolution_steps: Added the missing conditional forwarder for the corp.internal zone on the primary DNS resolver (DNS-RESOLVER-01.corp.internal, 10.40.2.10) pointing to DNSAUTH-INT-01.corp.internal (10.40.1.5) and validated the target forwarding path with dig queries.
Applied the same conditional forwarder configuration to the secondary DNS resolver (DNS-RESOLVER-02.corp.internal, 10.40.2.11) to restore consistent zone routing and redundancy across both resolvers.

Flushed DNS cache on both resolvers (DNS-RESOLVER-01 and DNS-RESOLVER-02) to clear stale negative and outdated NXDOMAIN entries for the impacted hostnames including api-gateway.corp.internal and inventory-svc.corp.internal.

Retested name resolution for affected corp.internal service names from resolver-side queries and from affected client networks — verified from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MS (10.40.17.55, user msandoval) in the Arlington office and from the Network Monitoring probe in us-east-dc1.

Confirmed monitoring and the dependent application (internal-service-app) could again resolve internal hostnames successfully. Maria Sandoval (E-40821) and Kevin Truong (ktruong) verified end-user and network-side restoration respectively, then documented the DNS forwarding configuration change under CHG-20260111-DNS.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS failures
description: Users and internal services were trying to reach internal.web.internal over HTTPS, but browsers displayed certificate warnings and dependent API clients failed TLS handshakes. The load balancer (LB-PROD-F5-01) in front of the internal web service was presenting an expired certificate and outdated chain, which blocked normal access to the internal web service and caused downstream internal API failures in us-east-1. The issue was initially reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40291) from the Portland office, who noticed API integration tests failing at approximately 11:05 UTC. Additional reports came in from developers on the internal-developers Slack channel, including jparker and dmorales, confirming that both browser-based and programmatic access to internal.web.internal were affected.
platform: F5 Load Balancer / Linux web nodes
observed_errors: 502 bad gateway (due to TLS handshake failure at LB)
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal.web.internal expired on the load balancer, and the renewed leaf certificate plus intermediate chain had not been deployed, causing certificate validation failures and TLS handshake errors.
resolution_steps: Requested and obtained a renewed TLS certificate for internal.web.internal from the internal Certificate Authority (serial 8B:12:D4:F7, valid 2025-12-13 through 2026-12-13) before restoring service. The CSR was generated by rpatel and approved by the PKI team lead Sarah Lin (slin, EMP-60112).

Installed the renewed leaf certificate and full intermediate certificate chain on the production load balancer that terminates TLS for the internal web service. The certificate bundle was deployed to LB-PROD-F5-01 (10.200.1.15) by rpatel at 11:40 UTC, replacing the expired leaf (serial 4A:7C:3E:91) and outdated intermediate with the current chain from the internal CA vault.

Reloaded the load balancer TLS listener so the endpoint stopped presenting the expired certificate and began serving the updated chain. The reload was executed on LB-PROD-F5-01 at 11:42 UTC with zero dropped connections using the graceful reload procedure.

Validated the HTTPS endpoint from multiple internal client perspectives to confirm the certificate subject matched the service name and the handshake completed successfully. Verification was performed from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (10.42.17.88, user mchen) in the Portland office and from a test host in Austin (10.42.22.61, user jparker), both returning valid certificate chains with no warnings.

Re-enabled and tested certificate expiry monitoring and renewal alerting so future notifications trigger ahead of the renewal window. The alert rule for internal.web.internal was restored in the monitoring platform with 30-day and 7-day expiry thresholds, and test notifications were confirmed delivered to infra-certs@corplabs.com and the on-call channel.

title: Internal hostname resolution failing via internal DNS resolver
description: Internal services were trying to resolve service-internal.company.local through the primary internal DNS resolver at 10.10.0.5 (DNS-RESV-01.infra.company.local) in the Newark datacenter, but the resolver intermittently returned NXDOMAIN while direct queries to the authoritative internal DNS server at 10.10.0.12 (DNS-AUTH-01.infra.company.local) returned the correct A record (10.20.5.44). This was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, employee ID E-40821) from the platform engineering team after the internal-api-gateway on host APPGW-PROD-02 began logging connection failures to service-internal.company.local. The issue prevented internal APIs that rely on name-based routing from reaching the internal endpoint by hostname and caused inconsistent application connectivity across the on-premises environment, affecting multiple downstream consumers.
observed_errors: NXDOMAIN (negative response) returned by internal resolver
inconsistent resolution between resolver and authoritative server
root_cause: One internal DNS resolver was missing the required conditional forwarder for the internal zone, causing some queries for service-internal.company.local to be routed incorrectly. The resolver then cached the negative response, so it continued serving stale NXDOMAIN answers even though the authoritative internal DNS server had the correct A record.
resolution_steps: Added the missing conditional forwarder for the internal company.local zone on the affected resolver DNS-RESV-01 at 10.10.0.5, pointing to the authoritative server DNS-AUTH-01 at 10.10.0.12, so requests are consistently sent to the correct authoritative internal DNS path. Change performed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Flushed the DNS-RESV-01 resolver DNS cache via dnscmd /clearcache to remove the stale negative NXDOMAIN entry for service-internal.company.local and force fresh lookup results for the affected hostname.

Retested resolution for service-internal.company.local against both the affected resolver DNS-RESV-01 (10.10.0.5) and the authoritative internal DNS server DNS-AUTH-01 (10.10.0.12) to confirm the resolver now returns the expected A record 10.20.5.44. Verified from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.40.12.88) and APPGW-PROD-02.

Validated that dependent internal API traffic on internal-api-gateway (APPGW-PROD-02) using name-based routing could resolve and reach service-internal.company.local normally after the DNS change. Marcus Delgado confirmed application connectivity was restored.

Updated DNS monitoring in Network Monitoring and operational guidance to alert on NXDOMAIN spikes for internal zones (company.local) and to verify conditional forwarder consistency across all resolvers (DNS-RESV-01, DNS-RESV-02). Added a quarterly forwarder audit task assigned to the network infrastructure team.

title: Software Center installation blocked by Endpoint Protection
description: I (Rachel Nguyen, emp ID EMP-40821) on a managed Windows 10 21H2 corporate laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-RN) was trying to install the CorporateTime application from Software Center. The install was blocked immediately by Endpoint Protection with the message 'Installer blocked by Endpoint Protection - policy: BlockUntrustedInstall' and cited an unknown or unapproved publisher. After the block, the application did not remain available in the Software Center install flow and retries produced the same result. Intune still showed the device as compliant, so the impact was limited to application deployment being prevented by endpoint security policy rather than device management health. My device IP is 10.42.18.97 and I'm based out of the Charlotte office in the Finance department.
observed_errors: Installer blocked by Endpoint Protection - policy: BlockUntrustedInstall
root_cause: Endpoint Protection policy BlockUntrustedInstall blocked the CorporateTime installer because its publisher/signature was not present in the approved allowlist, so Software Center could not proceed with the installation workflow on the managed device.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the Endpoint Protection BlockUntrustedInstall policy and confirmed the CorporateTime installer (CorporateTime_Setup_v3.2.1.exe) was being denied on WORKSTATION-DELL-RN because its publisher/signature was not in the approved trust list for the Charlotte device scope.
Added the application's approved publisher/signature to the Endpoint Protection allowlist and saved the policy change for the Charlotte device scope, as approved by Marcus Delgado (security_team).
Republished the updated security policy and triggered a device policy refresh so the managed laptop WORKSTATION-DELL-RN (IP 10.42.18.97) received the new trust configuration.
Forced an Intune inventory and Software Center policy sync on WORKSTATION-DELL-RN for user rnguyen to refresh application targeting and client-side policy evaluation after the security policy change.

Retried the CorporateTime installation from Software Center on WORKSTATION-DELL-RN and verified the installer was no longer blocked and the application completed installation successfully. Confirmed with Rachel Nguyen (rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com) that the application launched without issues.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to Finance shared drive
description: I was trying to open the Finance department folder on the mapped network share \\FINANCE\Shared\Finance from my Windows 10 workstation (WORKSTATION-PC-RG, IP 10.22.14.87). The share repeatedly prompted for credentials and then returned "Access is denied," preventing access to department files on the SMB file server. My username is rgarcia and I'm based in the Charlotte office. Impact was limited to my access to the Finance folder while the shared drive itself remained available for other team members.
platform: On-premises Active Directory / SMB file server
root_cause: User account was missing membership in the approved Active Directory security group that grants access to the Finance shared drive, and the endpoint was still presenting stale cached credentials/token data for the mapped drive session.
resolution_steps: Verified that access to \\FINANCE\Shared\Finance is granted through the approved AD security group DEPT_Finance_Read and confirmed that user rgarcia (EMP-40821, Rosa Garcia, rosa.garcia@corplabs.com) was not currently a member of the group.
Added rgarcia to DEPT_Finance_Read in Active Directory to restore the required share and NTFS permission path for the Finance folder. Change approved by Finance team lead Marcus Webb (mwebb).

Forced directory/group membership synchronization on DC-EAST-02.corplabs.internal and refreshed the user's logon security context on WORKSTATION-PC-RG (klist purge followed by gpupdate /force) so the updated DEPT_Finance_Read group entitlement would be included in the Kerberos access token.

Cleared stored mapped drive credentials (cmdkey /delete:FINANCE) and stale connection data on the Windows 10 endpoint WORKSTATION-PC-RG (10.22.14.87), then reconnected the mapped drive (net use F: \\FINANCE\Shared\Finance /persistent:yes) to the current Finance share path.

Validated that rgarcia could open \\FINANCE\Shared\Finance without further credential prompts or access denied errors. Confirmed with Rosa Garcia via phone at (704) 555-3192 that all Finance subfolders were accessible.
agent_questions: Hi Rosa, please try opening the Finance folder directly with \\FINANCE\Shared\Finance from your workstation WORKSTATION-PC-RG and confirm whether you still receive a credential prompt followed by access denied. Also, could you confirm you're logged in as rgarcia@corplabs.internal?

title: BitLocker not enabling and recovery key not escrowed
description: User Rachel Nguyen (emp ID FIN-40821) on a corporate-managed Windows 10 Enterprise 21H2 laptop (hostname LAPTOP-RNGUY-FIN) reported that Company Portal showed the device as noncompliant for disk encryption and BitLocker remained in 'Protection Off' state. No recovery key was visible in Azure AD for the device, so it could not meet the Intune encryption compliance requirement. Rachel attempted a reboot and manual sync from Settings > Accounts > Access work or school, but encryption did not start and no key was escrowed. The device is assigned to the Arlington office and connects from IP 10.42.18.97.
observed_errors: Intune device shows no encryption profile assignment
MDM sync error observed during troubleshooting (0x80180026)
root_cause: BitLocker could not enable because the TPM protector was not initialized on the device, and the assigned Intune disk encryption policy was not applied to the endpoint. Without an active protector and policy application, encryption did not start and the recovery key was not escrowed to Azure AD.
resolution_steps: Validated local BitLocker status on LAPTOP-RNGUY-FIN via 'manage-bde -status C:' and confirmed the OS drive was in 'Protection Off' state (Fully Decrypted, 0% encrypted) with no usable TPM protector configured for user rnguyen.

Initialized TPM readiness on the endpoint using Initialize-Tpm and confirmed TpmReady: True, then added a TPM-based BitLocker protector for the system drive C: via Add-BitLockerKeyProtector -MountPoint C: -TpmProtector.

Enabled BitLocker on the C: drive using Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -TpmProtector -RecoveryPasswordProtector so initial encryption could begin using the TPM protector. Advised Rachel Nguyen (phone ext. 4782) to keep LAPTOP-RNGUY-FIN plugged in and powered on during the encryption process.

Forced an Intune device sync on LAPTOP-RNGUY-FIN via Company Portal and corrected policy targeting in Endpoint Manager by adding the device to the Finance encryption group, so the active 'CorpLabs - BitLocker Encryption' disk encryption profile was applied to the device. MDM sync error 0x80180026 did not recur after the resync.

Verified the recovery key successfully escrowed to Azure AD under the device record for rnguyen@corplabs.com and confirmed BitLocker protection status changed to 'On' with manage-bde -status C: showing Percentage Encrypted: 100%.

Confirmed the device LAPTOP-RNGUY-FIN returned to compliant status in Intune/Device Compliance Service after policy and encryption state updated. Notified Rachel Nguyen at rnguyen@corplabs.com and manager David Patel (dpatel@corplabs.com) that the compliance issue was resolved.

title: Outlook not syncing mail on desktop and mobile (Exchange Online)
description: I was trying to receive new email in Outlook on my Windows 10 desktop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MR) and on my iPhone, but mail stopped syncing this morning around 06:00 EST on both devices. The Outlook desktop client showed a disconnected state and the inbox had not updated since approximately 02:15 AM. I checked Microsoft 365 service health at https://admin.microsoft.com and it did not show a broader outage, so the impact appears limited to my mailbox (mreeves@corplabs.com). This has blocked normal email access and I'm unable to respond to client proposals from the Richmond office. My employee ID is E-40821 for reference.
observed_errors: Last sync time several hours ago
root_cause: Likely stale client sync state affecting both the Outlook desktop profile and the mobile Exchange partnership for the mailbox, with no evidence of a Microsoft 365 service-wide outage. Device compliance or throttling remained possible during initial triage, but the most probable cause was client-side sync state requiring profile and partnership refresh.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects shortly
description: Multiple corporate users on Windows 11 managed laptops in the Frankfurt office were trying to connect to the corporate network with GlobalProtect VPN (v5.2.4). After approving the Okta MFA push notification, the VPN tunnel connected briefly and then disconnected within 20-40 seconds, leaving internal web apps (including the HR portal at https://hrportal.corplabs.internal), Intranet sites, and SMB file shares (\\fs-emea-01.corplabs.internal\shared) unreachable. The issue was first reported by Elena Vasquez (emp ID: E-40291) and subsequently confirmed by several other EMEA Corporate group members. The issue began immediately after the overnight device certificate maintenance window (2026-04-11 23:00–02:00 UTC) and was traced to expired endpoint device certificates used during post-authentication TLS validation on the GlobalProtect gateway gw-emea-02.corplabs.internal.
root_cause: Expired device certificates on affected corporate endpoints caused GlobalProtect post-authentication TLS handshake validation to fail, so the VPN session was established after Okta MFA but terminated shortly afterward.
resolution_steps: Renew the expired device certificate for each affected endpoint through the Device Certificate Service re-enrollment portal (https://certservice.corplabs.internal/renew). For the initial affected users evasquez and mhahn, certificates were renewed individually; a bulk renewal job was initiated by Priya Nair (E-31087) for remaining EMEA Corporate endpoints.

Refresh or re-push the GlobalProtect VPN profile on the endpoint so the client uses the renewed certificate and current certificate mapping. On WORKSTATION-DELL-EV and WORKSTATION-HP-MH this was done via the GlobalProtect agent settings panel under Certificate Configuration.

Restart the GlobalProtect client and reconnect to the VPN gateway (gw-emea-02.corplabs.internal) to force a new authentication and tunnel establishment sequence. Confirm the Okta MFA push completes and the tunnel remains stable beyond the previous 20-40 second failure window.

Verify the endpoint remains in the correct Corporate conditional access or certificate-mapped group in the Device Certificate Service console and confirm the renewed certificate is valid (new expiry 2027-04-12) and not expired. For user evasquez, confirmed group membership under OU=Corp Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal.

Confirm in gateway (gw-emea-02.corplabs.internal) and client logs that TLS handshake errors and disconnect event code 0x7A no longer occur. Validate sustained VPN connectivity for at least 30 minutes and verify access to internal applications (HR portal, intranet web apps) and SMB file shares. Final validation performed by Priya Nair and confirmed with affected users Elena Vasquez and Marcus Hahn.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to shared drive (mapped drive prompts for credentials) - resolved
description: I was trying to open the department shared folder at \\fileserver\Dept from a mapped network drive on my Windows 10 domain-joined device (WORKSTATION-HR-MREEVES). NTFS ACL review also showed historical deny entries, but because access was restored without an ACL change, those entries are treated as contributing conflicting evidence rather than the immediate cause of this incident.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the user's access path, confirmed the issue affected \\fileserver\Dept, and verified the user mreeves (Monica Reeves, EMP-40821) was already a member of the expected AD access group HR-Dept-Share-Access.

Checked the mapped drive and stored Windows Credentials on WORKSTATION-HR-MREEVES (IP 10.42.18.77), identifying cached credentials that were likely stale following the user's password change earlier that day.
Removed the stored credential for the shared drive target \\fileserver\Dept from Windows Credential Manager on WORKSTATION-HR-MREEVES to force fresh authentication for mreeves.
Deleted and recreated the mapped network drive using the current path \\fileserver\Dept so the session would establish with updated credentials for user mreeves.
Validated that the user Monica Reeves could open the shared folder \\fileserver\Dept successfully after remapping and no longer received repeated credential prompts on WORKSTATION-HR-MREEVES.

Documented the presence of historical NTFS deny ACL evidence and recommended follow-up review of folder inheritance and deny entries by the file server owners; notified mreeves@corplabs.com and agent Derek Langston of closure.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Nightly order sync jobs in the Order Sync Application were unable to complete because calls from the Integration Gateway (gateway-prod-ordersync.corplabs.internal) to the downstream partner API (partner-api.logisticshub.com) repeatedly timed out and returned 504 responses. The gateway logs on pod igw-ordersync-7b4d also showed authentication failures with "invalid_token," indicating the partner credential provisioned under service account svc-ordersync had expired. Retries were exhausted after 12 consecutive failures, causing approximately 4.5 hours of delayed downstream order data for the OrderProcessing group in us-east-1. Issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Atlanta fulfillment operations team.
root_cause: Expired downstream partner API token in the Integration Gateway credential configuration caused authentication failures, which manifested as repeated 504 timeout responses during nightly order sync retries until the job exhausted its retry limit.
resolution_steps: Validated from gateway logs on igw-ordersync-7b4d and failed sync attempts (ordersync-20251207-0100 through ordersync-20251207-0512) that partner API calls to partner-api.logisticshub.com were returning authentication-related errors including "invalid_token" alongside repeated 504 timeout failures. Reviewed by Kevin Marsh (kmarsh, EMP-90214) and confirmed with Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) from the Atlanta operations team.

Coordinated with the partner team via Priya Nair (pnair, EMP-78503) to rotate the expired API token for service account svc-ordersync and obtain a new valid credential (SHA256 fingerprint verified) for the downstream API integration with partner-api.logisticshub.com.

Updated the stored partner API credential for svc-ordersync in the Integration Gateway credential vault and restarted the gateway pods (igw-ordersync-7b4d, igw-ordersync-7b4e) on k8s-cluster-42 so new authenticated sessions were established against partner-api.logisticshub.com. Restart performed from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KM at 10.200.4.31.

Adjusted the integration retry policy for the Order Sync Application to use exponential backoff (initial 5s, max 120s, jitter enabled) and reduce immediate retry storms when downstream authentication or timeout conditions occur. Configuration change committed by kmarsh and reviewed by pnair.

Ran validation checks on the next scheduled sync (ordersync-20251207-2200) and confirmed subsequent nightly sync executions completed successfully with 200 OK responses from partner-api.logisticshub.com, then monitored backlog processing via the Monitoring System dashboard until all 1,247 delayed order records were cleared by 2025-12-08T02:15Z.
agent_questions: Reviewing the failed nightly syncs now — I can see the job history for svc-ordersync on k8s-cluster-42. Can you confirm whether the gateway logs on igw-ordersync-7b4d show authentication-related messages, especially any token or credential errors tied to the partner-api.logisticshub.com endpoint, in addition to the 504 timeouts? Also tagging Priya Nair from the integration platform team for visibility. — Agent: Kevin Marsh (kmarsh, EMP-90214)

title: Multiple users cannot join Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple employees across two floors in the US-East HQ could not join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID using the managed 802.1X/EAP-TLS wireless profile on Windows laptops and macOS devices. Affected users include Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) from Engineering and Derek Kowalski (EMP-51093) from Sales, among others. observed_errors: NAC access denied: EAP-TLS certificate validation failed
root_cause: Expired EAP-TLS server certificate on the wireless authentication path caused client trust validation failures during 802.1X authentication, and NAC subsequently denied access for affected sessions.
resolution_steps: Renew the expired EAP-TLS server certificate (expired 2026-05-05T23:59:00Z) from the internal CA and deploy the updated certificate and full trust chain to the RADIUS servers handling Corporate Wi-Fi authentication. Certificate renewal coordinated by Nathan Williams (nwilliams@corplabs.com).

Update the Wireless Controller certificate bundle to reference the renewed authentication certificate chain and restart or reload authentication services as required for the new certificate to become active. Validated by nwilliams after reload.

Validate NAC policy behavior after certificate deployment by confirming EAP-TLS sessions are accepted and correctly mapped to the intended access policy and VLAN assignment. Initial validation performed using rnguyen's device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN.

Re-test managed Windows and macOS clients against the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID, and where devices cached the prior failed state, have users forget and reconnect to the SSID or re-enroll the corporate wireless profile. Confirmed successful reconnection for Rachel Nguyen (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) and Derek Kowalski (WORKSTATION-MACBOOK-DK).

Monitor WLC, RADIUS, and NAC authentication logs for at least 24 hours to confirm certificate-related failures have ceased and that affected users including rnguyen and dkowalski can consistently authenticate successfully. Monitoring ownership assigned to Nathan Williams.

title: Intermittent internal name resolution failure for svc-db.internal
description: Users and monitoring systems in the Charlotte office were trying to resolve the internal service hostname svc-db.internal, but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN from some internal resolvers (notably dns-resolver-02.corp.internal at 10.12.4.12) while other resolvers returned the expected A record (10.50.20.35). The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40821) from the internal-devops team after a DNS zone update earlier the same day performed by network engineer Priya Nair. The failure impacted workstation access and monitoring consistency for the svc-db internal service across internal subnets in the us-east-1-internal environment.
observed_errors: Inconsistent A record answers between resolver-01 and resolver-02
root_cause: Inconsistent internal DNS state after the zone update: resolver-02 continued serving stale negative cache or outdated zone data for svc-db.internal while resolver-01 had refreshed, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN responses depending on which resolver answered the query.
resolution_steps: Verified the svc-db.internal A record (10.50.20.35), zone contents, and current SOA serial (2026011502) in the Internal DNS Zone to confirm the record existed and the post-change data committed by pnair was correct.

Compared lookup results across dns-resolver-01.corp.internal (10.12.4.11) and dns-resolver-02.corp.internal (10.12.4.12) and confirmed resolver-02 was the source of intermittent NXDOMAIN responses while resolver-01 returned the expected record 10.50.20.35 for svc-db.internal.

Flushed stale cache on the affected internal resolver dns-resolver-02.corp.internal (10.12.4.12) and reloaded the updated zone data so both resolvers served the same current answer (10.50.20.35) for svc-db.internal. Priya Nair confirmed the zone transfer completed successfully after the reload.

Reviewed resolver configuration for the internal zone on dns-resolver-02.corp.internal, including conditional forwarding and zone refresh behavior, to ensure resolver-02 was using the correct authoritative data path after the zone change. Corrected the forwarder target to point to the primary zone host rather than the lagging secondary.

Re-ran validation queries from affected internal paths — including Marcus Delgado's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.12.6.88) and Lisa Hwang's machine — and confirmed consistent successful resolution of svc-db.internal (10.50.20.35) across resolvers and Network Monitoring checks. Notified mdelgado@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm which resolver IP your workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD is using (we expect either 10.12.4.11 or 10.12.4.12) and whether the same lookup fails from other internal subnets so we can isolate whether the issue is client-specific or resolver-specific. You can run nslookup svc-db.internal from your machine and share the output. Also, can you confirm if colleagues on the same VLAN are seeing the same behavior?

title: Internal DNS resolver serving stale A record causing hostname resolution failures
description: Internal users in the Portland office and the finance-api application (running on host FINAPI-PROD-01) were trying to reach internal-service.corp.local, but name resolution intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or an outdated IP (10.10.5.21) while direct access by the current IP 10.10.8.33 still worked. The issue was first reported by developer Marcus Jennings (mjennings, emp ID EMP-40821) and affected automated CI/CD jobs as well as interactive API access after a DNS zone update performed on 2026-01-12. Symptoms indicated inconsistent data between the authoritative zone on ns1.corp.local and the internal resolver cache on dns-resolver-west.corp.local.
root_cause: Internal DNS resolvers retained stale cached data for internal-service.corp.local after the zone record changed, causing intermittent responses with an old A record or lookup failures until caches were refreshed.
resolution_steps: Corrected the A record for internal-service.corp.local in the internal authoritative DNS zone on ns1.corp.local to 10.10.8.33 and incremented the zone serial to 2026011201 so downstream resolvers could detect the update. Change performed by Priya Nair (pnair) and verified via zone transfer to ns2.corp.local.

Reloaded the authoritative nameserver ns1.corp.local using rndc reload corp.local and verified the authoritative response returned the expected current A record 10.10.8.33 and updated zone serial 2026011201 from multiple query sources.

Flushed cached entries on the primary internal resolvers dns-resolver-west.corp.local and dns-resolver-west-02.corp.local using rndc flush and restarted named resolver services where cache state did not clear cleanly. Performed by Rachel Dominguez (rdominguez) with confirmation from Network Monitoring dashboards.

Cleared local stub resolver caches on affected application hosts (FINAPI-PROD-01, build runner at 10.22.4.102) and test client workstations WORKSTATION-DEV-MJ and WORKSTATION-QA-TR using systemd-resolve --flush-caches to remove stale hostname data held outside the central DNS resolvers.

Validated resolution from affected paths with repeat lookups (50 iterations) against both resolver and authoritative sources from hosts in Portland and Seattle, then confirmed finance-api application smoke tests passed with HTTP 200 responses. Monitored DNS query alerts in Network Monitoring for 24 hours with no recurrence. Final sign-off by Marcus Jennings (mjennings) and Tomás Reyes (treyes).
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please compare name resolution for internal-service.corp.local using the normal internal resolver (dns-resolver-west.corp.local, 10.10.1.5) versus a direct query to the authoritative DNS server ns1.corp.local and confirm whether access by IP 10.10.8.33 still works. You can run: dig @10.10.1.5 internal-service.corp.local A and dig @ns1.corp.local internal-service.corp.local A from your workstation WORKSTATION-DEV-MJ. Also, could you share the output from any affected hosts? CC'ing Priya Nair (pnair) from the network team for visibility.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: Multiple users on managed Windows 10 21H2 laptops in the Frankfurt office were trying to connect to the corporate network through GlobalProtect while working remotely. Specifically, users including Rachel Whitmore (EMP-40218) and Darren Okafor (EMP-40225) from the Sales and Marketing group reported that after approving the Okta MFA prompt, the VPN tunnel established briefly for about 10-20 seconds and then disconnected, which prevented access to internal applications including the intranet, Confluence, and Salesforce during the short connected window. The issue was reproducible across several login attempts on devices such as WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RW (10.47.12.88) and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-DO (10.47.12.91), and aligned with certificate validation failures in the VPN client logs. Ticket submitted by rwhitmore@corplabs.com.
observed_errors: Tunnel dropped immediately after Okta approval (no user action)
Certificate validation failure logged for device cert
root_cause: Expired device certificate on affected endpoints caused GlobalProtect certificate validation to fail after successful Okta MFA, which triggered immediate post-authentication tunnel termination.
resolution_steps: Validated that Okta MFA completed successfully for rwhitmore and dokafor and confirmed the VPN disconnect occurred after authentication during the post-auth certificate validation stage on endpoints WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RW and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-DO.

Renewed the expired device certificate on affected endpoints WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RW and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-DO through the Device Certificate Service and confirmed the new certificate (valid through 2027-04-11) was present in the local endpoint certificate store for both machines.

Refreshed and re-enrolled the GlobalProtect VPN profile on both endpoints so the client used the current device certificate and active enrollment configuration. Profile re-enrollment performed remotely by desktop support technician Priya Nair.

Retested VPN connectivity on affected devices for users rwhitmore and dokafor to verify the tunnel remained established and internal applications (intranet, Confluence, Salesforce) were reachable without immediate disconnects. title: Expired TLS certificate and incomplete load balancer chain update caused internal TLS
description: Internal users across the Chicago office were trying to access the Internal Web Service (https://internal-ws.corplabs.com) and dependent Service API over TLS, but browsers showed certificate warnings and integrations failed validation with CERT_HAS_EXPIRED, ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR, and certificate verify failed. root_cause: The service certificate was renewed at the Certificate Authority, but the full renewed certificate chain was not correctly applied on the F5 load balancer. As a result, the load balancer continued serving the old expired chain to clients even though application-side renewal activity had been performed.
resolution_steps: Retrieved the renewed server certificate and complete intermediate chain from the internal Certificate Authority and verified the certificate matched the Internal Web Service endpoint naming requirements (CN=internal-ws.corplabs.com, SAN: internal-ws.corplabs.com). Verification performed by Tomás Reyes.

Uploaded the renewed certificate bundle to the F5 load balancer (lb-east-01.corplabs.internal) and explicitly updated the virtual server configuration to use the new full chain instead of the previously served expired chain, correcting the gap left by the earlier incomplete deployment.

Applied the load balancer configuration and reloaded the LB service on lb-east-01.corplabs.internal so the updated certificate chain was actively presented to clients in the Chicago office and all us-east-1 internal-services users.

Validated the served certificate chain from client and load balancer perspectives — confirmed from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK (10.42.17.89) and additional test hosts that the expired certificate was no longer presented and TLS handshakes completed successfully for the Internal Web Service and Service API. Maria Koduya (koduya) confirmed normal access restored.

Restored certificate monitoring and added load balancer chain verification plus deployment evidence requirements (including post-deployment client-side validation step) to the certificate rotation process to prevent recurrence. Alert subscription updated for pnandakumar@corplabs.com and treyes@corplabs.com.

title: Print jobs stuck on Print Server
description: Multiple users on the 3rd floor of the Arlington office were trying to print to the shared HP-LASERJ4100 queue on print-server-1 after a recent printer driver push (CR-2026-0287). Jobs submitted by staff including Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez, EMP-40821) and others remained queued for more than an hour, and the shared printer showed Offline or Driver unavailable, preventing normal office printing for approximately 40 users. Initial spooler restarts and manual queue clearing performed by technician David Kowalski did not resolve the issue, suggesting a server-side driver problem introduced by the recent change.
root_cause: A corrupted or mismatched HP-LaserJet 4100 driver package was installed on print-server-1 during the recent driver update, causing the Windows Print Spooler to throw service error 2147500037 and preventing queued jobs from processing.
resolution_steps: Removed the invalid HP-LaserJet 4100 driver package (v6.3.1) reference and reinstalled the approved driver package (v6.3.2, SHA256: 9d2f8a…e617c4) from the Workplace Services driver repository on print-server-1. Remediation performed by technician David Kowalski (dkowalski).
Validated the replacement driver package against the approved checksum (SHA256: 9d2f8a…e617c4) to confirm the installed driver matched the sanctioned bundle in the Workplace Services repository.

Cleared all 37 stalled jobs from the HP-LASERJ4100 print queue so corrupted jobs would not continue blocking spooler processing. Notified affected users including mgonzalez and rpatel to resubmit their print jobs.

Restarted the Windows Print Spooler service on print-server-1 and monitored Event Viewer for 15 minutes to confirm the service remained stable without repeating the prior spooler error 2147500037 condition.

Remapped the HP-LASERJ4100 shared queue to the corrected v6.3.2 driver configuration and completed successful print tests from three user workstations: WORKSTATION-PC-MG (mgonzalez, 10.42.16.88), WORKSTATION-PC-RP (rpatel, 10.42.16.91), and WORKSTATION-PC-LT (lthomas, 10.42.16.95). Flagged CR-2026-0287 for post-incident review with change owner jnelson.
