title: Intermittent DNS resolution for svc-auth.example.local
description: Multiple internal services were trying to reach the internal authentication endpoint svc-auth.example.local, but DNS responses became inconsistent for approximately 3 hours following a scheduled A record update performed by jmorales on 2026-01-12. Affected clients on the 10.40.16.0/24 subnet reported that some lookups returned NXDOMAIN while others returned the decommissioned IP 10.40.2.17, causing intermittent application failures across the Arlington data center and preventing dependent services from reliably reaching the auth service by name. The issue was initially reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) from the platform engineering team after observing authentication timeouts on her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN.
observed_errors: Intermittent NXDOMAIN responses from internal resolvers
Stale A record returned (old IP) by secondary resolver
dig +short returns mixed IPs depending on resolver queried
root_cause: Stale cached DNS data and incorrect conditional forwarding behavior on the secondary internal resolver caused inconsistent answers for svc-auth.example.local after the A record change, with some queries returning the retired IP and others returning NXDOMAIN instead of the current authoritative record.
resolution_steps: Verified the authoritative A record for svc-auth.example.local in the internal zone on DNS-AUTH-EAST-01.corp.example.local and confirmed the intended current IP 10.40.5.34 and reduced TTL of 300s were published correctly (SOA serial 2026011301, change applied by jmorales).

Identified the secondary resolver DNS-SEC-EAST-02.corp.example.local as the source of inconsistent answers and cleared its stale cache entries for the affected zone and hostname using rndc flush, removing the cached 10.40.2.17 record with the outdated 7200s TTL.

Corrected secondary resolver DNS-SEC-EAST-02.corp.example.local forwarding/zone handling so queries for the corp.example.local internal zone consistently followed the authoritative path via DNS-AUTH-EAST-01.corp.example.local instead of serving stale or negative cached responses.

Restarted DNS services (named) on the affected resolvers DNS-PRI-EAST-01.corp.example.local and DNS-SEC-EAST-02.corp.example.local to ensure fresh cache state and active configuration alignment across primary and secondary infrastructure in the Arlington data center.

Re-ran resolver probes from WORKSTATION-PC-DM (10.40.16.55) and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (10.40.16.102) against primary and secondary resolvers and confirmed both returned the same current address 10.40.5.34 with no further NXDOMAIN or old-IP responses. Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) confirmed auth service connectivity restored.

title: Device marked noncompliant
description: I was trying to access Microsoft 365 resources from my corporate Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-DELL-MR) this morning around 02:15 UTC, but Conditional Access blocked sign-in for my account m.reeves@corplabs.com because Intune marked the device as noncompliant. In the Intune portal, the device (enrolled under employee ID EMP-40821) had not checked in for 36 hours and the compliance failure was tied to the encryption requirement showing as Not Encrypted, even though BitLocker appeared enabled locally after a recent motherboard swap performed by our Charlotte hardware team. Impact was complete loss of access to M365 apps (Outlook, Teams, SharePoint) until device compliance reporting was restored. My manager, Denise Kowalski, flagged this as urgent since I have client demos scheduled today.
root_cause: Intune did not receive a valid BitLocker encryption compliance signal after a recent hardware swap, leaving the device on a stale check-in state and incorrectly evaluating the Windows endpoint as not encrypted; Conditional Access then blocked Microsoft 365 access based on the noncompliant status.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the device WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (enrolled to mreeves, IP 10.42.17.88) was affected by a stale Intune compliance state by reviewing the 36-hour check-in gap and the failed encryption compliance signal (encryption_status_not_reported / 0x87D1041C) in the device record.

Triggered a remote Intune device sync from the MEM admin center for WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and had Marcus Reeves run a targeted Company Portal sync locally to force fresh MDM compliance evaluation from the endpoint. Sync completed successfully at 03:04 UTC.

Verified locally that BitLocker protection was enabled on the OS drive (C:, AES-256) and re-applied the recovery key information via manage-bde so Windows management reporting and TPM-backed encryption status were correctly exposed to the new motherboard's TPM 2.0 chip.

Re-ran compliance evaluation in Intune for WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and monitored the device record until the encryption state updated from Not Encrypted to Compliant (encrypted) at 03:18 UTC and the overall device status returned to Compliant, restoring Conditional Access pass-through for m.reeves@corplabs.com.

Applied a temporary scoped Conditional Access exception (policy: 'CA-Temp-Bypass-MReeves') only during remediation to restore limited user productivity for mreeves on Microsoft 365 web apps, then removed the exception after Intune compliance was confirmed at 03:22 UTC. Notified manager Denise Kowalski that access was fully restored.

Also, can you verify the last time you successfully synced through Company Portal? I can see the device is enrolled under your account m.reeves@corplabs.com in the Sales_Laptops group.

resolution_steps: Validated the connection state across desktop (WORKSTATION-MREEVES) and mobile (IPHONE-MREEVES) clients for mailbox mreeves@corplabs.com to separate the desktop profile issue from the continuing mobile sync failure.
Rebuilt the desktop Outlook profile on WORKSTATION-MREEVES for user mreeves and confirmed desktop mailbox synchronization resumed normally with full folder hierarchy and inbox updates.

Cleared the mobile ActiveSync partnership for IPHONE-MREEVES in Exchange Online admin center and re-paired the iOS device to rule out a stale device association or compliance issue. MDM confirmed device compliance throughout.

title: Expired TLS certificate on load balancer causing internal web service TLS failures
description: Internal users were trying to reach https://internal.service.example.com, but the browser displayed certificate warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and TLS handshakes failed, making the internal web service unavailable over HTTPS. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office and quickly confirmed by several other developers on the internal_developers group. The affected HAProxy load balancer lb-internal-01 in us-east-1 was serving an expired certificate and stale intermediate chain, blocking normal access to the service until the expired certificate and certificate chain on the load balancer were corrected. Ticket opened on behalf of the team by infrastructure lead Priya Nair (EMP-40821).
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal.service.example.com expired on 2025-12-24, the load balancer continued presenting a stale certificate chain, and certificate renewal monitoring did not alert before expiration.
resolution_steps: Obtain a renewed TLS certificate for internal.service.example.com from the internal Certificate Authority (CorpLabs Internal Root CA) and confirm the SANs match the service hostname. Renewal request submitted by Raj Patel (rpatel, EMP-55934) and new certificate issued with serial 7B:22:A1:F0:9C, valid through 2026-12-24.

Deploy the renewed server certificate and the complete current CA chain to the HAProxy load balancer lb-internal-01 at /etc/haproxy/certs/internal.service.example.com.pem, replacing the expired certificate bundle (serial 4A:3F:C8:91:DE) and stale intermediate chain. Deployment performed by Raj Patel from bastion host 10.42.0.5.

Update the HAProxy TLS configuration (/etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg) on lb-internal-01 to reference the new certificate bundle and reload the proxy service (systemctl reload haproxy) so new client handshakes present the updated certificate and chain. Configuration change verified by rpatel.

Validate the endpoint from internal client and load balancer perspectives to confirm the certificate is no longer expired, the full chain is served, and browser/TLS warnings are cleared. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.42.17.88) and Lena Kowalski (lkowalski) from WORKSTATION-LT-LK (10.42.18.34) both confirmed successful HTTPS access with no certificate warnings.

Restore and test certificate expiry monitoring and renewal alerting in the Certificate Management Service so future renewals trigger before the next expiration window. Alert rule re-created for internal.service.example.com with 30-day and 7-day pre-expiry notifications to infra-alerts@corplabs.com. Monitoring configuration reviewed and signed off by Priya Nair (pnair, EMP-40821).

title: Intermittent disconnects from Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple Sales users on Windows 10 laptops in the Portland office were trying to connect to the Corporate Wi-Fi (SSID: CorpNet-Secure), but devices intermittently disconnected and then failed to complete 802.1X reauthentication after a certificate rotation on the wireless environment. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40218) and subsequently confirmed by at least six other Sales team members. Affected laptops could join the SSID but were rejected by NAC or received no IP address, leaving users without network access for normal work. The issue began around 06:15 PDT after the controller certificate change on WLC-WEST-01; renewing the controller certificate restored service for some devices, but others still required endpoint profile remediation and policy validation. Ticket escalated by team lead Marcus Dellinger.
observed_errors: No IP address assigned after join
root_cause: Wireless controller certificate rotation restored only part of the 802.1X trust chain; several endpoints still had stale corporate Wi-Fi profiles or certificate bindings, and NAC policy evaluation continued rejecting some Sales devices until profiles were re-enrolled and policy alignment was corrected.
resolution_steps: Renewed and validated the wireless controller certificate on WLC-WEST-01 so the 802.1X authentication service presented the correct server certificate chain to all connecting Sales endpoints in the Portland office.

Reviewed NAC authentication results for affected Sales devices (rnguyen, kmarsh, tokafor, and others) and confirmed policy rejections were tied to stale endpoint wireless profile or certificate state after the certificate change. Pedro Garcia (pgarcia) from the network team verified the NAC audit logs.

Re-enrolled the corporate Wi-Fi profile on impacted laptops — including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KM — to refresh the SSID configuration, trust settings, and device certificate association used for 802.1X authentication. Users rnguyen, kmarsh, and tokafor confirmed reconnection.

Confirmed affected devices could authenticate successfully, receive the expected network access policy, and obtain IP addressing (verified 10.42.17.x range) after rejoining Corporate Wi-Fi. Rachel Nguyen and Kevin Marsh both validated stable connectivity over a 30-minute observation window.

Prepared and scheduled an MDM push of the updated wireless profile targeting all Sales laptops in the Portland region, and coordinated follow-up NAC policy cleanup with Pedro Garcia (pgarcia) so temporary exceptions can be removed without reintroducing authentication failures. Follow-up review scheduled for 2026-04-27.
agent_questions: We confirmed the controller certificate on WLC-WEST-01 was renewed, but some devices are still failing 802.1X. Rachel Nguyen's laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN, IP 10.42.17.83) and several others in the Portland Sales group are affected. Please confirm whether affected laptops can join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) and whether they show no internet or no IP after connecting. You can reach me at ext. 4417 or pgarcia@corplabs.com if you need to discuss further.

title: Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service behind Load Balancer
description: Users in the Arlington office were trying to reach the Internal Web Service (svc-internal.corplabs.internal) over HTTPS through the F5 load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.corplabs.internal), but browsers and internal integrations continued to reject the connection with NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and TLS trust failures. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40821) at 08:32 UTC via the #infra-alerts Slack channel. The service remained intermittently inaccessible after a recent renewal effort, with reports indicating the issue was affecting internal clients in us-east-1 during normal application access. Additional reports came from jparker and dtran, who confirmed the same behavior from their workstations WORKSTATION-MC-4082 and WORKSTATION-DT-7761 respectively.
observed_errors: certificate expired presented by load balancer
root_cause: The F5 load balancer served a certificate bundle containing an expired intermediate certificate even though the endpoint certificate itself had been renewed successfully. Monitoring and deployment evidence were insufficient to confirm when the active LB chain diverged from the intended full bundle.
resolution_steps: Rebuild the full certificate bundle with the renewed server certificate (CN=svc-internal.corplabs.internal, serial 0A:3F:7B:22) and the correct current intermediate chain (DigiCert SHA2 Secure Server CA, valid through 2031-11-09) from the issuing CA. Bundle assembled by nwong and verified with openssl verify -CAfile.

Explicitly bind the corrected chain bundle (intermediate-digicert-2026.crt) to the F5 virtual server vs-svc-internal-443 via SSL profile ssl-svc-internal and remove the stale intermediate object intermediate-digicert-2024.crt and any legacy chain references from lb-prod-east-01.corplabs.internal. Configuration change approved by Robert Fielding (rfielding).

Validate trust from multiple client paths (tested from 10.42.18.97 in Arlington and 10.55.6.203 in Denver) and directly from the F5 configuration (tmsh show sys crypto cert-chain) to confirm no expired intermediate is presented. Maria Chen (mchen) and jparker confirmed HTTPS access restored without warnings from WORKSTATION-MC-4082 and WORKSTATION-DT-7761.

Add chain-level monitoring for the LB-served path on lb-prod-east-01 in the cert-monitor dashboard, covering both leaf and intermediate expiry for svc-internal, and require post-deployment evidence capture (automated openssl chain validation) for the active certificate bundle after every renewal job. Monitoring rule created by dtran (E-60215) and assigned to the Arlington infrastructure team.
agent_questions: Please confirm whether clients are failing on certificate expiry only or also reporting chain trust issues from the load balancer endpoint for svc-internal.corplabs.internal. Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) reported both browser warnings and API integration failures from host 10.42.18.97. Can the network team (cc: Robert Fielding, rfielding@corplabs.com) verify the full chain presented by lb-prod-east-01 on the svc-internal virtual server?

title: Laptop performance degradation
description: My Windows 10 21H2 laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, asset tag EP-NA-20481) became very slow immediately after login following overnight updates on 2026-02-06. observed_errors: High CPU usage by MsMpEng.exe after login (~80-90%)

Refresh endpoint management policy on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR via the Endpoint Management console and confirm the revised Defender scan schedule (12:00-14:00 window) and performance settings (ScanAvgCPULoadFactor=30) are applied successfully. Verified by agent Priya Nair (pnair).

Validate after policy refresh and backlog removal that MsMpEng.exe CPU usage on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR returns to normal baseline (<5%) after login and that Outlook and Chrome launch within normal time (<3 seconds) for user mreeves. Confirmed by Raj Kulkarni (rkulkarni) during follow-up remote session.

Provide Marcus Reeves with a temporary pause-scan workaround (Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true) only until the backlog is cleared, and then re-enable normal real-time protection once CPU utilization stabilizes below 10%. Contact support at (469) 555-3184 or mreeves@corplabs.com if symptoms recur.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing PaymentSync failures
description: PaymentSync backfill and scheduled synchronization jobs intermittently failed between 02:10 and 02:40 UTC on 2025-12-08 when the Integration Gateway (gateway-prod-east-07.payments.internal) timed out while calling the downstream payment API endpoint at https://api.payments.internal/v2/sync. This caused queued sync work on the paymentsync-worker pods in the us-east-1 Kubernetes cluster, delayed payment data updates for Finance Users, and repeated 504 timeout responses logged by the gateway. The issue was initially reported by Rajesh Menon (rmenon@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office after the PaymentSyncApp dashboard showed stalled jobs. Immediate recovery was observed after token rotation by ops engineer Lisa Cheng, but available validation evidence did not show token expiry, so the incident is best explained as downstream latency with token rotation treated as a coincidental or non-causal mitigation.
root_cause: Intermittent downstream payment API latency exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout window, causing 504 responses and PaymentSync job failures; token rotation coincided with recovery but was not supported as the primary cause by token validation evidence.
resolution_steps: Validated that the integration token for service account svc-paymentsync was still accepted by existing API Service token checks and recorded that the token rotation performed by Lisa Cheng (EMP-90274) did not have supporting evidence as the primary failure cause; no 401/403 rejections were logged.

Correlated the PaymentSync failure window (02:10–02:40 UTC) with Integration Gateway logs from gateway-prod-east-07.payments.internal showing repeated 504 responses and upstream latency averaging 7.2s against the 5s configured timeout threshold, confirmed via Monitoring System traces.

Applied a gateway-side stability change on gateway-prod-east-07.payments.internal by increasing the request timeout from 5s to 12s and adjusting retry and backoff behavior (exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries) to reduce repeated PaymentSync job failures during transient downstream slowdowns.

Escalated the incident (ESC-PAY-0819) to the downstream payment service team lead David Okafor (dokafor@corplabs.com, phone +1-571-884-2039) with the failure window, timeout evidence, Monitoring System trace IDs, and a request for extended request tracing and latency analysis on https://api.payments.internal/v2/sync.

Monitored queue recovery and PaymentSync processing from the Monitoring System dashboard after the gateway tuning change to confirm jobs resumed and the ~1,200-item backlog began clearing without further immediate failures; Rajesh Menon (rmenon) confirmed Finance Users data sync restored by 03:15 UTC.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures for internal services
description: Users in the Chicago office were trying to reach internal services by the hostname svc.internal.corp, but DNS resolution intermittently returned different A records after a same-day zone edit performed by network engineer David Kowalski (emp ID NE-40821). Some clients resolved the new address 10.10.5.21 and connected successfully, while others received the previous IP 10.10.4.9 and application requests to internal endpoints failed by name. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) at approximately 15:00 UTC. Impact was limited to internal services in corp-datacenter-1 and caused inconsistent connectivity and elevated DNS lookup failures in Network Monitoring dashboards.
observed_errors: NXDOMAIN not observed but inconsistent A record responses
Resolver returned stale A record 10.10.4.9 for svc.internal.corp after zone update
root_cause: A stale cached A record for svc.internal.corp remained on internal DNS resolver/forwarding paths after the authoritative internal zone was updated to 10.10.5.21, causing different clients to receive either the old address 10.10.4.9 or the new address depending on which resolver cache answered the query.
resolution_steps: Validated that the authoritative internal DNS zone on dns-auth-01.corplabs.internal for svc.internal.corp contained the intended A record value of 10.10.5.21 and confirmed the earlier zone change by David Kowalski (dkowalski) at 13:45 UTC had been applied correctly.

Flushed DNS cache entries on the internal resolver path using rndc flush on dns-res-02.corplabs.internal and dns-res-03.corplabs.internal — the primary and secondary resolver nodes involved in serving or forwarding the internal.corp zone to the Chicago subnets — to remove the stale 10.10.4.9 response.

Reviewed and verified conditional forwarder configuration on dns-res-02 and dns-res-03 for the internal.corp zone so queries were routed consistently to dns-auth-01.corplabs.internal as the correct authoritative source rather than returning mixed cached results.

Re-ran DNS lookups from multiple resolver paths and client subnets (10.22.14.0/24, 10.22.15.0/24) to confirm svc.internal.corp now resolved consistently to 10.10.5.21. Verified with affected users Maria Chen (mchen) and Jorge Ramirez (jramirez) that application connectivity was restored.

Documented TTL and change-propagation guidance for future internal zone edits — including a recommended post-change cache-flush checklist for all resolver nodes — so stale cached responses can be minimized and validated immediately after record changes. Shared documentation with the network team lead, Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com), for inclusion in the DNS runbook.

title: Expired TLS certificate causing Internal Web Service TLS outage
description: Users and internal systems were trying to reach internal.example.com over TLS, but the load balancer lb-int-01 presented an expired certificate and browsers showed certificate date warnings. Multiple teams reported the issue starting around 21:45 UTC, including the DevOps integration pipeline managed by rchen and the monitoring dashboard used by the Portland operations team. Dependent integrations (including the inventory sync service running on WORKSTATION-DEVOPS-RC) also began failing TLS handshakes with NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID, making the internal web service unavailable over HTTPS. The outage aligns with the certificate expiration date of 2025-12-14 after the automated renewal job (cert-renewal-scheduler, last configured by mwatkins) did not run and no renewal alert was raised. Ticket submitted by Danielle Ortiz (dortiz@corplabs.com, EMP-40821) on behalf of the internal_services user group.
root_cause: The TLS outage was caused by the certificate for internal.example.com expiring on the load balancer after the automated renewal process failed to execute and renewal monitoring did not alert. Recovery also required updating the full certificate chain on lb-int-01 so clients could validate the renewed certificate correctly.
resolution_steps: Obtain an emergency reissued certificate for internal.example.com from the Certificate Authority (CERTOPS-8841) after confirming the previous certificate (serial 3A:F2:9C:01) had expired on 2025-12-14. Emergency issuance approved by Sandra Liu (sliu@corplabs.com) and new certificate generated with notAfter of 2026-12-14.

Deploy the renewed server certificate and complete intermediate chain (including updated corplabs-intermediate-g3.crt) to lb-int-01 (10.22.4.60), then reload the nginx TLS configuration via 'nginx -s reload' to apply the new certificate bundle without full service restart.

Validate the endpoint from the client side (tested from 10.134.22.97 and WORKSTATION-DEVOPS-RC) and load balancer side to confirm the presented certificate subject matches internal.example.com, the expiration date is 2026-12-14, and TLS handshakes succeed without date warnings. Danielle Ortiz confirmed user-facing access restored from the Portland office.

Restore the cert-renewal scheduler by correcting the failed renewal execution path in /opt/certops/renew.sh (API endpoint URL had been changed without updating the script), confirming the next automated renewal cycle is scheduled for 2026-11-14, and assigning renewal ownership to mwatkins (EMP-30455) with backup to sliu.

Re-enable the cert_expiry_warning monitoring alert rule and test certificate expiration monitoring and alert escalation so future renewal failures or near-expiry conditions generate actionable notifications to the certops-alerts@corplabs.com distribution list and on-call pager for the Portland infrastructure team.

Update the certificate deployment and renewal runbook (RUNBOOK-CERT-017) to require post-deployment chain validation on the load balancer using openssl verify, tracked renewal ownership with named assignee, and mandatory 30/14/7-day expiry alert checkpoints.

Re-pushed the updated GlobalProtect configuration to all affected endpoints in the Frankfurt and London offices via the management console to ensure the active gateway address and certificate profile were aligned with the newly issued device certificates.

Verified Okta conditional access group membership for impacted users (mengstrom, rkapoor, and 6 additional EMEA remote workforce members) and resynced group membership where needed to rule out identity policy mismatch after MFA. Priya Nair (pnair) from Desktop Support confirmed macOS devices were correctly re-enrolled.

Validated stable VPN connectivity with test users mengstrom and rkapoor and monitored GlobalProtect gateway logs for 24 hours to confirm that tunnels remained established, no SSL_CERT_EXPIRED events recurred, and internal applications (HR portal, corporate file share) were reachable from both Windows and macOS endpoints.

title: Outlook shows 'Disconnected' and email not syncing on mobile
description: I'm Marcus Harris (employee ID EMP-40821) and I was trying to access and sync email in Outlook on my mobile device (iPhone, hostname MOBILE-IPHONE-MH), but the app began showing a disconnected state earlier today around 01:45 UTC and new messages stopped updating. My mailbox is marcus.harris@corplabs.com on Exchange Online. Desktop Outlook on my workstation WORKSTATION-MH-7204 may work intermittently, which suggests the mailbox itself is available but the affected mobile endpoint (IP 10.47.83.112) is not maintaining a healthy Exchange Online connection. I also reported receiving an Intune compliance notification on the phone and did not complete it, creating a likely block on mobile email access for this managed device. I'm based in the Birmingham office under the Sales - Mobile Users group.
root_cause: Mobile Outlook sync was blocked by an unremediated Intune device compliance issue, leaving the managed device out of compliance and preventing normal Exchange Online mobile synchronization. A stale Outlook session/profile on the endpoint remained a secondary possibility until compliance status was verified.
resolution_steps: Verify the affected mobile device MOBILE-IPHONE-MH status in Intune for user mharris (EMP-40821) and confirm whether the device is marked non-compliant or awaiting user remediation.

Have Marcus Harris complete the pending Intune compliance actions on the mobile device MOBILE-IPHONE-MH, including any required policy acknowledgement, passcode, or device management prompts, then confirm the device returns to a compliant state in the Intune portal.

After compliance is restored, fully close Outlook mobile on MOBILE-IPHONE-MH, reopen it, and re-authenticate the work account marcus.harris@corplabs.com so the app can refresh its Exchange Online session.

If the mailbox marcus.harris@corplabs.com still shows disconnected after compliance remediation, remove and re-add the work account in Outlook mobile on MOBILE-IPHONE-MH to rebuild the mobile sync partnership.

Confirm mailbox folders for marcus.harris@corplabs.com update normally on MOBILE-IPHONE-MH and that new email sends and receives successfully on the mobile device without the disconnected status returning. Agent Priya Nair to follow up with Marcus Harris via phone (+44 7700 934218) if further issues arise.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, this is Priya Nair from the service desk. Please confirm whether the mobile device (MOBILE-IPHONE-MH) showed any Intune or Company Portal compliance prompts before Outlook stopped syncing, and whether desktop Outlook on WORKSTATION-MH-7204 or Outlook Web Access at https://outlook.office365.com can still access the mailbox marcus.harris@corplabs.com. Also, can you confirm your current location — are you working from the Birmingham office or remotely?

title: Laptop severely slow after login
description: My corporate Windows 10 laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, asset tag LPT-04821) becomes severely slow immediately after login. I'm Marcus Reeves in the Philadelphia office, employee ID EMP-20947. CPU usage spikes above 90% in the first 1-2 minutes after I sign in with my account mreeves@corplabs.com, and common apps such as Outlook, Teams, and Chrome take 10-30 seconds to open. The issue recurred after an automatic policy refresh pushed overnight, preventing normal start-of-day work until login activity settled. My IP at the time was 10.42.18.77.
observed_errors: CPU spike >90% within 1-2 minutes after login
Long application startup times (10-30s vs expected 1-3s)
root_cause: Resource-heavy startup policy and multiple nonessential startup tasks combined with an endpoint protection scan backlog, causing sustained high CPU and disk activity immediately after user login.
resolution_steps: Reviewed login-time resource consumption on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (user mreeves, IP 10.42.18.77) and identified repeated CPU spikes linked to nonessential startup items and a CrowdStrike Falcon endpoint protection scan backlog of 14 queued items.
Disabled three unnecessary startup items (OneDrive sync pre-loader, Adobe Acrobat Update Service, and a legacy inventory agent) from the mreeves profile to reduce immediate post-login process load.

Refreshed device policy via Endpoint Management for CN=mreeves,OU=Corp Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal and validated that startup configuration no longer reintroduced the heavy login task combination after the reopen event reported by Marcus Reeves.
Ran a full manual CrowdStrike Falcon endpoint protection scan on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR to clear the 14 queued backlog items that were consuming CPU after sign-in.
Adjusted CrowdStrike Falcon endpoint protection scan scheduling to run during off-peak hours (daily at 01:00 EST) to prevent future overlap with user logon activity for the Philadelphia office group.

Removed 4.2 GB of temporary files from C:\Users\mreeves\AppData\Local\Temp and reclaimed disk space to reduce disk contention and improve overall application launch performance on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. Can you confirm whether the slowdown starts immediately after login on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and whether Outlook, Teams, and Chrome are all affected at the same time? Also, is your account mreeves the only one experiencing this, or have other users on your team in Philadelphia seen similar behavior?

title: Laptop slow
description: I have a corporate Windows 10 laptop (hostname LAPTOP-SALES-MR, asset tag EP-04821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (employee ID EMP-20947) becoming very slow immediately after sign-in. CPU remained elevated for several minutes, Microsoft Office and Outlook opened slowly, and normal post-login work was delayed. The device is located at the Charlotte office and connects via IP 10.22.48.115. Diagnostics tied the slowdown to Windows Defender (MsMpEng.exe) processing a queued/full scan at login, with low free disk space and multiple startup items increasing startup resource contention on the domain-joined endpoint.
observed_errors: Sustained high CPU (80-95%) by MsMpEng.exe after login
Low free disk space reported (<5% free)
root_cause: A backlog of endpoint protection scans was triggered at user login, causing Windows Defender to consume sustained CPU while low free disk space and several startup items amplified the performance degradation.
resolution_steps: Validated that MsMpEng.exe was the primary process driving 80-95% CPU utilization after login on LAPTOP-SALES-MR (user mreeves, IP 10.22.48.115) and confirmed a queued scheduled scan in Endpoint Management for device asset EP-04821.
Cleared the Defender scan backlog on LAPTOP-SALES-MR and allowed a single controlled scan cycle to complete so repeated scan attempts no longer retriggered at sign-in for user mreeves.

Removed temporary files and user cache data from C:\Users\mreeves\AppData\Local\Temp and browser cache directories to reclaim approximately 12 GB of disk space and reduce resource pressure during startup on LAPTOP-SALES-MR.
Disabled three nonessential startup items (CRM sync agent, legacy print utility, third-party updater) to reduce concurrent CPU and disk usage immediately after user login on LAPTOP-SALES-MR.

Ran an endpoint policy refresh on LAPTOP-SALES-MR via Endpoint Management to stop the scan-from-login scheduling condition and synchronize the device with current management settings for the Charlotte Sales OU.

Monitored CPU usage and application launch performance for 45 minutes after remediation on LAPTOP-SALES-MR and confirmed the laptop returned to normal responsiveness. Notified Marcus Reeves (mreeves) at mreeves@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, this is Danielle Cho from the endpoint support team. Please confirm whether the laptop LAPTOP-SALES-MR is slow only right after sign-in or throughout the day, and whether Task Manager shows any process using unusually high CPU. You can reach me at dcho@corplabs.com or ext. 4-7831 if you'd prefer to discuss by phone.

title: BitLocker did not enable and recovery key not escrowed
description: User Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) reported that his Windows 10 Surface Laptop 4 (hostname WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD) at the Phoenix office showed as noncompliant for disk encryption in Company Portal. BitLocker had not completed enabling on the C: drive, the device displayed a TPM protector not initialized condition (manage-bde status returned 'Protection Off'), and no recovery key was available in Azure AD for the device. The assigned Intune encryption policy ('Sales-Encryption-Win10') was present under his account mdelgado@corplabs.com, but Marcus was blocked from reaching a compliant state until BitLocker could start and the recovery key could be escrowed. Device IP at time of report was 10.42.18.97.
observed_errors: Recovery key not found in Azure AD (no escrow)
root_cause: BitLocker could not complete because the device TPM protector was not initialized, which prevented encryption startup and recovery key escrow to Azure AD.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the Intune disk encryption policy 'Sales-Encryption-Win10' was assigned to WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD (user mdelgado, EMP-40821) and that the latest compliance state was failing on encryption readiness rather than policy assignment.

Initialized the device TPM protector on WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD using Initialize-Tpm so BitLocker could create a valid protector on the operating system volume C:. Verified Get-Tpm returned TpmReady: True after initialization.

Started BitLocker encryption on the endpoint with manage-bde -on C: and verified that encryption began progressing successfully after TPM initialization — manage-bde -status showed 'Encryption in Progress' at 12% within the first few minutes.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key and escrowed the current recovery key to Azure AD via BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector so it became available to support and compliance services. Confirmed the key was visible in the Azure AD device blade for WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD.

Forced an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD and confirmed the Device Compliance Service updated to show encryption enabled and the device returned to compliant status. Notified Marcus Delgado at mdelgado@corplabs.com that his device is now fully compliant.

title: Users experience MFA prompt loop during SSO (Okta/Azure AD)
description: Multiple users reported they could not get through the SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) to reach Salesforce, Office365, and other SaaS applications because the sign-in process appeared to return them to MFA repeatedly. The failures started around 2026-05-15 after an identity platform change window (CHG-20260514-0087) that updated federation trust settings between Okta and Azure AD. Affected users include contractors such as Maria Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) and Raj Patel (rpatel@corplabs.com), who reported the issue from the Phoenix office. The problem was observed across different contractor groups provisioned through the new Azure AD sync.
root_cause: An upstream federated SSO processing fault after MFA completion prevented session establishment and redirected users back to the sign-in flow, creating the appearance of repeated MFA despite valid enrollment and policy scope.
resolution_steps: Collected Okta system logs and Azure AD sign-in traces for affected users mdelgado and rpatel showing successful MFA completion (verify_factor: SUCCESS) followed by federation redirect failure with error 'Invalid session state — missing group claim in token'. Traces captured from sessions originating at IPs 10.47.22.118 and 10.47.22.134 in the Phoenix office.

Confirmed MFA enrollment and conditional access policy assignment were healthy for mdelgado (EMP-30842) and rpatel (EMP-30917) to rule out account configuration issues. Both had active Okta Verify push factors and correct ExtContractors-West group membership.

Escalated the incident to the identity platform vendor and internal SSO engineering team lead Kevin Ostrowski (kostrowski, kevin.ostrowski@corplabs.com) for federation flow analysis of the SAML claim mapping issue introduced during CHG-20260514-0087.

Provided affected users (mdelgado, rpatel, and other impacted contractors in the Phoenix office) with a temporary direct-app access URL and alternate sign-in workaround via Okta bookmark app where available until the federation claim mapping issue is corrected by the SSO engineering team.
agent_questions: Please confirm whether the affected users — specifically those in the recently synced contractor access group (CN=ExtContractors-West,OU=Security Groups,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) — are all experiencing the same behavior. Can you verify whether the MFA screen loops after the user approves the push notification or before factor completion? Also, please have one of the affected users (e.g., mdelgado or rpatel) attempt sign-in while we capture a real-time trace from the Okta admin console.

title: Expired TLS certificate causing internal web service TLS outage
description: Users and automated clients were trying to reach internal-web-service (https://appportal.corp.internal) through the central Load Balancer (LB-EAST-01.corp.internal), but browser sessions showed certificate warnings and API connections failed during TLS negotiation. The outage was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corp.internal) from the Denver office and affected internal access to the service across the us-east-1 region, blocking normal application use for the internal-dev-team because the endpoint certificate (CN=appportal.corp.internal) had expired and the certificate chain presented by the Load Balancer was incomplete. Approximately 40 users and 12 automated service accounts were impacted.
root_cause: The TLS certificate presented by the central Load Balancer for internal-web-service expired on 2025-12-23, and the deployed chain was incomplete because the intermediate certificate was not being served.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the certificate presented by the Load Balancer LB-EAST-01.corp.internal for internal-web-service (CN=appportal.corp.internal, serial 4A:3F:9C:01:BB:72) was past its notAfter date of 2025-12-23T00:00:00Z and no longer valid for production TLS connections.

Requested and obtained a renewed end-entity TLS certificate from the internal Certificate Authority for the affected service endpoint appportal.corp.internal, new serial 7B:12:AE:44:CF:90, valid until 2026-12-23. CSR generated and submitted by koduya, approved by sliu.

Updated the Load Balancer LB-EAST-01.corp.internal TLS configuration to deploy the renewed certificate (serial 7B:12:AE:44:CF:90) and attach the required intermediate certificate chain (CorpLabs Internal CA G2) to the appportal.corp.internal listener.

Reloaded the Load Balancer LB-EAST-01.corp.internal configuration via the management console so new inbound TLS sessions presented the corrected certificate bundle; verified no active session drops during the reload window.

Validated from the client side — including from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (10.22.47.88, mchen) and WORKSTATION-DESK-RP (rpatel, Austin office) — that the service now completed TLS handshakes successfully without certificate date warnings or missing-chain validation failures.

Restored and verified certificate expiration monitoring and renewal alerting for appportal.corp.internal in the cert-ops dashboard, configured to trigger at 30-day and 7-day thresholds, with notifications routed to sliu@corp.internal and the cert-ops distribution list, to detect future certificate age and renewal job issues before service impact.

title: Users stuck in MFA prompt loop
description: Multiple users in the recently modified SSO-Portal-Users group were unable to open SaaS applications such as Salesforce and Confluence through the internal SSO portal (https://sso.corplabs.com). The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) from the Charlotte office, who noticed that after entering credentials, she and several colleagues were repeatedly returned to the Okta MFA challenge screen and eventually denied access with error Okta-ERR-1012. The issue started after a routine conditional access policy update performed on 2026-04-01 and blocked normal application access despite Azure AD showing successful token issuance for some of the same sign-in attempts. Affected users include rng_nguyen, d.kowalski, and at least four others in the same group.
root_cause: The MFA loop was caused by two identity-layer issues introduced around the same change window: stale Okta MFA factor enrollments for several affected users and a conditional access/application assignment mismatch for the updated SSO user group. Azure AD token issuance succeeded, but downstream access evaluation in Okta and group-scoped policy handling prevented successful session completion.
resolution_steps: Reset affected users' Okta MFA enrollments (rng_nguyen, d.kowalski, p.deshmukh, and three additional users identified in the SSO-Portal-Users group) and require fresh Okta Verify factor re-enrollment before retrying SSO sign-in at https://sso.corplabs.com.

Validate authenticator device time synchronization for users with token mismatch behavior — particularly rng_nguyen (WORKSTATION-RN-4821) and p.deshmukh — and correct any clock drift found on mobile authenticator devices to prevent future Okta-ERR-1012 events.

Update the group-based conditional access and application assignment scope in Azure AD to properly include the recently modified SSO-Portal-Users group, remove the conflicting exclusion rule from the legacy policy, and eliminate the policy mismatch that caused downstream access denial.

Retest sign-in for impacted users (rng_nguyen, d.kowalski, p.deshmukh) through the SSO portal to confirm a single MFA challenge completes successfully and target applications (Salesforce, Confluence) open without looping or access-denied errors.

Review Okta and Azure AD sign-in events for the SSO-Portal-Users group over the 48 hours following the change to confirm token issuance aligns with successful application access, no further MFA_PROMPT_LOOP events occur, and enrollment_token_mismatch errors have ceased for all affected users.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — thanks for reporting this. Can you confirm whether the MFA loop happens across all SSO apps (Salesforce, Confluence, the portal itself) or only specific ones? Also, were any of the affected users — yourself, d.kowalski, or others — recently moved into the updated SSO-Portal-Users group as part of the April 1st policy change? Please also let me know the workstation or device you're signing in from so we can cross-reference Okta device trust logs. — Kevin Marsh, Identity Support (ext. 4417)

title: Account locked after repeated failed sign-ins
description: I (Marcus Delgado, emp ID E-20487) was trying to regain access to my corporate account (mdelgado@corplabs.com) after repeated failed sign-in attempts from my iOS mobile device (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) triggered an AD lockout. The failed attempts originated from my home network IP 10.47.83.112 in the Raleigh office region. After completing a self-service password reset in the Password Reset Portal, I still could not authenticate to the Corporate SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com and continued to generate lockout events, blocking normal account access from mobile and SSO-connected services.
observed_errors: SSO authentication failure: invalid credentials after reset
root_cause: Active Directory lockout policy was triggered by repeated authentication attempts from the user's mobile device using stale cached credentials, and the password reset did not fully restore access until the account was unlocked and the mobile cached credentials/reset token path were corrected.
resolution_steps: Unlock the user's Active Directory account (CN=mdelgado,OU=Mobile Users,DC=corplabs,DC=internal) on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and verify the lockout state is cleared before additional sign-in attempts are made. Performed by Priya Nair.

Issue a fresh password reset token through the Password Reset Portal for mdelgado and complete a new password reset to ensure the credential change is accepted and current. Confirm the password last-set timestamp updates on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal.
Have Marcus Delgado remove saved account credentials (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from mobile mail and collaboration applications on WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD, then re-add the account using the new password.

Validate that no device or background client continues submitting stale credentials from the previously identified mobile source IP 10.47.83.112 (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-MD) and stop any remaining failed authentication attempts against DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal.

Confirm successful authentication by mdelgado to the Corporate SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com after reset propagation and verify no new AD Event ID 4740 lockout events occur on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal during the 30-minute observation window. Notify Marcus Delgado at 919-555-0173 upon closure.

title: account locked after repeated failed sign-ins
description: I was trying to sign in through the SSO Portal (https://sso.corplabs.com) on the morning of November 25th but received an account locked message after repeated authentication failures. My username is dmorales and I'm in the Finance department at the Charlotte office. A self-service password reset was completed in the Password Reset Portal, but SSO access remained blocked because my mobile device (iPhone, iOS 16.4) continued submitting stale saved credentials from the Outlook and Teams apps, preventing access to account resources until the lockout source was cleared. Please help — I have month-end close deadlines today.
observed_errors: SSO authentication failure after password change
root_cause: Cached credentials on the user's mobile device continued sending stale authentication attempts after the password reset, causing repeated AD lockouts and preventing the new password from being used successfully through SSO.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Active Directory lockout events on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal for account dmorales and confirmed the lockout was triggered by 11 repeated failed sign-in attempts from the user's mobile device (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-DM at 10.47.83.112) rather than a broader directory or SSO outage.

Unlocked the Active Directory account for dmorales (EMP-90274) after verifying the lockout source was isolated to the mobile device and ensuring no additional failed attempts were coming from other endpoints or services in the Charlotte office network.

Had Diana Morales remove saved credentials and clear cached authentication data on the mobile device (WORKSTATION-IPHONE-DM) by signing out of Outlook and Teams apps and re-adding the dmorales account with the updated password.

Issued a fresh password reset token via the Password Reset Portal and confirmed the password change for dmorales was accepted and propagated to DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal so the updated credential could be used for new authentication requests.

Validated that SSO sign-in at https://sso.corplabs.com succeeded for dmorales after the mobile credential cache was cleared on WORKSTATION-IPHONE-DM, and documented guidance for updating saved passwords on user devices to prevent repeat lockouts. Sent follow-up email to d.morales@corplabs.com with instructions.
agent_questions: Hi Diana, we confirmed that the account dmorales is currently locked in Active Directory (CN=dmorales,OU=Finance,DC=corplabs,DC=internal). The lockout was recorded on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal at 08:12 EST this morning. Are you still signed in on your mobile mail or collaboration apps (Outlook, Teams), and did the failures continue after you used the Password Reset Portal? Also, can you confirm the IP address your phone typically connects from — we're seeing repeated attempts from 10.47.83.112.

title: Software Center installation blocked for FinanceApp (entitlement missing) — resolved
description: Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40218) on managed corporate Windows device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN reported that FinanceApp v4.2.1 could not be installed from Software Center. The application was not appearing in the catalog for rachel.nguyen even after a manual sync and machine policy retrieval cycle, and when Rachel tried running an approved installer package separately via the Software Center available deployments link, the install did not complete — returning an entitlement authorization error. The missing software was preventing Rachel from accessing required finance workflows ahead of the Q2 close deadline. Device IP at time of report: 10.22.47.115.
observed_errors: Entitlement check failed: user/device not authorized to install this application
root_cause: FinanceApp deployment targeting is misconfigured or not being processed correctly in the endpoint management platform despite valid entitlement membership.
resolution_steps: Validated that the affected user rachel.nguyen (EMP-40218) and device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN were correctly synchronized in the FIN-FinanceApp-Entitlement Azure AD group and that no local Endpoint Protection or application control policy was blocking the FinanceApp installer.

Reviewed the FinanceApp deployment assignment in the Intune management console and identified that the application was not properly targeted to the device scope containing WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN — the deployment's device filter rule was excluding the Philadelphia office device collection due to a stale scope tag configuration.

Corrected the deployment targeting scope tag and assignment rule in the Intune management platform to include the Philadelphia device collection, then initiated a policy refresh to WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (IP 10.22.47.115) to force re-evaluation of the deployment.

Confirmed FinanceApp v4.2.1 became visible in Software Center on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN after the assignment correction and verified the installation completed successfully. Rachel Nguyen confirmed she could launch FinanceApp and access the required finance workflows.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — thank you for reporting this. Please confirm whether FinanceApp is missing entirely from the Software Center catalog on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN or whether it is visible but blocked when you attempt installation. Also, does a specific policy or entitlement error message appear (e.g., 'user/device not authorized')? If possible, please share a screenshot. I can see your device is enrolled in Intune under rachel.nguyen@corplabs.com — I'll begin checking entitlement group membership in the meantime.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to Finance shared drive (\\fileserver\Finance)
description: I was trying to open the Finance shared drive at \\fileserver\Finance from Windows Explorer using a mapped network drive (F:). The drive prompted for credentials and then returned Access Denied, preventing me from opening the Finance department folder needed for normal file access. The issue affected my account j.smith (Employee ID: EMP-71843) on my workstation WORKSTATION-PC-JS (IP 10.42.18.65), running Windows 10. I'm based in the Philadelphia office. My name is Janet Smith and I can be reached at janet.smith@corplabs.com or 215-555-0391. The issue was limited to my access to the Finance share.
root_cause: User j.smith did not have the required Active Directory security group membership for the Finance share. Because the user was not a member of FIN_Share_Read, the SMB ACL on \\fileserver\Finance denied access and the mapped drive re-prompted for credentials.
resolution_steps: Verified the Finance shared folder ACL on FS-EAST-01.corplabs.internal and confirmed access is granted through AD group FIN_Share_Read. The ACL was reviewed using Get-Acl on the share path.
Added user j.smith (Janet Smith, EMP-71843) to the FIN_Share_Read security group required for \\fileserver\Finance access. Change approved by team lead Robert Chen.

Refreshed the user's security context by forcing policy/group membership refresh (gpupdate /force on WORKSTATION-PC-JS) and having the user sign out and sign back in to pick up the updated group token.

Cleared stale mapped drive or cached credentials on the workstation WORKSTATION-PC-JS using 'cmdkey /delete:fileserver' and 'net use F: /delete', then remapped F: to \\fileserver\Finance so Windows would use the updated logon token.

Retested access to \\fileserver\Finance from WORKSTATION-PC-JS (IP 10.42.18.65) and confirmed the folder opened successfully without further credential prompts. Janet Smith verified she could read and write files in the Finance department folder.
agent_questions: Hi Janet, thank you for reporting this. Please test opening \\fileserver\Finance directly in Windows Explorer (not via the mapped F: drive) and confirm whether you receive Access Denied or a credential prompt. Also, could you run 'net use' from a command prompt on WORKSTATION-PC-JS and share the output so we can verify the current drive mapping state? — Agent Marcus Webb

title: Laptop slow after login — high CPU and nearly full disk
description: My managed Windows 10 corporate laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH, hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH) became very slow immediately after login following a recent Intune policy refresh on 2026-01-29. I'm logged in as mhassani and Outlook, Teams, and File Explorer each took 30-60 seconds to open or become responsive. Task Manager showed sustained high CPU (85-95%) and disk activity pinned above 90%. The C: drive had only about 8% free space remaining (~18 GB out of 238 GB), and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint showed multiple queued scan jobs in the protection history. This is impacting my normal post-login work — I'm based in the Dubai office and need the laptop for client meetings throughout the day.
observed_errors: Endpoint protection scan backlog / queued scans
root_cause: A recent endpoint policy refresh caused heavy startup processing and an endpoint protection scan backlog on a laptop with critically low free disk space. The combination drove sustained CPU and disk utilization during user logon, delaying application startup and overall desktop responsiveness.
resolution_steps: Validated the performance issue during logon on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH (user mhassani, IP 10.42.17.88) and confirmed sustained CPU at 85-95% and disk utilization above 90% alongside 4 queued Microsoft Defender for Endpoint scans and only 8% free disk space on C:.

Temporarily paused the active Defender protection scan workload on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH, cleared the 4 queued full-scan jobs from the backlog, and scheduled the required full scan during off-hours (02:00 GST) to avoid peak logon impact for mhassani.

Removed temporary files (9.2 GB), stale Teams cache (6.8 GB), and older browser cache data (3.1 GB) from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH to reclaim approximately 19 GB of local storage, bringing free space to ~16%. Increased the device storage quota in endpoint management policy to flag devices below 15% free and reduce immediate recurrence from low disk space.

Disabled 6 non-essential startup items (including redundant sync agents and third-party updaters) through Intune endpoint management policy for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH and forced an Intune policy refresh so the lighter startup configuration applied consistently to mhassani's profile.

Adjusted the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint scan schedule for the Dubai Sales - EMEA device group to stagger scan activity outside normal login periods (scans now trigger at 02:00 GST rather than at policy refresh) and documented the policy change in the EMEA endpoint runbook for reuse on similar devices. Notified Mariam Hassani at mariam.hassani@corplabs.com that the issue is resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Mariam, thanks for reporting this. I'm agent Callum Briggs (emp ID EMP-40821) and I'll be handling your case. Could you please confirm whether the slowdown starts right after you sign in as mhassani and whether Task Manager shows CPU or disk staying high while Outlook, Teams, or File Explorer are opening? Also, can you confirm the device hostname — is it WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH at IP 10.42.17.88? That will help me pull the right telemetry from our endpoint management console.

title: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key not escrowed
description: I noticed that a Windows 10 21H2 Azure AD joined device assigned to Marcus Delgado (employee ID EMP-40821) showed disk encryption as not enabled in Windows Security. The endpoint, hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD with IP 10.42.18.97, was listed in Intune as Noncompliant for the encryption requirement, and the BitLocker recovery key was not escrowed to the management service. A manual Company Portal sync initiated by the user did not correct the issue, leaving the device out of compliance and without recoverable key backup. The user contacted our Richmond helpdesk for assistance.
root_cause: The TPM protector was not initialized on the endpoint, which prevented BitLocker from starting correctly and blocked recovery key escrow to Intune.
resolution_steps: Verified the endpoint encryption state on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (user mdelgado, EMP-40821, IP 10.42.18.97) and confirmed BitLocker was not enabled while Intune showed the device as noncompliant for required encryption.
Initialized the TPM protector on the device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD so BitLocker could use the TPM-backed protector, confirmed via manage-bde -protectors -get C: showing a valid TPM protector.
Enabled BitLocker and started encryption on the system drive using the local BitLocker management tooling (manage-bde -on C:) on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD for user mdelgado.
Rotated and escrowed the current BitLocker recovery key to Intune to restore recovery key visibility in management, verified the key ID appeared in the Endpoint Manager device record for mdelgado.

Forced an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD via Company Portal and confirmed the device reported encryption enabled and returned to a compliant state. Notified Marcus Delgado (marcus.delgado@corplabs.com) of resolution.

title: Software Center installation blocked by endpoint protection policy

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service outage
description: Users were trying to access the internal-web-service over HTTPS through the load balancer (LB-EAST-PROD-01), but browsers showed certificate warnings and dependent clients failed TLS negotiation with ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and load balancer 525/SSL errors. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office and quickly confirmed by additional users across multiple internal networks including the Raleigh and Charlotte offices. Access to the internal web service was blocked until the expired certificate was renewed and the deployed chain was corrected on the load balancer. The ticket was escalated by Derek Owens (emp ID: E-40291) on the infrastructure team.
root_cause: The TLS certificate for the internal web service expired because renewal was not completed before the expiration date, and after renewal the updated full certificate chain was not yet deployed on the load balancer SSL configuration, causing client validation failures and TLS handshake errors.
resolution_steps: Verified the presented certificate on the HTTPS endpoint (internal-web.corplabs.com via LB-EAST-PROD-01) had expired and confirmed the service name required by clients matched the renewed certificate request. Verification performed by Derek Owens (dowens, E-40291) from WORKSTATION-DESK-DO at IP 10.42.18.52.

Renewed the TLS certificate with the internal Certificate Authority (ca-root.corplabs.internal) for CN=internal-web.corplabs.com and obtained the correct full certificate chain including required intermediates, new serial 7B:22:AE:04 with validity through 2026-12-25.

Uploaded the renewed certificate and updated the complete certificate chain on the load balancer LB-EAST-PROD-01 serving the internal web service, replacing the expired leaf and outdated intermediate certificates.
Restarted or reloaded the load balancer SSL profile on LB-EAST-PROD-01 so the new certificate and chain were actively presented to clients, confirmed by Derek Owens (dowens) at 02:15 UTC.

Validated successful TLS handshakes from the client and load balancer perspectives and confirmed users could reach the internal web service without certificate warnings. Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) in the Arlington office and users in the Charlotte office confirmed HTTPS access was fully restored from their workstations including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC.

Restored certificate renewal monitoring and added a daily pre-expiry alert check in the SSL monitoring policy to reduce recurrence risk. Priya Nair (pnair) configured the alert to trigger at 30, 14, and 7 days before expiration for all managed certificates.

Confirmed successful VPN connectivity on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (IP 192.168.4.37) for user mreeves and monitored PAN-OS authd and GlobalProtect client logs for continued stable sessions over a 30-minute post-change observation window. title: Unable to connect to Corporate Wi-Fi (expired certificate) — partial workaround applied

After the certificate was renewed on the controller and NAC policy engine, some Windows endpoints continued using stale or mismatched corporate Wi-Fi profiles and required profile re-enrollment.
resolution_steps: Validated that wireless controller WLC-EAST-01 was presenting an expired RADIUS/802.1X certificate (serial 7A:3F:02, expired 2026-04-25 03:59 UTC) and confirmed matching EAP-TLS authentication failures in controller and NAC logs on nac-east.corplabs.internal for users rnguyen, dholloway, and others.

Generated, signed, and deployed the replacement RADIUS/802.1X certificate to Wireless Controller WLC-EAST-01 and NAC policy engine (nac-east.corplabs.internal) so the authentication stack presented a valid server certificate; deployment performed by Marcus Tran (mtran) from the Network Support team.

Restarted wireless controller authentication services on WLC-EAST-01 to force the new certificate into active use and verified successful test reauthentication on known-good devices in the Austin lab, confirming EAP-TLS handshake completed without errors.

title: Print jobs stuck on Print Server
description: Multiple users in the Manhattan office were trying to print to shared queues hosted on central print server PS-NYC-01, but submitted jobs remained stuck in queue and never printed. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) at approximately 14:10 UTC, noting that her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN could not reach the shared HP LaserJet queues. From affected endpoints the printers appeared offline, while Print Management on the server showed 'driver unavailable' and a corrupted driver package after an SCCM driver deployment earlier that morning (deployment ID SCCMDrv-2026-0306). The issue blocked normal office printing for all affected users on the 12th and 14th floors until the server-side driver package was repaired.
observed_errors: Print spooler exception during driver load
root_cause: Corrupted printer driver package deployed to PS-NYC-01 during the morning SCCM driver update caused the Print Spooler to fail loading the driver, leaving shared print queues stuck and reporting printers as unavailable.
resolution_steps: Validated the issue by comparing affected queues (HP-14F-Color, HP-14F-BW, HP-12F-Color, HP-12F-BW, HP-12F-Scan, HP-14F-Scan) against a test queue rolled back to the prior known-good driver v6.2.9.800, confirming the newly deployed driver package v6.3.1.1024 was the trigger. Validation performed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado).

Removed the corrupted printer driver package v6.3.1.1024 and associated driver files from PS-NYC-01 using printmanagement.msc and manual cleanup of the DriverStore, then stopped and restarted the Print Spooler service to release the failed driver state. Confirmed spooler restarted cleanly with no orphaned driver references.

Installed the approved printer driver package v6.2.9.800 from the central repository (\\fs-nyc-02\DriverRepo\HP-UPD) after verifying the package checksum matched the approved version (9A3F…C814). Installation completed at 14:52 UTC by Kevin Wu (kwu, EMP-55210).
Cleared 47 stuck print jobs from the affected queues and remapped those queues to the refreshed driver package on PS-NYC-01. Users were notified via email to resubmit any critical jobs.

Tested printing from multiple user endpoints including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (Rachel Nguyen) and WORKSTATION-PC-KW (Kevin Wu) and monitored spooler activity for two hours to confirm jobs completed normally with no recurring driver-load errors. All six queues processed test pages successfully by 15:05 UTC.

Updated the SCCM deployment package SCCMDrv-2026-0306 to use the verified driver package v6.2.9.800 with correct checksum so the corruption issue would not be reintroduced on subsequent deployments. Change coordinated with Priya Sharma (psharma) on the SCCM packaging team.
agent_questions: We are checking PS-NYC-01. Can you confirm whether all shared printers appear offline from user PCs and whether this started after the morning driver deployment? I've asked Marcus Delgado from Desktop Support to pull Print Management logs. Please also confirm whether users on both the 12th and 14th floors are affected, and whether anyone can print to local USB-attached printers.

title: Laptop slow on login
description: Sales representative Marco Bellini (emp ID: EMP-40291) on a corporate Dell Latitude 5400 running Windows 10 21H2 at the Milan office reported recurring slow logon performance after signing in with username mbellini, with Outlook, Teams, and Edge taking 10-30 seconds to open. During login, CPU repeatedly spiked to 90-98% from msmpeng.exe and svchost, and low disk space on the laptop (hostname LAPTOP-MBELLINI-D5) contributed to delayed application launch. The issue reappeared after a prior remediation, indicating endpoint protection scan backlog and startup policy contention were still affecting normal use at the start of the workday. User can be reached at marco.bellini@corplabs.com or +39 02 8374 6120.
observed_errors: CPU usage spike to 90-98% attributed to msmpeng.exe and svchost on login
root_cause: Recurring endpoint protection scan backlog and login-time policy/startup contention, worsened by low free disk space, caused msmpeng.exe and svchost to consume excessive CPU during user sign-in and delayed application startup.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the endpoint protection state on LAPTOP-MBELLINI-D5, cleared the queued scan backlog of 14 pending definition updates via the Endpoint Protection console, and verified no pending scans remained after policy sync completed at 2026-02-02T12:10Z.

Adjusted the scheduled full scan window for the EMEA-Sales-EP policy group to off-business hours (01:00-04:00 CET) so scan activity would not begin during user logon for mbellini's endpoint policy set. Change coordinated with Priya Nair (pnair).

Refreshed endpoint management and protection policies on LAPTOP-MBELLINI-D5 via the Endpoint Management console, then confirmed the intended startup policy (EMEA-Sales-Startup-v3.2) was applied successfully on the laptop with no pending policy conflicts.

Disabled the identified non-critical startup service (Dell SupportAssist Agent) that was contributing to svchost-related contention during login on LAPTOP-MBELLINI-D5, reducing svchost CPU load at sign-in by approximately 15%.

Removed temporary files from %TEMP%, Windows Update cache, and Outlook OST rebuild staging directories on LAPTOP-MBELLINI-D5 to reclaim approximately 38 GB of disk space and restore adequate free space (45 GB, ~17.6%) for normal Windows and application startup operations.

Validated performance across two consecutive logins by mbellini on LAPTOP-MBELLINI-D5 and confirmed CPU returned to expected post-login levels (peak 32%, settling to 12% within 60 seconds) and affected applications (Outlook, Teams, Edge) opened without abnormal delay (all under 4 seconds). Marco Bellini confirmed the improvement via email at marco.bellini@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Marco, please confirm whether the slowdown on LAPTOP-MBELLINI-D5 (IP 10.42.17.88) happens immediately after login and whether msmpeng.exe or other protection processes are still at the top of CPU usage in Task Manager. Also checking if disk space on C:\ remained low after the last fix applied on 2026-01-19. Could you share a screenshot of Task Manager right after sign-in if possible?

title: Internal hostname intermittently fails DNS resolution for internal-portal.company.local
description: Users at the Chicago and Atlanta offices reported being unable to consistently reach the Internal Portal via hostname internal-portal.company.local, with DNS resolution intermittently failing beginning around 08:15 on 2026-01-10. The issue was first escalated by Marcus Delgado (EMP-40291) from the Chicago office, who noticed that nslookup queries from his workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD returned NXDOMAIN, while colleagues in Atlanta received the outdated IP 10.22.4.17 instead of the current service address. The elevated DNS error rates were visible across internal resolver clusters dns-res-east-01.corp.local and dns-res-east-02.corp.local, and the Monitoring Dashboard began alerting on lookup failures shortly after 08:15.
observed_errors: stale A record served by resolver cache
DNS lookup timeout from some resolvers
root_cause: A stale A record remained in the internal authoritative DNS zone after the service IP changed, and the affected record's long TTL allowed recursive resolvers to continue serving the outdated address. In parallel, some resolvers negatively cached failed lookups, producing intermittent NXDOMAIN responses until the authoritative record and resolver caches were corrected.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the authoritative internal zone on dns-auth-01.corp.local for internal-portal.company.local and corrected the A record from the stale 10.22.4.17 to the current service IP 10.22.8.40 on the zone master, incrementing the zone serial.
Reduced the TTL on the affected DNS record from 86400 seconds to 300 seconds to limit continued propagation of stale cache entries during recovery and future maintenance windows.

Flushed cache on the primary internal DNS resolver dns-res-east-01.corp.local handling the impacted zone queries from the Chicago office so new lookups would retrieve fresh authoritative data from dns-auth-01.corp.local.

Requested downstream resolver and forwarder cache clears on dns-res-east-02.corp.local (Atlanta) and other site resolvers where possible to remove stale or negatively cached entries for internal-portal.company.local across all affected sites.

Validated that authoritative name servers (dns-auth-01.corp.local, dns-auth-02.corp.local) and multiple site resolvers now returned the same updated IP 10.22.8.40, and confirmed via the Monitoring Dashboard that DNS error rates for internal-portal.company.local returned to baseline. Notified Marcus Delgado and Priya Nair that resolution was confirmed.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — can you confirm whether the Internal Portal service IP changed recently (we show a migration was scheduled for internal-portal.company.local last weekend) and whether users in both the Chicago and Atlanta offices are seeing NXDOMAIN or an old address (10.22.4.17)? Also, could you or someone from your team run 'nslookup internal-portal.company.local dns-res-east-01.corp.local' and share the output so we can compare resolver behavior? Please reach out to me at n.okafor@corplabs.com or ext 4-7823 if it's easier to discuss live.

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolving to old IP
description: Users and monitoring reported that app.example.corp intermittently failed to resolve after an internal DNS A record change performed on 2026-01-07 by the infrastructure team. Multiple developers in the Portland office, including Marcus Delgado (mdelgado), reported that some clients and recursive resolvers returned the previous IP 10.0.1.23, while others returned the new IP 10.0.2.45 or intermittently saw NXDOMAIN/timeouts. Affected workstations included WORKSTATION-MACBOOK-MD and others on the 10.12.0.0/16 subnet. This prevented internal services and developers from reliably reaching the application endpoint by hostname after the DNS update, impacting CI/CD pipelines and local development environments.
root_cause: Stale cached DNS data remained on specific recursive resolvers and at least one resolver was not honoring TTL/refresh behavior correctly after the internal A record was updated, causing mixed answers including the previous IP and intermittent NXDOMAIN during propagation.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the authoritative internal DNS zone on dns-auth-west-01.corplabs.internal for app.example.corp contained the intended A record value 10.0.2.45 (SOA serial 2026010802) and reviewed the recent record change committed at 12:55 UTC and TTL settings (300s).

Flushed cache entries via rndc flush on primary and secondary internal recursive resolvers (dns-rec-west-02.corplabs.internal and dns-rec-west-03.corplabs.internal) serving the affected clients in the Portland and Seattle offices to remove stale answers for app.example.corp.

Restarted the resolver service (named) on dns-rec-west-03.corplabs.internal where cached responses persisted despite the flush, addressing the resolver instance that was not honoring TTL refresh behavior correctly. Tanya Reeves (treeves) confirmed the service came back clean with no residual cache entries.

Verified resolver and forwarder behavior by querying the hostname from affected resolvers and known-good resolvers, including tests from Marcus Delgado's workstation (10.12.4.87) and Priya Nair's machine (10.12.4.92), until responses consistently returned 10.0.2.45 across all paths.

Validated end-to-end propagation with dig +trace and Network Monitoring probes across Portland and Seattle segments, then continued short-term monitoring (24-hour window) for residual stale responses from downstream or external recursive caches until they aged out. No further anomalies detected as of 2026-01-09T14:00 UTC.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service outage
description: Users were trying to access the internal web service at www-internal.example.com (VIP 10.42.16.80 on LB-PROD-EAST-02), but browsers displayed certificate warnings and dependent API integrations failed TLS validation with "x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid." The outage was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office around 06:20 UTC on 2025-12-21 and quickly confirmed by multiple teams in us-east-1. Both interactive UI access and automated internal service calls (including the deployment pipeline used by the internal-devops group) were blocked until the expired leaf certificate and load balancer chain were corrected. Ticket opened by DevOps lead Rajesh Kapoor (EMP-40291).
observed_errors: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid
root_cause: The leaf TLS certificate for the Internal Web Service expired at 06:19 UTC. Renewal alerting did not trigger in time, and the load balancer also required an updated certificate chain, causing client TLS validation failures across the service endpoint.
resolution_steps: Confirm the presented certificate on www-internal.example.com had expired (Serial 7A:3F:01:CC, notAfter 06:19 UTC) by running openssl s_client from WORKSTATION-RKAPOOR-PC, and identify the currently deployed chain on LB-PROD-EAST-02 (VIP 10.42.16.80) including the stale CorpLabs Internal CA G2 intermediate.

Generate and sign a replacement leaf certificate (new Serial 7A:3F:02:AB, valid until 2026-12-21) through the internal CA (CorpLabs Internal CA G2) for the service endpoint www-internal.example.com, with matching SAN entries.

Upload the renewed leaf certificate and the correct full certificate chain (leaf → G2 intermediate → root) to LB-PROD-EAST-02 (VIP 10.42.16.80) and verify chain order. Nathan Williams (nwilliams) confirmed correct deployment via the LB admin console.

Restart or reload the Internal Web Service on app nodes app-east-01 and app-east-02 so the renewed certificate is actively served to clients. Rajesh Kapoor (rkapoor) confirmed service came back online at 16:34 UTC.

Validate successful TLS handshakes and certificate trust from client (WORKSTATION-MCHEN-01, WORKSTATION-RKAPOOR-PC) and monitoring perspectives (monitoring.corplabs.internal synthetic checks), then restore and test certificate renewal alerting on certificate-renewal-daemon (cert-mgmt.corplabs.internal) for www-internal.example.com to ensure 30-day and 7-day pre-expiry notifications are sent to devops-alerts@corplabs.com to prevent recurrence.

Reconnected the mapped Engineering drive E: → \\FS-ENG-01.corplabs.internal\Engineering$ and verified the user mreeves could open the department folder without further credential prompts or Access Denied errors. Marcus Reeves confirmed full access restored at 2026-03-10T00:12Z.
