title: API calls to third-party timing out via Integration Gateway
description: Internal integration users on the data-ops team (reported by Marcus Delgado, emp ID EMP-40291) were trying to run overnight data syncs through the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-07) to a third-party vendor API (vendor: Nextera Data Services) in Kubernetes us-east-1, but requests intermittently stalled for 30-60 seconds and returned 504 Gateway Timeout responses. Multiple integration jobs failed — specifically jobs SYNC-4401, SYNC-4402, and SYNC-4405 — and data synchronization to the downstream CRM pipeline was delayed. The issue was observed starting around 09:30 UTC from workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MDELGADO (IP 10.42.17.88), with no confirmed recent application deployment, and token rotation history for service account svc-integ-nextera was initially unclear.
root_cause: Third-party API responsiveness degraded during the affected sync window, causing upstream requests from the Integration Gateway to exceed the configured timeout and return repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses. Token expiry could not be substantiated from available evidence, while the observed timeout pattern and gateway behavior were more consistent with downstream latency than authentication failure.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Integration Gateway failures on node igw-prod-east-07 during the affected 09:30–10:15 UTC window and confirmed repeated upstream timeout behavior (504 responses on jobs SYNC-4401, SYNC-4402, SYNC-4405) rather than an application-side parsing or routing error.

Validated available credential records for service account svc-integ-nextera in the credential vault and confirmed there was no clear evidence of token rejection or authentication-specific failures (no 401/403 codes) requiring emergency secret rotation. Flagged the 92-day-old token for scheduled rotation per policy.

Retried failed integration jobs (SYNC-4401, SYNC-4402, SYNC-4405) after the downstream Nextera Data Services API response pattern stabilized around 10:20 UTC to restore delayed synchronization. All three jobs completed successfully on retry as confirmed by Marcus Delgado.

Escalated the incident to the Nextera Data Services third-party provider (support reference NEXTERA-SR-88712) with the affected time window (09:30–10:15 UTC), 504 timeout pattern from igw-prod-east-07, and request latency symptoms for confirmation of downstream service degradation. Escalation handled by Sandra Cho (sandra.cho@corplabs.com).

Standardized the gateway retry and backoff handling guidance for the Nextera Data Services integration on igw-prod-east-07 (increased timeout to 45s, added exponential backoff with jitter) and documented the need to capture X-RateLimit-Remaining/Retry-After response headers and svc-integ-nextera token rotation history in future occurrences to speed isolation of rate-limit versus latency conditions. Documentation updated by Priya Nair in the integration runbook.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please provide Integration Gateway logs from igw-prod-east-07 for the 09:30-09:45 UTC window and confirm whether failed responses include rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After) or any authentication errors (401/403). Also verify the last known token rotation time for the svc-integ-nextera service account. You can pull the logs from the Monitoring System dashboard at https://monitoring.corplabs.internal/gateway/igw-prod-east-07. — Priya Nair, Integration Support (priya.nair@corplabs.com)

title: Outlook and mobile email not syncing
description: I was trying to access current mailbox content in Outlook on a Windows 10 workstation (WORKSTATION-OUTLOOK-MR) and on an iOS 15 mobile device, but Outlook displayed a disconnected state and new email stopped syncing across devices after a recent MDM policy update pushed on 2026-02-14. Mail delivery and folder updates were delayed in Exchange Online for the mailbox of Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com, employee ID EMP-40291), preventing normal email access. The user is based in the Frankfurt office within the Sales group and reported the issue from IP 10.47.83.112.
root_cause: A stale Outlook profile on the desktop and a deprecated Intune MDM compliance policy reference on the mobile device caused the device to be evaluated as non-compliant, which in turn led to Exchange Online mailbox disconnects and sync interruptions across Outlook and mobile email.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the affected mailbox for mreeves@corplabs.com and device state in Exchange Online and Intune to confirm the mobile device registered to Marcus Reeves (EMP-40291) was associated with a deprecated compliance policy reference CP-EMEA-2025-DEPRECATED and that mailbox connectivity was intermittently dropping from client IP 10.47.83.112.
Cleared the existing mobile sync partnership for the affected device belonging to mreeves so the mailbox could establish a fresh synchronization relationship after compliance was corrected.

Rebuilt the user's Outlook profile on the Windows workstation WORKSTATION-OUTLOOK-MR to remove the stale local profile state for mreeves and re-established the Exchange Online mailbox connection to mreeves@corplabs.com. This step was performed by desktop support engineer Lena Hoffmann.

Updated the device from the deprecated MDM compliance policy reference CP-EMEA-2025-DEPRECATED to the current policy version and forced a new compliance evaluation in Intune for user Marcus Reeves (EMP-40291) in the Frankfurt office.

Validated that the device returned to a compliant state and confirmed mailbox synchronization resumed successfully in Outlook desktop on WORKSTATION-OUTLOOK-MR and on the mobile device for mreeves@corplabs.com, then monitored for recurrence. Notified Marcus Reeves at +49 170 5529841 that service was restored.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus Reeves, please confirm whether the issue started immediately after the policy update on 2026-02-14 and whether Outlook on your desktop (WORKSTATION-OUTLOOK-MR) shows Disconnected while your iPhone also stops receiving new mail. Can you also verify you are connecting from the Frankfurt office network? Your mailbox account is mreeves@corplabs.com — I will begin reviewing Exchange Online connectivity logs and Intune compliance status for your device.

title: Many users cannot connect to Corporate Wi‑Fi after certificate expiry
description: Multiple users in the Marketing and Sales departments at the Dallas office were unable to join the corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-Secure) this morning. 802.1X authentication failed during EAP-TLS negotiation and NAC denied network access to all attempting clients. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) and subsequently confirmed across both managed and BYOD devices on the WLC-managed wireless environment spanning the Americas region. Affected users included teams in Dallas and São Paulo. Normal internal network access was unavailable until the wireless controller RADIUS/TLS certificate was renewed and limited connectivity was provided through the temporary guest SSID (CorpGuest-Temp).
root_cause: Wireless Controller RADIUS/TLS certificate expired, causing EAP-TLS authentication failures against NAC until the renewed certificate and updated chain were applied.
resolution_steps: Verified the Wireless Controller RADIUS/TLS certificate (CN=wlc-radius.corplabs.internal) on WLC-AMER-01 had expired at 2026-05-03T06:00:00Z and replaced it with a renewed certificate and valid intermediate chain on the affected controllers. The renewal was performed by network engineer Kevin Tran (ktran@corplabs.com, EMP-30455).

Restarted AAA/RADIUS services on the Wireless Controller (WLC-AMER-01) at 14:38 UTC so new 802.1X EAP-TLS sessions used the updated certificate chain. Service restart was coordinated with the Dallas NOC team.

Validated successful post-change wireless authentication in controller and NAC logs and confirmed devices could associate to the CorpNet-Secure SSID and receive normal access policy. Verified connectivity for users Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen), Marcus Delgado (mdelgado), and Priya Kapoor (pkapoor) across both Dallas and São Paulo offices.

Instructed affected users to forget and reconnect to the CorpNet-Secure SSID, and completed certificate re-enrollment on devices that still held stale trust or profile data. Priya Kapoor's laptop (WORKSTATION-PKAP01) and three additional BYOD devices required manual re-enrollment via the MDM portal.

Used the temporary guest SSID (CorpGuest-Temp) only as a short-term continuity measure during recovery, then documented follow-up actions to automate certificate renewal via the internal PKI platform and update certificate expiration monitoring in the NOC dashboard to alert at 30, 14, and 7 days before expiry to prevent recurrence. Follow-up task assigned to Kevin Tran.
agent_questions: Hi — are affected users seeing 802.1X or certificate-related failures when connecting to the CorpNet-Secure SSID? We've received reports from Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com) and several others in Marketing. Can you confirm whether the issue is happening on both managed and BYOD devices, and whether it's limited to the Dallas office or also impacting São Paulo?

title: Access denied to DeptShare (mapped drive prompting for credentials)
description: I was trying to open the department SMB share \\fileserver01\DeptShare from a mapped drive (Z:) on my Windows 10 workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MR, but the drive repeatedly prompted for credentials and then returned Access Denied (Error 0x80070005). The issue began after a recent Active Directory group cleanup last week. My username is mramirez (employee ID EMP-40218) and I'm based in the Charlotte office. I need access to the department files on the on-prem file server for an upcoming project deadline. My manager Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com) can confirm I should still have access.
root_cause: The user's account was removed from the Dept-FS-Access Active Directory security group during the recent AD cleanup, so the user's sign-in token no longer carried the group-based permission required for \\fileserver01\DeptShare.
resolution_steps: Verified that access to \\fileserver01\DeptShare is granted through the Dept-FS-Access Active Directory security group and confirmed the share and NTFS permissions were still correct for that group. Share ACL audit on fileserver01 showed Dept-FS-Access retained Full Control, and NTFS inheritance was intact on the DeptShare folder tree.

Added the affected user account mramirez (EMP-40218) back to the Dept-FS-Access group in Active Directory to restore the required group-based entitlement to the department share. Confirmed with manager Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com) that continued access was authorized for the user's role in the Charlotte office.

Instructed user Marco Ramirez to sign out and sign back in on WORKSTATION-PC-MR to refresh Kerberos and group membership tokens so the updated Dept-FS-Access membership would apply to the current session. Verified via 'klist tickets' that the refreshed token included the correct group SID.

Cleared cached Windows credentials for fileserver01 via Credential Manager on WORKSTATION-PC-MR and remapped the network drive using 'net use Z: \\fileserver01\DeptShare /persistent:yes' when credential prompts persisted after initial re-authentication, then retested access to the UNC path directly — access was confirmed restored.

Scheduled replacement of the stale Shared Drive Access Policy reference (policy rev. 2024-Q3) so future access reviews use the current policy version (2026-Q1), and flagged account mramirez for exclusion from automated AD cleanup tasks pending manager approval from Rachel Nguyen.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: Multiple remote users in the Frankfurt office on Windows 10 managed laptops were trying to connect to the corporate network through GlobalProtect VPN. Affected users included Maria Engstrom (m.engstrom, EMP-40291) and Tobias Keller (t.keller, EMP-40387). After approving the Okta MFA prompt, the VPN tunnel established briefly and then disconnected within seconds, leaving internal resources such as the Intranet and HR Portal unreachable. The issue was first reported from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-ME (IP 10.47.22.118) and was reproducible across multiple endpoints. The issue began this morning, was reproducible after re-authentication, and blocked normal remote access to internal applications.
observed_errors: CERT_EXPIRED: device certificate validation failed during post-auth
TUNNEL_TEARDOWN: client disconnected immediately after MFA success
root_cause: Expired device certificate on affected endpoints caused GlobalProtect post-authentication session validation to fail after successful Okta MFA, triggering tunnel teardown.
resolution_steps: Validated that Okta MFA was succeeding for m.engstrom and t.keller and correlated the immediate tunnel drop with certificate validation failures (CERT_EXPIRED, TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE) in GlobalProtect client logs on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-ME and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-TK.

Renewed the expired device certificates through the Device Certificate Service for affected endpoints WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-ME (m.engstrom, EMP-40291) and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-TK (t.keller, EMP-40387) and required certificate re-enrollment where the local certificate was no longer valid.
Refreshed and pushed the updated GlobalProtect client profile to affected devices in the Frankfurt office so the active VPN profile matched the renewed endpoint certificate state.
Verified conditional access group membership (RemoteWorkers) and policy alignment for m.engstrom and t.keller to ensure renewed certificates satisfied post-authentication access checks.

Had affected users m.engstrom and t.keller reconnect to GlobalProtect and confirm the VPN session remained established and internal applications (Intranet, HR Portal) were reachable from their respective endpoints.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether the Okta push is approved successfully and whether GlobalProtect drops before sign-in completes or only after it briefly shows connected. Also, can you confirm the gateway you're connecting to and whether Tobias Keller is seeing the same behavior on his device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-TK? You can reach me at n.osei@corplabs.com if needed.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: Remote user Marcus Delgado (EMP-40291) was trying to connect to the corporate network from a managed Windows 10 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-MD) at the Phoenix office using GlobalProtect. After approving the Okta MFA push notification on his device, the VPN tunnel connected briefly to gateway vpn-uswest.corplabs.com and then disconnected immediately, leaving internal applications such as the Internal Intranet App unreachable. The issue began after a recent device provisioning task on 2026-04-08 and was limited to a single corporate endpoint with client IP 10.47.83.112. Marcus reported the issue via email at m.delgado@corplabs.com.
observed_errors: GlobalProtect: session terminated due to certificate validation failure
root_cause: The affected endpoint presented an expired device certificate during post-MFA TLS validation. Okta MFA completed successfully, but GlobalProtect rejected the expired certificate and terminated the VPN tunnel immediately after authentication.
resolution_steps: Renewed the endpoint device certificate for WORKSTATION-DELL-MD through the Device Certificate Service (new cert serial 8B:3F:22:A1, valid through 2027-04-11) and confirmed the new certificate installed successfully on Marcus Delgado's laptop under the Personal certificate store.

Pushed an updated GlobalProtect VPN profile to WORKSTATION-DELL-MD via the management console so the active profile aligned with the renewed device certificate and pointed to gateway vpn-uswest.corplabs.com.

Cleared the stale local GlobalProtect profile and expired certificate association (serial 4A:7C:91:DE) cached on the device by removing entries from the PanGPS credential manager on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD.
Had Marcus Delgado re-enroll the VPN client using his credentials (mdelgado) and complete a fresh Okta MFA sign-in to establish a new tunnel session to vpn-uswest.corplabs.com.

Validated that the VPN session on WORKSTATION-DELL-MD remained connected and internal applications (including https://intranet.corplabs.com) stayed reachable during a 2-hour observation window from 09:15 to 11:15 UTC. User confirmed full connectivity from home IP 73.188.42.56.

Scheduled proactive remediation and expiry monitoring for other devices in the Remote Workers group with expired or near-expiry device certificates. Desktop support lead Raj Mehta created a recurring Device Certificate Service audit report filtered to the Phoenix and us-west-2 region endpoints, with 30-day advance expiry alerts sent to the IT operations team at it-ops@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, please confirm whether the VPN drops before MFA approval or only after the Okta prompt is approved on your device, and whether internal apps (e.g., the Intranet portal at https://intranet.corplabs.com) ever become reachable during the session. Also, can you verify the hostname of the affected laptop? We show it as WORKSTATION-DELL-MD assigned to your account mdelgado.

title: Laptop slow
description: I have a Windows 10 Pro Dell Latitude 5500 (hostname WORKSTATION-DL5500-MR, asset tag MKT-04821) assigned to Maria Reyes (emp ID E-20487) in the Marketing group becoming very slow immediately after login, with CPU rising above 85-90% within minutes and common applications such as Outlook and Chrome taking 20-30 seconds to open. The issue was reported from our Philadelphia office and affected normal post-login work. Investigation traced the root cause to endpoint protection activity and concurrent startup load on the laptop.
root_cause: Queued endpoint protection scans were triggering at user login while several nonessential startup applications were also launching, causing sustained CPU contention and delayed application startup.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Task Manager resource usage on WORKSTATION-DL5500-MR after login by user mreyes and confirmed CPU spikes (88-92%) were tied to EndpointProtectionService.exe activity and concurrent startup processes.
Cleared the queued endpoint protection scan backlog (four deferred full-disk scans) on WORKSTATION-DL5500-MR to stop repeated scan execution immediately after sign-in.
Disabled three nonessential startup applications (Adobe Updater, OneDrive auto-sync, Teams background launch) on WORKSTATION-DL5500-MR to reduce concurrent CPU load during the login sequence.

Refreshed device policy from endpoint management for WORKSTATION-DL5500-MR so scan behavior and startup-related policy state were updated on the laptop; confirmed successful policy sync at 2026-01-30T02:10Z.

Removed temporary files from C:\Users\mreyes\AppData\Local\Temp and C:\Windows\Temp, reclaiming approximately 8 GB of disk space on the 256 GB SSD to reduce endpoint performance pressure and help prevent future scan queuing.

title: Endpoint shows BitLocker disabled and no recovery key escrow
description: Company-managed Windows 11 laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-DELL-MR) assigned to Marcus Reeves (employee ID E-40291) in the Sales group is marked noncompliant for disk encryption in Microsoft Intune. I was trying to confirm BitLocker protection and locate the recovery key in Azure AD for device IP 10.22.47.118, but the device shows "Not Encrypted," no recovery key is escrowed, and I cannot satisfy encryption compliance after a reboot and manual Intune sync. The user is based out of the Charlotte office. Impact is limited to the affected endpoint remaining out of compliance and without recoverable BitLocker protection.
observed_errors: Azure AD: No BitLocker recovery key present
root_cause: BitLocker encryption did not start because the device had no active key protectors despite the encryption policy being assigned. Diagnostic evidence indicates the TPM was present but not initialized for BitLocker use, which prevented protector creation and therefore prevented recovery key escrow to Azure AD and left the device noncompliant in Intune.
resolution_steps: Initialize TPM/BitLocker protection on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (user mreeves, Marcus Reeves) and add a TPM-based protector to the OS volume C: using manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm so the drive has an active BitLocker key protector.

Enable BitLocker encryption on the system drive C: after confirming the protector is present via manage-bde -on C:, then verify the drive no longer reports "No key protectors" in manage-bde output on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR.

Back up the newly created BitLocker recovery key to Azure AD using BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector for the C: volume and confirm the recovery key is visible from the device record for mreeves@corplabs.com.

Force an Intune sync on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and reapply the assigned BitLocker/device encryption policy "Corp Endpoint Encryption - Windows" so the endpoint refreshes compliance and encryption state. Technician Priya Nair (pnair) confirmed sync completed successfully.

Validate that Intune changes from "Not Encrypted" to an encrypted/compliant state for WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (Marcus Reeves, E-40291) after policy and compliance evaluation completes. Confirmed device now shows compliant in the Charlotte office Sales group.

title: Internal hostname fails to resolve — stale A record in internal DNS
description: Multiple internal users and monitoring agents were trying to reach app.example.internal, but name resolution intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or the outdated IP address 10.20.5.47 from internal DNS. The issue was first reported by Priya Nambiar (emp ID E-40291) from the Austin office, who noticed the internal-app-service dashboard was unreachable by hostname. Additional reports came in from the Portland development team. The application could not connect to its backend by hostname, impacting internal app access across datacenter-1. Investigation focused on the internal BIND 9 zone data on dns-primary-01.dc1.internal and resolver cache behavior after a stale A record remained in the zone for a decommissioned address (10.20.5.47) instead of the current backend at 10.20.8.112.
observed_errors: Application error: unable to resolve host
root_cause: A stale A record for app.example.internal remained in the internal DNS zone and pointed to a decommissioned IP. Resolver and downstream cache entries then served outdated or failed responses, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN and incorrect address resolution.
resolution_steps: Corrected the A record for app.example.internal in the internal DNS zone file /etc/named/zones/db.example.internal so it pointed to the active backend IP 10.20.8.112 instead of the decommissioned address 10.20.5.47.

Incremented the zone serial from 2025121801 to 2026010501 and reloaded named on the primary DNS server dns-primary-01.dc1.internal via `rndc reload example.internal` so the updated zone data was published correctly.

Reloaded or synchronized the change to secondary DNS server dns-secondary-02.dc1.internal to ensure consistent authoritative responses across internal resolvers. Verified zone transfer completed via `rndc zonestatus example.internal`.

Flushed cached DNS entries on the primary and downstream resolvers (dns-primary-01 and dns-secondary-02) using `rndc flush` to remove stale responses for 10.20.5.47 and force retrieval of the updated record.

Validated name resolution from affected client paths including WORKSTATION-L490-PN (pnambiar, 10.30.14.88) and Network Monitoring dashboard checks, confirming that app.example.internal consistently resolved to the correct address 10.20.8.112.

Recommended adjusting the internal DNS TTL policy from 86400s to 3600s for application-tier hostnames to reduce the duration and impact of stale cached records in future changes. Flagged for review by the network team lead Deepak Rao.

title: AD account locked after repeated failed sign-ins
description: I was trying to sign in to the SSO portal at https://sso.corplabs.com from an iOS mobile device (hostname IPHONE-SALES-MR) but received an "account locked" message after several failed sign-in attempts. My username is mreeves and my employee ID is EMP-40291. When attempting self-service recovery through the Password Reset Portal, the reset link returned an "expired token" message. The issue blocked access to SSO-connected resources until the AD lockout was cleared, a valid reset token was issued, and stale mobile credentials were removed. I'm based in the Charlotte office and need access restored for client meetings today.
root_cause: Active Directory lockout policy was triggered by repeated failed sign-in attempts from the user's mobile device using stale cached credentials, and the previously issued password reset token was no longer valid.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Active Directory lockout activity on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal and confirmed Event ID 4740 entries tied to repeated failed authentication attempts from the user's mobile device (IPHONE-SALES-MR, IP 10.47.83.115) for account mreeves.
Unlocked the user's Active Directory account (mreeves, EMP-40291) in the admin console to restore sign-in eligibility, performed by Derek Huang on the identity_team.

Issued a new password reset token through the Password Reset Portal and confirmed the token was accepted for password reset by mreeves; the updated password propagated to DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal successfully.

Advised the user to clear saved credentials on the mobile device (IPHONE-SALES-MR), sign out of affected SSO-connected apps, and reauthenticate with the updated password through https://sso.corplabs.com.

Monitored for recurring lockout behavior after remediation on DC-EAST-03.corplabs.internal for account mreeves and confirmed no continued stale authentication attempts were observed from IP 10.47.83.115 or any other source.

title: Intermittent API timeouts from Integration Gateway causing delayed data sync
description: Application support engineer Priya Nair (emp ID: E-40291) reported delayed synchronization between the CRM Application and the third-party Salesforce Data API beginning around 2025-12-05 09:00 UTC. Intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout responses were returned by the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal), causing some scheduled API integration jobs to fail or complete late. Monitoring System dashboards showed correlated spikes in outbound latency from the gateway to the downstream API endpoint https://api.partnersync.io/v2/data. A gateway pod restart on node igw-worker-04 and temporary timeout increase from 30s to 90s did not remove the issue, and available logs on the gateway did not show clear token expiry errors or enough detail to distinguish between rate limiting and downstream latency. Ticket raised from the Arlington office.
root_cause: Primary cause was downstream API latency causing Integration Gateway requests to exceed the configured timeout window, with incomplete gateway access logging and missing token rotation context initially delaying confirmation. Token expiry was not supported by available evidence, and the existing retry/backoff behavior was insufficient to absorb intermittent latency spikes without causing job failures.
resolution_steps: Collected and correlated Integration Gateway timeout events from igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal with Monitoring System data for the incident window (2025-12-05 09:00–11:00 UTC) to confirm that 504 responses aligned with outbound latency spikes to the downstream API at https://api.partnersync.io/v2/data rather than gateway pod health issues on igw-worker-04.

Validated available authentication evidence for service account svc-apisync and reviewed token age and rotation details with Tomás Rivera to rule out an obvious expired or recently changed API credential as the trigger for the timeouts.

Adjusted the integration retry and backoff behavior in the apijobs-prod namespace configuration (max retries increased from 3 to 5, exponential backoff base raised from 2s to 5s) to better tolerate intermittent slow downstream responses and reduce immediate scheduled job failures during latency spikes.

Kept the increased request timeout (90s, up from the default 30s) in place as a temporary mitigation only where needed to allow delayed sync jobs (crm-daily-sync, inventory-hourly-push) additional time to complete during downstream slowness.

Escalated the latency pattern and 504 evidence to the downstream API provider PartnerSync for investigation of service responsiveness and any request-throttling conditions affecting the Integration Gateway, coordinated by Janet Cho (jcho@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office.
agent_questions: We confirmed repeated 504 responses from the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal) with matching outbound latency spikes visible in Monitoring System between 09:02 and 10:47 UTC. Hi Priya — please provide gateway access logs for the incident window and confirm the API token age or any recent credential rotation for service account svc-apisync so we can rule out auth or throttling issues. Also, can you confirm whether the integration jobs running under namespace apijobs-prod were all affected or only specific sync schedules? — Marcus Delgado, Integration Support

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to shared drive - Finance folder
description: I was trying to open the Finance shared drive at \\FS1\Finance from my Windows 10 domain-joined workstation (WORKSTATION-PC-LH) at the Frankfurt office. My employee ID is EMP-40291 and I need this resolved urgently as month-end close is approaching.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: Users on managed macOS and Windows devices at the Austin and Dublin offices were trying to connect to the corporate GlobalProtect VPN (portal gp-portal.corplabs.com) to reach internal applications, but the tunnel disconnected immediately after they approved the Okta MFA prompt. Authentication appeared to succeed briefly—users saw the 'Connected' status for 2–3 seconds—then the session was reset and internal CRM, Confluence, and other SAML-protected internal apps remained unreachable. The issue was first reported at approximately 06:10 UTC by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) from the Sales team and quickly confirmed by additional users including Marcus Delgado (Engineering). The issue began this morning following the routine certificate rotation window (scheduled 2026-04-13 22:00–02:00 UTC) and affected multiple users globally across both macOS 14.4 and Windows 11 23H2 endpoints.
observed_errors: Tunnel closed by peer immediately after authentication
Device certificate expired: certificate has expired
root_cause: Affected endpoints were presenting expired device certificates to the GlobalProtect gateway after successful Okta MFA, causing the gateway to terminate the VPN session immediately after authentication.
resolution_steps: Generated and deployed renewed device certificates to affected managed endpoints (including WORKSTATION-MACBOOK-RN for rnguyen and WORKSTATION-PC-MD for mdelgado) through the Device Certificate Service, issuing new certs from the CorpLabs Device CA with a validity period through 2027-04-14.

Refreshed the GlobalProtect VPN profile on impacted devices so the client used the current enrolled certificate. On macOS endpoints this required clearing the stale profile via `sudo /Applications/GlobalProtect.app/Contents/Resources/gp-refresh-profile` and on Windows via the GP Settings > Profile Refresh option.

Validated on test and affected endpoints (WORKSTATION-MACBOOK-RN, WORKSTATION-PC-MD, and three additional devices in Austin and Dublin) that the device certificate was no longer expired and matched the active VPN profile by running `certutil` / `security find-certificate` checks.

Had users rnguyen and mdelgado reconnect to GlobalProtect and complete Okta MFA again to confirm the tunnel stayed established and internal applications (CRM, Confluence) were reachable. Both users confirmed stable VPN sessions and successful access to internal resources. Contacted remaining affected users by phone (Rachel Nguyen at 512-555-0147) to confirm resolution.

Advised users to complete device re-enrollment if prompted by certificate renewal workflows and monitored gateway logs on gw-vpn-east-01.corplabs.internal for repeat post-MFA disconnects over the following 24 hours. Escalated to the PKI team (contact: pkiadmin@corplabs.com) to investigate why the automated rotation window failed to renew certificates on these endpoints.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please retry the GlobalProtect connection from your device (WORKSTATION-MACBOOK-RN) and confirm whether the VPN drops before MFA approval or immediately after you approve the Okta push prompt. Also let us know whether internal apps like CRM and Confluence remain unreachable after the disconnect. If possible, export the PanGPA log from GlobalProtect and attach it to this ticket. You can reach me at l.chen@corplabs.com if you need to share files directly.

title: Expired TLS certificate on load balancer causing internal service TLS failures
description: Users and internal clients were trying to access the internal-api service through the corporate load balancer (haproxy-lb-01.corp.local), but browsers displayed certificate expiration warnings and dependent integrations failed TLS handshakes. The outage was first reported by Marcus Jennings (emp ID E-40821) from the Portland office at approximately 05:30 UTC. The certificate presented for internal-api.corp.local had expired and the load balancer continued serving the old CA-signed chain, blocking normal access to the internal web service for the internal-devs user group.
root_cause: The TLS certificate presented by haproxy-lb for internal-api.corp.local expired, and the renewed full certificate chain was not deployed on the load balancer, so clients received the old expired certificate during handshake.
resolution_steps: Requested and obtained a renewed CA-signed TLS certificate for internal-api.corp.local from the internal Certificate Authority (CorpCA-Root), with a new validity period of 2025-12-20 to 2026-12-20. CSR was generated by Raj Kulkarni (rkulkarni) and approved by team lead Sandra Cho.

Replaced the expired certificate and updated the full certificate chain on haproxy-lb-01.corp.local at /etc/haproxy/certs/internal-api.pem, confirming correct certificate concatenation order (leaf → intermediate → root) and file permissions (0640, owned by haproxy:ssl-cert).

Reloaded and restarted the HAProxy worker processes on haproxy-lb-01.corp.local (systemctl restart haproxy) so the renewed certificate was loaded into active memory and presented on new TLS sessions. Verified no active session drops during the restart window.

Validated the served certificate from the client perspective — Marcus Jennings confirmed from his workstation (10.42.17.88) and Priya Desmond confirmed from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PD that the new expiration date (2026-12-20), correct hostname (internal-api.corp.local), and complete chain were being presented without warnings.

Restored and tested certificate monitoring so renewal alerts trigger 30 days before expiration. Raj Kulkarni re-enabled the alerting rule and added Sandra Cho (scho@corplabs.com) and the infra-alerts distribution list as notification recipients, ensuring future unnoticed certificate lapses are prevented.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — can you confirm whether the browser warning is specifically for internal-api.corp.local and whether internal clients (including CI runners on WORKSTATION-DEVBOX-MJ) are failing TLS handshake at the load balancer endpoint? Also, is the issue affecting users at other sites or just Portland? This is Raj Kulkarni from the network team following up.

title: Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service caused TLS failures
description: Users were trying to reach https://internal-api.local and dependent CI integration tests, but browsers showed certificate warnings and automated clients failed TLS handshakes. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the DevOps team in the Ashburn data center. The internal API became unreachable over HTTPS because the presented certificate had expired on 2025-12-23 and the load balancer LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal continued serving the old certificate chain, blocking internal-api-consumers and integrations until the TLS configuration was corrected. Multiple downstream services including the CI pipeline orchestrated from WORKSTATION-DEVOPS-MC were impacted.
observed_errors: TLS handshake failure: certificate has expired
Browser warning: Your connection is not private
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal-api.local expired on 2025-12-23. Renewal monitoring was not active, and although a renewed certificate was obtained, the load balancer continued serving the old certificate chain, causing client trust failures and TLS handshake errors.
resolution_steps: Requested and obtained a renewed TLS certificate (serial 7B:D4:11:A8, valid until 2026-12-23) for CN=internal-api.local from the internal Certificate Authority, submitted by dmorris under change request CHG-88412.

Deployed the renewed certificate to the Internal Web Service host WEBSVC-EAST-02.corplabs.internal and replaced the expired certificate material (old serial 3A:F2:9C:01) in the /etc/ssl/certs/internal-api directory.

Updated the load balancer SSL profile 'internal-api-ssl' on LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal with the correct renewed certificate and full certificate chain (leaf + CorpLabs Issuing CA G2 intermediate) so clients no longer received the old expired chain.

Restarted the load balancer SSL service on LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal (service haproxy reload) to ensure the new certificate chain was actively presented on the internal-api.local:443 endpoint. Confirmed via openssl s_client that the new serial 7B:D4:11:A8 was being served.

Validated HTTPS access from browser (Maria Chen on WORKSTATION-DEVOPS-MC at 10.24.16.88) and CI perspectives (build agent at 10.24.18.5) to confirm the certificate was current, matched the endpoint name CN=internal-api.local, and completed TLS handshakes successfully without warnings.

Restored certificate expiration monitoring by adding CN=internal-api.local to the cert-manager alert policy with a 30-day pre-expiry notification threshold, assigned certificate ownership to dmorris (DevOps), and documented certificate renewal ownership and policy updates in the Ashburn infrastructure runbook to prevent recurrence.

title: Device reported noncompliant — missing encryption flag and stale check-in (Intune)
description: User Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) reported that her corporate Windows 10 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN) was marked noncompliant in Intune, causing Conditional Access to block access to corporate email via Outlook. The device, checking in from the Portland office, showed a missing encryption compliance signal in Company Portal, and the Intune device record indicated the last successful check-in was 5 days ago (2025-12-29). The issue affected her single managed endpoint (IP 10.47.83.112) and prevented normal email access until compliance state was refreshed and the encryption requirement was correctly detected.
root_cause: The device remained noncompliant because its Intune compliance state was stale after not checking in for 5 days, and the assigned deprecated RequireEncryption_v1 compliance policy did not reliably detect the BitLocker encryption status following recent OS changes. This combination left Conditional Access enforcing a noncompliant state even after device remediation began.
resolution_steps: Triggered a remote sync from the Intune admin center for device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (user rnguyen@corplabs.com) to force the device to check in and refresh compliance evaluation. Performed by Derek Castillo (EMP-55190).

Initiated an on-demand compliance policy re-evaluation for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and confirmed the device was processing the assigned policy set again, including the RequireEncryption_v1 and platform health policies.

Directed Rachel Nguyen to enable BitLocker via the Control Panel and install pending Windows updates (including KB5034441) so the required encryption and platform health signals could be reported correctly on the next sync.

Verified on the next device check-in (2026-01-03T01:05Z) that the encryption signal was present on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and the device compliance state returned to compliant, restoring Rachel's Conditional Access to corporate email.

Raised follow-up remediation ticket (INC-DCP-0054) assigned to Marcus Webb to replace the deprecated RequireEncryption_v1 policy with RequireEncryption_v2 across the Sales user group so future devices would report encryption status reliably after OS updates.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — I can see the device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (enrolled under rnguyen@corplabs.com) is marked noncompliant and has not checked in for 5 days in Intune. The last successful sync was 2025-12-29T14:33Z. Please open Company Portal and confirm whether the failure shown is encryption-related, and whether BitLocker or Windows updates are currently pending. Also, can you confirm you're still working from the Portland office so we can rule out any network-level issues?

title: Internal Web Service TLS certificate expired causing TLS failures via Load Balancer
description: Users and internal systems were trying to reach the Internal Web Service over HTTPS at https://intweb.corplabs.internal, but browsers showed certificate warnings and API clients failed TLS validation through the load balancer (LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal). The issue was first reported by Priya Narayanan from the Portland engineering team, who noticed that dependent microservices on WORKSTATION-DEV-PN were unable to complete TLS handshakes. The service became effectively unavailable for normal secure access after the endpoint certificate passed its expiry date on 2025-12-22, and the load balancer continued serving an outdated certificate chain. This blocked internal application access and dependent integrations for the engineering/internal-services group until the renewed certificate and full chain were deployed.
observed_errors: TLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed
root_cause: The Internal Web Service TLS certificate expired, the renewed certificate chain was not fully deployed on the load balancer, and a misconfigured certificate-expiry monitoring rule failed to alert before expiration.
resolution_steps: Requested and obtained a renewed TLS certificate from the internal Certificate Authority (CA-EAST-01.corplabs.internal) for the Internal Web Service endpoint intweb.corplabs.internal. The CSR was generated by Sandra Liu and approved by infrastructure lead Tom Brennan (tbrennan).

Built and validated the full certificate bundle, including the required intermediate chain (ca-intermediate.pem), to confirm the endpoint name (CN=intweb.corplabs.internal) and trust chain were correct. Validation was performed from WORKSTATION-DEV-PN by Priya Narayanan to confirm client-side trust.

Updated the load balancer LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal to use the renewed certificate bundle and reloaded its configuration so it stopped serving the old chain. Marcus Delgado applied the configuration change and confirmed the full chain was now being presented via openssl s_client verification.

Deployed the renewed certificate bundle to the Internal Web Service endpoint and verified successful HTTPS handshakes from client paths using the load balancer. Priya Narayanan and Raj Mehta confirmed that browser access and API integrations from the Portland office were restored without certificate warnings.

Corrected the certificate monitoring and renewal alert rule (cert_expiry_warning) in cert-rotation-agent so future expirations and failed renewals are detected before service impact. Sandra Liu updated notify_days_before from 0 to 30 and added a secondary alert at 7 days. A test alert was sent to the infrastructure team distribution list to confirm delivery.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please confirm whether the browser warning shows the certificate as expired and whether API clients are failing only through the load balancer HTTPS endpoint (LB-EAST-01.corplabs.internal). Also, can you check from your workstation whether a direct connection to the backend on port 8443 shows the same error? I've looped in Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, ext. 4417) from the network team to assist. You can also reach me at ext. 3289 if needed.

title: GlobalProtect VPN disconnects immediately
description: Multiple remote users on Windows 10 managed laptops in the Charlotte office were trying to connect to the corporate network through GlobalProtect from the US-East region. Specifically, users including Rachel Simmons (rsimmons, EMP-40821) and Derek Huang (dhuang) reported that after approving the Okta MFA prompt, the client showed successful authentication but the VPN tunnel immediately tore down, leaving internal resources such as the intranet, finance web app, and corporate file shares unreachable. The issue began the same morning around 08:45 EDT, recurred after an initial fix on at least one endpoint (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RS, IP 10.47.22.118), and impacted the RemoteWorkers group.
root_cause: Expired or not properly re-enrolled device certificates on affected endpoints caused post-MFA certificate validation to fail. In addition, an inconsistent conditional access group assignment prevented the renewed certificate and active VPN profile from aligning with the expected GlobalProtect access policy, which led the tunnel to be torn down immediately after successful Okta authentication.
resolution_steps: Validated the device certificate state on affected endpoints (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RS for rsimmons and WORKSTATION-DELL-DH for dhuang) using the Device Certificate Service console and renewed certificates that were expired or not accepted by the VPN gateway — rsimmons's certificate had expired 2026-04-19 and was reissued with a new validity period through 2027-04-19.

Re-enrolled WORKSTATION-DELL-DH where the certificate refresh from the March rotation did not persist correctly due to an incorrect issuing CA, and confirmed the new certificate chain and validity period were present on the device. Marcus Patel (mpatel) performed the re-enrollment via Device Certificate Service.

Refreshed and re-pushed the GlobalProtect VPN profile to both WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RS and WORKSTATION-DELL-DH so the client profile matched the current certificate enrollment and gateway requirements for the US-East region.

Corrected the conditional access group assignment so that rsimmons and other impacted users in the RemoteWorkers group were added to the VPN-CertAuth-Allowed policy group, ensuring devices matched the intended VPN access policy after MFA. Change verified by Priya Nair (pnair).

Tested reconnection for both Rachel Simmons and Derek Huang after Okta MFA approval and verified the VPN tunnel remained established on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RS (IP 10.47.22.118) and WORKSTATION-DELL-DH, and internal applications including the intranet, finance web app, and corporate file shares were reachable without immediate disconnect.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether the GlobalProtect client on your laptop (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RS) shows authentication succeeded before the disconnect, and whether internal apps such as the intranet and finance web app remain unreachable immediately after the Okta MFA approval. Also, can you confirm whether Derek Huang is seeing the same behavior on his device?

title: Integration Gateway API calls timing out and returning authorization errors
description: During the nightly synchronization window starting at 02:00 UTC on 2025-12-07, internal applications routed through the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal) were unable to complete downstream API data sync jobs. The issue was first flagged by Rajesh Menon from the platform engineering team after the HR data pipeline and finance reconciliation feeds both failed. Monitoring dashboards on the Monitoring System and gateway access logs showed repeated HTTP 401 Unauthorized responses from the downstream API endpoint (api.dataservices.corpsync.internal/v2/sync), followed by cascading API call timeouts at the 30-second threshold. This increased job failure rates across 14 scheduled integration tasks and delayed data synchronization for multiple internal consumers including payroll and inventory services. Investigation by the application team focused on authentication token health and downstream API availability, ultimately determining that the gateway service account token (svc-igw-sync) had exceeded its 30-day rotation window by 15 days.
observed_errors: integration job failure during nightly sync
root_cause: The Integration Gateway service account API token had expired because token rotation had not occurred within the 30-day policy window, causing downstream API authentication failures (401 Unauthorized). Repeated retries during nightly sync jobs then cascaded into request timeouts.
resolution_steps: Rotate the Integration Gateway service account API token for svc-igw-sync in the secrets manager (Vault path secret/igw/prod/api-token) and update the Kubernetes secret igw-api-token in namespace igw-prod used by the gateway deployment. Rotation performed by Marcus Tan (E-50921) and verified by Lina Chowdhury.

Restart the Integration Gateway pods in the igw-prod namespace on k8s-cluster (us-east-1) so the running containers load the newly rotated token from the updated Kubernetes secret instead of the expired cached credential. Confirmed 3/3 pods recycled successfully by Marcus Tan.

Validate authenticated calls from the gateway (igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal) to the downstream API (api.dataservices.corpsync.internal/v2/sync) and confirm that 401 Unauthorized responses are no longer present in logs. Post-rotation test calls returned HTTP 200 with average latency of 195ms.

Re-run the 14 failed or pending synchronization jobs (including HR sync, finance reconciliation, and inventory feed) and verify they complete within the expected 30-second timeout window without elevated retries. All jobs completed successfully; Rajesh Menon confirmed data consumers received updated records.

Update token rotation monitoring and alerting in the Monitoring System so missed rotations beyond the 30-day policy for svc-igw-sync and other gateway service accounts are detected at the 25-day mark — 5 days before expiry — ensuring alerts reach the platform operations team (marcus.tan@corpsync.com, rajesh.menon@corpsync.com) before nightly sync processing is impacted.
agent_questions: Hi Rajesh — we are seeing both API timeouts and 401 Unauthorized responses during the nightly sync window (02:00–04:00 UTC). Logs from igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal show failures across multiple integration job IDs. Can you confirm whether the failures affect all scheduled sync jobs or only a subset, and whether there was any recent credential or secret change for the gateway service account svc-igw-sync? Also, please confirm if your team or anyone in DevOps — perhaps Lina Chowdhury — performed a manual secret rotation recently. I'm checking from my workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RM at 10.42.17.88.

title: unable to complete SSO login — MFA prompt loop (Okta/Azure AD)
description: I was trying to sign in to the corporate SSO Portal at https://sso.corplabs.com to reach SaaS applications, but the login flow repeatedly returned to the MFA challenge instead of completing authentication. My username is mreeves and I'm logging in from my workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR at IP 10.42.17.88. Okta sign-on activity showed repeated authentication failures and no successful assertion for the account (employee ID EMP-40291), preventing access to downstream apps through Okta/Azure AD SSO. I'm based in the Charlotte office and need access restored urgently for a client deliverable.
root_cause: Stale MFA factor enrollment on the user's Okta profile caused invalid MFA assertion validation during SSO, resulting in repeated challenge loops. The failed challenges were consistent with incorrect TOTP validation and were likely worsened by clock drift on the user's authenticator device.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the user mreeves's Okta sign-on events from IP 10.42.17.88 (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR) and confirmed repeated MFA challenges with no successful SSO assertion completion.

Validated that the user mreeves's access and policy scope in the Azure AD group 'SSO-SaaS-Users' were still correct in the identity path and that the issue was isolated to MFA completion rather than app assignment.
Reset the user mreeves's MFA enrollment in Okta to remove the stale factor registration causing the failed authentication loop; this was performed by Priya Nair on the identity team.

Guided the user to re-enroll their authenticator factor and resynchronize the device clock before generating new MFA codes. Marcus Reeves confirmed the new TOTP enrollment was active and codes were validating correctly.
Retested the SSO Portal login from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and verified that MFA completed successfully and the user mreeves regained access to SaaS applications without further prompt loops.

description: I (Mina Kim, emp ID EMP-90274) was trying to install the Contoso VPN client from Software Center on my managed Windows 10 21H2 x64 device (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK, IP 10.42.17.88), but the installation was blocked by Endpoint Protection before it could proceed. title: Multiple users cannot connect to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Multiple corporate users at the Charlotte office were trying to join the corp-employee SSID on managed devices, but after the overnight certificate rotation window (scheduled 2026-04-24T02:00Z) they either failed 802.1X authentication, disconnected immediately after associating, or connected without receiving network access. Users were blocked from normal wireless connectivity for corporate work because authentication to the Wireless Controller-backed RADIUS service (radius01.corp.eastnet.local) was failing. Initial reports came from Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40821) and at least six other employees on the 3rd floor. Affected hostnames include WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN and WORKSTATION-SURFACE-KP among others. The issue was escalated by the Charlotte site lead, Derek Whitfield (derek.whitfield@corplabs.com).
root_cause: The Wireless Controller's RADIUS server certificate expired at 2026-04-24T02:00Z, causing 802.1X EAP authentication failures and preventing many clients from completing wireless authentication and DHCP access on the corporate Wi-Fi network.
resolution_steps: Reissued and installed a new valid RADIUS certificate (CN=radius01.corp.eastnet.local, valid through 2027-04-24) on the Cisco Wireless Controller WLC-EAST-01 for 802.1X authentication, coordinated by network engineer Marcus Jennings (mjennings).
Restarted the controller authentication services on WLC-EAST-01 so the renewed certificate was actively presented to wireless clients; verified certificate thumbprint matched the newly issued cert.

Cleared cached EAP and authentication sessions on the controller (47 stale sessions) to force affected devices to perform a fresh authentication exchange; confirmed rnguyen, kpark, and pdeshmukh devices reconnected successfully within minutes.

Applied a temporary NAC exception (policy override group 'CERT-RENEWAL-TEMP') for impacted endpoints to restore access while clients refreshed trust and profile state; exception set to auto-expire 2026-04-25T06:00Z.

Instructed remaining affected users — including two legacy Windows 10 devices belonging to Tom Hadley (thadley, EMP-30287) — to forget and re-add the corp-employee SSID or re-enroll legacy device profiles via the self-service portal if they still held stale certificate trust information. Confirmed all users restored by end of business.
agent_questions: Hi Rachel — please confirm whether all affected users are failing exclusively on the corp-employee SSID and whether devices show an authentication failure immediately after joining or only after they briefly connect. Also, can you check if Kevin Park (kpark, EMP-51934) on your team is seeing the same behavior on his device WORKSTATION-SURFACE-KP? We want to determine if this is isolated to specific endpoints or a broader infrastructure issue affecting the Charlotte site.

title: Internal Web Service TLS outage
description: Users across the Portland office were unable to access the internal web service at https://portal.internal.corplabs.com over TLS starting around 12:45 UTC on 2025-12-18. Browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and internal health checks on the Kubernetes cluster failed TLS handshakes after the service certificate (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com) expired. An initial renewal was applied by the infrastructure team, but internal consumers routed through the F5 load balancer (lb-east-01.corplabs.internal) still received the expired leaf certificate, causing continued service unavailability for approximately 200 users in the Internal Services group. The incident was reopened by Marcus Delgado after the first closure, and was not fully resolved until certificate deployment and chain validation were completed end to end across both the backend pods and the load balancer termination point.
root_cause: The renewed TLS leaf certificate was issued, but the load balancer continued serving the expired leaf certificate and chain because the renewal/deploy workflow did not fully propagate the updated certificate to the LB. Certificate monitoring and renewal alerting also failed to trigger the expected redeploy validation before expiration.
resolution_steps: Renewed the TLS leaf certificate for portal.internal.corplabs.com through the internal Certificate Authority (ca.corplabs.internal), generating a new certificate (serial 7A:3F:01:CC, SHA-256 fingerprint verified) and confirmed the replacement certificate validity dates (2025-12-18 through 2026-12-17) and SAN coverage for portal.internal.corplabs.com.

Updated the load balancer lb-east-01.corplabs.internal with the renewed certificate, private key, and full certificate chain (leaf + intermediate CA), then reloaded the LB configuration via the Load Balancer Controller so it stopped presenting the expired leaf certificate (serial 4E:91:DA:07). Reload confirmed by Priya Nair at 13:52 UTC.

Redeployed the renewed certificate to the internal web service pods (portal-web-* in namespace prod-services) via kubectl rollout restart to keep the service endpoint and LB termination points in sync, verified by Rachel Owens.

Validated TLS handshakes and certificate presentation from both internal (10.42.17.88, WORKSTATION-PC-MD) and external paths to confirm the renewed chain was being served without date or trust errors. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) confirmed access restored from the Portland office.

Restored certificate expiration monitoring and renewal alerting (re-enabled Prometheus alert rule 'cert-expiry-30d'), and added an operational check to verify load balancer certificate sync after future renewals. Alert notifications configured to infra-certs@corplabs.com and on-call channel.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether the certificate warning appears only on the public service path (https://portal.internal.corplabs.com) or also from internal consumers behind the load balancer (lb-east-01.corplabs.internal), and whether the browser still shows a date-invalid certificate (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID). Could you also share the hostname or IP you're testing from? We want to rule out DNS caching. — Priya Nair, Infrastructure Engineering

title: Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service causing TLS failures (Load Balancer
description: Users were trying to access the internal web service (internal-web.corplabs.internal) over HTTPS, but browsers displayed certificate warnings and dependent clients failed TLS validation. The internal-web-service became unavailable over TLS in the Richmond data center after the service certificate expired on 2025-12-17, and the Load Balancer (LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal) was serving an incomplete chain. This was first reported by Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40821) via the IT portal. The issue blocked normal internal service access for the internal-services user group until the certificate and chain were corrected.
observed_errors: TLS handshake failed / certificate verify failed
root_cause: The Internal Web Service TLS certificate expired before renewal completed. The outage was compounded by the Load Balancer presenting an incomplete certificate chain because the required intermediate certificate was not updated, and certificate monitoring/renewal alerting did not trigger before expiration.
resolution_steps: Obtain a re-issued valid TLS certificate for the Internal Web Service from the internal Certificate Authority, ensuring the certificate SAN matches internal-web.corplabs.internal. Re-issuance was requested by Kevin Marsh (kmarsh) and approved by Sandra Liu.

Deploy the renewed certificate and private key to the Internal Web Service containers in the Richmond data center and reload the service so it presents the new non-expired certificate (new notAfter: 2026-12-17T23:59:59Z).

Update the Load Balancer LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal to include the correct intermediate certificate chain issued 2025-11-30, then reload the listener configuration so clients receive the full chain. Performed by Kevin Marsh.

Validate the HTTPS endpoint from both service-side and client-side perspectives to confirm the certificate is current, the chain is complete, and TLS handshakes succeed without browser warnings. Marcus Delgado confirmed access restored from WORKSTATION-PC-MD and Priya Nair confirmed from her workstation.

Restore and test certificate monitoring alerts and the automated renewal workflow so expiration and renewal failures are detected before the next renewal window. Alert rule for internal-web.corplabs.internal re-enabled and verified by Sandra Liu; test alert fired successfully at 2025-12-18T20:15:00Z.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether users are seeing a browser certificate date warning (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) or a full trust-chain warning, and whether the issue affects all HTTPS access to internal-web.corplabs.internal. Also, can you let us know which client machines or teams are impacted? My name is Sandra Liu and I'll be handling this ticket. You can reach me at x4177 if needed.
